gloss_en: the Hebrew letter vav (sixth letter, numerical value six, shaped like a hook/staff), as a letter-symbol expounded homiletically/kabbalistically — signifying drawing-down, connection, and addition (e.g. filling the vav of kavod, the Tablets six-by-six, the six days of creation)

the vav within the letter aleph — the diagonal stroke of the aleph's written form, conceived kabbalistically as a vav joining its two yud-points (identified variously with the firmament between the upper and lower dots, and with the opening/connection between the two yuds of the divine Names)
the second vav
the act of eating on Shabbat (partaking of the Shabbat meals as a holy act of eating — oneg Shabbat through food, from which the Sitra Achra has no portion and which blesses the six weekdays)
oneg Shabbat — the mitzvah-delight of the Sabbath (עֹנֶג שַׁבָּת), the sanctified pleasure/enjoyment of Shabbat, exemplified by holy Sabbath eating, which subdues enemies as fasting does

the delight of Shabbat eating (oneg akhilat Shabbat) — the pleasurable act of eating on the Sabbath as a devotional practice, which (in Likutey Moharan I:57) perfects speech into peace, contrasted with the peace of weekday fasting; one compound phrase appearing in two word orders

the revelation of God's glory — נִתְגַּלֶּה כְּבוֹדוֹ (יִתְבָּרַךְ), that the honor/glory (kavod) of the Blessed One becomes manifest and revealed (hitgalut ha-kavod), specifically through humanity and its increase
His glory was revealed AND magnified — compound action adding נתגדל (magnification) to the revelation
His glory was increased and magnified — different verbal heads (נתרבה/נתגדל, not נתגלה) and different Torah (lm2:8)

The perfection/completion (shlemut) of the Holy Tongue — the state in which lashon ha-kodesh is made whole by elevating the good within Targum/the seventy languages; a quality attained by a person (paradigmatically Joseph) that rectifies the covenant (tikkun ha-brit), cools sexual heat, saves from nocturnal emission, illumines the letters within every created thing, and enables dream interpretation (Likutey Moharan I:19). Not the Holy Tongue itself, but its state of completeness.

Leshon HaKodesh — the Holy Tongue (Hebrew) as the sacred language through which the world was created; identified in Likutey Moharan 19 with Chavah/the woman/holy speech (dibbur) and with ruach hakodesh, the language whose power casts down the seventy languages and restrains the lust of adultery — the Holy Tongue itself as an entity, distinct from the separate concept of its 'perfection' (shlemut leshon hakodesh)

Perfection/completeness of speech (שְׁלֵמוּת הַדִּבּוּר) identified with the Holy Tongue (לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ) in Torah lm2:2 — the wholeness of the faculty of speech attained through the one complete language, contrasted with the deficient 'stammering' tongues of the nations, linked to Shabbat-speech and serving as the means to draw Shabbat's joy into the six weekdays; construct head is שלמות הדבור (speech), not שלמות לשון הקדש of lm1:19
forms: שלמות הדבור שהוא בחינת לשון הקדש

gloss_en: the act of breaking/subduing the lust for money (shevirat ta'avat mamon) — shattering, cooling, or nullifying the craving for wealth (equated with the idolatry of money), achieved through truth, charity, and tikkun ha-brit; the rectification (tikkun) of this desire, not the lust itself nor money as such
the lust for money itself
the rectification statement (menstrual blood, money-lust) — a statement, not a concept name
The desire for money being rectified (rectification-action; head תיקון/נתתקן, distinct from the 'breaking' action)

The Beit HaMikdash — the Holy Temple in Jerusalem as an edifice/place, treated as a bechina (symbolic aspect) identified with da'at (holy awareness), kodesh/reishit, the secrets of Torah, and the 'house' (bayit) illuminated by Shabbat; not a generic house, sanctuary vessel, or the Mishkan

The act of building/constructing the Holy Temple (binyan Beit HaMikdash) — understood as the renewal of the mochin (mentalities) and Da'at, per Berakhot 33 ('whoever has knowledge, it is as if the Temple was built in his days'); the constructive act, not the Temple edifice itself
The burning/destruction of the Temple (the act) — distinct action, opposite valence
The labor/work of building the Temple — construct head מלאכה (labor), distinct from the abstract 'building' and from the Temple itself
Novel Torah insights (chiddushei Torah / chiddushin de-Oraita) — original interpretations or innovations newly generated in Torah study, as an act of creative renewal of Torah
The Torah novellae that a person innovates (in lm1:118 equated with the aspect of Mashiach)

The novel Torah insights (chiddushei Torah) that one reveals/expounds publicly — in lm2:60's RaShbY–R. Akiva teaching, the act of revealing Torah novellae, which draws down kindnesses (chasadim) and Godliness into the listener's mind

loosening the mouth of the mute — the Talmudic dictum (Sanhedrin 100a on "ve-alehu li-terufah") that the tzaddik's healing speech opens mute mouths, i.e., restores the power of holy speech; identified with the coupling of kissing (zivug ha-neshikin) that precedes and enables loosening the womb of the barren
to release the 'mouth' of the barren (open the womb)

canonical_he: להתיר פה אלמים להתיר פה עקרות
gloss_en: the paired formula naming both releases together
forms: להתיר פה אלמים להתיר פה עקרות

gloss_en: The Name of the Holy One, blessed be He (שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ־בָּרוּךְ־הוּא) — God's Name conceived as the vessel that bounds and contains the divine life-force from the Life of all life; in Likutey Moharan I:56 identified with the Torah, whose letters, words, verses, and sections function as measures (midot) delimiting that life-force
The wrath of the Holy One (God's anger, per 'the king's wrath')
The prayer of the Holy One (God's prayer / simple mercies)
The Holy One, blessed be He (God Himself, not a possessed attribute)
the imaginative faculty (koach ha-medammeh) — the psyche's image-producing power, shared with animals, source of fantasies, dreams, and desires, opposed to intellect/memory

the rectification (tikkun) of the imaginative faculty — the act of repairing and purifying the koach ha-medammeh (the imagination), so that it no longer produces false fantasies and can instead support faith and prophecy (as taught in Likutey Moharan II:8); not any other kind of 'tikkun,' nor the imaginative faculty itself unrectified
the rectification of imagination AND faith (the paired phrase)
The 'brain/mind' as expressed in relation to the ears (hearing the words of the wise)
The 'brain/mind' as expressed in relation to the nose (fear of God, 'beginning of wisdom')
The 'brain/mind' as expressed in relation to the eyes (the eyes being opened)
The 'brain/mind' as expressed in relation to the mouth ('the beginning of Your word is truth')
The lust of adultery/illicit sexual desire (the desire itself, as a base concept)

The act of breaking/subduing (shevirah) the lust for adultery — the deliberate conquest performed upon the sexual lust, which serves as a means (e.g., for rectifying the mochin/mind); distinct from the lust of adultery itself
The rectification of the lust of adultery (act of tikkun; distinct construct head from 'breaking')
The lust of adultery that has been nullified (the lust in its nullified state/event)

Eretz Yisrael — the Land of Israel as a spiritual reality in Likutey Moharan: the locus and embodiment of faith (emunah), prayer, miracles, Divine providence (hashgachah) beyond nature, patience (erech apayim), and the totality of holiness; both the physical Holy Land one merits to reach and its mystical aspect (bechinat Eretz Yisrael)

The holiness of the Land of Israel (kedushat Eretz Yisrael) — the sacred quality inhering in the Land (expressed as 'the air of the Land of Israel makes wise'), generated by God's watchful gaze ('eyes of Hashem') aroused through His glorying in Israel; an attribute of the Land, distinct from the geographic Land itself
Inheriting/inheritance of the Land of Israel — an action/event of acquiring the Land, not the Land itself

'A woman who fears the Lord' (eshet yir'at HaShem, Prov 31:30) — the biblical phrase as a kabbalistic symbol of malkhut, the kingdom of Heaven personified as the mistress (gevirta, opposed to the harlot/maidservant), and identified in LM I:49 with the aspect of counsel (etza)
yirat Hashem — fear/awe of God as a spiritual state, identified with shame (busha) revealed on the forehead and with the light of tefillin (Binah upon Ze'ir Anpin)

The 'covenant of salt' (berit melach [olam], Num 18:19) — an epithet for the tzaddik, who like salt sweetens the world's bitterness and expels bad blood; distinct from the plain 'eternal covenant' (ברית עולם), which lacks the salt motif
The eternal covenant, tied to prayer / the 18 blessings and 'tzaddik chai almin'; no salt element — a different construct phrase

Masa u'matan — business dealings / commerce, the worldly activity of buying, selling, and trade (Zevulun's 'going out'), which Rabbi Nachman homiletically re-reads as 'carrying and giving' (lifting fallen sparks and returning them, the union of tzaddik and Knesset Yisrael); not physical burden-carrying or a prophetic 'massa' (oracle)

Business dealings conducted in faith/honesty (masa u-matan be'emunah) — commerce carried out with faithful integrity, contentment with one's portion, and trust in God; a qualified spiritual mode of trade that fulfills 've'ahavta', renews the mind within emunah, and is distinct from bare משא ומתן by the qualifier באמונה
The one who conducts business in faith — the agent/doer, not the activity itself
that the seed of Amalek be consumed/destroyed (finite piel verb כלה); glossed as 'yadber amim tachteinu' in Torah 6
the cutting-off/extermination of the seed of Amalek (verbal noun); in Torah 35 identified with sparks rising from among the nations, per the 11 incense spices
to cut off the seed of Amalek (infinitive of purpose); in Torah 6 identified with Yehoshua, the lower point

The manna (מָן) — the miraculous heavenly bread that fed Israel in the wilderness ('lechem min hashamayim'), which Rebbe Nachman treats as the aspect of da'at (knowledge, esp. the fiftieth gate) and of livelihood without toil; NOT the preposition מִן ('from')

Oil (shemen), the noun for anointing/lamp oil — the substance used for anointing (David's malchut, 'oil of gladness'), fueling the seven lamps of the Menorah, and figuratively the bodily moisture/lachluchit that fuels the brain-wick and heals the lungs; NOT manna, NOT 'fat/fatness' (shaman/shuman) as a verb or adjective, and NOT 'eighth' (shemini)

Haman the wicked (the villain of the Book of Esther), Amalekite adversary of Mordekhai — embodiment of pride (ga'avut), the malkhut of the sitra achra, and idol worship (he made himself an object of worship); a proper name, NOT הַמָּן 'the manna'

The practice of telling/recounting stories of the deeds of tzaddikim (לְסַפֵּר, pi'el infinitive 'to tell' — the verbal act of narrating, not the stories/סִפּוּרִים themselves and not counting/סְפִירָה), a spiritual counsel that purifies thought and rescues from troubles
Narrations/tellings of stories of tzaddikim (nominal construct ספורי) — characterized as mochin de-gadlut
The stories of tzaddikim themselves (the tales as object) — characterized as bechinat or

The Light of the (Divine) Countenance (or ha-panim) — the shining of God's face as divine illumination: renewal of the intellect/soul, truth and faith, and the revelation of the encompassing lights (makifim) and illumination of the Divine will; not the showbread (lechem ha-panim) nor any physical face

The drawing-down (hamshakhah) of the Light of the Divine Countenance (Or ha-Panim) — the act of channeling/eliciting the illumination of God's Face, identified in Likutey Moharan 21 with the revelation of the mochin (mentalities) and the flow of Divine effluence; the dynamic act of drawing the light down, not the light itself
The shining/radiance of the Light of the Face — the event/manner of its shining forth, not the light itself
the Tablets of the Covenant (luchot ha-brit) given at Sinai — the stone Tablets of the Ten Commandments, six tefachim long and six wide (Bava Batra 14a), hence the aspect of the letter vav
'mi-luach' — the from-the-tablet wordplay quoted as a term

The Tablets (luchot) of the Covenant on which the Torah was engraved at Sinai — the stone tablets (whose length and breadth are six handbreadths, hence linked to the letter vav), also identified with the 'tablet of the heart' (Prov. 3:3) and the broken Tablets

The unification (yichud) of the Holy One, blessed be He, with His Shekhinah — the kabbalistic union of the transcendent Divine (Kudsha Brich Hu) and the indwelling Divine Presence, effected as an act/state through holy speech and deeds
The Holy One, blessed be He (the divine referent itself), not the act of union

canonical_he: יחוד קדשא בריך הוא ושכינתה אפין באפין
gloss_en: The face-to-face (apin b'apin) union of the Holy One and His Shekhinah — a specific mode/quality of the union, distinct from the unqualified yichud
forms: יחוד קדשא בריך הוא ושכינתה אפין באפין

gloss_en: The World to Come (olam ha-ba; Aramaic: alma d'atei) — the eschatological realm/future world of ultimate reward and truth, entirely Shabbat, without eating or drinking, whose essence is the attainment of knowledge of God's divinity

The honor/glory of the World to Come (kevod olam ha-ba) — a construct phrase with kavod as head: the higher, future-world honor of God attained through the second repentance (repenting on one's first repentance) in Likutey Moharan I:6, contrasted with the honor of this world; not the World to Come itself, nor kavod in general
A semblance/foretaste OF the World to Come — the experience (in this world) of recognizing all events are for one's good; a taste of, not identical to, the World to Come
the rain-clouds (avei matra)

the voice's striking against the rain-clouds (avei mitra) — the moment, per Zohar Pinchas 235b, when the outgoing voice (of forceful prayer) collides with the dense rain-clouds, thereby producing audible thunder

elucidations of the Torah (be'urei ha-Torah) — the explanatory expositions/novellae of Torah drawn down by the tzaddik-sage, homiletically linked to be'er (well); not the well itself nor any other sense of the root
expositions and homilies of the Torah (the paired phrase — stays whole per your rule)
drawing down the expositions (the act)

the spoken utterance (dibbur) of Torah study and prayer — the verbal articulation of Torah and tefillah, identified in Likutey Moharan I:75 with 'tzedek' ("righteousness you shall speak", Ps. 58:2) and with the aspect of legs/standing (raglin), whose words effect the clarification of the fallen sparks
the holy speech (speech of holiness) of Torah and prayer — qualified head adds 'of holiness'
cherut (חֵרוּת) — freedom/liberty as emancipation from servitude and exile (the opposite of shi'bud), e.g. the freedom of a ben chorin, of Shabbat, and of Pesach; not חָרוּת 'engraved'

blackness (shacharut) — the black/dark quality, as in the black of the eye's pupil, which contracts, limits, and encompasses what stands before it; the constricting darkness by which the lower intellect condenses the higher light (not 'youth' as in Ecclesiastes 11:10, and not shachar 'dawn' itself, though homiletically linked to shacharit)
Cherut — freedom/liberty (as in ben chorin, freedom of the covenant)

the sparkling/flashing forth (hitnotzetzut) of the light of the merit of the Patriarchs (zechut avot — Avraham, Yitzchak, Yaakov), whose radiance enables drawing down the holiness of the Land of Israel even in exile (LM I:55)

davar (דָּבָר) — 'word/thing/matter'; the noun for speech/utterance or a thing/matter, used homiletically as bechinat yirah (fear, LM1:15, 'az nidberu yirei H'') and bechinat Malkhut (LM1:4, 'kol davar asher yavo va'esh')
medaber — 'the speaker': the human/articulate level in the fourfold hierarchy of creation (mineral, vegetable, animal, speaker), i.e., humankind defined by the faculty of speech
devarim — 'words' (plural), specifically וידוי דברים = confession, בחינת מלכות

The seven lamps of the Temple menorah (shiv'at ha-nerot) as a mystical structure — corresponding to the seven orifices of the face (mouth, two nostrils, two eyes, two ears) upon the menorah of the head/brain, and mapped onto the seven clouds of glory, the seven wedding-feast days, and the oil-fed lights whose sanctification draws the surrounding lights (makifin) within

The sanctification of the seven lamps (of the menorah, symbolizing the seven apertures/orifices of the face — eyes, ears, nostrils, mouth) — the act of sanctifying them (kedushah as construct head / the verbal act מקדשין), which enables bringing the surrounding lights (makifin) inside; NOT the lamps themselves, nor sanctity in general

Idolatry / foreign worship (avodah zarah, also avodat elilim) — worship of other gods, which Rabbi Nachman extends as the paradigm of all corrupted faith: heresy, falsehood, arrogance, and any turning away from God (e.g., anxiety over livelihood)
Idolatry and the heresies/denials — a coordinated compound pairing avodah zarah with kefirut, not the bare term for idolatry
all the remedies/cures (the noun concept itself)
the falling/descent of all the remedies (an event/state predicated of the remedies, not the remedies themselves)
the receiving of all the remedies (an action of reception, distinct from both the remedies and their falling)

canonical_he: כלי וצנור לקבל על ידו החסד
gloss_en: The vessel and channel (kli ve-tzinor) fashioned through fear of God (yirah) that enables one to receive the divine kindness (chesed) gradually, since unbounded chesed cannot be received directly (Likutey Moharan II:4)
forms: כלי וצנור לקבל על ידו החסד
כלי וצנור לקבל על ידו השפעת החסד

canonical_he: חקיקה וצנור לקבל על ידו החסד
gloss_en: An engraving/carving and channel to receive the chesed — distinct head noun (חקיקה 'engraving') vs כלי 'vessel'
forms: חקיקה וצנור לקבל על ידו החסד

gloss_en: The joy of the festival (Yom Tov)
The essence/root of festival joy — a different construct head (עקר) governing 'joy of Yom Tov', not the joy itself
A predication that a person 'has' festival joy (a clause/state), distinct from the abstract concept of festival joy

The act of a fallen person actively seeking and asking 'Where is the place of His glory?' (Ayeh mekom kevodo) — the searching itself, which revives him and lifts him back to the supernal glory (Likutey Moharan II:12), not the liturgical phrase as such
The liturgical question 'where is the place of His glory' (from the Kedushah) itself — the object, not the act of seeking it

"Luminaries of light" (me'orei or) — the supernal holy luminaries drawn from the Name of God, the aspect of Shabbat and of the light of the eyes (the three colors of the eye and the pupil), the holy counterpart opposing the מאורי אש (luminaries of fire)
The shining/prevailing of the luminaries of light — the act of these lights illuminating and overpowering, not the lights themselves
The departure/withdrawal of the luminaries of light — the state of their removal (heaven forbid), opposite of their shining

The mochin (mentalities/supernal intellect) of the Land of Israel — the consciousness rooted in Eretz Yisrael, source from which all minds (even those of the Diaspora) receive and draw sustenance, identified with the aspect of no'am (pleasantness) as in Zechariah 11:7 (Likutey Moharan II:71)
The charity of the Land of Israel — tzedakah as the vessel to receive the supernal no'am; distinct concept (charity, not intellect)

erekh apayim — 'long of nostrils/breath', i.e. slow to anger: the divine attribute of forbearance (from the Thirteen Attributes, Ex. 34:6), expounded by R. Nachman as patient endurance in divine service — extending one's spirit/breath (as in the sigh that draws the spirit of life) and remaining unshaken by any obstacle; attained through faith (emunah) and the Land of Israel

Targum — the Aramaic translation-language (leshon Targum / leshon Arami), the intermediate tongue mixed of good and evil, corresponding to the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil and to kelipat Nogah, whose good must be elevated into (and thereby builds and perfects) the Holy Tongue while its evil is cast down
the tzaddik (צַדִּיק) — the righteous person/saintly leader, guardian of the covenant (like Moses, Joseph); the noun 'righteous one,' not the abstract quality of righteousness (צֶדֶק)

THE Tzaddik (ha-tzaddik) — the singular true tzaddik of the generation, the 'head' (rosh) of the Jewish people from whom all the generations are drawn; the Moses-figure/leader archetype to whom one travels (e.g., for Rosh Hashanah) and whose passing is mourned; not tzaddikim in general nor the sefirah Yesod as such

Chashmal — the kabbalistic luminous 'garment' (malbush, equal in gematria to chashmal) from Ezekiel's vision, expounded as chash-mal ('silent-speaking'/'silence-circumcision'): the protective enclothing level linked to circumcision (milah), to the kelipah of Nogah that can be absorbed into holiness, and to 'speaking truth in one's heart' that clothes and guards faith (as tefillin straps)
mal of chashmal — the 'mal' (speech/circumcision) component extracted from the word chashmal, symbolizing the bonfire of seventy stars that is spoken-down and nullified through the Holy Tongue

Tikkun ha-brit — the rectification and guarding of the covenant of sexual holiness (the brit/organ of procreation): repairing pgam ha-brit and maintaining shemirat ha-brit (sexual purity, including tikkun for keri); the general positive tikkun of the brit associated with Yosef — not 'covenant' in the sense of a treaty/pact between parties, nor circumcision as mere ritual act
Rectification FOR the blemish of the covenant — remedy for damage already done (Elul kavanot); construct head is 'rectification for the blemish', not 'the covenant' itself

"The way of the eagle in the heavens" (derekh ha-nesher ba-shamayim, Proverbs 30:19) — the scriptural phrase employed in Likutey Moharan I:29 as a mystical figure for the rectification of the covenant (tikkun ha-brit) and its link to heaven, whiteness, and effortless livelihood

The verse Psalms 29:2 "Hishtachavu la-Hashem be-hadrat kodesh" ("Bow down to the Lord in the splendor of holiness"), cited as a proof-text whose initial letters spell קבלה (Kabbalah) and which embodies yichuda ila'ah (the Supernal Unification, the Shabbat union)

"Ve'ahavta" — 'And you shall love [the Lord your God]' (Deut 6:5), the qal perfect-consecutive verse-word of the Shema; in LM 1:210 it is the commandment fulfilled through honest business dealings (per Yoma 86a, 'that the Name of Heaven become beloved through you') and is identified as the aspect of Abraham, the lover of God — not any other form of the root אהב

Verse fragment (Psalms 119:109): 'and Your Torah I have not forgotten' (ve-Toratekha lo shakhachti) — the conclusion of 'My soul is in my hands always,' expounded in LM I:46 as the memory-preserving effect (segula for zikaron, averting forgetfulness/mochin de-katnut) attained through clapping the hands during prayer

"The fear of the LORD is his treasure" (Isaiah 33:6) — the scriptural phrase יִרְאַת ה' הִיא אוֹצָרוֹ, cited as the aspect of fear/awe of God functioning as a storehouse (otzar), linked to the Talmudic 'he made her like a storehouse of wheat' (עֲשָׂאָהּ כְּאוֹצָר)

The verse-phrase "yir'at HaShem hi tit'hallal" — "a woman who fears the LORD, she shall be praised" (Proverbs 31:30), read as: fear of God is itself praise/tehillah, hence the aspect of prayer; linked to the nose (chotem/echetam) and to smelling with the fear of the LORD (Isaiah 11:3)

Faith (emunah) — the noun אֱמוּנָה: belief/trust in God and His providence, the spiritual faculty of faith (identified in Likutey Moharan with prayer, malchut, the Land of Israel, Shabbat, and the rectified imagination); not אֻמָּנוּת (craft), אָמְנָה (pact), or אֹמְנָה (nurture/guardianship) as independent senses — even where the 'omen/nurturing' etymology (וַיְהִי אֹמֵן אֶת הֲדַסָּה) is cited, it is invoked as an aspect of emunah itself

Raglin/raglayim — the feet/legs, the lowest limbs of the body (Aramaic raglin), used as a homiletic bechina for the lowest levels: speech, livelihood/money, the rebukers of the generation, the wife/nukva, standing in Torah and prayer, dancing, and the sefirot Netzach-and-Hod

Regel — the noun 'foot' (singular of raglayim), the lowest limb; used as a homiletic hub in Likutey Moharan for whatever stands at the 'lowest level' or 'carries' a person: counsel/advice ('kol ha-am asher be-raglekha' = those following your counsel), commerce/travel for business ('semach Zevulun be-tzetekha'), prayer, wealth ('ha-yekum asher be-ragleihem'), the wife ('raglei chasidav yishmor'), and — via the cognate verb ragal/nirgan — slander and strife ('lo ragal al leshono'). Distinct from רֶגֶל 'pilgrimage festival', הֶרְגֵּל 'habit', or רָגִיל 'accustomed'.

"The tzaddik is the foundation of the world" (Proverbs 10:25) — the scriptural phrase 'tzaddik yesod olam' as used kabbalistically to identify the righteous one with the sefirah of Yesod, the channel/foundation sustaining the world

The Scriptural phrase (Deut. 33:18) "Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out" (שְׂמַח זְבוּלוּן בְּצֵאתֶךָ) — the blessing of the tribe of Zebulun, invoked as the archetype of engaging in commerce/business dealings (masa u-matan, the 'going out') in holiness, and hence as the emblem of the rectification of the craving for money

water (Heb. מַיִם / Aram. מַיָּא) — the liquid element as a symbolic bechina in Likutey Moharan: the heart poured out before God ('pour out your heart like water'), charity/tzedakah, and the male and female waters (mayin dukhrin u-nukvin) from which man is formed; the physical noun 'water' itself, not any other word sharing these letters
sea (yam, the body of water) — used as a kabbalistic symbol for Malkhut: the 'mouth' of speech into which all streams flow (LM I:38) and the sea of faith in which a path is opened (LM II:87)
soul (nefesh) — the animating life-force/soul of a person, lowest of the triad nefesh–ruach–neshamah; includes plural nefashot (souls); not to be confused with any other reading of the letters נפש
chesed — lovingkindness: the divine attribute/sefirah of benevolent kindness (right-hand side, personified by Abraham), manifest in acts of charity, teaching Torah to others, and drawing people near

chasadim — the kabbalistic kindnesses (plural of chesed): the supernal lights/forces of divine benevolence associated with the right side and Chesed, which illuminate (nehiru de-chokhmeta), sweeten and subdue the gevurot (severities); a technical Lurianic/Zoharic term, not ordinary human acts of kindness

The Torah — God's revealed teaching/law (the noun תּוֹרָה, 'instruction'), encompassing Written and Oral Torah and its study (עסק התורה); identified with the Divine Name and with 'zot ha-Torah adam' — not any other sense of the letters ת-ו-ר-ה

Speech/utterance (dibbur) — the faculty and act of spoken word, the divine speech that is 'the breath of His mouth,' the aspect of Malchut-of-the-mouth, Shechinah, and the gevurot emerging through the five articulations of the mouth; plural = the utterances/spoken words (not the insect 'bee' or the name Deborah)

the still and pure air (avir ha-nach ve-ha-zakh) — in Likutey Moharan I:17, the tranquil, purified atmosphere created when love is acquired through giving tzedakah, wherein the spirits (ruchot) of lover and beloved cleave and rest in one another, with no 'bad wind' of hatred separating them; its expanse grows the more people one gives charity to

The sinless breath (hevel she'ein bo chet) — the holy, sin-free breath of the mouths of Torah-learning schoolchildren, identified in Likutey Moharan I:37 with the air of the Land of Israel, through which the patriarchs are revealed and judgment (216/din, mantzpakh) is sweetened and elevated

Malkhut/kingship — the abstract noun מַלְכוּת denoting the sefirah of Kingship/divine sovereignty: the 'lower wisdom' (chokhmah tata'ah) that governs each world, bechinat dalet/nun 'that has nothing of its own' but receives from Chokhmah; identified with speech ('malkhut peh'), prayer, faith, fear/awe, the Shekhinah, honor, and holy kingship (malkhut dikdusha) as opposed to the kingship of the Other Side — not the concrete nouns מֶלֶךְ (king) or מַלְכָּה (queen)
Halakhot — the legal rulings/laws of Torah studied by Torah scholars (הֲלָכוֹת, from הֲלָכָה), homiletically linked to תַּהֲלוּכוֹת, the orderly 'walking' flow of the blood

spring/wellspring (מַעְיָן, a flowing water-source) — Kabbalistic symbol of Chochmah (wisdom), the point-like source (yud) from which intellect/Binah flows like a river; distinct from the homograph מְעַיֵּן 'one who studies/contemplates'
'in the eye' — preposition ב + עַיִן (eye); context of memory dwelling in the eye and guarding against 'evil eye'
when one has faith
when one has faith of that specific kind

Ein Sof — the Infinite; God's boundless, undifferentiated infinitude (and its light) prior to and beyond creation, above all souls and beyond intellectual grasp, where completeness and unity of will are absolute
the Will of Ein Sof (Ra'ava d'Ra'avin) — a divine attribute/state of the Infinite, not the Infinite itself

The altar (mizbe'ach) of the Temple as expounded in Likutey Moharan I:17 — the aspect of holy eating, identified with a person's table that atones like the altar (Berakhot 55a) and with 'the altar in the portion of the one who snatches' (Binyamin); its completion subdues the foolishness of the intellect, whose kelipot draw their sustenance from eating

Being physically present at the moment of the tzaddik's departure from this world (histalkut) — when the supernal spirit descends and a great illumination is revealed, benefiting all present with length of days (Likutey Moharan I:66)

Shabbat, the seventh-day Sabbath (the holy day of rest, שַׁבָּת) — which testifies to God's unity and the creation of the world, and serves in Likutey Moharan as the aspect (bechina) of faith, truth, teshuvah, the World to Come, da'at, the inner point, the luminaries of light, and the Name of the Holy One

Bat (בַּת, 'daughter') as an exegetical unit — the 'daughter' of 'Avraham had a daughter and Bakol was her name' (Bava Batra 16b), which R. Nachman expounds as the bat-component of the word Shabbat (shin + bat) and as bat-ayin (pupil of the eye), identified variously with faith, prayer, and blessings; not the word Shabbat itself, not 'house of' (beit), and not a measure (bat)

The glory/honor of God (kevod Hashem) — the divine honor or manifest glory attributed to the Holy One Himself (as in 'the glory of the LORD appeared in the cloud', 'blessed is the glory of the LORD from His place'), which a person can merit, reveal, or elevate; distinct from honor given to Torah, to the righteous, or to human beings, though it may parallel them

Holy boldness (azut di-kedushah): the sanctified brazenness/audacity of holiness — spiritual firmness drawn from joy and expressed in the holy voices (e.g., the shofar cry, the sigh) — by which one receives the Torah, attains faith, approaches the true tzaddikim, and breaks the insolence of the body and of the Other Side; the opposite of azut of the sitra achra
Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa — the sage who embodies the attribute of faith (emunah)
The wife of Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa — a distinct figure (construct head 'wife of'), tied to the completeness of the letters of faith-speech, not the man himself

receiving the drops of the tzaddik's intellect (tipei ha-sekhel) — the seminal-drop-like emanations of the righteous one's mind, transmitted to a person through the counsel (eitzah) he receives from the tzaddik, likened to the drop that descends from the brain to the counseling kidneys (Likutey Moharan I:7)
forms: הוא מקבל טפי השכל של הצדיק

gloss_en: the counsel (eitzah) of the tzaddikim — advice received from the true righteous ones, which is 'entirely seed of truth' and the channel through which one receives the drops of the tzaddik's intellect, leading to truth, faith, and redemption (Likutey Moharan I:7)

the counsel/advice (etzah) of the tzaddikim — guidance received from the righteous generally (indefinite plural, no specific tzaddik as referent), which in Likutey Moharan I:7 is identified with the aspect of truth (emet) that one merits through it

Akum (acronym עובדי כוכבים ומזלות, 'worshippers of stars and constellations'): the idolatrous nations / idolatry itself as a spiritual category — the force of avodah zarah characterized by separation (peruda), sterility, and the side of death (sitra d'mota), opposed to holy unity
The seventy nations (specific enumerated collective, 'dark faces'); distinct from the general concept of idolatry
The greatness of the Creator (the divine attribute/reality itself)
The revelation/manifestation of the greatness of the Creator — the process of disclosing it (achieved via charity to a worthy poor person), not the greatness itself

Servant/slave (eved, singular noun) — the bondman as a spiritual aspect (bechinah): the cursed Canaan 'servant of servants' linked to the serpent, and the moon termed 'My servant' (Zohar on 'hinei yaskil avdi'); the sub-lunar four elements are likewise 'servants'

Servants/slaves (avadim, plural of eved) — subordinate attendants; used homiletically for entities that serve something higher: the evil traits of the four elements (called 'servants,' being under the moon, itself termed 'servant') and the premises/introductions that attend and serve the wisdoms

Length of days (arikhut yamim) — longevity in the sense of lengthening, expanding, and sanctifying one's days; attained through fear of Heaven and Torah study, linked to the aspects of the elder (zaken) and the rectifications of Atik, and serving as the vessel to receive wealth/contemplation

the spirit/breath of life (ruach chayim) — the animating vital spirit that sustains every thing and fills its lack, identified in LM 1:8 with erech apayim (patience, 'lengthening one's breath'), drawn down by the tzaddik through sighing, Torah, and prayer; distinct from the ruach se'arah (stormwind of the kelipah)
the spirit of THE life (definite) — 'ruach ha-chaim di-kdusha', the holy life-spirit; article-marked variant

judgment (mishpat) — the divine/personal attribute of judgment: weighing and judging one's own deeds and affairs (self-judgment that averts judgment from above), identified with the middle pillar (amuda de-emtza'ita), Jacob, and Aaron; the sefirotic quality of balanced justice, paired with tzedakah
judgments/laws (plural — the parashah/genre sense)

Kavod (כָּבוֹד) — glory/honor, especially the Divine glory: identified with Malkhut (kingship), likened to fire, garments/externality, and light; the honor of Heaven that is elevated through humility and revealed through the supernal delight (not כָּבֵד 'liver/heavy')

'Mah' (מָה, "what") — the kabbalistic aspect/divine name Mah (Havayah spelled with alephs, gematria 45 = Adam), denoting self-nullification, humility, and Chokhmah ('koach mah'); the interrogative used as a mystical designation (Torah as 'mah ha-edot', wisdom as 'mah', man as 'mah'), not the plain interrogative pronoun

Beast/animal (behemah) — the animal dimension of the human being: the body, materiality, and the imaginative faculty (koach ha-medameh) with its desires, standing in contrast to 'adam' (intellect, soul, form); e.g., the sacrificial animal embodying the imagination to be broken

When a person yearns (choshek) with intensified desire — specifically desire heightened in proportion to the obstacle — which empowers him to actualize the matter from potential to actual and automatically break the obstacle (Likutey Moharan I:66)

Binyamin (Benjamin) — Jacob's youngest son and the tribe named for him, the 'ben-yamin' (son of the right) born in Eretz Yisrael, in whose tribal portion the Beit HaMikdash stood; hence a bechinah of da'at, mochin, and tefillin, and linked to the 'right side' / Land of Israel
Nimin — strands/threads/hairs (נימין בחינת שערות), a distinct word meaning strings/hairs

The 'building of Malkhut of holiness' (binyan ha-malkhut di-kedushah) — the constructed edifice/structure of the sefirah of Kingship on the side of holiness, identified in the Arizal's writings with the two live pure birds (of the metzora purification), built up through melody (neginah), in contrast to the Malkhut of the kelipah whose mochin are the impure birds

'Bereishit' — the first word of the Torah understood as a supernal divine utterance: in LM I:22 the complete utterance (maamar hashalem), aspect of 'before creation', the heard/Nishma and hidden dimension; in LM II:12 the same word as the sealed/hidden utterance (maamar satum) from which vitality flows even to the lowest places. Not the book of Genesis as a text, nor the plain temporal sense 'in the beginning'.

'Reishit' (רֵאשִׁית) — the 'first/beginning' as a theological category: identified with chochmah/wisdom ('reishit chochmah', Ps. 111:10), with the birthright (bechora) merited by Yaakov, and with kodesh/holiness ('every first is holy', Jer. 2:3); not the mere temporal adverb 'at first'

converts (gerim) and returnees to God (ba'alei teshuvah) whom one 'makes' — i.e., people brought to conversion or repentance, through whom the Divine glory is chiefly elevated to its root (Likutey Moharan I:14)

Night (laylah) — the nighttime as a symbolic aspect (bechinah) of darkness and constriction: dimmed vision, poverty and distress when 'the end of all flesh' rules, faith/Malkhut ('Your faithfulness in the nights'), the lesser luminary, and the domain of Oral Torah/Gemara study — as opposed to day/light/Chokhmah

Circumcision (brit milah) — the commandment of cutting the foreskin, identified with the sanctity/rectification of the covenant (tikkun ha-brit) and the 'mal' of Chashmal (chash-mal); NOT the homograph milah meaning 'word/utterance'

bringing forth from potential (koach) into actuality (po'al) — the philosophical act of actualization, identified in Likutey Moharan with speech (dibbur), which externalizes the latent intellect (e.g., lm1:25 'your lips' as the actualizer; lm1:66 actualization via the completeness of speech)

Simchat Torah — the festival of 'Rejoicing of the Torah' (concluding the Sukkot season), which Torah 74 identifies as the aspect of 'speech with knowledge' (dibbur be-de'ah), corresponding to Jacob, in contrast to Hoshana Rabba as speech without knowledge

Joy of Torah and mitzvah (simchat Torah u-mitzvah) — the rejoicing experienced in performing Torah study and mitzvah observance together, which as a spiritual force elevates all lower levels called 'feet' (regel); a compound construct distinct from the holiday Simchat Torah and from 'joy of Torah' alone

The illuminating speech (dibbur ha-me'ir) — speech/utterance that shines with light, attained only by making God's honor complete through humility and self-abasement (one's own honor as nothing), which then illuminates the way to repentance and to the depths of Torah understanding (Likutey Moharan I:11); identified with the 'tzipparta' (bird) of the Zohar; covers singular (דבור המאיר) and plural (דבורים המאירים) forms and the periphrasis 'the speech that will illuminate for him' (דבור שיאיר לו)
his words are heard/heeded by the creatures (the world at large) — tied to the LM1:5 context of gevurot producing thunder and voices heard from above
one's words are heeded/accepted by one's fellow — condition attained through fear of Heaven when speaking with a companion (LM2:7)
blood (dam) — the bodily life-fluid, bearer of the nefesh (vital soul) and seat of dinim (judgments) and of the temperament (its purity yields joy, its murkiness in the spleen yields sadness)
footstool (hadom, as in 'footstool of His feet'); here expounded via demimah (stillness/silence) — not related to 'blood'

Heels (akevayim, עֲקֵבַיִם) — the anatomical heels of the feet, treated in Torah 41 as a kabbalistic aspect: identified with the legs/pillars (raglin), embodying din (judgment) via the gematria akev = 2 × Elokim, the low point where the external forces (chitzonim) can take hold

Heel (singular) — the anatomical heel of the foot (Hebrew ʿaqev), the lowest bodily extremity; homiletically linked to feet/רגלין (Torah 22, reading Deut 7:12 'ekev tishme'un' as heel) and to Yaakov as the lowly one (דל, Torah 177); distinct from the plural עקבים and from עֵקֶב in its plain biblical sense of 'consequence/because'

"Why is Your clothing red?" (madua adom lilvushekha, Isaiah 63:2) — the proof-verse of red-stained garments, applied in LM 1:29 to the Shekhinah reddened/stained (menstrual blood, city of blood, stain on garments) through blemish of the covenant

zeal for the LORD of Hosts (קִנְאַת ה' צְבָאוֹת) — the act of being jealous/zealous on God's behalf against His desecrators, which Likutey Moharan II:65 (citing Tosafot, Bava Batra 10b, on Nevuzaradan) reckons as equivalent to tzedakah (charity)
the Lord of Hosts — the divine name/attribute itself, invoked as the model of piety to emulate

The Aramaic (Zoharic) devotional formula לְאַדְבָּקָא מַחֲשַׁבְתָּא בְּעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי — 'to attach/bind one's thought to the World to Come' — used in Likutey Moharan I:54 as the spiritual state underlying memory (zikaron) and effected 'in totality/generality' (בִּכְלָלִיּוּת) through sleep, when the soul ascends to the World to Come; not any literal physical clinging or other sense of דבק
The phrase/divine designation 'Hashem Elokai' (Hashem my God)
The unification/yichud of 'Hashem Elokai' — an act of unification, not the phrase itself

clapping of the hands (mecha'at kaf/kapayim) — the physical act of striking palm against palm during prayer, which in Likutey Moharan (esp. Torahs 44–46) unites right and left, arouses the divine 'hands,' sweetens judgments, nullifies strife and foreign thoughts, and places one's prayer in the air of the Land of Israel

clapping the hands (מְחִיאַת כַּפַּיִם) during prayer — the devotional practice of striking one's palms together while praying, taught by Rabbi Nachman as arousing supernal effects (wings of speech, unification)

mutual truth-clarification: people, through interpersonal peace, jointly investigating and explaining the truth to one another (leading each to cast off the falsehood of his silver-idols) — Likutey Moharan I:27
forms: הם חוקרים ומסבירים זה לזה האמת

gloss_en: The illumination/radiance of the hands (he'arat ha-yadayim) — the spiritual light revealed in the hands through the spirit (ruach) of the tzaddik, manifested in clapping hands (and paired with the illumination of the feet in dancing), which nullifies heresy and increases faith (Likutey Moharan I:10)
The revelation/manifestation OF the illumination of the hands — a distinct state (revelation) predicated on the illumination, not the illumination itself

The plain/simple level of Torah (peshata de-oraita, Aramaic) — the revealed, exoteric layer of Torah study, exemplified by monetary law and identified with conducting business in faith; contrasted with the inner/mystical levels
The STUDY of the plain meaning of Torah — an activity/state (a form of 'sleep'), distinct from the peshat itself

Knowledge of the Torah (yediat ha-Torah) — cognitive mastery/study-knowledge of the Torah, identified with Chokhmah and mochin d'gadlut (expanded consciousness), which serves as the means to sweeten harsh judgments
Knowledge and comprehension/attainment (hasagah) of the Torah — adds the distinct element of hasagah, not merely knowing

The serpent (nachash) — the primordial snake of Eden as the mystical archetype (bechinah) of evil: the cursed force of servitude/Canaan, cunning-for-evil, and the enticer toward self-interest; not divination (nichesh) or copper (nechoshet)

Ha'alat Mayin Nukvin — the kabbalistic 'raising of the feminine waters' (MaN), the arousal-from-below effected through yearning/love, peacemaking, and the words of Torah and prayer, which ascends to unite the upper and lower realms and rectify the fallen sparks of creation

Torah and prayer (Torah study and tefillah as one paired devotional practice — the joint verbal/spiritual means by which good is refined from evil, feminine waters are elevated, and 'standing' is achieved)
words/utterances of Torah and prayer — the spoken dibburim, not the practice of Torah-and-prayer itself
the joining/union of chasadim and gevurot (the act of connecting them, = peace/shalom)
chasadim and gevurot themselves (the paired divine attributes)

Patience / forbearance (arikhat apayim, 'slowness to anger') — the attribute of erekh apayim that a person merits through faith (the aspect of the Land of Israel), the opposite of fierce anger (charon af), enabling one to withstand every obstacle and confusion in divine service (LM I:155)
Embrace of the right hand (Zohar Pinchas), i.e. the act/state of embracing — head is 'embrace', not the hand itself
Right hand, an aspect of love (ahavah) — the hand itself, not an action upon it

Desecration of the Sabbath (chilul Shabbat) — the sin of profaning Shabbat, homiletically linked via the root ח-ל-ל to chalal (void/corpse), signifying the withdrawal of holiness and, since Shabbat is one's 'first wife,' the shortened steps of a widower
The rectification/repair of Sabbath desecration — a state/process about חלול שבת, not the desecration itself
Teshuvah me-ahavah: repentance motivated by love of God (which transforms sins into merits), as distinct from repentance motivated by fear

Kodesh (קֹדֶשׁ) — 'holiness / the holy' as an abstract substantive noun: the sacred quality or domain itself (not the verb 'to sanctify,' not kiddushin/betrothal as an act, and not a sanctified place-name); identified in Likutey Moharan as the aspect of chochmah/mochin, 'reishit' (firstness), divine influx (shefa), and the chuppah/makifin
The Temple / sanctuary (במקדש = in the Temple, from the mishnaic thumb-counting passage); distinct place-noun, not the abstract quality 'holiness'
The 'tallit' (garment/encompassing) of the klipah — the impure shell, identified with the tallit of Edom
The subjugation/subduing of the tallit of the klipah — an action upon the shell-garment, not the garment itself

The Zoharic Aramaic phrase 'trein re'in d'la mitparshin' — 'the two companions who are never separated' — designating the inseparable pair Chokhmah and Binah (the divine letters yud-heh, the two aspects of the divine mind); here embedded in the clause 'that the two never-separating companions should draw near (to each other)'

canonical_he: כשאדם יודע שכל מארעותיו הם לטובתו
gloss_en: The awareness that all of one's experiences/happenings (me'ora'ot) are for one's good — the state of knowing this, taught in Likutey Moharan I:4 to be a foretaste of the World to Come, expressed in blessing 'HaTov veHaMeitiv' on everything without distinguishing kindness from judgment
forms: כשאדם יודע שכל מארעותיו הם לטובתו

gloss_en: being able to gaze upon the ultimate purpose (the tachlis — the all-good, all-one final aim of the world to come), attained by fully shutting one's eyes to the vanities of this world and directing one's inner vision toward that ultimate end (Likutey Moharan I:65)

the ability to pray, sing melodies, and give thanks to God — the capacity for prayer and song that is restored by finding and gathering one's own good points (Likutey Moharan I:282's 'Azamra' teaching), as opposed to the inability to pray caused by sadness and self-condemnation
to return in repentance; the act of repenting/teshuvah
the longing/yearning to return in repentance — a desire-state about teshuvah, not the act itself

The kabbalistic unification (yichud) of the Tzaddik (Yesod) with Knesset Yisrael (the Congregation of Israel, Malkhut), effected when the tzaddik-giver bestows influx/blessing upon the receiver — likened in LM I:54 to the curtain (yeria) bestowing upon the Ark of the Covenant and to masa u'matan

Complete/perfect repentance (teshuvah shelemah) — the total, settled return to God in which one is wholly transformed from evil to good and evil is entirely rejected; identified with Shabbat and total rest (nayecha/menuchah), as opposed to partial, fluctuating repentance (the 'run and return' of the weekdays)
One who performs complete repentance — the penitent/agent, not the state of teshuva itself

The heart being guarded/protected from the power of the imaginative faculty (koach ha-medammeh) — safeguarding the heart against illusory imagination so that memory of the ultimate purpose (the World to Come) is preserved, as taught in Likutey Moharan I:54
The eye being guarded from the power of imagination — distinct organ (עין) from the heart-form

the spiritual practice/capacity of binding one's thought and mind (mochin, aspect of chasadim) to the words of one's speech in Torah and prayer (aspect of gevurot), i.e., putting full mental focus into the holy words one utters (Likutey Moharan I:80)
forms: יכולין לדבר, דהינו לקשר המחשבה אל הדבור

gloss_en: The six weekdays (sheshet yemei ha-chol) — the six profane days of the week as opposed to Shabbat, which in Torah 79 correspond to the six orders of the Mishnah (and to Metatron), comprising the six halakhic categories of valid/invalid, impure/pure, forbidden/permitted
The weekdays — as an aspect of Yetzirah/formation (in Torah 66); no six-fold enumeration
might/strength (oz, עֹז) — divine might as in 'v'uzo bashechakim', identified in LM 17 with the aspect of yirah (fear/awe); distinct from the homograph עֵז/עִזָּא 'goat'
Boaz (the name) / 'with strength' — distinct from bare oz; check the context if you care which

the all-inclusive totality of the colors/hues (Aramaic gevanin) — the kabbalistic unification of all colors into one inclusive whole, associated with Tiferet/truth (e.g., the changing colors of the face in shame, the colors of the eye)
the revelation/manifesting of the totality of colors (a verbal phrase — an action/event about the concept, not the concept itself)

The first teshuvah (initial repentance) in Likutey Moharan Torah 6 — the repentance a person does at his current level of comprehension, corresponding to the honor/glory of this world (kevod olam hazeh), upon which one must later do a second 'teshuvah on the teshuvah' corresponding to the World to Come

The totality/collective of the sinews (kelaliut ha-gidin) — the aggregate of the body's sinews/channels as a mystical unity in Likutey Moharan I:29, identified with the ruach/spirit (the eagle, 'no spirit rose in any man') and with tzedakah/charity ('sow for yourselves for charity'), whose rectification elevates the mochin

The blemish of the totality of the sinews (pegam kelaliyut ha-gidin) — the spiritual defect afflicting the collective network of the body's sinews/gidin, identified in Likutey Moharan I:29 as an aspect of the blemish of the covenant (pegam ha-brit) and of the blemish of the garments; the defect concerning the sinews as a whole, not the sinews themselves

Rock (tzur, צוּר) — the flint-rock as a mystical bechinah in Likutey Moharan I:20: identified with the sela-rock from which speech issues and with the heart ('Rock of my heart', Ps. 73:26), the rock that was opened so waters flowed (Ps. 105:41), i.e., the heart-rock that gushes forth Torah explanations when opened by prayer; not the verb צוּר 'besiege/form', not צוֹר Tyre, and not the Divine epithet Tzur as such
'The Rock' — appears in lm2:15 in a context of the true tzaddik / baalei tzedakah, distinct referent (likely a divine epithet, 'the Rock' = God) rather than the rock-as-heart bechinah of lm1:20

complete da'at (דַּעַת שָׁלֵם / הַדַּעַת הַשָּׁלֵם) — the whole, perfected state of the faculty of knowledge/awareness, mature consciousness free of confusion or foolishness (as opposed to the immature or confused da'at of a minor, or of one under servitude/exile)

Gadlut ha-mochin — 'expanded consciousness': the state of enlarged, mature mental faculties (mochin) in which the intellect is clear and luminous, identified with mercies and kindnesses (rachamim va-chasadim), the opposite of constricted consciousness (mochin de-katnut) which is judgments
To raise/elevate the (divine) honor — here via Torah of chesed (learning in order to teach)
To raise the honor AND the kingship (away) from them — a distinct act, effected via tzedakah, of rescuing honor+malchut from those who hold them
the blemish/flaw of the altar (a defective state of the mizbe'ach)
to complete/rectify the blemish of the altar (the act of repair, achieved via converts) — not the blemish itself

The Oral Torah (Torah she-be'al peh) — the orally transmitted body of Torah teaching exemplified by the Gemara and halakhic derivation, treated as the feminine/receptive divine aspect (malkhut, Shekhinah, night, Rachel, David)
The practice/remedy of studying Oral Torah at night (the tikkun for hearing melody)

the remaining languages of the (seventy) nations — all gentile tongues other than Targum/Aramaic (which is Nogah, mixed good-and-evil); these other languages are complete evil, corresponding to the bonfire of the seventy stars, with no good to be clarified from them (Likutey Moharan I:19)
the languages of the nations in general (the 'encompassing evil', רע הכולל)
Melody/song that is not in holiness (the unholy melody itself)
To rectify/elevate the melody that is not in holiness (an action/tikkun performed upon the unholy melody, per David HaMelech elevating it)
the spirit of impurity (as an entity/state; identified with the 'stormy wind' and Esau's aspect)
driving out the spirit of impurity (the action of expelling it, via heat/fire of the heart)

The retzuah — the leather strap (paradigmatically the tefillin strap, and by extension the lashing/shoe-strap of the Sages' dicta), symbolizing the encompassing lights (makifin) of Malkhut/faith, yirah (fear) entering the mochin, and the surplus of the mochin (motrei mochin)

Mochin — the kabbalistic 'brains': the supernal intellective faculties (Chochmah-Binah-Daat consciousness) that descend into and illuminate the mind, as in 'mochin de-gadlut'; the plural Aramaic/mystical term for the mental lights, not the anatomical brain per se nor any other homograph

salt (melach) — the substance that sweetens/counteracts bitterness, invoked as the 'covenant of salt' (brit melach olam): the covenant/tzaddik is salt that sweetens the bitterness and sorrow of livelihood and expels the turbid, bad blood that causes sadness and desires
'send' (imperative shalach), i.e. charity — 'shalach lachmecha al pnei ha-mayim'

Sarah (שָׂרָה) — the biblical matriarch, wife of Abraham and mother of Isaac, whose name is expounded (per Rashi/Berakhot 13a, from שׂרר 'to rule') as 'she who rules over the entire world'; the aspect of malchut/sovereignty, homiletically linked to song (shir, 've-sharim ke-cholelim') and to ruling speech (dibbur)
Marah — the place of bitter waters (Exodus 15), symbol of blemished bris / bitter waters
poverty (עֲנִיּוּת) — the state/condition of being poor and materially destitute, as a spiritual consequence (e.g., of idle talk, evil speech, or arrogance), the opposite of wealth (עשירות)

poor person / pauper (עָנִי, fem. עֲנִיָּה) — one who possesses nothing of their own and must receive from others; used kabbalistically for the destitute recipient-aspect (Malkhut as 'poor and lowly, having nothing of her own,' and the Ark of the Covenant as the pauper receiving from the curtain/giver). Not עֳנִי 'affliction' or the verb ענה 'to answer.'
when one studies Torah
when one studies Torah in the aforementioned way
The brazenness/insolence of the body, an aspect of the Other Side (sitra achra)
The breaking/shattering of the body's brazenness (an action performed upon 'עזות הגוף', not the thing itself)

the voices/sounds of holiness (kolot di-kedushah) — the plural holy voices identified in Likutey Moharan I:22 with holy boldness (azut di-kedushah) and with the shofar blasts (tekiah–shevarim–teruah), which break the brazenness of the body/Sitra Achra and enable drawing close to the true tzaddikim (the holy shepherds)
holy voice/sound (singular) — used in lm2:79 in a distinct context (Yitzchak / ketz / awakening the sleeping)

Prophecy (nevuah) — the divine prophetic inspiration/spirit drawn from the 'place whence the prophets draw,' encompassing the ten levels of prophecy exemplified by Moses; the revelatory influx that rectifies the imaginative faculty and faith and redeems prayer

the hidden/concealed dimension (nistar) — the esoteric, secret aspect of Torah (as opposed to nigleh, the revealed), associated with 'the hidden things belong to God' and with the legs/thighs that are 'in concealment'

the hidden things (nistarot, plural of nistar) — matters of Torah/divine service too lofty and concealed for a person to act upon at his level (aspect of 'we will hear'/nishma, e.g. the Torah's words surrounding a mitzvah), contrasted with the revealed things (niglot) that one can practically fulfill

the nullification of one's arrogance (gadlus as self-aggrandizement/haughtiness) — a person's inflated self-importance being annulled, e.g., through closeness to the tzaddik or receiving the light of Yom Tov (Likutey Moharan I:135)
revelation of the aspect of Y-H (the divine name spelled yud-heh)
revelation of the aspect of the Name of Hashem (day after Yom Kippur, distinct construct head from Y-H)

the holy utterance (ha-dibbur ha-kadosh) — sanctified speech itself, the divine faculty of holy speech symbolized by the supernal rose ("his lips are roses"), from which the unworthy must be denied sustenance
holy utterances/words (plural, indefinite) — distinct number and definiteness from singular form; different Torah context

Voice/sound (kol) as a mystical aspect (bechinah): the holy voice issuing from the throat, identified with heaven, prayer, the shofar blast, and the river watering the garden of Eden — the audible outcry directed toward God

Voices/sounds in the plural (kolot) — the manifold vocal expressions of crying out, sighing, shofar blast, and song — which collectively constitute the aspect of azzut (holy boldness, per Ps. 68:34 'a voice of strength'); the plural multiplicity of voices, distinct from the singular concept of kol

The imaginative faculty (koach ha-medameh, הַמְדַמֶּה) — the imagination as a psychic power that opposes and confuses the intellect/spirit of prophecy, identified in Likutey Moharan I:54 with the evil spirit, spirit of folly, and depressed spirit (atzvut ruach), which is subdued through joy and music; not the verb 'resembles/compares' in other contexts
"Limping on his thigh" (Gen. 32) — the state of blemish of the legs (pegam ha-raglin) before rectification
Rectifying/mending the aspect of "limping on his thigh" — the act of tikkun of that blemished state, not the state itself

The 'spirit of folly' (ruach shetut, per Sotah 3a) — the irrational spirit of madness identified with the evil inclination and the imaginative faculty, which enters a person, deludes him into sin, and opposes/confuses the holy spirit of prophecy
The nullification/annulment of the spirit of folly (a predicated state) — distinct from the spirit of folly itself

Scent, fragrance (רֵיחַ) — an odor perceived through the nose/nostrils, the spiritual sense of smell linked to purity and awe of Heaven (as in 'תְּהִלָּתִי אֶחֱטָם לָךְ' and 'וַהֲרִיחוֹ בְּיִרְאַת ה''); distinct from the homographs/near-forms רֵאָה 'lung' and רוּחַ 'wind, spirit'
scents, smells (plural) — distinct surface form from singular ריח

Peace within one's own self/bones (שָׁלוֹם בַּעֲצָמָיו) — internal peace between a person's body and soul, the first of the two kinds of peace in Likutey Moharan I:14 (contrasted with peace with the world/others), attained through fear of Heaven and echoing Psalms 38:4 'there is no peace in my bones because of my sin'

Protection afforded by the mitzvah of tzitzit against the counsel of the serpent (atzat ha-nachash) — i.e., guarding a person from adultery/sexual immorality and the serpent's impurity (zuhamat ha-nachash), thereby enabling receipt of the tzaddik's true counsel (Likutey Moharan I:7)

the insights/understandings of the Torah (tevunot ha-Torah) — the deep comprehension of Torah's meaning, identified in Likutey Moharan I:11 with 'the heavens,' attained through illuminating speech and the two unifications; the longer variant לְעָמְקָהּ ('to its depth') merely adds an adverbial qualifier to the same construct phrase

Shifra — the biblical midwife (Exod. 1:15; identified with Yocheved, Sotah 11b), whose name denotes beautifying (meshaperet) the newborn; in LM II:71 the aspect linking birth (holada), the fetal sac/placenta (shafir ve-shilya), beauty of form (yefeh to'ar/Yosef), and the flow of supernal pleasantness
Para — 'cow', here homiletically equated with prayer (tefillah)

chiddush ha'olam — the renewal/createdness of the world: the doctrine, apprehended through faith rather than intellect, that God created the world anew by His will and continually renews it (as opposed to the world being eternal), the basis for His power to change nature

the future renewal of the world (chidush ha-olam le-atid) — the eschatological re-creation of the world in the time to come, when the world will be rebuilt through chesed and conducted solely by divine providence and wonders rather than nature

God as 'the Place of the world' (מְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם) — the classic rabbinic epithet (Bereishit Rabbah 68) that the Holy One is the place/locus of the world while the world is not His place, i.e., He encompasses and contains all creation rather than being contained by it
the simple unity (of God)
the revelation of the simple unity (the event)
speech (that comes about) by means of truth
the truth illuminating/shining into speech — a process/action, not the speech itself

Exemption from all labor and worldly occupation (מְלָאכָה וְעֵסֶק) for one's livelihood — the stated benefit of giving charity in LM2:4, whereby the world is sustained through God's kindness and one need not engage in any work or business
forms: אין צריכין לעשות שום מלאכה ועסק

gloss_en: The rectification (tikkun) of the aspect of the 'zaken' (זָקֵן, the elder — God's appearance as an elder at Sinai, per Rashi on 'Anokhi'), accomplished through beginning charity anew, and identified in Torah lm2:4 with the festival of Shavuot ('be-shavuoteichem'); by this rectification the nursing of the 'forehead of the snake' is nullified
forms: נתתקן בחינת זקן, שהוא בחינת שבועות

gloss_en: The pilgrimage festival (regel / yom tov) as the revelation of the Divine Will (ratzon) — the festival day, in Likutey Moharan II:4, understood as the time when God's Will is revealed, which thereby 'rinses and washes the bloods' so they circulate properly (playing on regel = festival, not the anatomical foot per se)
forms: רגל ויום טוב שהוא התגלות הרצון

canonical_he: ישמח צדיק כי חזה נקם וכו'
gloss_en: Verse quote (Ps. 58:11) 'The righteous shall rejoice when he sees vengeance' — cited in Likutey Moharan II:4 for the joy of the tzaddik/Israel when the revelation of the Divine Will (through the festival's call and charity) shows that God, not nature, governs, and He will avenge the oppressions of the nations
forms: ישמח צדיק כי חזה נקם וכו
ישמח צדיק כי חזה נקם" וכו

gloss_en: the supernal Will was revealed (revelation of the divine/supernal Ratzon)
the Will was revealed (revelation of the Ratzon, unmodified)
The aspect/category of the Tabernacle (Mishkan) as a concept
The act/state of becoming an aspect of the Tabernacle — a predication, not the concept 'aspect of Tabernacle' itself

canonical_he: הצדקה פותחת ומרחבת הפתח יותר ויותר
gloss_en: Charity's special power (segulah) to open and progressively widen the opening (petach) of any beginning in divine service more and more — the aspect of 'patoach tiftach' (Deut. 15:8), by which tzedakah eases 'all beginnings are difficult'
forms: הצדקה פותחת ומרחבת הפתח יותר ויותר
פותחת יותר ויותר ומרחבת הפתח יותר

gloss_en: a true Rebbe/master together with his students (רַבִּי עִם תַּלְמִידִים) — the master–disciple configuration whose gathering of students around the Rav (the 'yeshivah') collects and rectifies the scattered portions of faith (Likutey Moharan II:5)
a TRUE/authentic rabbi with students — qualified form specifying the genuine master; 'אמתי' is a loaded Breslov qualifier, not an orthographic variant

Tikkun ha-mochin — the rectification/repair of the mochin (the kabbalistic 'mentalities'/intellective faculties of the brain, i.e., the mind as bearer of Da'at), whose restoration produces the aspect of tefillin covering the brain and sweetens the state of the mochin's departure (sleep)
The essence/main point of the rectification of the intellect — construct headed by עקר ('essence of'), a statement about what the tikkun principally consists of, not the tikkun itself
Yom Kippur (the Day of Atonement), the annual fast day of the 10th of Tishrei on which atonement is granted and the heavenly judgment is sealed
Tefillin as mochin (the intellects/brain-lights) — the paired node juxtaposing tefillin and mochin per the Kabbalistic identification in Torah lm2:5
tefillin as mochin — tefillin identified with the brain-consciousnesses (mochin), rectified by breaking sexual lust so the body's moisture/oils feed the brain like oil to a burning lamp
Raising up the fallen faith (elevating sparks of holy faith that fell into the false beliefs of the nations) — the act which thereby produces converts (gerim), whether actual or potential (LM II:5)
meriting the renewal of the world that is to come (the future/eschatological renewal)
meriting the renewal of the world (unqualified renewal of the world)

the sanctity (kedushah, construct head) of the camp of Israel — the holiness inhering in Israel's encampment (in LM II:8 identified with guarding the covenant/sexual purity, the 'three parasangs' of Israel's camp that Og sought to overwhelm)
the camp of Israel itself (the entity), not its holiness

The teaching-image that the intellect (sekhel) burns like a candle fueled by the body's fattiness (shamnunit ha-guf) — the mind sustained like a flame by bodily oil, per 'the candle of Hashem is the soul of man' (Likutey Moharan II:8)

the clarification and rectification (birur ve-tikkun) of the imaginative faculty (koach ha-medammeh) — the purification of the imagination effected through the spreading of prophecy ('by the hand of the prophets I was imaged', Hosea 12:11), which in turn rectifies true holy faith

nefel (נֵפֶל, pl. נְפָלִים) — a stillbirth/miscarried fetus that emerges from the womb before its time; used in LM II:20 as the figure for teachers/leaders who become publicly famous (מפורסמים) before their proper time (not the verb נָפַל 'to fall' or the adjective 'fallen')

drawing near / coming close to God (Hitkarvut la-Shem) — the devotional act of a person being brought close to the blessed Creator and His true service (root ק-ר-ב in the reflexive hitpael, לְהִתְקָרֵב אֵלָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ); not physical proximity, sacrificial offering (קָרְבָּן), or battle (קְרָב)

the magnification/increase (hagdalah) of the supernal kindnesses (chasadim) in which Da'at is clothed — the kabbalistic aggrandizement of the chasadim effected e.g. through drinking wine in proper measure (Likutey Moharan II:26)

the removal/departure of the ruach-kin'ah (spirit of jealousy, identified with the spirit of Mashiach resting on the burned books), achieved so that it not disrupt the peace of the holy couple (LM II:32)
the eyes of Israel are opened (spiritual perception granted to Israel specifically)
the eyes of the world are opened (perception granted to the whole world) — distinct from 'of Israel' by its possessed head

The 'luminaries of fire' (me'orei eish) — the kabbalistic forces of harsh judgment (dinim) that prevail when the 'luminaries of light' (me'orei or, associated with the Name of God, the light of the eyes, and Shabbat) are subdued; in Likutey Moharan II:67 they are the burning force behind the destruction of the Holy Temple, linked to fire and ash

The subduing of the 'luminaries of fire' (me'orei eish, נִכְנָעִין מְאוֹרֵי אֵשׁ) — the state/process in which the fiery luminaries (the destructive forces by which the Temple was burned, the 'ashes' of Isaiah 61:3) are brought low through mourning over the Temple/Zion, allowing the luminaries of light (Shabbat) to prevail; refers to the act of their subjugation, not to the luminaries-of-fire entity itself
the setting/sinking of the light (shki'at ha-or) — the sun's light sinking in the west, used in LM II:67 as the figure for the departure of the light of the eyes caused by weeping
the setting of the light in the west (the specific image)

the gaze of the sage of the generation upon a person — the true tzaddik, the comprehensive mind (moach ha-kollel) of the generation, seeing and looking at an individual, which sparks that person's mind (from מִסְתַּכֵּל, hitpael of ס-כ-ל, 'to gaze'; not related to סָכָל 'fool')

The true leader (ha-manhig ha-amiti) of all Israel — the archetypal tzaddik-leader identified with the aspect of Moses, who embodies the encompassing spirit (ruach ha-kolel) and comprehensive Da'at, knowing how to engage the individual spirit of each person
A true leader (indefinite) — one who is like Moses and can apportion greatness to each; possibly generic rather than the single archetype

Psalms (Tehillim) — the biblical Book of Psalms, specifically its devotional recitation (amirat Tehillim), taught in LM II:73 as a segulah for attaining repentance by reaching one's gate among the 49 gates of teshuvah

The forty-nine (mem-tet, 49) gates of repentance (teshuvah) — the humanly attainable gates of return out of the fifty gates of teshuvah, the fiftieth being God's own teshuvah; corresponding to the 49 letters of the names of the twelve tribes and the 49 days of the Omer count

"not in order" (shelo k'seder) — the state of reversed/disrupted sequence, typified by the reverse alphabet tashrak and by Chavah as the 'behind' (achor) aspect opposite Adam's 'before' (kedem); experientially, events going contrary to one's will (opposition of will), the root of war and heart-sickness (davai) in LM2:82

The Hebrew letter yud (י) — the smallest letter of the alphabet, tenth letter with numerical value ten, understood kabbalistically as the letter of the Divine Name corresponding to Chokhmah (supernal Wisdom) that bestows vitality upon Malkhut/dalet

kohen — the priest (Aaronide priest of the Temple service; includes the verbal form 'to serve as priest'), which Likutey Moharan treats as the aspect of chesed and holy love (Avraham) and of Torah/prayer; not any other word spelled כהן
"Abraham My lover/friend" (Isaiah 41:8) — the scriptural epithet of Abraham as the one who loves God, invoked as the aspect of love of God linked to the kohen/priest (Chesed)

Malkhut (the sefirah of Kingship, identified with prayer) in a state of lowliness and smallness (shiflut u-katnut) — the diminished, fallen Malkhut symbolized by the 'short wife,' the 'little sister,' and the 'small luminary' (the moon), which must be raised up (as in 'I will raise up the Sukkah of David') in Likutey Moharan I:49
'achot lanu ketanah' — verse Song of Songs 8:8 'we have a little sister,' prooftext for Malkhut/prayer in its state of smallness (katnut)
the 'hind let loose' (ayalah sheluchah) — the swift doe of Jacob's blessing to Naphtali (Gen. 49:21), used as an epithet for the Land of Israel and the attribute of truth

the supernal Mother (Imma/Binah) who covers/shelters Her children like a sukkah — the Zoharic phrase 'Imma dimesakhekha al benin' (Tikkunei Zohar 3), identifying the sukkah's covering with the protective hovering of the sefirah Binah over her offspring

The verse-phrase "If you call out to Understanding" (Proverbs 2:3, אִם לַבִּינָה תִּקְרָא), homiletically read as "call Binah 'Mother'" (אֵם) — identifying the sefirah Binah with the supernal Mother who suckles and covers Her children (as in sukkah/schach imagery)
'ezrekha' (your help) — the word 'help' in Psalms 20:3, linked to Genesis 2:18 'ezer' (helpmate/wife), signifying the aid sent from holiness

"I will make him a helper" (Genesis 2:18) — God's declaration to create a helper (Eve/Chavah) for Adam, cited in Likutey Moharan I:19 as the aspect of Chavah and the Holy Tongue (leshon ha-kodesh), linked to "May He send your help (ezrekha) from the holy place"

the thirty-nine lashes (malkot) — the judicial flogging penalty of lamed-tet (39) stripes derived from "forty he shall strike him, no more" (Deut. 25:3), as cited from Tikkuney Zohar 48; distinct from the thirty-nine (lamed-tet/tal) labors or lights

"Forty he shall strike him, he shall not add" (Deut. 25:3) — the Scriptural verse prescribing the forty (in practice thirty-nine) lashes of court-administered flogging (malkot), cited as the aspect of the 39 lashes linked to blemishing the covenant
the sigh (anachah) as lengthening of breath — the teaching that a groan extends the breath, embodying erekh apayim (patience) and restoring the vital spirit to what is lacking
the Kingdom of Heaven (Aramaic malkhuta di-shmaya) — the divine sovereignty/Shekhinah as Malkhut, whose yoke one accepts, identified as the 'mistress' (gevirta) and the God-fearing woman
'ishah maskelet' — the 'intelligent woman' of Proverbs 19:14, symbol of the Targum/Aramaic language which is ambivalent: sometimes maskil (enlightening), sometimes meshakel (bereaving)
Israel who arouse from below — the Jewish people's initiative of arousal-from-below (itaruta dil'tata) that sustains the supernal Torah, praised as 'Fortunate are you, Israel'
'ashrekha Yisrael mi khamokha' — verse Deuteronomy 33:29 'Fortunate are you, Israel, who is like you,' prooftext for Israel's unique power of arousal from below

holy judgment (Aramaic dina kadisha) — divine judgment/severity rooted in the side of holiness (associated with Elokim, Isaac/Gevurah drawn from Chesed, and loving reproof), as opposed to dina dimsa'ava, judgment from the impure Other Side
'et asher ye'ehav Hashem yokhiach' — verse Proverbs 3:12 'whom God loves He reproves,' prooftext for holy judgment (dina kadisha): distancing that begins drawing-close
'et ha-maor ha-katan' — verse Genesis 1:16 'the small luminary' (the moon), symbol of Malkhut/prayer in diminished smallness

"You are a priest" (atah khohen) — the scriptural phrase from Psalms 110:4 ("You are a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek"), addressed to Abraham/the priestly archetype, invoked in Likutey Moharan I:54 as the aspect of the kohen linked to love ("Abraham My lover") and to the priest's kemitzah ("and the priest shall scoop")

the thirty-nine categories of labor (lamed-tet melakhot) — the 39 forms of work forbidden on Shabbat, representing weekday toil and the curse of earning bread by the sweat of one's brow, associated with the serpent's venom (opposite of the 'tal/39 dew' of Torah)
'be-ze'at apekha tokhal lechem' — verse Genesis 3:19 'by the sweat of your brow you shall eat bread,' the curse of worldly toil corresponding to the 39 labors, opposite of the dew of Torah
shor she-baTorah — the 'ox' among the four chayot (Merkavah creatures) as manifested within Torah: its dimension of rulership/authority ('through me princes rule')
'bi sarim yasoru' — verse Proverbs 8:16 'through me princes rule,' prooftext for the ox-aspect (rulership) within Torah

the verse-phrase "It is the glory of God to conceal a matter" (Proverbs 25:2, kevod Elokim haster davar) — the scriptural motto of divine concealment, cited in Likutey Moharan I:6 as the aspect of Keter, of "do not probe what is covered from you," and of the hidden upper level of teshuvah

the dictum 'Into that which is concealed from you, do not inquire' (ba-mekhusseh mimkha al tachkor, Chagigah 13a citing Ben Sira) — the injunction against probing hidden divine matters, linked in Likutey Moharan 1:6 to concealment ('the glory of God is to conceal a matter') and to the covering firmament above which is the throne
falsehood/the lie (sheker) — untruth as a spiritual force opposed to emet (truth), characterized as manifold ('many calculations'), linked to idolatry and to tears/salty water
'bikshu chishvonot rabim' — verse Ecclesiastes 7:29 'they sought many calculations,' prooftext that falsehood is manifold/plural while truth is one
sweetening anger with compassion — the practice of not acting cruelly when angered but tempering rage with mercy, per 'in wrath remember compassion'
'be-rogez rachem tizkor' — verse Habakkuk 3:2 'in wrath remember compassion,' prooftext for sweetening anger with mercy

the commandment 'to appoint a king' (לְמַנּוֹת מֶלֶךְ) — one of the three mitzvot Israel was commanded upon entering the Land (Sanhedrin 20b), interpreted as the aspect of 'the pride of Yaakov' / 'a star shall shoot forth from Yaakov' and of the vav within the alef (the firmament)

"the pride of Yaakov" (ge'on Yaakov) — the scriptural phrase from Psalms 47:5 ("He chooses our heritage for us, the pride of Yaakov whom He loves"), interpreted in LM 1:6 as the aspect of kingship/appointing a king over Israel (linked to "a star shall shoot forth from Yaakov"); not ga'on in the sense of a Torah sage or of arrogance
'dover emet bilvavo' — verse Psalms 15:2 'one who speaks truth in his heart,' identified with the chashmal-garment drawn from Binah (the heart) to clothe faith
"A star shall shoot forth from Yaakov" (Numbers 24:17) — Bilaam's messianic prophecy of a star rising from Jacob, cited as the scriptural aspect of kingship/the anointed king

Prayer (tefillah, תְּפִלָּה) — the devotional act of addressing God in praise and petition, the 'service of the heart' (standing worship / the Amidah's eighteen blessings), identified with faith and the power to change nature; NOT the homograph tiflah (תִּפְלָה, 'unseemliness/folly') or tafel ('unseasoned')
'hod ve-hadar' — the phrase 'majesty and splendor' (Psalms 104:1), aspect of prayer as chayei sha'ah (temporal life), the footstool-feet of holiness clothed in this world
exhaling and inhaling the breath — the act of respiration (motzi u-makhnis ha-ruach), embodiment of the creatures' 'running forth and returning' and of ruach ha-kodesh
'ha-chayot ratzo va-shov' — verse Ezekiel 1:14 'the living creatures ran forth and returned,' prooftext for breathing as the oscillating movement of vitality

Halakhah — the revealed corpus of Torah law (הֲלָכָה), paired contrastively with Kabbalah as its hidden counterpart; in Likutey Moharan 11 it corresponds to the Lower Unification (yichuda tata'ah), the weekday union, and the level of 'razin' (secrets), acronym of הָרִיעוּ לַה' כָּל הָאָרֶץ

"Shout joyfully to the LORD, all the earth" (Psalms 100:1) — the verse whose initial letters spell Halakhah, expounded in Likutey Moharan I:11 as the aspect of the Lower Unification (yichuda tata'ah), the weekday union
Kabbalah — the esoteric mystical tradition of Torah (hidden wisdom, 'secrets of secrets'), as opposed to revealed Halakhah; not 'receipt', 'acceptance', or 'reception' in the mundane sense
atma — the 'thigh' (Aramaic) raised for Rabbah bar bar Chanah, symbolizing 'the earth is My footstool,' the lower point (nekudah tachtona)

"and the earth is My footstool" (Isaiah 66:1) — the scriptural phrase ve-ha'aretz hadom raglai, denoting the earth as the footstool of God's feet, i.e., the lower point/level of holiness clothed within this world
've-hagut libi tevunot' — phrase from Psalms 49:4 'the meditation of my heart shall be understanding,' cited amid the nose/fear-of-God tikkun of the beard
