binah libba — 'Binah is the heart' (Tikkunei Zohar dictum): Binah as heart-joy, one of the two 'wines' alongside the wine of Oral Torah/Malkhut
binah la-ittim — 'understanding of the times' (I Chron. 12:33), the aspect of the pilgrimage festivals (regalim) to which Malkhut is elevated through rebuke
grain and food (bar u-mazon) — the Aramaic/Hebrew pair denoting physical sustenance and provisions, used as an aspect (bechinah) of livelihood (parnassah), linked to the 'well' (beira) in LM 31
beira — Aramaic 'well/pit' as symbol of parnassah, grain and sustenance (bar u-mazon), the well of livelihood

canonical_he: יראה, שבאה לאדם מכח אדם עצמו
gloss_en: the lower fear — yirah aroused by the person's own effort/initiative (as opposed to supernal fear that descends of itself), the human-generated awe that awakens shefa
forms: יראה, שבאה לאדם מכח אדם עצמו

gloss_en: cypresses (beroshim) — the cypress tree of Isaiah 55:13 ('instead of the briar shall rise the berosh'), used homiletically as an aspect linked to carob (charuvin), Mordekhai, and birsha
birsha — Aramaic word for cypress/beroshim (from Rabbah bar bar Chana tale), tree-symbol expounded in the lesson

house (bayit) — the noun 'house/dwelling structure' used symbolically for an enclosed, settled domain of holiness: the Temple/house of prayer, the inner 'house' of da'at, the house whose 'head' (rosh bayit) is the mochin; distinct from any other word sharing the letters בית
the tzaddikim of the generation seated in a circle (iggul) — the concept of the righteous positioned around the world in circular order functioning as a tribunal
beit din — a court of judgment: the circle of tzaddikim as the tribunal from which each person's mishpat (merit or liability) and allotted parnassah issue
beita ila'ah — the Zoharic 'Upper House,' i.e., Binah the heart, called 'Mi' (Who), paired against the Lower House Malkhut/'Zot'
bekhorah — the birthright/firstborn portion ('double mouth'), taken by Yosef for guarding the brit, symbolizing prayer's twofold content (praise of God and requesting one's needs)

bara — the Hebrew verb 'created' (second word of Genesis 1:1), denoting the act/entirety of creation; in LM 22 it is the revealed 'half utterance' (aspect of son, Torah, lower Wisdom) relative to 'Bereishit,' the complete utterance of before-creation

son (ben) — the male child/offspring in relation to a father, used as the kabbalistic aspect of the lower, receiving level (the 'half utterance' of the small son echoing the father's complete utterance, lower Eden/lower Wisdom), and homiletically expounded (e.g., 'Yitzchak ben Avraham', 'yashuv benekha') as alluding to teshuvah; not to be confused with homographic readings such as בֵּין 'between'

memory / remembrance (zikaron) — the spiritual faculty of retention and recall, the capacity to keep one's awareness attached (e.g., to the World to Come and to Torah learned), opposed to forgetfulness (shikhchah); not a memorial object or the verb 'to remember'
ben zakhar — a male son/child, the offspring whose birth depends on unblemished memory (zikaron), forfeited by forgetfulness (as with Avshalom)
ben chakham — the 'wise son' of the Haggadah's four sons, identified with Yitzchak (laughter/joy: 'a wise son gladdens his father')
Ben Nannas — the Tanna Shimon ben Nannas (expert in monetary law, Bava Batra 175b), taken as symbol of emunah/faithful business dealing

Esau (Esav), the biblical brother of Jacob, son of Isaac — archetype of the wicked one and the kelipah (husk of impurity), the dross descending from judgment; not the homograph עָשׂוּ ('they made/did')
ben rasha — the 'wicked son' of the Haggadah's four sons, identified with Esav

Ishmael (יִשְׁמָעֵאל) — the biblical son of Abraham and Hagar, whose name ('God has heard') makes him the aspect of prayer/heard supplication and, as a penitent, the son who does not know how to ask; the personal name, not any other word from the root שמע
the son 'who does not know how to ask' of the Haggadah's four sons, identified with Yishmael the penitent — repentance as wordless asking of atonement
ben tam — the 'simple/wholesome son' of the Haggadah's four sons, identified with Yaakov 'ish tam' (Gen. 25:27)

canonical_he: כשמביא הארה וברכה לתוך תחלת המחשבה
gloss_en: bringing illumination and blessing into the primordial divine 'thought-first' (techilat ha-machshavah, the root of souls) by blessing and illuminating one's Torah study, so that the souls rooted there sparkle and are blessed (Likutey Moharan I:14)
forms: כשמביא הארה וברכה לתוך תחלת המחשבה

gloss_en: beno yihyeh talmid-chakham — the outcome that one's son becomes a Torah scholar, secured by blessing the Torah first and rooting study in the primal divine thought (Nedarim 81a)
banim chayim v'kayamim — living, enduring children, granted through marital union in holiness and breaking the animal soul (Nedarim 20b)

melody / musical playing (neginah) — the act and sound of music-making, as with an instrument or song, treated as a spiritual force (aspect of ruach, builder of Malkhut, sweetener of judgments); not to be confused with the homograph for a scriptural cantillation accent in its technical grammatical sense

the two live pure birds (shetei tzipporim chayot tehorot) of the metzora's purification rite (Lev. 14:4), which in LM I:3 are the source from which the kosher person's melody (neginah) is drawn and are identified, per the Arizal, with the building of the Malkhut of holiness
madregat Avraham — the spiritual level/rank of Avraham, i.e. the ba'al nefesh whose every meal is Lechem HaPanim ('walk before Me')
ba'al nefesh — 'master of the soul,' one who rules his appetites; the Avraham-level eater whose meals are the aspect of the Showbread
ba'alei lashon hara u'machloket — slanderers and quarrel-mongers who spy about (meraglim, the 'regel/foot') separating friends and spouses ('nirgan mafrid aluf')

expert in running forward (baki be-ratzo) — the first of the two expertises in the ways of teshuvah in Likutey Moharan I:6: mastery of the ascent/advance ('If I ascend to heaven, You are there'), never standing still at any level attained but ever striving higher; identified with the Zohar's 'entering' (ayil) and the segol of Ekyeh spelled out to 161 (KSA)

entering (Aramaic ʿayil/ʿayel, from the Zohar's "ʿayil ve-nafik" — he who enters and exits): the movement of ascent/entry into holiness, identified with "expert in running forward" (baki be-ratzo) and "If I ascend to heaven, You are there"; not any noun meaning ram or upper/above

nafik — Aramaic verb 'exits / goes out' from the Zohar's phrase 'praiseworthy is he who enters and exits' (zaka'ah man de'ayil ve-nafik), denoting the exiting/withdrawal movement paired with entering (ayil); in LM 1:6 the aspect of 'expert in returning' (baki be-shov)

"expert in returning" (baki be-shov) — the second of the two expertises required for walking the ways of teshuvah in Likutey Moharan 6: the mastery of descent/withdrawal (Zoharic "ve-nafik," exiting), corresponding to "if I make my bed in Sheol, behold You are there" (Ps. 139:8) and the chirik of the Divine Name Sa"G (63) — never despairing but seeking God even when fallen from one's level

"nishma" — "we will hear", the second term of Israel's declaration at Sinai "na'aseh ve-nishma" (Exodus 24:7), used as the aspect of the hidden/lofty dimension of divine service (as opposed to "na'aseh", the revealed), identified with prayer, fear, and supernal Eden
charuvin — carob trees (of R. Chanina ben Dosa's sustenance), identified as the aspect of 'beroshim' (cypresses) in the symbolism of faith

creation in potential (beri'ah be-koach) — the latent, not-yet-actualized state of creation, associated with prayer and the awakening of Chokhmah, as opposed to beri'ah be-fo'al, creation in actuality associated with Torah
beriah b'foal — creation in actuality, the Torah's mode ('amon/uman,' craftsman-actor) as opposed to prayer's creation-in-potential (Chokhmah)
beriat ha'olam — the creation of the world, effected within the chalal hapanuy (Vacated Space) after tzimtzum, via divine speech; the paradigm of machloket (dispute)

the showbread (lechem ha-panim) — the twelve loaves perpetually arranged on the golden table in the Temple 'before God' (Lev. 24); in Likutey Moharan, the paradigm of food/eating raised to the aspect of 'panim' (the inner face/intellect/divine countenance), as opposed to bread of hester panim (hidden face)

Shaddai — the Divine Name (שַׁדַּי), expounded as 'He Who said to His world: Enough (dai)' and 'there is enough in My Godliness for every creature'; associated with the covenant (brit), Shabbat-rest, and tzimtzum (constriction)

ruach ha-kodesh — the holy spirit; divine inspiration/prophetic afflatus bestowed on a person (the spirit of holiness that enables inspired speech, as with Esther and David), not ordinary wind, breath, or a spirit of folly
chok — 'statute' (Ps. 81 'ki chok l'Yisrael hu'), the aspect of the brit/covenant sealed in the flesh ('chok bish'ero sam')
brit ila'ah — the supernal covenant, aspect of the sun, enclothed in Metatron/the Ziz-bird's wing (lower unification)

canonical_he: בשביל זה באין עליו בזיונות ושפיכות דמים
gloss_en: the state in which humiliations and bloodshed come upon a person — degradations suffered before teshuvah, while Ehyeh/Keter is still hidden from him
forms: בשביל זה באין עליו בזיונות ושפיכות דמים

gloss_en: am — the people/masses, the 'flesh' (basar) relative to the true sage who is their soul/essence (etzem), broken by hearing his sigh

flesh (basar) — the bodily flesh/corporeal substance, as opposed to bone/essence (etzem); e.g. the people as 'flesh' relative to the sage's 'essence', Eve as 'flesh of his flesh', and the holy body called 'flesh' — not the homograph biser/besorah (to announce, tidings)
bat ayin — the pupil (black) of the eye, the contracting blackness that limits and contains great things; linked to Avraham's daughter 'Bakol' (Bava Batra 16b)

addition/increase (tosefet/tosafot) — surplus or excess beyond the essential measure; in Likutey Moharan the aspect of superfluous 'more' (linked to arrogance/idolatry via 'not because of your abundance,' and to the blemish of the covenant as wasted extra). NOT the medieval Talmudic glossators (the Tosafot) nor Sabbath 'tosefet' as a halakhic time-extension term.
pride/arrogance (ga'avah) — the negative character trait of haughtiness and self-aggrandizement, condemned as gassut ha-ruach and linked by Rabbi Nachman to idolatry and poverty
Ge'ulah — the Redemption: the national-messianic deliverance of Israel from exile, brought about through repentance and faith (as in 'in Nissan they are destined to be redeemed')
Sefer HaZohar — the Book of the Zohar, the foundational kabbalistic work attributed to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, through which Torah will not be forgotten from Israel
haughtiness, arrogant pride (ge'ut) — the vice of self-exaltation, associated with idolatry and with Haman; not ge'ut as 'majesty/exaltedness of God' nor 'rising tide/surging of the sea'

Redemption (ge'ulah) — the messianic/national deliverance (as in 'the essence of the Redemption'), whose core is the revelation of Da'at; the noun גְּאֻלָּה, not the verb גָּאַל nor גֹּאֲלָה/defilement (גֹּעַל-related homographs)
hitdabkut b'tzaddikim — attachment/closeness to the tzaddikim, the virtue that guides the perpetually soul-thirsty ('tzam'ah nafshi') so they not drink 'foul water'
Gevurah — the kabbalistic sefirah of divine might/severity, the attribute of restraint and judgment (din) associated with Isaac and with fear/awe, counterpart to Chesed (lovingkindness)

importance/esteem (chashivut) — the abstract noun of standing and worth (from ḥashuv, 'important'), especially the elevated status and honor of Israel paired with grace (chen), homiletically linked to 'ship' (sefinah, via safun ve-chashuv) and identified with Malkhut/fear of Heaven

Gevurot — the Kabbalistic 'severities/mighty forces' (plural of Gevurah): the divine powers of judgment and constriction on the left side (side of Isaac/din), which manifest as forceful voice and thunder, as the five gevurot in da'at emerging as speech, and which require sweetening at their root
raglo — 'his foot' (of Yosef, Gen. 41:44), symbol of gevurot/severities and speech ('tzedek yikra'ehu l'raglo'), paired against 'his hand'=mochin
the Divine Name AGLA — the kabbalistic acronym of "Atah Gibor Le'olam Adonai" (You are mighty forever, my Lord), a Name associated with gevurot (severities/mighty powers)
the mistress (Aramaic gevirta) — the noble lady/matron of the house, symbolizing Malkhut/the kingdom of Heaven (the 'woman who fears God'), in contrast to the evil maidservant (shifcha bisha)

"great" (gadol) — the adjective of greatness, used by Rabbi Nachman (LM I:250, from Deut. 4:7 'mi goy gadol') as the aspect denoting Divine providence above nature, manifest in God hearing prayer and altering nature
difficulty in childbirth (kishui leiled) — the hard labor pains of delivery, used as the aspect of anguish in the birthing of the soul
giddul hanefesh — the raising/growth of the soul with its pains ('as one mourns a firstborn,' tza'ar hagiddul), companion to the soul's difficult birth
mountain (har) — the geographic elevation, used homiletically as a symbolic aspect (e.g., of greatness/malkhut, or of the Temple/da'at); not to be confused with other letter-sharing forms

greatness/exaltedness (gedulah) — the noun גְּדֻלָּה denoting elevated stature, honor, and majesty, identified in Likutey Moharan 58 with Malkhut/the Shekhinah (as opposed to the verb גָּדְלָה 'she grew' or the adjective גְּדוֹלָה 'great, fem.')
geder adam — the defining category 'man' (as opposed to beast), attained through tzedakah ('na'aseh adam'), the status of possessing speech
gevanin — the colors (fire and water = shamayim), the hues shining from supernal Imma into the tefillin

Asiyah — 'action/deed' as the aspect of concrete doing, identified with the World of Asiyah (the lowest of the four kabbalistic worlds, the realm of physical action and the body); the noun עֲשִׂיָּה, not a verb form of עשה
sak — the sack (of Yosef's brothers), symbol of the body that fasting empties yet in which the 'bundle of money'/desire remains bound
ofanim she'baTorah — the 'wheels' (Ofanim-angels) within Torah, identified as the bodies of halakhot (gufei halakhot)
gufei halakhot — the essential corpora/bodies of halakhic law, which are the Ofanim ('wheels') of the Torah's Chariot
Gehinnom — the netherworld of post-mortem punishment and purgation (hell; homiletically linked to 'Gei Ben Hinnom,' the Valley of Ben Hinnom)
galgalim — the celestial spheres/wheels, which charity embodies ('a wheel that revolves in the world,' Shabbat 151b)
the blemishing of faith, prayer, and Eretz Yisrael — the sin-state (Avraham's 'How will I know?') that causes descent into Egypt/exile, the anti-miracle realm
exile (galut) — the collective banishment/diaspora state of Israel away from the Land of Israel (e.g., the Egyptian exile), caused in Likutey Moharan 7 by a deficiency of faith/prayer
chesron emunah — deficiency of faith, the root cause of exile (Song 4:8 'me'rosh amanah'), faith being the aspect of prayer and miracles
galut Mitzrayim — the Egyptian exile, archetype of all exiles, incurred by blemished faith/prayer; Egypt being the inversion of miracles and prayer

the pidyon (redemption-money ritual) together with the sweetening (hamtakah) of harsh judgments — the paired act of giving a redemption payment that mitigates heavenly decrees, e.g., as the prerequisite permitting a physician to heal
'l'hafnot eilekha kol rish'ei aretz' — the Aleinu phrase 'to turn to You all the wicked of the earth,' interpreted as the converts (gerim)

Torah of kindness (torat chesed, Prov. 31:26) — Torah study done altruistically, learning in order to teach others (Sukkah 49b), which elevates the fallen glory and the faculty of speech and draws converts and penitents into holiness

the worry and craving for livelihood (parnassah) — the anxious preoccupation with and lust for earning one's sustenance, which Rabbi Nachman (LM I:23) identifies with darkness, sorrow (be-itzavon), and the darkened face of the money-craving
mi'shalom — speech's derivation from peace ('adabrah na shalom,' Ps. 122:8): peace/love as the precondition enabling the words of prayer

Tzedek — 'righteousness/justice' (the noun צֶדֶק), used by Rabbi Nachman as a scriptural-kabbalistic term (e.g., 'tzedek tedaberun', 'tzedek yikra'ehu le-raglo') identified variously with Malkhut, garments, speech of Torah and prayer, and feet; not the verb צָדַק ('to be right'), not צְדָקָה ('charity'), and not the planet Jupiter

Teruah — the broken, staccato shofar blast (one of the three shofar sounds: tekiah, shevarim, teruah), which Rabbi Nachman expounds homiletically via the root ר-ע-ה/ר-ו-ע as shepherding, melody, speech, and the spirit of prophecy
awakening from sleep (hitorerut ha-shenah) — the arousal of one who slumbers spiritually, as in the shofar's call 'Awake, you sleepers, from your slumber'; שֵׁנָה 'sleep', not שָׁנָה 'year'

externality (chitzoniyut) — the outer, external dimension or aspect of something, the garment-like surface level (e.g., speech vs. thought, bodily service vs. Torah and prayer), always contrasted with penimiyut (inwardness)

canonical_he: תורה שלומדין בצר לאדם, בעניות ובדחקות
gloss_en: Torah studied in a person's distress, in poverty and hardship — night-Torah (aspect of layla/darkness) that rectifies speech and draws the day's thread of chesed
forms: תורה שלומדין בצר לאדם, בעניות ובדחקות

canonical_he: רוח פיו של הקדוש ברוך הוא
gloss_en: ruach piv shel HaKadosh Barukh Hu — the breath of God's mouth, i.e. the aspect of divine speech/dibbur (Chagigah 12b cosmology)
forms: רוח פיו של הקדוש ברוך הוא

gloss_en: begadim levanim — white garments, symbol of rectified speech (Malkhut=mouth) that must be kept free of every stain

bird (Aramaic tzipparta, the giant bird of Rabbah bar bar Chana's tale in Bava Batra 73b, standing ankle-deep in water; expounded in LM 11 as the symbol of speech/the illuminating word mediating between man and heaven) — not tzippor as mere ornithological term, nor tzafra 'morning'

Hoshana Rabba — the seventh day of the festival of Sukkot, marked by the willow (aravah) rite; treated in Likutey Moharan 74 as the aspect of speech without knowledge (dibbur belo de'ah) and of judgment (din) associated with Isaac

speech without knowledge (dibbur belo de'ah) — Torah words uttered/stammered without understanding, which nonetheless ascend on high; associated with Hoshana Rabba and the willow (aravah, resembling lips), opposite of speech with knowledge (Simchat Torah)

canonical_he: דבור ממשיך באורי התורה גם כן משם
gloss_en: speech that draws down Torah-explanations — dibbur flowing from the opened Supernal Heart (via prayer's arousal of mercy) which channels be'urei haTorah
forms: דבור ממשיך באורי התורה גם כן משם

gloss_en: Midbar Tzin — the Wilderness of Tzin (Num. 20), homiletically 'chilled speech' (dibbur metzunan), where Miriam died and the Well/Torah-explanations departed
dibbur metzunan — chilled, cooled-off speech, the fallen state of words no longer 'like fiery coals,' causing the soul's departure and loss of Torah-explanations
the good within speech — the tov in an utterance that makes it heard and accepted ('the good — everyone desires it')
dibbur nishma v'nitkabel — speech that is heard and accepted, the only utterance that qualifies as true dibbur (vs. Ps. 19:4)

the narrative words of the Torah surrounding a commandment — the Torah's speech-utterances (e.g., "And the Lord spoke to Moses") that frame the explicit command itself, embodying the hidden (nistar) service of "we will hear" (nishma), as distinct from the revealed commandment one knows how to fulfill (na'aseh)
words of Torah (divrei Torah) — the spoken/written verbal content of Torah teaching, as in "the words of this Torah" (Deut. 29:28) and Torah discourse one speaks; not physical objects or events
nivzeh b'einav nim'as — being despised and lowly in one's own eyes (Ps. 15:4), the self-effacement guarding God's honor that lets one speak illuminating words
anavah v'katnut — humility and smallness/self-effacement, making one's honor as nothing before God's honor, the prerequisite for illuminated speech (Malkhut=mouth)
speaking words of truth before God — honest speech in hitbodedut/prayer by which God becomes one's light to find the many openings out of darkness and exile
me'arah — the cave (in Abba Shaul's gravedigger tale), symbol of devekut/attachment ('k'ma'ar ish v'loyot,' I Kings 7)
devekut — cleaving/attachment of the soul to God; the state of devotional union and self-nullification in the Infinite, especially as achieved in prayer
devekut achorei hakedushah — the kelipah's parasitic attachment at the 'back' of holiness: Pharaoh (=oref, nape) and his three ministers (windpipe/esophagus/veins) sucking vitality from behind speech
davar echad la-dor — "one leader/spokesman per generation" (Sanhedrin 8a dictum), here a designation of Malkhut as the singular divine word/speech inserted into impurity by sin
yetedot u-masmerot — pegs and nails (Rashi's gloss of sikkta), symbolizing words of Torah as "nails well-planted" per Ecclesiastes 12:11

thunder / thunderclaps (רַעַם, pl. רְעָמִים) — the celestial peals of thunder, which in Likutey Moharan symbolize the powerful voice a person emits in prayer (born of the gevurot) that strikes and awakens the heart, straightening its crookedness
kisse in the Torah-domain — the "throne" as Torah's concealment: matters that Atik Yomin covered, hiding themselves within Torah narratives
devarim she-kissah Atik Yomin — the esoteric matters "which the Ancient of Days concealed" (Pesachim 119a), secrets cloaked in the Torah's stories

fish (the aquatic creature, דָּג; Aramaic equivalent כַּוְרָא) — used homiletically as a symbol, e.g. for the tzaddik of the generation or for Israel who 'multiply like fish' (וְיִדְגּוּ לָרֹב); not to be confused with דָּאֵג (worry) or the proper name/idol Dagon
pechatim — pits/ditches (from the Tanna's parable), symbolizing the mineral element (domem) whose bad traits the tzaddik's face nullifies
domem — the inanimate/mineral element, lowest of the four kingdoms, source of a class of bad character traits

Ibbur — 'gestation/pregnancy': the embryonic state in which the mochin (divine intellect/influx) are concealed and constricted as in a womb, prior to their 'birth' (leidah); associated with judgment and with Yaakov ('in the womb he grasped the heel')

tzimtzum — the kabbalistic contraction/constriction: the divine self-limitation that produced the Vacated Space (chalal ha-panui), associated with judgment (din) and, by extension, the constriction of the intellect
Minchah — the meal-offering of fine flour and, by extension, the afternoon Minchah prayer instituted by Isaac; associated with the aspect of judgments (dinim)

the north wind (ruach tzafon) — the northern wind of Berakhot 3b that blew upon King David's harp at midnight, causing it to play; homiletically linked to the spirit hidden (tzafun) in the heart and to the side of judgments/gevurot
hastarat panim — divine hiding of the Face, the state of concealment identified with judgments (dinim) and Israel's distress

canonical_he: מחמת אהבה שהקדוש ברוך הוא אוהב אותך
gloss_en: the love with which the Holy One loves you — divine love as the reason both mercy (YHVH) and judgment (Elokim) are for one's good; echad = gematria ahavah
forms: מחמת אהבה שהקדוש ברוך הוא אוהב אותך

gloss_en: panah oref — "turning the back of the neck," the divine posture of judgment (din), opposite of the face which is compassion
din ve-rachamim — the paired attributes judgment-and-mercy, corresponding to the two yods of "vayyitzer" and the vowel tzeirei
dina de-malkhuta dina — the halakhic principle "the law of the kingdom is law," civil-royal judgment as an aspect of din/Malkhut
de-yitbarkhun kulhu shita yomin — Zoharic phrase "so that all six weekdays be blessed," the purpose of Shabbat eating as source of the week's abundance

dal — 'the lowly/poor one': the adjective דַּל denoting poverty and lowliness, used as a mystical aspect (the humble 'heel' quality of Yaakov, and Malkhut as the poor one possessing nothing of her own)
dalut — poverty/destitution as a spiritual state (not the letter dalet), the impoverished condition linked to the garment/skin of tefillin passage

the 'four wings/corners' (dalet kenafot) — the Aramaic 'dalet' (four) paired with 'kenafot' (wings/corners), denoting the four corners of the earth (as in 'mi-kenaf ha-aretz'), homiletically linked to the letter Dalet within the letter Hei; not the word 'door' (delet)
shilya — the placenta/afterbirth, womb-membrane where the fetus rests, forming the closed-mem shape from the two "doors of the womb" (Job 3:10)

menstrual blood (dam niddah) — the blood of a menstruant woman, used in Likutey Moharan 29 as the aspect of the Shekhinah's defilement/redness caused by blemish of the covenant (e.g., 'Why is Your clothing red?', the stain on the garment)
admimut — redness as substance: the menstrual-blood red (dam niddah) in wine and in the woman's excessive bleeding, emblem of unsweetened din
the stain and grease-spot on his garment — the ketem/revav of ritual stain law, symbolizing serpent's defilement and menstrual blood from disgracing the kingdom

demimah — silence/stillness (דְּמִימָה, from ד.מ.ם, as in kol demamah dakah): the hushed quieting of speech in the face of insult, which in Likutey Moharan I:6 forms the chirik point, linked to 'hadom' (footstool) and the lower dot of the letter alef
tears (dim'ot) — the salty water wept from the eyes, associated with speech/prayer and bearing a portion of eyesight/providence
be-Shabbat — on the Sabbath day as halakhic time-frame for visiting the sick, when one says "She [Shabbat] can have mercy" (Shabbat 12a)
knowing the Torah — the third cognitive stage after learning and understanding, which constitutes Da'at (knowledge) among the three intellects

Life (chayim) — vitality/aliveness as a spiritual quality and state, the plural noun חַיִּים meaning "life" (including eternal life of the World to Come), as opposed to death; not the personal name Chaim

eyes (inflected forms of עַיִן, 'eye': construct 'eyes of' / 'my eyes'), homiletically expounded as the seat of intellect/consciousness (sekhel, chokhmah, da'at) via Gen 3:7 'and the eyes of both were opened'
achdut shel chesed u-gevurah — the unification of Kindness and Severity, the essence of Da'at: not distinguishing chesed from din, blessing ha-tov ve-hameitiv on all

barrels of oil (Aramaic 'garvei de-mishcha' from Rabbah bar bar Chana's tale, Bava Batra 74a — the three hundred barrels of oil filled from an eyeball), interpreted as the aspect of da'at/intellect via the holy anointing oil

the mikveh of the Fiftieth Gate — the ritual immersion pool identified with the highest of the fifty gates of Binah (the Sha'ar HaNun), associated with Shavuot immersion and supreme Da'at (per Likutey Moharan I:56)

great Da'at — the expanded, supernal knowledge/consciousness (associated in LM I:56 with the manna and the mikveh of the Fiftieth Gate), whose revelation opens speech and makes God's faithfulness known
Bilaam — the gentile prophet of Balak's story, counterpart to Moshe as the da'at of the kelipah ("among the nations there arose — Bilaam")
da'at di-kelipah — the knowledge/intellect of the husk (unholy side), the impure counterpart of Moshe's holy da'at, embodied in Bilaam
da'at kol Yisrael — the collective knowledge/consciousness of all Israel, which Moshe embodies as the generation's da'at
da'ato shel he-chakham — the sage's da'at (knowledge) as the "man seated upon the throne" of the Merkavah imagery; "without knowledge the soul is not good" (Prov 19:2)

hadrat panim — the 'splendor/majesty of the countenance' (from 'vehadarta penei zaken', Lev 19:32): the radiant glory of the face associated with the elder/beard (the 13 tikkunei dikna), source of the thirteen hermeneutical principles of Torah exposition, attained through rectification of the covenant
derushei ha-Torah — homiletical expositions of Torah via the thirteen hermeneutic principles, drawn from the thirteen tikkunei dikna, aspect of hadrat panim

derekh — 'way/path' (the noun, gematria 224 = 2×112/twice YB"K or twice baki): the mystical 'path in the sea' of the Elul kavanot, identified with marital union (zivug) and the covenant, as in 'all flesh corrupted its way' (Gen 6:12); not any homographic verb form or other root-derivative
derekh ha-memutza — the middle/mean path that inclines neither right nor left, identified with mishpat, the central pillar
chasid — the pious one distinguished by good deeds (paired with lamdan in Torah), imitating God, corresponding to the name Hashem Tzeva'ot
emet ha-amiti — the truest/ultimate truth, the highest grade of truthful speech before God, whose attainer is lit by God's own light
kefiyat ha-yetzer — subduing/coercing the evil inclination, the act through which one reveals love/Chesed, the "day that goes with all days"
mitzvat tzitzit — the commandment of fringed garments, a protection against the serpent's counsel and sexual immorality (covering arayot, per Tikkun 18)
limud zekhut on the wicked — the act of advocating merit for a rasha, by which one is saved from his evil eye (as God too defends the wicked to shield the tzaddik)
being saved from the evil eye — the person's rescue from the rasha's ra ayin, achieved through finding merit in the wicked one
shor she-ba-nefesh — the "ox" within the soul: the polished light added to the soul when its scattered fragments are gathered and the will shines
hadlakat ha-ner — the act of kindling the (Chanukah) lamp near the doorway, embodying the illumination of glory ("the earth shone from His glory")
he'arat ha-kavod — the illumination/shining of divine glory (Ezekiel 43:2, "the earth shone from His glory"), enacted by lighting the candle and returned to its root in yirah

canonical_he: שלחן, דהינו על־ידי אכילה בקדשה כנ"ל
gloss_en: shulchan — the table as site of eating in holiness, a person's table being keter malkhut (Yoma 72b), the aspect of kavod/King of Glory
forms: שלחן, דהינו על־ידי אכילה בקדשה כנ"ל

gloss_en: he'arat panim — the shining of the Face: divine countenance turned toward the glory, opposite of hastarat panim caused by gluttonous eating

canonical_he: הבדל שבין גדר אדם לגדר בהמה
gloss_en: the distinction between man and beast — humans nursing from breasts placed "at the place of binah" (Berakhot 10a) vs. animals nursing below; understanding as the human differentia
forms: הבדל שבין גדר אדם לגדר בהמה

gloss_en: cessation/interruption of the breath (hefsek ha-neshimah) — the stopping of the life-sustaining respiration of cool air, which in Likutey Moharan I:60 is identified with worthless exhaled vapor (hevel), the 'vanities of the nations' and 'vanity of beauty,' and thus the negation of the rain- and wealth-bringing power of breathing
hevel ha-yofi — "charm/beauty is vain" (Prov 31:30) read as the vain breath: the cessation/interruption of breathing, the nations' empty havalim that bring no rain

the breath of the mouths of schoolchildren (hevel pihem shel tinokot) — the sinless breath/vapor emitted by young children studying Torah, the Talmudic paradigm of 'breath without sin' that sustains the world
young children / infants (tinokot) — schoolchildren whose breath is without sin, identified as the aspect of the cherubim (which had child-like faces) from which the prophets draw their sustenance
hagdalat ha-sekhel — enlargement of the intellect/mochin (embodied in tefillin), expanding the mind to grasp God's daily hints

elder (zaken) — the aged sage as a spiritual aspect: one whose days are lengthened and expanded with added holiness, identified with Atik/tikkunei Atik, length of days, splendor of countenance (hadrat panim), and 'one who has acquired wisdom' (Kiddushin 32b); not zakan 'beard'

canonical_he: הוא דר באוירא דארץ־ישראל, ויש לו אלוקי
gloss_en: dwelling in the air of Eretz Yisrael and "having a God" — the state attained by clapping hands in prayer, per "whoever dwells in the Land is as one who has a God" (Ketubot 110b)
forms: הוא דר באוירא דארץ־ישראל, ויש לו אלוקי

canonical_he: שמחפש ומוצא בעצמו עדין מעט טוב
gloss_en: seeking and finding in oneself a remaining bit of good — the introspective act (Azamra, LM I:282 theme) of locating one's own good points to avoid sadness and reach joy
forms: שמחפש ומוצא בעצמו עדין מעט טוב

gloss_en: giving tzedakah to this tzaddik — the act of donating charity specifically to the unique tzaddik who is yesod olam
being blessed immediately — the state of the giver receiving instant blessing upon giving to the tzaddik-yesod
study of the poskim — Torah study devoted specifically to the halakhic decisors and their decided legal rulings (as opposed to Talmudic dispute or other genres of study)
the revelation of chesed as love and yearning ('cholat ahavah') — disclosure of the kindness-attribute at the guarded brit, manifest as longing for God

the hand (yad) — the bodily hand as a mystical symbol and active organ: the hand of clapping, music, and joy ('you shall rejoice in all the undertakings of your hand'), of prophecy ('by the hand of the prophets I was imaged'), of judgment/the square ('My hand takes hold of judgment'), and embodying the Name Havayah (yud = 10, dalet = 4); NOT the grammaticalized idiom עַל־יַד / עַל־יָדָם ('by means of, through the agency of')
Havayah — the four-letter Divine Name YHVH, here encoded in yad (yud=10 letters, dalet=4), the Name of mercy that sweetens judgments
the letter/name heh — signifying Havayot, the Names of Havayah (mercy) invoked in hand-clapping to sweeten Elokim-judgments

Havayot — plural of Havayah, the Tetragrammaton (YHVH); the Divine Names YHVH, kabbalistically associated with the kindnesses (chasadim); not 'existences/entities' in the philosophical sense nor Talmudic dialectics (havayot d'Abaye v'Rava)

Procreation/begetting (holadah) — the act of engendering and bringing forth offspring, i.e., conception and childbirth, extended in Rabbi Nachman's teachings to spiritual begetting (birthing souls, Torah novellae); the verbal noun of ה-ל-ד/י-ל-ד hif'il, not 'birth' as an event of being born (לידה) nor any other root
'arkhuvateh da le-da nakshan' — 'his knees knocked one against the other' (Daniel 5:6, applied in Zohar/Idra), interpreted as the aspect of holadah, procreative bringing-forth
possessing the two expertises (baki be-ratzo/baki be-shov, 161=KSA and 63=SaG) — the dual mastery of ascent and descent ('esak shamayim / atzi'ah she'ol') that forms the derekh of teshuvah

walking in the ways of repentance (holekh be-darkhei ha-teshuvah) — actively traversing the path of teshuvah, attained in Likutey Moharan I:6 through the two expertises (baki be-ratzo / baki be-shov, entering and exiting)
through each and every act of teshuvah — repentance performed repeatedly, each one effecting the higher and lower unifications
the refinement of the voice of one's song — purification of vocal melody in proportion to the purification of wisdom via the 13 middot; the kaneh (windpipe/wisdom-acquirer) producing clarified sound

honoring those who fear God (mechabed yir'ei Hashem) — the act of according honor to God-fearing people, which returns the exiled glory (kavod) to its root in fear/awe (yirah), per Psalms 15 'and those who fear the Lord he honors' (Likutey Moharan I:14)

Returning/elevating the divine glory (kavod) to its root, namely to fear of Heaven (yirah) — the spiritual act in Likutey Moharan I:14 of restoring exiled honor to its source in awe of God, accomplished by honoring God-fearers and making converts and penitents, which perfects fear and brings peace
the drawing-near of converts or penitents — the approach of gerim and ba'alei teshuvah that generates new hitpa'arut (glory/splendor) for God
Moshe's humility (anavah/anvetanuto) — his self-nullification of all sense of greatness even when praised by the King, enabling 'mecheni na'
Moshe's power to atone — the capacity in Moshe's hand to effect kapparah for the sin of the golden calf through his self-effacing prayer
praying while binding thought to speech — the mode of tefillah in which machashavah is consciously attached to dibbur, forming the vessel of blessing
the formation of the aforementioned vessel (keli) — the receptacle for blessing made by every Jew (each a tzaddik/aleph) through thought-bound prayer
afiyah — 'baking' (afinan, from Rabbah bar bar Chanah's tale) as the tzaddikim's ripening/preparation of the accumulated prayers, building the Shekhinah toward union

preparation for the marital union (zivug) — the Shekhinah's readying of herself for divine coupling, as baking and cooking are the preparation for eating (eating being the aspect of zivug), effected through the accumulation of prayers in Likutey Moharan I:2
bishul — 'cooking' (bashlinan) of the prayers by the tzaddikim of each generation, maturing them so they bear fruit rather than lying barren
hakhna'ah — submission/humility, the self-lowering identified with yirah and Malkhut, as God 'diminishes Himself' to ask for fear
subduing the yetzer hara — striking the ship-sinking 'wave' with clubs engraved 'Ehyeh', i.e., vanquishing the evil inclination through Torah (God's Names, the vav of the Luchot)
joy produced by playing an instrument with the hand — simchah built as the musician's hand rises and falls sorting good spirit from sad spirit ('ve-nigen be-yado')
subduing the medameh — the humbling of the imaginative faculty, the ruach ra'ah/ruach shtut, achieved by the hand-played melody that clarifies the spirit of prophecy
the heart hears — the hearing-capacity of the lev awakened by thunder (gevurot-voice), yielding 'the meditation of my heart is understanding'
razin — 'secrets' (Aramaic), here identified specifically with Halakhah (vs. razin de-razin = Kabbalah), the lower-unification garment of governance
studying Torah shelo lishmah — learning for the title 'Rabbi' (self-aggrandizement), an inferior mode of study
the diminished worth of such study — the state in which shelo-lishmah learning lacks full importance (yet night-study draws a protective thread of chesed)

the peace present within the generation (ha-shalom she-ba-dor) — the interpersonal harmony among the people of a given generation that enables them to discuss truth together and thereby draw the world to God's service (Likutey Moharan I:27)

speech of the Holy Tongue (dibbur shel leshon ha-kodesh) — articulated holy speech in Hebrew, the creative sacred language, which in Likutey Moharan I:19 nullifies the lust for adultery (the bonfire of the seventy stars)
the pyre of the seventy stars nullified — the medurah of shiv'in kokhvin (Zoharic image of the lust of niuf/gilui arayot, 'leimor') extinguished by perfecting Lashon HaKodesh
the mochichim — the rebukers of the generation, symbolized as raglin (feet/legs, 'ekev'), to whom the judgments are revealed
the food becoming blessed — the state of nourishment blessed through awakening the sparkling letters (the 32 Elokim of Creation) within eating and drinking
guf naki — a clean body, free of superfluous waste (motarot/excrement), attained via emunat chakhamim (contrast: mocker judged in boiling excrement)

clapping of the palms/hands (hamcha'at kaf) — the devotional act of hand-clapping (esp. in prayer/joy), which in Likutey Moharan 10 reveals the illumination of the hands and nullifies heresy and idolatry

hands (yadayim/yadin) — the paired bodily limbs, right and left hand, used as a mystical aspect (bechina) in Likutey Moharan: symbolizing wisdom/holiness, the revealed Torah, receiving (kabbalah), clapping in prayer, north-south, and heaven (fire and water); not the verb 'to judge' (yadin from din) nor any other homograph

sleep (שֵׁנָה) — the state of slumber in which the mind/soul rests and is renewed; used by Rabbi Nachman both literally (bodily sleep induced by the cold-moist lungs) and expansively (constricted consciousness, simple Torah study, faith-based commerce as modes of 'sleep')

west (מַעֲרָב) — the cardinal direction of sunset, opposite the east/sunrise; used as the symbolic locus of receiving/gathering (the poor who collects charity, 'from the west I will gather you') and of the setting/withdrawal of light
the collector of tzedakah, i.e., the poor man — the recipient/gatherer of charity, symbolized as ma'arav (west, 'from the west I will gather you')

the revelation of the mochin — the kabbalistic 'mentalities' (intellects) becoming manifest, as when Torah insight matures from gestation (ibbur/Yaakov) into revealed consciousness (Yisrael = 'li rosh'), linked to the drawing down of the light of the Divine countenance
the drawing-forth of the ruach — extension of the spirit/breath (the pulse-animating ruach), symbolized by the vav of the melafum vowel

Chokhmah — wisdom/intellect (sekhel): the divine wisdom and illuminating intellect present in every thing, identified with the sefirah Chokhmah, the vitality (chiyut) that enlivens all creation ('the wisdom gives life to them'), equated by Rabbi Nachman with sekhel/mochin de-gadlut

sweetening (hamtakah) — the kabbalistic mitigation of harsh judgments (dinim), effected by ascending from constricted consciousness (mochin d'katnut) to expanded consciousness (mochin d'gadlut) through wisdom/Torah knowledge

mochin d'gadlut — 'expanded consciousness/mentalities' (Kabbalistic term): the mature, broadened state of the divine intellects associated with Chokhmah, light, mercy (chasadim), and sweetening of judgments, opposite of mochin d'katnut (constricted consciousness)
love and mutual inclusion of souls — ahavah by which all nefashot are encompassed together (lacking in R. Akiva's students), producing light and joy ('anan ba-chavivuta talya')
Chokhmah as knowledge of Torah — wisdom qua yedi'at haTorah, the sweetener of Yitzchak's din, embodied in Yaakov (speech with knowledge)

sweetening of the judgment of Isaac — the mitigation (hamtakah) of the harsh din/Gevurah personified by the patriarch Isaac (aspect of the Nefesh), accomplished through Chokhmah/knowledge of Torah and embodied in Jacob who is born from Isaac (Likutey Moharan I:74)

The sweetening of the judgments (hamtakat ha-dinim) — the kabbalistic mitigation, softening, and nullification of harsh heavenly decrees (dinim/gevurot) by drawing compassion (chasadim) upon them at their root, as through joy, dance and clapping, melody, self-judgment, and attachment to the tzaddik
holiness and purity of thought — kedushat ve-taharat ha-machashavot, root-level sweetening of judgments ('all is clarified in thought'), the reason for Rosh HaShanah travel to tzaddikim

birth, childbirth (leidah) — the act of giving birth, used as the archetype of emergence from concealment/gestation into revelation (e.g., Torah revealed after hiddenness, mentalities birthed after withdrawal, judgment sweetened at delivery)
one who receives counsel from the sages of the generation — accepting eitzah from chakhmei ha-dor, which expands the constricted mind and sweetens dinim
ezer ve-hayeshu'ah — help and salvation, itself defined as the sweetening of judgments drawn from the supernal intellect (Even Shetiyah/Kodesh Kodashim)
he'arot u-nesi'ut panim — illuminations and the 'lifting of the Face' (Divine favor), the un-hiding of God's face that sweetens and nullifies dinim (vs. hastarat panim)

canonical_he: כשמכה כף אל כף ומחבר הידים בתפלה
gloss_en: striking palm against palm in prayer — clapping/joining the hands during tefillah, whereby 3 yad-Havayot (SheLaV=336) sweeten the 3 Elokim of the throat
forms: כשמכה כף אל כף ומחבר הידים בתפלה

gloss_en: 'va-afalteihu' — 'I will rescue him' (Psalm 91:14), the deliverance-clause read as the sweetening of judgments effected by heart-desire (ki vi=42=3×yad) expressed in clapping
the elevation of the feet/legs (raglin) through sacred dancing — when the legs are uplifted by means of the dances, effecting spiritual rectification (Likutey Moharan I:10)

the nullification of arrogance (ga'avah) — the abolishing of haughtiness/pride, which Likutey Moharan 10 equates with idolatry ('avodah zarah') and heresy, effected through the tzaddik, the spirit in the heart, and dancing/clapping, thereby increasing faith
the nullification of avodah zarah — idolatry abolished through dancing and hand-clapping powered by the joyful ruach of the heart

Dancing and clapping of the hands (rikudin ve-hamcha'at kaf) — the devotional bodily acts of dance and hand-clapping, which in Likutey Moharan I:10 reveal the illumination of the hands and feet, sweeten harsh judgments, and nullify arrogance and heresy, increasing faith

the exile of the Malkhut (Divine Kingship) of holiness — the current state in which the sefirah of holy Kingship is in exile, so its mochin/da'at cannot be drawn down (the reason melody is blemished and cantors lack da'at, per Likutey Moharan I:3)
ha-neginah nifgemet — the blemishing of melody/song when Malkhut of holiness is in exile, explaining why cantors (chazanim) lack da'at, since melody derives from the prophetic source
hanhagah — leadership/governance of the world, the functional aspect of Malkhut (kingship) that is blemished and turned to heresy when one without perfect faith presumes to lead
hitlabshut ha-Kabbalah ba-halakhah — the enclothement of Kabbalah (razin d'razin) within Halakhah (razin), symbolizing God's weekday governance, the Lower Unification (yichuda tata'ah)

canonical_he: הנהגת הקדוש ברוך הוא בששת ימי החל
gloss_en: God's governance (hanhagah) of the world during the six weekdays — the Holy One, blessed be He's mode of conducting creation on the ordinary (non-Sabbath) days, identified in Likutey Moharan 11 with the Lower Unification (yichuda tata'ah) and with the enclothement of Kabbalah within Halakhah
forms: הנהגת הקדוש ברוך הוא בששת ימי החל

gloss_en: charity (tzedakah) given on the Sabbath — the monetary giving performed on the holy Shabbat specifically, which corresponds to the future renewed sun (as opposed to weekday charity, which corresponds to the present sun)

canonical_he: הנותן כח לבחינת שלש רגלין הנ"ל
gloss_en: ha-noten koach li-vchinat shalosh raglin — that which empowers the three 'legs' (festivals) aspect: the two kinds of tzedakah (weekday charity = present sun; Shabbat charity = future renewed sun of the World to Come)
forms: הנותן כח לבחינת שלש רגלין הנ"ל

gloss_en: mizrach — East as a symbol for the GIVER of tzedakah, from 'from the east I will bring your seed' and 'sow for yourselves for tzedakah' (opposed to West = the poor recipient)
the giver of charity — the person who gives tzedakah (alms) to the poor, agent noun phrase 'one who gives charity' (ha-noten tzedakah)
chakhamim lehara — 'wise to do evil' (Jer. 4:22), evil cleverness identified with the primordial Serpent (nachash), in the secret of circumcision
ha-nekudah ha-tachtonah shel temunat alef — the LOWER dot of the letter Alef's form, symbolizing demimah (silence/stillness), the chirik vowel, 'the earth is My footstool' (hadom)
gazing / contemplative beholding (histaklut) — the act of directing one's inner gaze, e.g. at the divine intellect within every thing or toward God in trust
ashrei — 'praiseworthy' (Ps. 119:1) expounded as a term of histaklut (gazing), i.e., gazing upon the intellect (Yaakov ish tam) present in every thing
stimat ha-einayim — the physical act of shutting/sealing the eyes tightly (even pressing with a finger) required to gaze upon the light of the ultimate purpose (takhlit)
histaklut ha-zot — this particular gaze upon the takhlit (the all-good, all-one ultimate purpose), attainable only with completely closed eyes

chalal (חָלָל) — a void/empty space that is simultaneously the slain corpse of Deuteronomy 21:1 ("when a chalal is found in the land"), signifying the withdrawal (histalkut) of holiness/vitality; linked by wordplay to chilul (desecration) of Shabbat — not a flute (chalil), nor the profaned priest (chalal) in its halakhic sense
ein lo emunat chakhamim — the deficient state of lacking faith in the Sages, equated with the 'departure of the sages' and the pele ('wonder') of Isaiah 29:14; remedied by a vow

the departure/withdrawal (histalkut) of the Torah sages — the loss or removal of the wise men and their wisdom (per Isaiah 29:14 as expounded in Eichah Rabbah), caused by lack of faith in the Sages and linked to the aspect of 'wonder' (pele)

the Great Hand (yad ha-gedolah) — the divine hand of God's unlimited providential capacity to provide sufficiency, which Rabbi Nachman identifies as the aspect of contentment (histapkut), derived from "Is the hand of God too short?" (Numbers 11:23)

Contentment (histapkut) — being satisfied with sufficient provision; the trait of finding one's material needs fully met and desiring no more, as in 'a tzaddik eats to the satisfaction of his soul' (root ס-פ-ק, sufficiency)
tithe (ma'aser) — the giving of a tenth of one's produce/income as a sacred obligation, which in LM 221 brings about contentment (histapkut) and the aspect of the Great Hand

bizyonot u-shefikhut damim — humiliations and 'bloodshed' (shaming that drains the face's blood) suffered before repentance, manifesting the hiding and turning-away of the face of the Name Ehyeh (EKY"H)
hastarat ve-hachzarat pnei EKY"H — the hiding and turning-back of the 'face' of the divine Name Ehyeh from the sinner before teshuvah, experienced as disgrace and bloodshed
tekiah — the single long, unbroken shofar blast (one of the three shofar sounds alongside shevarim and teruah), from the root ת-ק-ע (to blow/thrust)
resolution (terutz) — the answer that resolves a kushya (textual/learning difficulty), reconciling apparently contradictory statements; not tarutz 'you shall run' (from רוץ)

"the one who makes peace" (ha-oseh shalom, הָעוֹשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם) — the liturgical/scriptural epithet for the peacemaker, invoked in Likutey Moharan I:75 as the aspect of resolving dispute (e.g., a teirutz reconciling contradictory ideas), identified with the elevation of mayin nukvin; not the abstract noun 'peace' itself
meshaber ga'avato — the act of breaking one's own pride/arrogance, the measure of which determines the elevation of divine glory (kavod), linked to Mount Tabor
ha'alaat ha-kavod — the elevation/raising of the divine glory, accomplished through Torah and proportional to the breaking of one's pride and attaining humility
kol ha-dibburim she-medabrim be-Torah u-tefillah — all words spoken in Torah study and prayer, functioning as ha'alaat mayin nukvin (raising of the feminine waters) that bind one to God

yearnings and longing (kisufin ve-hishtokekut) — the soul's desirous craving for holiness that constitutes the will (ratzon), forms the soul in potential, and effects the elevation of the feminine waters (mayin nukvin)

verbal confession (vidui devarim) — the spoken, articulated enumeration of one's sins, ideally before a Torah scholar (tzaddik), by which the aspect of Malkhut is rectified and elevated and the world of speech repaired; not silent remorse or the general concept of repentance

canonical_he: העלה את המלכות מבין הסטרא אחרא
gloss_en: he'elah et ha-malkhut mi-bein ha-Sitra Achra — the act of raising Malkhut (fallen kingship) out from among the Other Side, effected through verbal confession ('death' / destruction of sixty cities)
forms: העלה את המלכות מבין הסטרא אחרא

gloss_en: la itgalya — 'not revealed' (Sifra DiTzniuta on Ze'ir Anpin), the concealed/hidden (he'lem) dimension within humanly attainable wisdoms, their inner makif aspect

concealment (he'lem) — the hidden, occluded state of the divine intellects/influx (mochin) when they are not revealed, likened to gestation (ibbur); the noun 'hiddenness,' not the verb 'to ignore' (hit'alem) nor 'youth' (elem)
ha-peh nishlam be-or gadol — the mouth/speech perfected with great light: through the delight of Shabbat eating (unlike weekday fasting) speech of peace is completed ('adabrah na shalom')
havlei ha-goyim — the 'vanities of the nations' (Jer. 14:22, idolatry), identified as interruption/cessation of the breath (neshimah) that brings rain and wealth

sons/children (banim) — human offspring/progeny, used by R. Nachman as a bechina symbol (e.g., children as 'students of God,' as fruits growing on the soul's branches, or sons as the higher intellect/settled da'at); distinct from the homograph bonim ('builders')
ha-peirot ha-gedelim ba-anafim — one's children as the 'fruits' growing on the soul-tree's branches (money/soul-light); the robber who takes the branch (money) takes the fruits (children's souls)
've-holakhti ivrim be-derekh lo yada'u' — the verse 'I will lead the blind by a way they knew not' (Isa. 42:16), signifying the tzaddik guiding the penitent onto the straight path (crossroads)
ha-tzaddik horah lo derekh yashar — the tzaddik's act of instructing the penitent in the straight path, the 'crossroads' (parashat derakhim) aspect following confession
ke-she-yotz'in Yisrael me-chokhmatan shel ha-umot — Israel's exodus from the wisdom/philosophy of the nations, whereupon the tzaddik-sun emerges 'like a groom from his chuppah' and shines
'be-kan'o et kin'ati' — the verse of Pinchas's zeal (Num. 25:11), signifying the tzaddik who envies no other tzaddik in this world or the next but is zealous only for God alone
nekudot shel kissufin — the vowel-points formed by one's yearnings/longings ('nikhsefa ve-gam kaltah nafshi'): good or evil desires create good or evil nekudot (souls) that animate the letters

canonical_he: הצטרפותן של אותיות התורה, לפעל איזהו פעלה
gloss_en: hitztarfutan shel otiyot ha-Torah — the combining/pairing of the Torah's letters to effect an action, good or evil, determined by the vowel-points born of one's yearnings
forms: הצטרפותן של אותיות התורה, לפעל איזהו פעלה

gloss_en: oved Elokim — 'one who serves God' (Mal. 3:18), matched with Ben Zoma who 'gazed and died': the heart inflamed beyond its level by the tzaddik's light unto death

"he gazed and died" (heitzitz va-met) — Ben Zoma's fate in the Four-who-entered-the-Pardes narrative (Chagigah 14b): peering at the supernal light beyond one's level and perishing from it; in Likutey Moharan I:31 the archetype of the 'servant of God' whose heart is inflamed by the tzaddik's illumination above his rung to the point of death

canonical_he: מי שיוצא מדעתו מחמת שעולה למעלה ממדרגתו
gloss_en: ha-yotzei mi-da'ato me-chamat aliyah le-ma'alah mi-madregato — one who loses his sanity by ascending above his spiritual level: Ben Azzai's 'gazed and was stricken,' the aspect of 'lo avado' (did not serve Him)
forms: מי שיוצא מדעתו מחמת שעולה למעלה ממדרגתו

gloss_en: "gazed and was stricken" — the Talmudic phrase (Chagigah 14b) describing Ben Azzai's fate upon entering the Pardes: he peered at the divine mysteries and was harmed/driven from sanity, emblematic of one who loses his mind by ascending beyond his spiritual level

canonical_he: הקדוש־ברוך־הוא חומד מלמעלה לשכן עם האדם
gloss_en: HaKadosh-Barukh-Hu chomed mi-lemalah lishkon im ha-adam — God's desiring from above to dwell with a person, aroused by truth (emet, acronym of 'amah tekhalenah milemalah'), per 'God is near to all who call on Him in truth'
forms: הקדוש־ברוך־הוא חומד מלמעלה לשכן עם האדם

gloss_en: HaKadosh-Barukh-Hu oseh al yado mofetim — God's performing miracles/wonders through one who breaks the craving for eating (ta'avat akhilah), linked to 'yisa Hashem panav'
HaKadosh-Barukh-Hu shokhen imo — God's dwelling with a person as the reward of truth ('God is near to all who call upon Him in truth'), the light one finds at the opening; falsehood drives Him away
sa'ara be-igula — 'hair in a circle' (Tikkun 70): hairs as circuits/roundabout channels through which the mochin's illumination exits — the circling preliminary explanations leading to the point

canonical_he: הקדמות המסבבין עד שבאים אל המכון
gloss_en: hakdamot ha-mesavevin — the roundabout introductions/preliminaries (of a lower intellect clothing a higher one) that circle until arriving at the intended point (mekhuvan), like hair-circuits
forms: הקדמות המסבבין עד שבאים אל המכון

gloss_en: hakdamot shel kol ha-chokhmot — the premises/axioms of every wisdom, called 'servants' (Pharaoh's avadim) that serve the wisdom, in the Vacated Space (chalal ha-panui) teaching
osek be-masa u-matan be-emunah — conducting business/commerce in faithfulness, i.e., engaging monetary law (pshat of Torah), equivalent to offering the tamid sacrifice and burning the incense

hakravat ha-korban tamid ve-haktarat ha-ketoret — the daily tamid offering and incense-burning as cosmic acts (raising ChaBaD of Asiyah into Yetzirah, holy sparks via eleven spices) enacted by honest commerce
hasagot Elokut — perceptions/apprehensions of Godliness, attainable only via many tzimtzumim (contractions) from cause to effect, higher intellect clothed in lower, like teacher to student
divine providence (hashgachah) — God's direct watchful supervision and governance of the world, associated with the eye/seeing and transcending the fixed order of nature

eyes (עֵינַיִם/Aram. עֵינִין) — the paired organ of sight, used by Rabbi Nachman as the symbolic seat of perception: guarded vision (tzitzit vs. straying after the eyes), judgment ('Ein Mishpat'), divine providence/watchfulness, wisdom, and livelihood ('the eyes of all look to You'); not the homographic ma'yan-sense of a water-spring standing alone
hashgachah shleimah — complete divine providence, drawn down only after breaking the craving for money through tzedakah (the 'generous spirit' cooling the heart's heat)
hasagat Elokuto — the comprehension of God's Divinity, the essence of the World to Come ('they will all know Me'), each new attainment prompting teshuvah upon the prior one
hasagat ha-Torah — the attainment/comprehension of Torah, the cognitive grasp of Torah merited upon reaching the level of Da'at (Proverbs 8:12, Daniel 2:21)

bittul she-nitbatel el ha-takhlit — the state of self-nullification in which one is absorbed into the ultimate End/purpose (God), reached through suffering, whose residual reshimu yields Torah innovations

canonical_he: השיג שכל היסורין הם טובות גדולות מאד
gloss_en: the attainment, within nullification to the End, of the insight that all sufferings are actually very great goods — the perception consoling one over afflictions
forms: השיג שכל היסורין הם טובות גדולות מאד

gloss_en: Joy / gladness (simchah) — the spiritual-emotional state of joyfulness in serving God, the antithesis of sadness and depression (atzvut, marah shechorah); the noun שִׂמְחָה, not the verb שָׂמַח or the adjective שָׂמֵחַ
matar — rain as a symbol: the downflow of divine bounty and blessings prepared through controversy for the sake of Heaven
hashpa'ot u-verakhot — divine effluences and blessings, the bounty symbolized by rain (matar)
hit'havut ha-nefesh — the coming-into-being/formation of a soul, generated by a Jew's yearning and longing for God (Psalms 84: 'my soul yearns')
al yedei ha-ahavah — 'through love': love (chesed, right side, Abraham) as the agent by which empowerment/overcoming occurs ('many waters cannot extinguish the love')
hitgabrut — empowerment/prevailing, the strengthening (gevurah-overcoming) whose main source is love, per 'Sit at My right hand'
the kabbalistic act of combining the gevurot (severities, left) within the chasadim (kindnesses, right) — 'left within the right' (Psalms 20:7)
revelation (hitgalut) — the becoming-revealed/manifest of what was hidden, esp. the disclosure of Torah and Divinity to a person (as opposed to concealment/gestation)
'in the perfection of deeds and the refinement of the intellect' — the pair of matter (instruments of action) and form (intellect, 'father in wisdom') on which one's spiritual money depends
Song of Songs 5:4 'My beloved sent his hand through the opening' — proof-verse for the revelation of the illumination of the hands (clapping in prayer that nullifies idolatry)

shofar — the ram's horn blown ritually (esp. on Rosh Hashanah), whose blast awakens sleepers, arouses fear/trembling, and whose form is narrow above and wide below; homiletically linked to yofi (beauty, 'shapru') and teruah

the revelation of fear/awe (hitgalut ha-yir'ah) — the manifestation or disclosure of reverent awe of God, as when yir'ah becomes openly felt (e.g., aroused by the shofar or by the King's garments of glory)

hitgalut ha-hitpa'arut — the revelation of the King's glory/adornment (splendid garments on the royal celebration day), identified with the revelation of fear, which leads to revelation of the will/love

The cleaving of spirit to spirit (Aramaic: itdabbekut rucha be-rucha) — the Zoharic term for the intimate spiritual union effected through 'kisses' (neshikin), as when the spirit of the Tanna bonds with the spirit of one who studies his teaching, or the upper union of Netzach and Hod; distinct from bodily union (guf be-guf)
mitzvah — a divine commandment / religious precept performed as a sacred deed (מִצְוָה), which Rabbi Nachman links homiletically to לשון התחברות, 'connection/joining'

hitchabrut — joining/connection: the act of becoming attached or bound together (verbal noun of ח.ב.ר, hitpael), used for attachment to God and the joining together implied in mitzvah/tefillah etymologies

the joining/binding of the mind (thought) with speech — the union of one's consciousness with the words of prayer, identified in Likutey Moharan I:80 as an aspect of peace (shalom) and of Yosef, achieved when thought is bound to the spoken words of prayer
mal'akhei libo — 'the angels/messengers of his heart', the flaming enthusiasm (hitlahavut) of the heart within the heart-Temple, vulnerable to the external forces

the fiery enthusiasm (hitlahavut) of the heart — the burning ardor/spiritual fervor kindled in the heart, likened to a flame (generated by the motion of the intellect, and identified with the 'angels of the heart' that burn away the kelipot)
tenu'at ha-sekhel — the movement/motion of the intellect, which by the heat-generating nature of motion gives birth to the heart's enthusiasm

verbal confession (viduy devarim) — spoken articulation of one's sins — made before a Torah scholar (talmid chakham), the Breslov practice by which the tzaddik guides the penitent according to his soul-root and Malkhut is restored to its root

canonical_he: יספר לפני התלמיד חכם, הינו ודוי דברים
gloss_en: the practice of recounting before the Torah scholar — viduy devarim, verbal confession of sins spoken before the talmid chakham, remedy for the bad traits of the four elements
forms: יספר לפני התלמיד חכם, הינו ודוי דברים

gloss_en: the principle that the disciples receive 'double' (pi shenayim) of the master's spirit at the tzaddik's passing (Elisha-Elijah model), the great illumination revealed at histalkut
anafim — 'branches' of the wife's soul-tree: the sparkling and spreading of her soul's light, symbolizing the money allotted to a man with his spouse

the sparkling and outward spreading of the light of the wife's soul (hitnotzetzut ve-hitpashtut orah) — the radiance emanating from the trunk-light of her nefesh, identified in Likutey Moharan I:69 with a man's allotted money as the 'branches' of the tree whose fruits are children
the awakening/arousal of Chokhmah (Wisdom) that occurs in prayer — 'creation in potential', the renewal of the world before it emerges into actuality in Torah
the drawing near of Israel to their Father in Heaven — the closeness achieved chiefly through tikkun ha-brit ('I bore you on eagles' wings and brought you to Me')
hatarah/hasibah of eating — 'Vayasev' read as reclining at a meal (Midrash Shemot 20): the festive-meal sense of God 'leading around' Israel, linked to the five mouth-articulations

canonical_he: ואז ימין ה פשוטה לקבל תשובתו
gloss_en: 'and then God's right hand is outstretched to receive his repentance' — the divine acceptance attained via the two expertises (baki in ascent/descent, KS"A and S"G) forming the derekh of teshuvah
forms: ואז ימין ה פשוטה לקבל תשובתו

gloss_en: the spiritual practice of judging oneself — that a person adjudicate all his own affairs and conduct (from שָׁפַט, to judge), thereby enacting 'judgment below' so there is no judgment from above, removing all fears and elevating pure fear of God (Likutey Moharan I:15)

madregah tachtonah me'od — the very lowest spiritual rung, where one must still believe God is present ('if I make my bed in Sheol, You are there'), drawing holiness from Havayah in the S"G (63) expansion

canonical_he: כשאדם זוכה לבוא לאיזו מדרגה בקדשה העליונה
gloss_en: the state of having ascended to some rung of supernal holiness yet not resting there but striving ever higher — drawing holiness from the Name Ehyeh in the KS"A (161) expansion, 'expert in running' (baki be-ratzo)
forms: כשאדם זוכה לבוא לאיזו מדרגה בקדשה העליונה

gloss_en: Numbers 20:8 'And you shall speak to the rock' — proof-verse mapped to the chotem (nose) in the third tikkun of the beard, the hidden full path beneath the nostrils
simchah shel mitzvah — the joy of performing a commandment, the joyful state connected with verbal confession (viduy devarim) of one's sins

the day of death (yom ha-mitah) — the Talmudic phrase from Sotah 21a for one's dying day, which Rabbi Nachman (LM I:4) reads as an allusion to verbal confession, since 'all who are executed confess' (Sanhedrin 43b)

Death (mitah) — the noun denoting dying / the state or event of death, opposed to life (chayim); includes death as the counterpart of darkness, foolishness and the body, death of the condemned (who confess before execution), and punishments figuratively termed 'death'. Not מַטָּה (bed/staff) or any other homograph; verbal inflections of the root מ-ו-ת (e.g., וּמֵתָה 'and it dies') expressing this same sense of dying belong here.

the annulment (breaking) of anger by means of compassion — the spiritual practice, taught in Likutey Moharan I:18, of sweetening one's rage (ka'as / charon-af) with mercy (rachamanut) so that no cruelty results, in the aspect of 'in wrath, remember compassion' (Habakkuk 3:2)
the thought (machashavah) that one binds to speech in prayer — the mental component whose linkage to the spoken word forms the vessel of prayer
the yod (letter/point) that is formed — the small point produced in constructing the aleph-vessel through binding thought to speech in the Jew's (tzaddik's) prayer
'Vayitzer' (Gen 2:7, spelled with two yods) — the double formation: for good and for evil, for reward and for punishment; the tzeirei vowel as judgment-and-mercy
MaNTzePaKh — the five final-form letters (mem, nun, tzadi, peh, khaf) instituted by the 'seers' (prophets), symbolizing the veins (veridin) and 216/din, the aspect of judgment
veins (veridin) — the blood vessels of the body, homiletically split as ri"u (216) + din (judgment) and linked to the final letters mantzpa"kh in Likutey Moharan I:37
Zohar dictum 'break the chet of kaneh (reed)' — the letter-operation from Psalms 68:31 'Rebuke the beast of the reed', guarding the mind from turning chametz
'and make from it a heh' — transforming the broken chet into the letter heh, thereby turning the letters of chametz (leaven) into matzah: keeping wisdom unleavened

canonical_he: זדונות, דהינו המחשבות זרות, נעשין לו כזכיות
gloss_en: the transformation whereby deliberate sins — here the alien/stray thoughts in prayer — are converted into merits (zedonot na'asin ke-zakhuyot) for one who rules in his prayer
forms: זדונות, דהינו המחשבות זרות, נעשין לו כזכיות

canonical_he: זה תנצל מבחינת חמץ, שהיא סטרא דמותא
gloss_en: the deliverance, via breaking the chet into heh, from the aspect of chametz which is the 'side of death' (sitra de-mota) — escape from leavened, deadened intellect
forms: זה תנצל מבחינת חמץ, שהיא סטרא דמותא

gloss_en: the filth/contamination of the primordial Serpent (zuhamat ha-nachash) — the spiritual defilement injected into humanity by the Serpent in Eden, which in Likutey Moharan is linked to the 39 curses/forbidden labors and to melancholy of spirit

the radiance of the firmament (zohar ha-rakia, Daniel 12:3) — the luminous brightness of the heavenly expanse, invoked in Likutey Moharan I:29 as the shining/whitening aspect of the heavens linked to the crimson thread that whitens sins

zivug — coupling/union: the kabbalistic (and marital) act of pairing and uniting two entities (e.g., the supernal union of masculine and feminine aspects, the joining of souls or letters), from the root ז-ו-ג 'to pair'
mittah — a bed (the sleeping/marital couch, as in placing one's bed between north and south), symbolizing marital union (zivug); not matteh (staff/rod or tribe)
zahav — gold as symbol of zivvug (coupling/union), aroused from the left side/north ('From the north gold comes', Job 37:22; Zohar Vayeshev 186b)

the counsels/advice (etzot) that one receives from the tzaddikim — the tzaddik's guidance whose reception is likened to marriage and union (nisu'in ve-zivug), engraving truth in the recipient (LM I:7)

the physical (bodily) coupling — zivug ha-gufani, the corporeal marital union that, in Kabbalistic sequence, follows the 'coupling of kisses' (zivug ha-neshikin) and effects procreation/opening of the womb
the pairing and combining of the Torah's letters (via the vowel-points) — symbolizing the couplings of bodies (zivvugei ha-gufot)
zivvug ha-neshikin — the kabbalistic 'coupling of kisses', the mouth-to-mouth union effected by speech ('loosening the mouth of the mute'), preceding bodily union
zivvuga de-Kudsha-Brikh-Hu u-Shekhinteh — the supernal union of the Holy One and His Shekhinah, effected by Israel's prayers, linked to the splitting of the Sea into twelve paths

"because of tzitzit" — the merit of the tzitzit commandment (guarding the eyes, linked to 'metzitz min ha-charakim') as the cause through which Joseph merited 'ben porat,' being protected from the serpent's union and attaining holy union (zivvuga di-kedushah)
zivvuga di-kedushah — the holy marital union (as merited by Joseph, 'ben porat'), opposite of the serpent's union of the Sitra Achra, guarded by the eyes/tzitzit
the pairing and combining of the nekudot (vowel-points) themselves — symbolizing the couplings of souls (as distinct from the letters = bodies)
zivvugei ha-nefashot — the couplings/matings of souls, the soul-level unions symbolized by the combining of the vowel-points, whereby arriving souls bring stray or repentant thoughts

purity of the heart (ṭohorat ha-lev) — the spiritual cleansing of one's heart, as in Psalms 51 'create for me a pure heart,' which in LM I:156 enables receiving divine inspiration (ruach ha-kodesh) and ever-new words in secluded prayer before God

canonical_he: זוכה לדבר בכל פעם דבורים חדשים
gloss_en: zokheh ledaber bekhol pa'am dibburim chadashim — the merited state of speaking ever-new words in hitbodedut prayer before God, a personal ruach ha-kodesh modeled on David composing Psalms
forms: זוכה לדבר בכל פעם דבורים חדשים

gloss_en: lefi ha-zivvug she-gorem bitfilato — the measure/quality of the supernal union (zivvug of the Holy One and the Shekhinah) that a person causes through his prayer, the determining cause of his own match
zokheh le-zivvugo — meriting one's earthly marriage partner (one's match), granted in correspondence to the supernal union effected by one's prayer
zokheh limtzo ha-petach — the attainment of finding the opening/doorway (to holiness/light) achieved through truth, since God the illuminating light is present only where there is no falsehood
he'arot ha-avot — the illuminations of the three Patriarchs (Avraham, Yitzchak, Yaakov), whose light enables Shabbat, ceasing of the enemy, and peace, rebuilding the gate of holiness
ha-tze'akah — the cry/scream (in prayer) that births the mochin (intellects) out of their concealment, the first prerequisite for attaining holy da'at

meriting to give birth to the mochin (intellects/divine consciousness) out of their hidden concealment — the drawing forth of concealed intellect from its state of hiddenness (ta'alumah), likened to a birth brought about through crying out (as in the laboring woman's cry), in Likutey Moharan I:21
tze'akah be-Torah u-tefillah — crying out in Torah study and prayer, the means for drawing concealed surrounding lights (makkifin) toward revelation

the power of growth and the power of sprouting — the vegetative, nurturing force that makes things grow (koach ha-godel ve-koach ha-tzomeach), which Likutey Moharan I:155 identifies with faith (emunah), via 'va-yehi omen et Hadassah' (raising/nurturing) and 'Emunah — this is Seder Zeraim'

meriting to receive moral rebuke (mussar) from the true rebuke-givers/admonishers of the generation — attained through faith, and identified in Likutey Moharan I:22 with the 'seal of the feet' (chotam ha-raglin)

the seal of the hands (chotam ha-yadin) — the kabbalistic 'seal' impressed on the hands, which in Likutey Moharan I:22 is identified with faith (emunah), the inner of the two seals ('a seal within a seal') whose outer counterpart is the seal of the feet

zokhin li-teshuvah ve-nishlam ha-da'at — the state attained via Torah of repentance completed and da'at (mind) restored/settled, whereby scattered letters and combinations return to their place and mercy can be aroused

canonical_he: שעמד בנסיון ושבר הקלפה שקדמה לפרי
gloss_en: she-amad ba-nisayon ve-shibber ha-klipah she-kadmah la-pri — one who withstood the sexual trial and broke the husk (klipah) that precedes the fruit, i.e., shattering the lust of ni'uf, the tikkun ha-klali of all seventy evil traits
forms: שעמד בנסיון ושבר הקלפה שקדמה לפרי

gloss_en: The remembrance/retention of the Torah — that the Torah not be forgotten from Israel (זִכְרִירַת/זְכִירַת הַתּוֹרָה, as in R. Shimon bar Yochai's promise 'לֹא תִּשְׁתַּכַּח תּוֹרָה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל'), i.e., the enduring preservation of Torah knowledge in the Jewish people; not memory in general nor any other homograph
Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai (Rashbi), the Tannaitic sage and traditional author of the Zohar, who promised that the Torah would never be forgotten from Israel

The spirit of prophecy (ruach nevuah) — the holy 'good spirit' of Divine inspiration that rests upon prophets, associated with ruach ha-kodesh, memory, and the rectified imaginative faculty, opposed to the melancholy 'evil spirit' of folly
Ze'ir Anpin (zeira de-anpin) — the kabbalistic partzuf 'Small Face,' here denoting all wisdoms attainable by the human mind, revealed-yet-not-revealed, as opposed to hidden Atik
avuha de-abba — 'the father's father' (grandfather) in the Talmudic carob story, symbolizing the aspect of zaken/Atik, the ancient primordial level
charuv — the carob tree of Choni's story, symbolizing zaken/Atik (the Ancient One), linked via berosh-cypress to Mordekhai and rav chesed by gematria

Atik (the Ancient One) — the kabbalistic partzuf Atik/Atik Yomin, the most ancient and concealed divine countenance, associated in Likutey Moharan 60 with the elder (zaken), abundant kindness (rav chesed), and the stories of ancient years from which all seventy faces/years receive vitality; not the ordinary adjective עתיק 'old/ancient thing' nor עתיק 'copied/removed'
chut ha-shani — the scarlet thread (of Zerach, Genesis 38), symbolizing the shining of the light of the Divine countenance (or ha-panim) upon one, opposite the darkness of livelihood-worry
impure waters (Aramaic/Zoharic 'mayin mesa'avin') — kabbalistic term for ritually defiled waters, symbolizing contaminated seed resulting from blemishing the covenant (pegam ha-brit)
zera tamei — impure/contaminated seed, the defiled 'bitter waters' state of one who blemished his brit (covenant), rendering him unable to pray with all his bones
pure waters (Aramaic 'mayin dadkhyan', the Zoharic term for purified waters, symbolizing holy seed and sexual purity through guarding the covenant)
holy seed (zera kodesh) — seed/progeny sanctified in purity, denoting sexual purity through guarding the covenant (shemirat ha-brit), as opposed to blemished seed

embrace (chibbuk) — the kabbalistic act of embracing, associated with the right hand/arm of Chesed (kindness), as in 'his right hand embraces me' (Song of Songs); the sheltering embrace symbolized by the sukkah

canonical_he: אהבה, שהצדיק מקבל את החרפה באהבה
gloss_en: ahavah — love as the tzaddik's loving acceptance of insult/disgrace (from the scholar's arrogant words), constituting the aspect of 'embrace' (chibbuk)
forms: אהבה, שהצדיק מקבל את החרפה באהבה

gloss_en: the shadow of the hand (tzel yad) — God's sheltering hand-shadow of Isaiah 51:16 ('and in the shadow of My hand I have sheltered you'), identified with the sukkah's covering and the embrace of the right hand (Zohar Pinchas 214b); not 'shadow' generically nor a physical hand

renewal of the mochin (the kabbalistic 'brains'/intellects) — the refreshing of consciousness/daat, identified in Likutey Moharan I:35 with the light of the countenance and the renewal of the soul, and linked to the building of the Temple

chiddush ha-neshamah — the renewal of the soul, identified with the light of the countenance and renewal of the mochin, equated with building the Beit HaMikdash ('one with da'at is as if the Temple were built in his days')
chiddush ha-sekhel, haynu chiddush ha-neshamah — renewal of the intellect, i.e., of the soul, effected through sleep ('new every morning'), when weary mochin are refreshed
nesher she-bivchinat nefesh — the eagle within the soul-level (nefesh): the renewal the soul undergoes in its ascent in ibur (gestation), per 'your youth is renewed like the eagle'

canonical_he: חדוש שנתחדש הנפש בעליתה בבחינת עבור
gloss_en: chiddush she-nitchadesh ha-nefesh ba-aliyatah bivchinat ibur — the soul's renewal achieved in its ascent through the state of gestation (ibur), the 'eagle' renewal of Psalm 103:5
forms: חדוש שנתחדש הנפש בעליתה בבחינת עבור

gloss_en: nesher she-ba-Torah — the eagle among the four chayot within Torah: chiddushin d'Orayta, novel Torah insights, per 'renewed like the eagle'
hitorerut chadash ve-cheshek nimratz la-Torah — a fresh awakening and intense yearning for Torah granted to lesser souls unable to innovate, itself a form of chiddush (renewal)
chiddushin — novelty/renewals: here the category of Torah-newness that includes even renewed desire and awakening for Torah in those who cannot themselves innovate

"We will do and we will hear" (na'aseh ve-nishma) — Israel's declaration at Sinai (Exodus 24:7) accepting the Torah, action preceding hearing; in Likutey Moharan the aspect linked to joy, acceptance of the Torah, and the two crowns of Shabbat 88a
chedvat Hashem — 'the joy of God is your stronghold' (Nehemiah 8:10): divine joy/gladness that is the source of holy boldness (azut dikdushah), attained via na'aseh ve-nishma

According honor to an elder (sage) who has forgotten his Torah learning — the Talmudic dictum (cf. Berakhot 8b) that one must still show respect to a zaken whose learning has departed from him, applied in Likutey Moharan I:67 as the counsel that restores wisdom/honor lost through prayer without heartfelt intention
chozer ve-nitgaleh chokhmato — the wisdom that departed (the elder who forgot his learning) returning and being revealed again, via the cold reviving waters of da'at from the true tzaddik
lefi ha-teshuvah, lefi ha-machaloket — the correspondence whereby answers/books (responsa) arise in measure with the dispute/questions raised, each machaloket generating a needed sefer
chozer ve-shav el emunat chakhamim — returning in repentance to faith in the Sages, whereby books once mocked ('making many books') regain their necessity and worth
