she-osin retzono yitbarakh — Israel's fulfilling of God's will, the purpose of creation, whereby they return and cleave to their root and are re-included in Him, the Necessary Existent

canonical_he: חוזרין ניצוצי חלקי המזבח למקומם ונשלם המזבח
gloss_en: chozrin nitzotzei chelkei ha-mizbeach limkomam ve-nishlam ha-mizbeach — the return of the scattered holy sparks of the altar's parts to their place via converts (gerim), completing/repairing the blemished altar that empowered idolatry
forms: חוזרין ניצוצי חלקי המזבח למקומם ונשלם המזבח

gloss_en: keshe-lomed ba-laylah — studying Torah at night, which draws a thread of chesed (loving-kindness) that protects one even when learning she-lo lishmah (for the title 'Rabbi')
bechinat yadayim ha-nal — the aforementioned aspect of the two hands (the strong hand and the hand that magnifies/strengthens), by which the 'hardness of birthing' is removed when new honor arrives
cholefet ve-overet ha-kishui leyled — the passing away of the birthing-hardness (difficulty of labor, kishui leiled) effected through the 'hands,' per 'my bow is renewed in my hand'
cholkim alav — the opposition/dispute against one: people contesting and interrogating him ('who is he?'), the fate of one who pursues honor of kings rather than honor of God

wall (chomah) — a protective city wall / fortification, used as the symbol of guarding enclosure: the 'high wall' of wealth (Prov 18:11) whose breach is anger (Prov 25:28) and the wife as one's wall (Yevamot 62b); not cheimah (wrath) or chamah (sun)

suppression of anger (kevishat ka'as) — the act of conquering/restraining one's wrath, equated in Likutey Moharan I:59 with wealth as the aspect of a protective 'wall' (chomah), i.e. being slow to anger (ma'arich af)
chotam — the seal: the tzaddik as the 'seal' of the holy covenant ('his offspring He sealed with the sign of the brit'), i.e., the guardian of the brit (shomer ha-brit)

the 'seal of the feet' (chotam ha-raglin) — the kabbalistic inner seal of the two seals ('a seal within a seal') in Likutey Moharan 22, attained by receiving rebuke from the true rebukers of the generation, paired with the outer 'seal of the hands' (faith)
ma'asim tovim — good deeds, the primary source of the heart's strength to contain intellect; when wisdom exceeds deeds the heart cannot hold the returning thought
chizzuk ha-lev — the strengthening/fortification of the heart, achieved chiefly through good deeds, enabling the heart to contain intellectual thought
chazanim hem belo da'at — the folk-saying that cantors are fools lacking da'at, explained by the exile of Malkhut of holiness which blemishes melody drawn from the prophets' place

Mashiach — the Messiah, the anointed redeemer of Israel whose advent brings the final redemption; in Likutey Moharan identified as the aspect of the nose/breath ('ruach apeinu meshiach H'', who 'smells and judges'), of prayer, and embodied in Moshe and the tzaddik of the generation (not a generic anointed priest/king, and not the verb מָשַׁח 'to anoint')
yirat shamayim — fear of Heaven as the sanctification of the nose (chotem), per 'he shall smell with the fear of God' (Isaiah 11:3), one of the four sanctified facial organs

peace that has no mouth (shalom she'ein lo peh) — a mute, speechless peace lacking the power of articulate speech, likened to the beasts of the field (Job 5:23) and associated with chametz/the letter chet in LM 57, as opposed to the articulate peace of matzah/hei and the five articulations of the mouth

the animate/animal (chai) — the 'living creature' level in the hierarchy of beings (mineral, vegetable, animal, speaker), i.e., the beast possessing life but lacking the power of speech; not the adjective 'alive' predicated of God or man, nor the noun 'life' (chayim)

wild beast (chayah ra'ah) — the dangerous predatory animal, paired with 'bandits' (listim), used in LM 1:4 as the aspect of the bad traits of the animal element (chai), i.e. idle speech and its offshoots, from which charity to a Torah scholar saves
idle speech (devarim beteilim) — vain, purposeless talk; the bad trait of the 'speaking' (medaber) element, linked with lashon hara, which brings poverty (Likutey Moharan I:4)

chiyut — vitality, the animating life-force that sustains a person or thing (drawn from prayer, wisdom/intellect, or the Divine Name); the abstract noun 'life-energy,' not chayot (living creatures/angelic beings) and not chayot (wild animals)
the Hebrew letter Chet (ח, eighth letter of the alphabet), expounded as an expression of chiyut (vitality) and as the aspect of wisdom/the sun that gives to Malkhut
machashavot kedoshot — holy thoughts, which are the aspect of pure (kosher) animals set to battle impure ones in the parable of kings watching animal combat
chayot tehorot — pure/kosher animals as the symbol for holy thoughts in the royal animal-combat parable, opposed to impure animals (evil thoughts)
evil thoughts (machashavot ra'ot) — morally bad or impure thoughts arising in a person's mind, likened in Likutey Moharan I:233 to impure (non-kosher) animals set to battle against holy thoughts
chayot temeiot — impure/non-kosher animals as the symbol for evil thoughts, set against pure animals (holy thoughts) in the kings' combat parable
chatzar — the courtyard (of the women's house, Esther 2:11) as symbol of chitzoniyut/externality, i.e. thoughts and speech in which God is hidden; not chatzer as enclosure per se

the lower point (nekudah tatah) of the letter Alef — the dot beneath its diagonal vav, symbolizing (in Likutey Moharan I:6) silence/stillness ('the earth is My footstool'), the chirik vowel, the moon, and Yehoshua, as opposed to the upper point (Moshe/sun/throne)

chirik d'SaG — the chirik vowel-point of the divine name SaG (63), linked to 'al tasseg' (moving back a boundary), symbolizing descent/retreat and the expertise-in-returning (baki b'shov) of 'I make my bed in the abyss'
the ant resting in the serpent's mouth — Zoharic/aggadic image invoked alongside the sukkah-as-intellect (Binah) teaching about building a house through wisdom

the Sage of the Generation (chakham ha-dor) — the singular leading Torah sage/true tzaddik of his generation, the 'comprehensive mind' (moach ha-kolel) from whom all individual minds of the generation receive their illumination
the soul (neshamah) — the higher, divine soul of a person, associated with intellect and the heavens, as opposed to the body

sekhel pashut — 'simple intellect,' the first of three intellectual faculties, corresponding to the sefirah Chokhmah ('You made them all with wisdom'), prior to comprehension (Binah) and knowing (Da'at)
chelek Eloah mima'al — the 'portion of God from Above' inherent in every Jew, identified as the aspect of Chokhmah/wisdom (Psalms 104:24)

rebuke/reproof (tokhachah) — the moral admonition delivered by the mokhiach (rebuker), whose opening of the mouth reveals wisdom and thereby kindness (chesed), likened to the voice of the shofar horn (Likutey Moharan I:30)
b'or panekha — 'in the light of Your countenance' (Psalms 89:16), interpreted as the intellect/sekhel, per 'a man's wisdom lights up his face' (Ecclesiastes 8:1)
shemen mishchat kodesh — the holy anointing oil (Exodus 30:25) as symbol of intellect/da'at, underlying the Rabbah bar bar Chanah 'barrels of oil' from the eyeball
the firstborn (bekhor) — the firstborn son himself, identified as the aspect of the intellect/reishit (as in Yaakov, the 'firstborn' who embodies chokhmah)

Chokhmah Tata'ah — the kabbalistic "Lower Wisdom" (Aramaic tata'ah, "lower"), the derivative wisdom identified with Malkhut/Elokim that governs each world and receives from the Supernal Wisdom (Chokhmah Ila'ah) as a student from a teacher; not ordinary human cleverness nor the Upper Wisdom itself
chokhmah ha-manheget et ha-olam — the 'wisdom that governs the world,' i.e. Lower Wisdom (Chokhmah Tata'ah)/Malkhut of holiness that can fall into the exile of the four kingdoms
Abba and Imma — the partzufim 'Father and Mother,' i.e. Chokhmah and Binah (Yod-Heh, the mochin), to which Yesod ascends per the Zohar; grasped by one who rectifies the brit
Chokhmah and Binah — the paired sefirot of Wisdom and Understanding (the supernal 'father and mother,' Abba and Imma, corresponding to the letters Yod-Heh and constituting the mochin/mentalities)

hands and feet (yadin ve-raglin) — the paired bodily limbs as a unified symbolic aspect in Likutey Moharan: hands corresponding to the revealed dimension (revealed Torah, wisdom/holiness, clapping) and feet to the concealed dimension (hidden Torah, speech, faith, dancing), whose illumination is revealed through the tzaddik/spirit of the heart
Chokhmah and Dibbur — the paired wisdom-and-speech corresponding to hands ('lift your hands in holiness') and feet, both encompassed in Yosef ('no man shall raise hand or foot without you')

the complete utterance (ma'amar ha-shalem) — the full divine saying, exemplified by 'Bereishit' as the first of the ten utterances of creation, associated with the father, supernal Wisdom, prayer, the hidden, and Ein Sof, as opposed to the 'half utterance' (chatzi ma'amar) of any lower level relative to the level above it (Likutey Moharan I:22)

Supernal Wisdom (Chokhmah Ila'ah) — the kabbalistic upper Wisdom, the sefirah of Chokhmah as the hidden divine source-wisdom (aspect of father, Bereishit, the complete utterance, root of the Torah), from which Lower Wisdom (Chokhmah Tata'ah) and all worldly wisdoms derive
the Chokhmah that extends through all the worlds — wisdom as immanent life-force ('You made them all with wisdom'), symbolized by the yud of the word yam (sea)

meishra d'sakina — 'the bed/plain of knives' from the Rabbah bar bar Chanah tale, interpreted as Lower Wisdom/Malkhut, the 'learning' (haskein, Numbers 22:30) by which the tzaddik knows whose prayer confused him

lower Eden (Eden Tata'ah) — the kabbalistic lower Eden corresponding to lower Wisdom (Chokhmah Tata'ah), the revealed level associated with 'son,' 'we will do,' and the half utterance, as opposed to supernal Eden

the wisdoms of the Torah — the illuminating intellectual insights/teachings contained within the Torah (chokhmot ha-Torah), identified with light, form, life, and the divine name Yud-Heh, as opposed to worldly folly and darkness

external/secular wisdoms (chokhmot chitzoniyot) — profane, non-Torah branches of knowledge originating in the kelipot (the 'reed of the husks', 'daughter of Pharaoh'), opposed to the holy wisdoms of Godliness
chalav — milk as symbol of Torah ('honey and milk under your tongue,' Song 4:11), with which the tzaddik-of-the-generation, called 'mother,' nurses Israel
gam — the word/particle 'also,' tied to challah whose dough-measure is 43 (מ"ג = gimel-mem, letters of גם) eggs, in the merit-of-the-Patriarchs (chalah zekhut avot) wordplay

challah — the dough-offering (terumah) separated from the first of one's kneading, the priestly portion whose minimum dough measure is forty-three eggs' volume (Numbers 15:19-20), linked to inheriting the Land of Israel; not the verb חָלָה ('was exhausted/entreated')
'We went through fire and water' (Psalms 66:12) — verse read as the illness of fever (kadachat), heat and cold, afflicting one who descends to animal level by eating animal food

the illness of fever (ḥoli ha-qadaḥat) — the febrile sickness of alternating heat and cold (fire and water), which in Likutey Moharan I:263 results from eating animal food and embodies a blemish of the mind (da'at)

Pharaoh (Par'oh), the king of Egypt of the Exodus narrative — the proper name, homiletically expounded by Rabbi Nachman via the roots of nullification/disruption (tafri'u) and revelation (hitgalut) as a symbol for forces of emptiness (e.g., the Vacated Space, the imaginative faculty); not any common noun sharing the letters פרעה
the good subjugated under their hand — the captive good held by the nations/heretics, consisting of imprisoned portions of Jewish souls, which draws them back to recognize the faith of Israel
chelkei nishmot Yisrael — the portions of the souls of Israel held captive among the nations, constituting all the 'good' subjugated there

the Rav — the teacher/master who imparts Torah to a disciple; the giving counterpart in the rav–talmid (master–student) pair, likened to sun vs. moon and to Upper Wisdom transmitting to Lower Wisdom (not רַב 'much/many' nor a rabbinic title-name)

the Side of Death (Sitra deMota) — the Aramaic kabbalistic term for the demonic realm of death and impurity (the sitra achra as the domain of the Angel of Death), associated in Likutey Moharan with chametz and the idolatrous nations
chametz — leavened bread/dough forbidden on Passover (the noun חָמֵץ, 'leaven'), used symbolically in contrast to matzah
chomer — 'matter' in the philosophical matter-form pair (chomer/tzurah), aligned with body, animal, foolishness, and darkness as against soul, man, wisdom, and light
the five fingers of the left hand — bodily symbol of the five Gevurot, root of the five articulation points of the mouth to which speech must be elevated
the five Gevurot — the kabbalistic five forces of severity/strength (corresponding to the five fingers of the left hand and the five articulation points of the mouth) through which speech is produced
the five Chasadim — the five kindnesses of Da'at embodied in tzedakah (charity is chesed, 'reap according to kindness'), by which tzedek is transformed into tzedakah
five Chasadim and five Gevurot — the ten kindnesses-and-strengths constituting Da'at, source of the seminal drop, and reason for reciting ten psalms (Tikkun HaKlali)
the Five Books of the Torah (Chumashim) — the Torah's letters as the heh of the Name Yah, corresponding to the five articulation points of the mouth

the five articulation points of the mouth (chameshet motza'ot ha-peh) — the five phonetic organs (throat, palate, tongue, teeth, lips) from which all letters/speech issue, the physiological source of the power of speech

the Malkhut (Divine Kingship/Sovereignty, the sefirah of Kingship) that the sinner degraded and cast down through his sins — the debased Divine Kingship which arouses God's wrath (per LM I:4 on Proverbs 16:14)

grace/favor (chen, חֵן) — the winning charm that makes one's words and prayers enter and be accepted in the heart of the one petitioned; in LM 1:1 the true grace and importance of Israel, formed by joining the letters chet (chokhmah) and nun (malkhut), identified with Malkhut of holiness

ship, seafaring vessel (Aramaic סְפִינְתָּא, Hebrew סְפִינָה) — the ship of the Rabbah bar bar Chanah sea-tales, expounded homiletically via the root ספ"ן (סָפוּן, 'esteemed') as the grace and importance of Israel; not the ceiling/covering (סִפּוּן) itself

revealing one's Torah to others — the tzaddik's act of outward teaching, the aspect of chesed spreading outward ('a Torah of kindness on her tongue,' Proverbs 31:26), source of dispute with the concealing tzaddik
the Ma'amarot — the ten utterances by which the world was created, identified as chesed ('the world is built on kindness,' Psalms 89:3), aspect of sukkah/embrace
bringing Torah-scholar tzaddikim into one's home — hospitality to true scholars, equivalent to offering the daily tamid sacrifice (Berakhot 10b), the sole means of attaining chesed
shimmush — attending upon and serving the Torah scholars one hosts (standing over them to serve), the service through which one merits chesed
shitin batei — 'sixty houses' of Hagronya (Talmudic tale), read as chesed/Avraham per 'sixty are the queens' (Song 6:8, Rashi) and 'houses of malkhut'—God's kindness in accepting human-termed prayer
atra amikei — the 'deep place' where R. Yonah prayed for rain (Ta'anit 23b), interpreted as chesed, per 'the sun is deeper than the shade' (Shevuot 6b)
the Maharsha's interpretation — the bird perching in the tree (ilana) explained as Avraham who 'planted an eshel' (Genesis 21:33), the protective thread of chesed against the serpent
El Elokim — the paired divine names (gematria of their full spellings = 485 = Tehillim) representing Chesed and Gevurah, by which the seminal drop is extracted from the kelipah

Chesed and Gevurah — the paired kabbalistic sefirot of Lovingkindness (divine benevolence, water) and Might (divine severity/restraint, fire), invoked as a pair corresponding to the Names El and Elokim, to Da'at's five Chasadim and five Gevurot, and to the heat and moisture of the seminal drop
chamimut v'lachut — heat and moisture, the fire-and-water powers within the seminal drop, corresponding to Chesed and Gevurah
tippah — the seminal drop, composed of fire and water / heat and moisture, i.e. Chesed and Gevurah, issuing from Da'at and extractable from the kelipah

'chesed is revealed at the mouth of the amah' — Idra Rabba (Naso 142a) dictum: kindness manifests at the opening of the male organ, linking chesed to the guarded brit ('My covenant is faithful to him')
chanikhav — 'his disciples/initiates' (Genesis 14:14) whom Avraham armed, read midrashically as the Chasadim (kindnesses), drawn along the green line from Binah
've-ahavat chesed' — the phrase 'to love kindness' (Micah 6:8), interpreted as the inner Chasadim (chasadim penimiyim)
chasadim ha-penimiyim — the 'inner kindnesses,' interior Chasadim signified by 'to love kindness' (Micah 6:8)
kiddushin — betrothal/sanctification of marriage, an aspect of the chuppah, i.e. the holy divine influx as encompassing (makkif) lights

chuppah — the wedding canopy of the marriage ceremony, interpreted as the encompassing/surrounding lights (makifin) of divine influx that envelop the tzaddik (as in 'each tzaddik is burned by his fellow's chuppah')

half utterance (chatzi ma'amar) — the Zoharic/Tikkunim notion that each lower level (e.g. 'bara', the son, na'aseh, lower Wisdom, creation itself) is only an incomplete, hinting speech relative to the complete utterance (ma'amar hashalem, 'Bereishit') of the level above it

the entirety/totality of creation (kelaliyut ha-beriah) — all of created existence taken as a whole, which relative to the pre-creation state in Ein Sof is only a 'half utterance', identified with the word 'bara' in Genesis 1:1

the letter Tav (תָּ"ו), final letter of the Hebrew alphabet, expounded in Likutey Moharan 1 as denoting engraving and inscription (chakikah u-reshimah), per Ezekiel 9:4 'and set a mark (tav)' — the impression marked upon the heart
chakikah — engraving/inscribing, the meaning of the letter tav ('set a mark/tav,' Ezekiel 9:4), a mark impressed so words find grace and enter the heart

dust / earth (the substance עָפָר, Aramaic עַפְרָא) — the lowly element of soil, used as a symbolic aspect (of prayer, the humble tzaddik with drawing power, the earth-element source of sadness, and wealth as 'dusts of gold'); not עֹפֶר 'fawn'

Sword (ḥerev) — the bladed weapon, expounded as the aspect of prayer, the principal weapon of Mashiach/Yosef ('with my sword and my bow'); not the homograph חָרֵב 'destroyed/dried up' or חֹרֶב 'dryness/Horeb'

"a sword for the LORD" (cherev la-Hashem) — the scriptural phrase of a sword devoted to God (cf. Isaiah 34:6, Jeremiah 47:6), used in Likutey Moharan I:37 as an aspect linked to breath without sin and to the charity of the Land of Israel; the noun חֶרֶב (sword) with the divine dative, not the adjective חָרֵב (dry/desolate)
the 'double-edged sword' (ḥerev pipiyot) of Psalms 149:6 — the two-mouthed/two-edged sword homiletically linked to the mouth (peh), symbolizing speech and prayer

Mordekhai — the righteous Jewish hero of the Book of Esther (the proper name, expounded via 'mar deror'/pure myrrh), serving in Likutey Moharan as the aspect of freedom/revealed Torah, denial of idolatry, the tzaddik, Malkhut, and abundant kindness

"engraved upon the tablets" (charut al ha-luchot, Exodus 32:16) — the phrase describing God's writing incised on the Tablets of the Covenant, homiletically re-read (Eruvin 54a) as cherut, "freedom," and identified here with the revealed Torah

foreskin (orlah) — the physical/spiritual foreskin covering the Covenant, identified with the three impure husks (kelipot) and with disgrace (cherpah, per Genesis 34:14); not the feminine adjective 'uncircumcised' (עֲרֵלָה) nor orlah-fruit of a tree's first years
the deeds/stories of the wicked — 'darkness' in the Midrash on 'dividing light from darkness,' opposite of the light that is the tzaddikim's deeds

The hidden (esoteric) dimension of Torah — Torah she-be-nistar, the concealed secrets of Torah (sitrei orayta, the hidden light) destined to be fully revealed in the future, attained in this world through prayer with self-sacrifice; contrasted with the revealed Torah (nigleh)
chashkhut v'hastarat ha-yedi'ah — darkness and concealment of knowledge, the 'darkened countenance' (anpin chashukhin) confronted in toiling and 'dying' over Torah

garment (levush) — the kabbalistic 'garment'/clothing: an outer covering that veils and mediates inner spiritual light (e.g., the chashmal, the cloud, the tzimtzum, stories clothing Torah); the noun לְבוּשׁ 'garment', not the verb לָבוּשׁ 'clothed/wearing'
shome'a mi-menagen kasher ve-hagun — the act/state of hearing melody from a worthy, fit musician, which benefits one's divine service (contrast: hearing from a wicked musician)
tov lo — the beneficial spiritual state ('it is good for him') resulting from hearing music played by a kosher musician, aiding service of the Creator
tallit adom — the 'red tallit' of the kelipah, garment-symbol of the impure spirit/Esav, opposite of the white tallit of the Thirteen Attributes
sheretz — a creeping thing/vermin as source of ritual impurity, symbolizing the impurity that mixed into and confused one's prayer (the mud-creature in the fish's nostrils)
tum'ah — ritual impurity/defilement that becomes mixed into a person's prayer and divine service, confounding it (symbolized by the sheretz in the fish's nostril)
Yud-Heh (Y-H) — the first two letters of the Tetragrammaton as a Divine Name, kabbalistically denoting the pair Chokhmah and Binah (Abba and Imma, the mochin, 'two companions that never separate')
'until its full stature (shi'ur komah) is completed' — the completion of the full measure/structure of Malkhut-prayer's stature, linked to the joining of the hands as Yad Ramah

the coming of the Messiah — the future eschatological arrival of Mashiach (יָבוֹא מָשִׁיחַ, 'Mashiach will come'), who, identified here with Moshe, will complete and fully erect the stature of the Shekhinah built up by the prayers of the tzaddikim of every generation; not any other sense of 'coming' or of the root משח (e.g., anointing oil or an anointed priest/king generally)
'let him learn [Torah] not for its own sake' (she-lo lishmah) — the concession of studying Torah with ulterior motive, as a stage toward lishmah
'the serpent will swallow it' — the nachash/serpent of the kelipah devouring the prayer/offering not properly guarded, image of the Other Side seizing what lacks rectification

"hands for the Torah" (yadayim la-Torah) — the three intellectual faculties (Chokhmah, Binah, Da'at) functioning as the three 'hands' (the Great, Strong, and Exalted Hand) by which the Torah is grasped and received; not physical hands in any other context

canonical_he: יד הגדולה ויד החזקה ויד הרמה
gloss_en: the triad Yad ha-Gedolah, Yad ha-Chazakah, Yad ha-Ramah — the three divine 'hands' corresponding to three Havayah Names, mapped to right hand, left hand, and their union in clapping
forms: יד הגדולה ויד החזקה ויד הרמה

gloss_en: the moment of striking when the two hands join in clapping during prayer — the act of union of right (Great Hand) and left (Strong Hand) producing the Exalted Hand
Yad Ramah — the 'Exalted Hand,' the third divine hand/Havayah formed by the joining of right and left hands at the clap, sweetening judgments
tzafon ve-darom — north and south as directional symbols of the two hands (left/Gevurah and right/Chesed), between which the 'bed' (union/prayer) is placed
barukh — the word 'Blessed' (opening of blessings) identified as the aspect of the hands, channel of blessing
the revealed (nigleh) — the exoteric, openly manifest dimension of Torah, contrasted with the concealed/esoteric (nistar); niphal participle of ג-ל-ה, 'that which is revealed'
kiblu — 'they accepted' (Esther 9:27, re-acceptance of Torah in Mordekhai's days), expounded as the aspect of hands (receiving), paired with kiymu = feet
omer se'orim — the barley-omer offering, symbolizing Mordekhai (omer) and Esther (se'orim), the aspect of hands and feet / revealed Torah and ruach ha-kodesh
the three intellects — Chokhmah (simple intellect), Binah (comprehension), Da'at (knowledge), which serve as the 'hands' grasping the Torah
yedi'ah shelemah — complete knowledge: the da'at that unifies Chesed and Gevurah, blessing 'ha-tov ve-ha-meitiv' on all without distinguishing kindness from judgment
Joshua (Yehoshua bin Nun), Moses' disciple and successor — the biblical figure who battles Amalek and receives light from Moshe as the moon from the sun
fulfilling 've-ahavta' — the state of fulfilling 'You shall love Hashem' by making Heaven's Name beloved through honest business dealings (Yoma 86a)

canonical_he: יהיה לו פרנסה בלא יגיעה וטרח
gloss_en: parnasah without toil — the reward-state of receiving livelihood effortlessly, granted through fulfilling 've-ahavta' via faithful commerce
forms: יהיה לו פרנסה בלא יגיעה וטרח

gloss_en: the initial Yud — the letter Yud at the beginning, i.e., the upper Yud of the letter Aleph, identified with the Yud of the essential Name Havayah, symbolizing the initial thought and potential (koach) before actualization (Likutey Moharan I:66)

the Yud at the end — the lower/final Yud of the letter Aleph's two Yuds, identified with the Yud of the Name Adonai (the appellation), symbolizing the end of the deed and actualization (po'al), as expounded in Likutey Moharan I:66

knowing the Divine letters inherent in every thing — the attainment (via perfection of the Holy Tongue, Likutey Moharan I:19) of perceiving the letter-combinations embedded in all objects, e.g. in foods, which enables one to interpret dreams
knowing how to answer the heresy (apikorsut) in one's heart — the capacity, gained via studying poskim/peace of holiness, to refute the evil inclination's inner arguments
'when his face shines with this purification' — the state of the illuminated countenance produced when the heart receives light from the 32 Elokim of Creation
ahavah ve-shalom — love and peace among Israel (via 'love your fellow as yourself' accepted before prayer), the precondition enabling speech in prayer
being able to speak in prayer — the enabled state of articulate tefillah that flows from peace/love, since speech's essence derives from shalom
anashav ha-mekoravin elav — the tzaddik's close followers/disciples, through whom alone his otherwise ungraspable greatness can be perceived
understanding the greatness (ma'alah) of the tzaddik — the attained comprehension of the tzaddik's stature, achievable only indirectly through his followers
reaching that which is hidden from him — attaining the concealed level via prayer lishmah, binding thought firmly to the words of the prayer

Hitkashrut la-tzaddikim — the devotional act of binding/attaching oneself to the true tzaddik(im): being connected and drawn close to the tzaddik (through love and self-nullification before him), which serves as the channel for receiving holiness, pure consciousness, speech, and all beneficial influences
sensing the holiness of Yom Tov — the felt experience of festival sanctity, attainable only through attachment to the tzaddik who embodies it
arousing the shefa (divine bounty) in the world — the effect achieved through yirah (fear of Heaven), whereby one's words are heeded (Berakhot 6b)

canonical_he: יחזק ויגבר מחשבתו על איזה דבר שבעולם
gloss_en: strengthening and intensifying one's thought upon some worldly matter — the focused mental act (with nullified sensations) that has power to actualize its object
forms: יחזק ויגבר מחשבתו על איזה דבר שבעולם

gloss_en: the power to effect that it be so — thought's efficacy to bring about its object in reality (even wealth) when concentrated with total focus

canonical_he: התפארות של השם יתברך שמתפאר בישראל
gloss_en: God's glorification-in-Israel (hitpa'arut): the splendor/pride (pe'er) that the Blessed One takes in His people Israel, which the tzaddik reveals; corresponding to God's own tefillin in which Israel's praise is written (Likutey Moharan I:17)
forms: התפארות של השם יתברך שמתפאר בישראל

gloss_en: yom huledet ha-melekh / yom genusia de-malka — the King's birthday: the 'birth' of Malkhut when the tzaddik reveals God's glorification in Israel

crossroads (parashat derakhim) — the parting/fork of roads from the Talmudic parable (Sotah 21a), interpreted as the point where the Torah scholar separates out for the penitent his own path according to his soul-root through verbal confession

canonical_he: כשמרצה למסר נפשו על קדוש השם
gloss_en: being willing (fully consenting) to surrender one's life for the sanctification of the Divine Name (mesirut nefesh al kiddush Hashem), as the practice/counsel in Likutey Moharan I:80 linked to Yosef and to peace
forms: כשמרצה למסר נפשו על קדוש השם

gloss_en: the hermeneutic rule 've-eleh mosif' — 'wherever it says ve-eleh it adds' (Exod 21:1 derash), read as the aspect of Yosef (he who adds), guarding the brit/tzitzit

canonical_he: יוצא המלכות מבין הקלפות, ונתבטל ממשלתם
gloss_en: the exodus of Malkhut from among the kelipot and nullification of their dominion — Yom Tov's essential work of raising holy Kingship from the four impure kingdoms
forms: יוצא המלכות מבין הקלפות, ונתבטל ממשלתם

gloss_en: the extraction from one's bones of the sin-letters engraved upon them — through verbal confession the evil letter-combinations of transgressions, inscribed on the bones (Ezekiel 32:27), depart from the bones as they are formed into the words of confession (Likutey Moharan I:4)

canonical_he: שבהעברה בעלמא, יכול להעביר העולם מנגד עיניו
gloss_en: the tzaddik's ability, with a mere passing gesture, to remove 'the world' (this-worldly obstruction) from before one's eyes — clearing the small earth that blocks the righteous' sunlight
forms: שבהעברה בעלמא, יכול להעביר העולם מנגד עיניו

gloss_en: yichud between sun and moon — the unification of chamah and levanah (Moshe's face = sun / Yehoshua = moon), upper and lower points, throne imagery of Ps 89
attaching one's thought to Alma de-Atei (the World to Come) — the constant remembrance-practice that effects the unification 'Hashem Elokai' and guards against death of the heart
tzedakah flowing from giver to receiver — the charitable bestowal that effects the yichud of Tzaddik and Knesset Yisrael (curtain bestowing upon the Ark)
revival / resurrection (techiyah) — the noun for restoring life, as in the revival of the dead (techiyat ha-metim); not the verb form תִּחְיֶה ('you/she shall live')

Yichuda Ila'ah — the Supernal Unification (Aramaic kabbalistic term from the Zohar): the higher divine unification, associated in Likutey Moharan 11 with Kabbalah, the union of Shabbat, the supernal covenant, and the name Shaddai — as opposed to Yichuda Tata'ah, the Lower Unification

canonical_he: מי שהוא שומר הברית, שזווגו משבת לשבת
gloss_en: the covenant-guarder whose marital union is from Shabbat to Shabbat — the higher grade of shemirat ha-brit, embodying Yichuda Ila'ah (the Supernal Unification)
forms: מי שהוא שומר הברית, שזווגו משבת לשבת

gloss_en: Shaddai of Shabbat — the divine Name Shaddai as 'He who said to His world dai (enough),' self-contraction from all labors, aspect of Yichuda Ila'ah

Yichuda Tata'ah — the kabbalistic "Lower Unification" (Aramaic: יחודא תתאה), the lower mode of divine union associated in Likutey Moharan 11 with weekday union (zivug shel chol), God's governance during the six weekdays, Metatron, Halakhah, and "razin" — paired with and contrasted to Yichuda Ila'ah (the Supernal Unification)
desha'im — the grasses (of Creation/Ps 104), symbol of the six weekdays under Metatron's dominion, the aspect of Yichuda Tata'ah (the Lower Unification)
ziz — the Ziz Sadai, the mythical giant bird of Psalms 50:11 read by Rav Ashi as symbolizing the Lower Unification (yichuda tata'ah) paired with the Supernal Unification
the root of the birthright — the supernal source of firstborn status (bekhorah), identified in Likutey Moharan 41 with Binah and with the wine that brings joy (not bikkurah, an early-ripening fig)
the joy-bringing wine (yayin ha-mesameach) — wine that gladdens, a kabbalistic aspect of Binah and the root of the Gevurot/birthright blessing (as in the wine Yaakov brought Yitzchak)
shoresh ha-gevurot — the kabbalistic 'root of the Gevurot' (severities), identified with the joy-bringing wine that Yaakov drew down to sweeten judgment ('and he brought him wine and he drank')

bitul kol hargeshotav ve-chomriyutav — the state of nullifying all one's senses and physicality, required (as with Moshe's 'erase me') so that praise even from a great king breeds no self-aggrandizement

attaining shlemut ha-da'at — the capacity to reach perfected/complete da'at (expanded consciousness), via the three things that broaden a man's mind: a fitting wife (matter), dwelling (yirah), and vessels (Berakhot 57b)

the fitness to build a house — being permitted to engage in building without harm ('whoever builds becomes impoverished,' Sotah 11a) because one builds with wisdom, per 'through wisdom a house is built' (Prov 24:3)
the ability to speak words in holiness and purity — speech empowered by peace (shalom) that joins the opposites Chasadim (Havayah) and Gevurot (Elokim)

canonical_he: יכול להבין ולתפס דבורו של הצדיק
gloss_en: the capacity to understand and grasp the tzaddik's speech — attained only after properly rectifying the sign of the holy covenant (brit), since Yesod ascends to Abba/Imma (Chokhmah-Binah, Yod-Heh mochin)
forms: יכול להבין ולתפס דבורו של הצדיק

gloss_en: the mitzvot — the divine commandments of the Torah, the religious precepts performed by a Jew (as in הַמִּצְווֹת, the commandments one fulfills, ideally with joy), not any other sense of the root צ-ו-ה
simchat ha-mitzvot — the joy in performing the commandments, through which (with yirah) one can discern whether a heavenly decree has been sealed (Rabbah bar bar Chana's ship-and-arrow allegory)

the action of pacing to and fro within one's house — Elisha's walking 'once this way and once that way' (II Kings 4:35), likened to the lung's wings fanning the heart, an act with power to revive the dead
yakhol lehachayot metim — the power to resurrect/revive the dead, achieved through pacing back and forth like Elisha reviving the Shunamite's son (II Kings 4)

canonical_he: כשעיניו מאירות וצופות, בבחינות שדה צופים
gloss_en: the state of the field-master's eyes shining and watching — the tzaddik's illuminated vision when souls do God's will, the aspect of 'Sedeh Tzofim,' the field of watchers/seers (Numbers 23:14)
forms: כשעיניו מאירות וצופות, בבחינות שדה צופים

gloss_en: the ability to pray with a clear, lucid intellect (sekhel tzach) — praying with purified, unclouded mental clarity, attained (in Likutey Moharan I:93) through conducting business dealings in faithfulness
the qualification to pray before the amud — fitness to serve as sheliach tzibbur (prayer leader), earned by gathering the good points in every Jew, even Jewish sinners, into melodies

tasting sweetness in prayer — the capacity to sense sweetness in the words of tefillah, the aspect of 'all my bones shall say' (Ps 35:10), lost by one who blemishes the brit (whose prayer the 'dog' devours)
one who enters into the joy — the person who, entering the joy of the mitzvot, can thereby discern whether a decree is before or after sealing and on which limb of the 'stature' it falls
chokhmah in its proper standing and completeness — wisdom whole and intact, the state of 'one against two,' enabling one to wage God's wars ('wisdom is better than weapons of war,' Eccl 9:18)
waging the wars of Hashem — the capacity to fight God's battles through perfected wisdom rather than weapons, subduing adversaries who pursue the weak of Israel

canonical_he: יכול ללמד לתלמידים חכמתו, ולא יזיק להם.
gloss_en: teaching students without harming them — the ability to transmit one's wisdom safely to disciples, achieved by measuring out one's words with mishpat ('sustains his words with judgment')
forms: יכול ללמד לתלמידים חכמתו, ולא יזיק להם.

gloss_en: the state of having bitachon and giving tzedakah — trust in God ('trust in Hashem and do good,' Ps 37:3) that enables proper charity, which in turn forms perfected speech

turning chirping-sounds into speech — the power to transform inarticulate voice/chirps (tziftzufim) into articulate holy words, effected through tzedakah born of bitachon ('by your mouth — this is charity')

the ability to interpret dreams (pishron chalomot / mefasher chelmin, as Yosef did) — i.e., to decode the letter-combinations that form dreams in deep sleep, an ability granted by perfection of the Holy Tongue (Likutey Moharan I:19)
receiving the holiness of Yom Tov — the capacity to sense festival sanctity, gained through attachment to the tzaddik who is himself the aspect of the festival's holiness

seeing one's own lowliness (leading to complete teshuvah) — the Shabbat-enabled vision of one's shiflut, since ShaBaT = shin (three colors of the eye) + bat (pupil), 'See that God has given you the Shabbat'

canonical_he: יכול לשפך לבו כמים לפני ה
gloss_en: pouring out one's heart like water before Hashem — the nighttime hitbodedut of conversing with one's heart and searching one's spirit ('I recall my melody at night... my spirit searches,' Ps 77)
forms: יכול לשפך לבו כמים לפני ה

gloss_en: the Torah's receiving from Chokhmah Ila'ah — Torah's capacity to draw from Supernal Wisdom ('Torah issues from Chokhmah Ila'ah'), possible only when Torah is complete via the Oral Torah
drawing down the shefa — the capacity to bring down divine abundance, tied to revealing God's Kingship whereby the kelipot are subdued beneath the Shekhinah

canonical_he: יכולים לקרב ולהוכיח את מי שצריכין להוכיח
gloss_en: the ability to draw near and rebuke those needing rebuke — fitness to admonish and bring people close, tied to studying Torah aloud with the mouth (calling the Life of life by name)
forms: יכולים לקרב ולהוכיח את מי שצריכין להוכיח

gloss_en: speaking words in holiness — the power to utter holy speech through shalom, which joins the opposites Chasadim and Gevurot, the aspect of Yosef and mesirat nefesh for kiddush Hashem
bringing our mishpat to light — the power, via emunat chakhamim (faith in the Sages, 'do not deviate right or left'), to issue judgment along the central pillar, the balanced middle path

drawing down the holiness of Eretz Yisrael in exile — the capacity to reveal the Land of Israel's kedushah even under the Sitra Achra in bitter galut ('even also this, in the land of their enemies,' Lev 26:41)
earning money legitimately — the capacity to gain wealth only by traversing and breaking the 140 'voices' of the craving for money, since abundance flows from truth

canonical_he: יכולין לקבל רוח נבואה, רוח הקדש
gloss_en: receiving ruach nevuah / ruach ha-kodesh — the capacity to receive the spirit of prophecy/holy spirit, via the musician's hand separating the good spirit from the melancholy evil spirit (as with Elisha's minstrel)
forms: יכולין לקבל רוח נבואה, רוח הקדש

gloss_en: the charity (tzedakah) of the Land of Israel — charity given to/for Eretz Yisrael, a higher form of tzedakah than that of the diaspora, through which one is included in the air of the Land of Israel (the holy sinless breath); an Aramaic-construct term (tzedakah d'Eretz Yisrael) in Likutey Moharan 37 and 44

being included in the air of Eretz Yisrael — incorporation into the avira de-Eretz Yisrael, the holy sinless breath (like the breath of schoolchildren) through which the patriarchs are revealed and judgment repelled
subduing and casting down all the enemies — the overthrow of all opposing foes (as the 'great mountain' before Zerubavel), 'not by might nor by power but by My spirit' (Zech 4:6-7)
The kabbalistic dictum 'Malkhut is the mouth' (from Patach Eliyahu, Tikkunei Zohar): the sefirah of Malkhut identified with the mouth and faculty of speech (Oral Torah, the Name Adonai)
Yam shel Shlomo — the molten Sea of Solomon in the Temple standing on twelve oxen, symbol of Malkhut/the God-fearing woman resting on the twelve tribes of God (Zohar Vayechi 241)

measures (middot) — delimiting measures/vessels that bound and contain the divine life-force in fixed quantity (as the Torah's letters, words, verses, and sections measure out the life-force from the Life of all life); the quantitative-limit sense of מִדָּה, not character traits, not units of clothing, and not the sefirot as ethical attributes
yamim — 'days' as a symbol for the middot (divine attributes/measures), the vessels bounding the life-force, per 'the measure of my days, what it is' (Ps 39:5)
shefa ruchaniyut — spiritual abundance, the 'right hand' of the Torah ('length of days in her right hand,' Prov 3:16), flowing to the world that is entirely long, the upper worlds
yemina — the kabbalistic Right side (Chesed), Aharon's side in the Korach dispute, unified with the left through hand-clapping
the Torah insofar as it is called 'peace' (shalom, per Proverbs 3:17 'all its paths are peace') — Torah study/engagement as the means to find God equally in good fortune and misfortune (LM I:33)

canonical_he: ימצא השם יתברך בין בטיבו בין בעקו
gloss_en: finding God (Hashem, blessed be He) equally in both good fortune (b'tivu) and adversity (b'aku) — the undivided perception of the Divine in all one's experiences, expressed by 'In the Lord I praise the word, in God I praise the word' (Ps. 56:11), which is the goal attained through Torah and the tzaddikim who are called peace (LM I:33)
forms: ימצא השם יתברך בין בטיבו בין בעקו

canonical_he: צדיקים שנקראו גם כן ברית שלום
gloss_en: the tzaddikim (righteous ones) insofar as they are also called 'brit shalom' (covenant of peace, per Numbers 25:12) — the righteous as embodiments of the covenant of peace, through whom one finds God in both good fortune and adversity (Likutey Moharan I:33)
forms: צדיקים שנקראו גם כן ברית שלום

gloss_en: ve-hatznea — 'and [walk] humbly' (Micah 6:8) read as the sefirah Yesod, the third sukkah-wall of 'even a handbreadth,' which 'reveals a tefach and conceals a tefach'

Yesod (יְסוֹד), the ninth sefirah — the kabbalistic divine attribute of 'Foundation' associated with the tzaddik, covenantal purity, and the principle of concealing/revealing (not the ordinary noun 'foundation of a building' or 'element')
tefach — the handbreadth measure: the sukkah's minimal third wall (Sukkah 6b) symbolizing Yesod, which 'reveals a handbreadth and conceals a handbreadth'
melichut — saltiness, the quality that causes thirst, identified with yissurin/sufferings ('a covenant is said of salt and a covenant is said of sufferings,' Berakhot 5a)
yissurin — sufferings/afflictions as a covenantal category likened to salt (Berakhot 5a), whose felt burning is the soul's thirst, cooled by Torah innovations
yasir mimenu orlat lev — the removal of the 'foreskin of the heart' (spiritual blockage), effected by wisdom-speech awakening the heart
yasir me'alav kol ha-pechadim — the removal of all fears from oneself, achieved by self-judgment (mishpat) of one's affairs

the lung (rei'ah) — the anatomical breathing organ with its five lobes (kanfei rei'ah), which cools the heart's heat, draws moisture/fat to sustain the body and mind, and whose breath is treated as a spiritual archetype; NOT the verb ra'ah 'to see'
dibburei emet — words/utterances of truth issuing from the tzaddik's thanksgiving, identified with Yaakov and the sefirah Tiferet
temimei darekh — 'the wholesome of way' (Ps. 119:1), epithet for those who gaze upon the inner intellect, linked to Yaakov ish tam

the spiritual practice of gazing upon (contemplating) the divine intellect (sekhel) that inheres in every thing, whereby the sekhel illuminates one's way and draws one close to God (Likutey Moharan I:1)
attaining an ever-greater comprehension (hasagah yeteirah) of Divinity — each new level of perception in the World to Come
doing teshuvah upon one's previous comprehension — repenting of the earlier, now-inadequate perception of God after attaining a higher one

"let your voice strike your skull" — the practice in Likutey Moharan 5 of praying with full force so that the voice of prayer reverberates against one's skull, thereby generating the aspect of thunder (ra'am) that straightens the crookedness of the heart

cloud (עָנָן) — the meteorological/theophanic cloud mass, as in the cloud of divine glory and the rain-bearing cloud; symbolically the aspect of Yitzchak (darkness/dimmed sight) and of a garment ('He made the cloud its garment'); not the personal name Anan and not עוֹנֵן/מְעוֹנֵן (to practice soothsaying)
Yitzchak and Yishmael, Yaakov and Esav — the four descendants of Avraham corresponding to the Haggadah's Four Sons and the four kingdoms in holiness
middat ha-din — the divine attribute of strict judgment, here identified as the root/aspect of the yetzer hara
gala — the 'wave' in Rabbah bar bar Chanah's ship tale (Bava Batra 73a), symbol of the yetzer hara that seeks to sink Israel's worth

"poor and wise" (misken ve-chakham) — the poor but wise youth of Ecclesiastes 4:13, applied as an epithet of the good inclination (yetzer tov) and of Malkhut, which is destitute of its own and receives all from Chokhmah

the good inclination (yetzer tov) — the innate human impulse toward good, counterpart of the evil inclination; in Likutey Moharan 1 identified with the 'poor and wise' one of Ecclesiastes 4:13 and the aspect of Malkhut, which has nothing of its own save what it receives from Chokhmah
yerei Elokim — 'God-fearer,' the fear-of-God quality defining Malkhut of holiness (as opposed to Malkhut of the Sitra Achra)

the 'remembrance' (pekidah) of barren women — God's remembering/visiting of the barren so that they conceive and bear children (as with Sarah), the opening of closed wombs, used in Likutey Moharan 60 as the paradigm of procreation drawn down through awakening people from spiritual sleep and telling stories
damim u-gevurot — the blood and severities (gevurot) released in childbirth, embodying the aspect of yirah (fear)
oznayim — the ears as the organ upon which yirah (fear of God) depends ('fear hangs on the ears,' Tikkun 70), enabling perfected holy speech
ba-keseh — 'at the covered/appointed time' (Ps. 81:4), expounded as kisse/concealment: hidden fear-of-God given over to the heart, root of glory
contemplation by the intellect of God's greatness and exaltedness — the higher fear (yirat ha-romemut) arising from knowing He is great and sovereign
the 'first' (higher) fear — yirah stemming directly from God's greatness and exaltedness, above fear reached via lower frights
tzaddikei ha-dor — the righteous leaders of the generation, sole conduits through whom fear and love of God are received

fear and love (yirah va'ahavah) — the paired devotional emotions of awe/reverence of God and love of God, received via the tzaddik and corresponding to fire and water (the two components of 'shamayim,' heavens)

the downward chaining (hishtalshelut) of the Divine severities (gevurot) — the degeneration of holy Gevurah as it descends through the worlds into coarsened form, identified in LM 1:5 with the 'dross of gold' (suspita de-dahava) and manifesting as external fear (fear of things other than God) that blocks the voice in the stopped-up intellect

external fear (yirah chitzonit) — fallen, degraded fear directed at things other than God, arising from the downward chaining of the gevurot and identified with the 'dross of gold' (suspita de-dahava), which blocks the voice within the stopped-up intellect (as opposed to true fear of Heaven)
fear ascending out of the kelipah and the nations — yirah fallen into lowly frights (beasts, officials) being raised back to holy fear via self-judgment
shiflut — lowliness, making oneself like dust (afar), whose 'drawing power' attracts Godliness; why God desired Israel's self-diminishment
pogmin b'Malkhut — blemishing the sefirah of Malkhut, the sin that empowers Peor/Sitra Achra to 'open its mouth'

canonical_he: יש לו כח לפער פיו בצרופים רעים
gloss_en: Peor's power to open its mouth with evil letter-combinations (tzerufim ra'im) — the Sitra Achra's corrupt speech enabled by blemished Malkhut
forms: יש לו כח לפער פיו בצרופים רעים

gloss_en: peace below (shalom l'matah) — the state following revelation of the Covenant of Peace after breaking the orlah, which arouses peace above
yeshut v'taharah — 'existence and purity,' the post-Creation state symbolized by pure marble (shayish tahor) in the Pardes account
completing and erecting the structure of prayer — the tzaddikim of each generation raising seemingly unanswered prayers and building the full stature (like Moshe erecting the Mishkan)
avodat ha-Torah — the service of Torah study, ranked above commerce; the 'Yissachar in your tents' vocation
'Yissachar b'ohalekha' — the blessing-phrase (cf. Deut. 33:18) denoting Yissachar the tent-dwelling Torah scholar, counterpart to Zevulun's commerce

The counsel to ensure that the utterances (dibburim, spoken words — not devorim, bees) leave one's mouth in truth, i.e., speaking truthfully so that God will yearn to dwell with the speaker (Likutey Moharan I:9)
God's yearning from above to dwell with you — the Holy One's desire, drawn solely to truth, to make His dwelling with the truthful person (the ark's 'amah from above')
the nullification of the kelipot (husks of impurity) — their annihilation through joy, as in Israel's future joyous exodus from exile
subduing one's animality (behemiyut) — 'plowing' the beast-nature ('your field for your cattle'), which reveals the totality of the supernal colors

the revelation of the Patriarchs (Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob) in the world — the manifestation of the Avot to dispel judgment, darkness, forgetfulness, and foolishness (per Lev. 26:42, 'I will remember My covenant with Jacob'), as expounded in Likutey Moharan I:37
removal of the clouds covering the eye — dispelling the anannin (alien thoughts in prayer) that blind the eye of judgment, restoring Ein Mishpat
yit'aved ra'am — the 'thunder is made' (Zoharic idiom): the purifying thunder produced by the quarrels among true tzaddikim that expels the Other Side

the straightening-out (removal) of the crookedness in your heart — the phrase from Likutey Moharan I:5 (based on Berakhot 59a on thunder), denoting that the heart's twisted, insincere bends are smoothed away so it can rejoice and receive Torah
studying Shas — the counsel (eitza) of learning the Talmud/Gemara (the Oral Torah, comprising the sixty tractates), especially at night, as a rectification

rectifying the six rings (shit izka'in, Zoharic Aramaic) of the windpipe (kaneh/trachea) — the tikkun of the six cartilage rings of the throat from which voice and melody issue, achieved through nightly study of Oral Torah (Gemara), enabling one to hear melody from any person (Likutey Moharan I:3)
Eretz Kena'an — the Land of Canaan expounded as 'ka'an ani' (here is a pauper), the state of poverty caused by machloket (strife)

"here is a poor person" (ka'an ani) — the Talmudic wordplay (Pesachim 50a) reading Canaan/Kena'ani as kan + ani, denoting poverty/loss of livelihood, applied by Rabbi Nachman to the state caused by dispute (Land of Canaan = presence of a pauper)
Kena'an — the name Canaan itself as wordplay 'ka'an ani' (here is a poor man), signifying poverty from dispute (per Pesachim 50a)
Edom — the nation/kingdom of Esau ('who comes from Edom'), identified with the liver (kaved), seat of anger and blood
kaved — the liver, bodily organ of blood and anger corresponding to Edom/Esau, subdued through fasting or Shabbat eating
shultanei rugzin — the Zoharic 'rulers of wrath' (Terumah 135b), wrathful powers embodying the angry liver that flee on Shabbat
kaved ko'es — 'the liver is angry' (physiological dictum): the liver as seat of anger, whose power is nullified by holy Shabbat eating

the crown of kingship (keter malkhut) — the royal crown, drawn from the Talmudic teaching (Yoma 72b with Rashi) that a person's table corresponds to the crown of Malkhut, linked to honor/glory ('the King of glory')
kevod El — 'the glory of God' (Ps. 19:2) as an epithet for prayer ('render glory His praise'), the vessel into which Torah-letters/souls are enclothed

the glory/honor of God (kevod Elokim) — Divine glory as opposed to human or royal honor; the concealed honor belonging to God (per Proverbs 25:2), identified in Likutey Moharan with Malkhut, the 'King of Glory,' which one merits by fleeing personal honor
zevichat ha-yetzer hara — the 'slaughtering' of the evil inclination, accomplished by silence (dom) under insult, God felling its 'corpses'
kavod Eloki — Divine honor/glory (as opposed to one's own honor), attained by staying silent under disgrace and not defending personal honor

canonical_he: על־ידי שמירת הברית בשני הבחינות הנ"ל
gloss_en: shemirat ha-brit in its two aspects — guarding the covenant (sexual purity) in both its higher and lower modes, the means of sustaining 'the glory of God forever'
forms: על־ידי שמירת הברית בשני הבחינות הנ"ל

gloss_en: guarding the covenant (shmirat ha-brit) in both of its two aspects — the Supernal Unification (yichuda ila'ah) and the Lower Unification (yichuda tata'ah), i.e., Shabbat/weekday union, trees/grasses, Kabbalah/Halakhah — the dual sexual-covenantal purity practice in Likutey Moharan I:11 that brings God's honor to completeness

The perfected/complete state of God's honor (kavod Hashem yitbarakh bi-shleimut) — the condition in which the divine glory attains wholeness, achieved (in LM I:11) through guarding the covenant in both unifications and through utterly distancing oneself from arrogance, which in turn enables the illuminating speech
shye'yitrachaku me-hagadlut ad katzeh acharon — the required action of distancing oneself from arrogance/self-aggrandizement to the utmost extreme, precondition for returning to the Land of Israel
kavod nitgaleh — the state of divine glory becoming revealed, effected through Torah wisdom that rectifies and restores the soul to its root
teshuvah al teshuvato — the second, higher repentance done upon one's first repentance after attaining greater perception of God's exaltedness; corresponds to the honor of the World to Come
kevod olam hazeh — the honor of this world, the level corresponding to first/initial repentance (as opposed to World-to-Come honor of the second teshuvah)
kevodo nit'aleh — the state of God's glory being elevated, accomplished through Torah acquired via humility, in proportion to one's breaking of pride (Mount Tabor teaching)

canonical_he: לפנות את המחין מחכמות חיצוניות וממחשבות זרות
gloss_en: clearing the mochin (mental faculties) of external/secular wisdoms and foreign thoughts — the 'chametz-removal' of the mind required so the voice striking the brain produces thunder
forms: לפנות את המחין מחכמות חיצוניות וממחשבות זרות

canonical_he: מצותא ומריבה שיש בין הצדיקים השלמים
gloss_en: the quarrel and strife (matzuta u-merivah) among the perfect tzaddikim — disputes between righteous ones that one must believe serve only holy purposes
forms: מצותא ומריבה שיש בין הצדיקים השלמים

gloss_en: the purpose of tzaddikim's quarrels: to drive away the sitrin achranin (the Other Sides, forces of impurity)

canonical_he: גבורות בחינת רעמים, צריך לשתף עמהם אהבה
gloss_en: the requirement to join love (ahavah/chesed) with the gevurot that are the aspect of thunders — combining left in right so thunder-voice is produced
forms: גבורות בחינת רעמים, צריך לשתף עמהם אהבה

gloss_en: striking the glory (kavod) — the aspect of wisdom (chokhmah): the goal that the gevurot/thunders, once joined with love, impact 'glory' (identified with chokhmah per Prov. 3:35) so that thunder is produced (Likutey Moharan I:5)
the requirement to combine love (ahavah) with fear/awe (yirah) — pairing right-side chesed with left-side gevurah in divine service
the goal 'so that thunders (re'amim) be produced' — thunder as the outcome of joining love with fear, the voice striking the purified brain
the teaching that the quarrel among tzaddikim exists 'only for your sake' — as a personal rebuke for one's damaged brain-drops (seminal blemish)

potential (koach) — the latent, not-yet-actualized state of a thing, paired with and opposed to po'al (the actual/actualized), as in bringing something 'from potential to actual'; the initial thought before the deed
ruach dil'ela — the 'spirit above,' the upper of the two spirits corresponding to koach (potential) as against the lower spirit of actuality
techilat ha-machashavah — the initial thought preceding a deed ('end of action in thought first'), the aspect of potential (koach) before actualization

the power/faculty of speech (koach ha-dibbur) — the human capacity for articulate verbal expression, rooted in the mouth and its five articulation points, which distinguishes humans from mute beasts and is drawn from the aspect of the Tzaddik
receiving 'this power' from Edom — appropriating from Edom the coercive force needed (to punish the wicked) in order to reach the Land of Israel
the power to punish the wicked (with sword and slaughter) — the coercive force for subduing the slanderers of the Land who prolong exile

kelipot — the 'husks' or shells of impurity in Kabbalah: parasitic forces of evil that surround and conceal holiness the way a peel surrounds a fruit, deriving vitality from it while being superfluous to it
chalom — the dream as manifestation of the koach ha-medammeh (imaginative faculty), which seeks to rest upon one who reviews halakhot

the Mishkan — the wilderness Tabernacle (מִשְׁכָּן) erected by Moses, treated in Likutey Moharan I:70 as the aspect of the 'drawing force' (koach ha-moshech) that draws down Godliness, homiletically linked to מָשַׁךְ (to draw) and שָׁכַן (to dwell)

the drawing/attracting force (koach ha-moshech) — the gravitational-like power of earth/dust that pulls things toward itself, which in Likutey Moharan I:70 is the aspect of the humble tzaddik (Moses, dust) and of the Mishkan, drawing down Godliness
chakhmei ha-dor — the Sages of the generation, sole authorized interpreters of Torah via the thirteen hermeneutical principles
the healing power received from the Torah — Torah's remedy 'to all his flesh,' accessible only through the generation's Sages who expound it

the power/force of prayer (koach ha-tefillah) — praying with bodily force so that "all my bones shall say" (Ps. 35:10), the physical energy invested in the words of prayer, corresponding to the 28 letters of the Act of Creation (LM I:48)
the state in which all souls yearn to be included in his soul — the magnetism of one who guards his soul/name from anger and enlarges the wall of wealth
kol ha-kolot dikdushah — all the holy voices/sounds, identified with azut dikdushah (holy boldness)
azei panim — the brazen-faced ones of the generation who seize fallen honor (kingship without a crown) when eating-lust blemishes Malkhut
kelavim azei nefesh — 'greedy-souled dogs' (Isaiah 56:11), the dog-image of the brazen-faced ('face of the generation like the face of a dog,' Sotah 49b)
kulo echad — 'entirely one,' the total unity that is the aspect of emet (truth), opposite of falsehood which stems from distance from Oneness

"one eyeball" (chad galgala de-eina) — the Zoharic/Idra Aramaic phrase for the single orb of the eye of the Holy Ancient One, identified with the future "one eye of mercy" (eina chad de-rachamei) of undivided compassion, cited in LM 1:4 as the aspect of "kulo haTov vehaMeitiv"
kulo ha-tov ve-hameitiv — the future state when all blessing will be 'Who is good and does good,' identified with the single eye of mercy (eina chad de-rachamei) of the Idra
kulo tov — 'entirely good,' the ultimate purpose (tachlit) of Oneness, per 'on that day Hashem will be one' (Zechariah 14:9; Pesachim 50a)
klei holadah — the organs/vessels of procreation, linked to shevarim and to trust ('Shall I bring to the breaking-point and not give birth?' Isaiah 66:9)

the weaponry of Mashiach (kelei zeino shel Mashiach) — the Messiah's armament, which is essentially prayer (identified with the nose/breath and the guarded covenant), by which he wages all his battles and conquests
kelayot — the kidneys as bodily organs, counted as the vessels of procreation and the seat of bitachon (trust)

the attribute (middah) of Tiferet — the sefirah of harmonizing beauty/splendor identified with Yaakov and truth, which comprises the totality of the colors (kelalut ha-gevanin) and unites fire and water (heavens)
kelalut ha-gevanin — the totality/inclusion of all the colors, defining the sefirah Tiferet (attribute of Yaakov/emet)

spirit/wind (ruach, Aramaic rucha) — the vital breath or animating spirit-force: the life-breath blown into the nostrils, the wind of the lungs that cools the heart, the spirit residing in the tzaddik ('a man in whom there is spirit'); distinct from revach (profit/space) which shares the letters רוח
the chasadim within the body/torso — kindnesses clothed in all the middot, the embodied loves comprising the totality of the traits
kelaliut ha-middot — the all-inclusiveness of the character traits, in each of which chesed/love is clothed
kelaliut ha-kedushah — the totality of holiness, the supra-natural providential state attained via the Land of Israel which contains all ten holinesses
kelaliut shivah ro'im — the collectivity of the Seven Shepherds (Abraham through David), embodied in the true tzaddikim
the power and fervor of the beginning — the initial burst of enthusiasm ('all beginnings are hard') that sets the measure of one's ongoing service
the principle that one's ongoing conduct in divine service proceeds according to [his beginning] — each visit to the tzaddik must therefore be made totally anew
corresponding to the four kingdoms-in-holiness (arba malkhuyot shebikdushah) — the holy counterparts of the four exiles, mapped onto the Haggadah's four sons
Canaan eved avadim — 'Canaan, slave of slaves' (Genesis 9:25), epithet of the serpent whose banishment on Motzaei Shabbat (Eliyahu's revelation) repels the slaves' sleep
hitlabshut — enclothement/garbing, identified with 'kanaf' (wing/covering), per 'your Teacher shall no longer be covered (yikanef)' (Isaiah 30:20)
wing (kanaf) — the wing/garment-corner as a covering that conceals, linked via Isaiah 30:20 've-lo yikanef od morekha' to the aspects of enclothement (hitlabshut) and the Throne
kenafayim — the 'wings' aroused by clapping hands in prayer, the source from which speech issues ('a winged creature shall tell the matter,' Ecclesiastes 10:20)
throne (kisei) — the Divine Throne of Glory (Kisei HaKavod), the seat of God's manifest kingship as in Ezekiel's vision ('above the firmament the likeness of a throne'); not any homograph of כסה/כוס
kisei kavod — the Throne of Glory, symbolized by the circular letter samekh (numerical 60), linked to 'sixty queens' and nullification of the forbidden in sixty
gevanin ila'in — the 'supernal colors/hues' (Zoharic Aramaic term for the upper sefirotic lights), here identified with silver and gold
kesef ve-zahav — silver and gold as a paired symbol: the physical embodiment of the supernal colors/hues resting on money
ra'ah — 'the evil' unleashed from the north (Jeremiah 1:14), identified as anger (ka'as) descending from the Gevurot, twin of money/gold

anger/wrath (ka'as) — the emotion of rage; in lm1:68 human anger rooted in Gevurot sharing a source with money ("from the north"), and in lm1:18 God's anger (kaʿaso) expressed as concealment of the Divine face
hastarat penei Hashem — the concealment of God's face caused by Israel's lack of faith/heresy, itself an expression of divine anger and wrath
kefirah ba-avodah zarah — the denial/repudiation of idolatry, the trait embodied by Mordecai the 'ish Yehudi' (whoever denies idols is called a Yehudi)

the birds of the kelipah — impure spiritual forces ('birds' dwelling in the husk of impurity) that suckle from the breasts of Malkhut and constitute the mental faculties (mochin) of the Malkhut of the kelipah; the source from which a wicked musician draws his melody (Likutey Moharan I:3, after the Zohar and the Arizal)
the principle 'when it (truth) dwells with you, He will illuminate you' — divine light dwells and shines according to the measure of one's truth, since God is the essence of truth

burnt-offering (olah) — the sacrificial offering wholly consumed on the altar, interpreted in LM I:108 as the aspect of a broken spirit (not the feminine participle 'ascending' עוֹלָה, nor עַוְלָה 'injustice')
hamtakat ha-charon af — the sweetening/mitigation of divine wrath, effected via 'potei'ach et yadekha' whose final letters spell ChaTaKh (= twice ruach), distinguishing right hand from left

canonical_he: כשר ופסול טמא וטהור אסור ומתר
gloss_en: kasher/pasul, tamei/tahor, asur/mutar — the six paired halakhic categories (fit/unfit, impure/pure, forbidden/permitted) comprising the six orders of Mishnah, corresponding to the six weekdays and Metatron
forms: כשר ופסול טמא וטהור אסור ומתר

canonical_he: לסתם את עיניו, ולכון ההסתכלות אל התכלית
gloss_en: the act of shutting one's eyes and aiming one's gaze at the ultimate purpose (tachlit) — contracting physical sight amid suffering so as to focus on the distant final goal
forms: לסתם את עיניו, ולכון ההסתכלות אל התכלית

gloss_en: the practice of binding and elevating speech to its root (Imma/supernal Mother) — 'chariots of Pharaoh' read as tefillin-lights revealed from Imma
learning Torah with another person — the act of teaching a fellow, classed as 'writing' since the tongue engraves words on the student's heart
ketivah — writing as a category of Torah transmission: the tongue as 'the pen of a ready scribe' inscribing teaching on the tablet of the student's heart
the letter kaf — the alphabet letter symbolizing Keter (Crown), the inner soul-dimension linked to the Shekhinah as nefesh
'that which orders and settles the intellect' — the faculty of arranging/composing the mind, identified as Keter (from kattar, 'to wait'), blessed by the inner dimension of the blessings

the upper dot of the letter Alef (the yod-point above the diagonal vav in the letter's form), symbolizing in Likutey Moharan I:6 the concealed supernal throne / Keter, identified with the sun, Moshe, and the higher level of teshuvah
seyag — the 'fence' around wisdom ('a fence for wisdom is silence'), identified as Keter, the encircling crown formed out of silence that surrounds Chokhmah

a person's table (shulchano shel adam) — the rabbinic phrase for one's dining table as a locus of spiritual significance, likened to the altar and to the crown of kingship (cf. Chagigah 27a, Yoma 72b)
shufra di-shufra — 'the beauty of beauty' (Zoharic term): the choicest illumination from the 32 (lamed-bet=lev) Elokim of Creation that nourishes and names the heart
the Mishkan (Tabernacle) in its built state — corresponding to the 39 (lamed-tet/'tal') lights merited by guarding the brit
lamed-tet orot — the thirty-nine ('tal', dew) lights, the illuminations preserved by one who guards the covenant (opposite of the 39 labors/lashes)
the Mishkan (Tabernacle) in its destroyed state — corresponding to the 39 lashes (malkot), the punitive counterpart to the 39 lights (Tikkun 48)
the counterfactual state 'had your brain(-drops) not been blemished' — i.e., if one's seminal/mind drops were intact, referring to pegam ha-brit in the mind

canonical_he: לא היה נשמע לך מריבות שבין הצדיקים
gloss_en: the consequence 'you would not hear the quarrels between the tzaddikim' — hearing tzaddikim's disputes is a rebuke signaling one's own blemished mind-drops
forms: לא היה נשמע לך מריבות שבין הצדיקים

gloss_en: the state of having no distress on the road — safety in travel, contingent on shemirat ha-brit ('all roads are presumed dangerous'; hence visiting one's wife before a journey)

canonical_he: לא יחסר כל טוב, ויהיה כלו טוב
gloss_en: the future messianic state 'no good will be lacking and all will be entirely good' — the era of 'ha-tov ve-ha-meitiv' when increased Da'at brings eternal life
forms: לא יחסר כל טוב, ויהיה כלו טוב

gloss_en: 'lo yitama' — the priestly prohibition against defiling oneself for a corpse (Lev 21), read as guarding the brit from sexual impurity, root of tum'ah
'lo avado' — 'one who does not serve Him' (Malachi 3:18), the type among the four who entered Pardes who ascends beyond his level and is stricken (Ben Azzai's hetzitz ve-nifga)
the alephs in holiness — the holy aleph-letters identified with Leah, which when fallen become the opponents' weariness (hal'ot) and scorn of God-fearers

Leah — the matriarch, wife of Yaakov, understood kabbalistically as the partzuf Leah: the concealed feminine (alma d'itkasya, the hidden world), positioned at the back of the head/neck (oref), the 'first nukva,' associated with the heart and the sweetening of harsh judgments (not the verb לָאָה 'to be weary,' though wordplay with lo'eh occurs)
korban olah — the burnt offering, which is in the aspect of Leah; the daily olat tamid sweetens her judgments against the impure 'worm' of the kelipah

the heart (lev) — the inner organ as the spiritual seat of emotion, intention, memory, and devotion; the inner 'tablet' and hidden chamber of the person (and, cosmically, the supernal Heart), on which Torah is inscribed and from which prayer, joy, and warm speech flow
the Concealed World (alma d'itkasya) — the Zoharic Aramaic term for the hidden, covered supernal world (associated with Leah/Binah), as opposed to alma d'itgalya, the revealed world
the act of swiftly expelling the ruach shetut (spirit of folly) from within oneself — accomplished by binding oneself in soul-love to the true tzaddik
lev nishbar — the broken heart: the heart's contrite state connected with expelling the spirit of folly and being incorporated into the tzaddik's heart

canonical_he: לבוא לאלו הרועים, שהם כלליות של הקדשה
gloss_en: coming/gaining access to the true shepherds (ro'im) who are the collectivity (kelaliyut) of holiness — attainable only through holy boldness (azut, 'bold as a leopard')
forms: לבוא לאלו הרועים, שהם כלליות של הקדשה

gloss_en: hitkarvut la-tzaddikim — drawing close to the tzaddikim and following the path of their counsel, whereby their advice engraves truth (emet) in a person
coming/arriving at truth (emet) — the attainment of truth itself, possible only via closeness to tzaddikim and receiving their counsel (a union/zivug)

canonical_he: תורה שמאירין להם אל מקום שהם שם
gloss_en: the Torah that shines to people in the very place where they are — Torah-light reaching sinners and converts 'chutzah' (outward), via its 600,000 letters matching the 600,000 souls, to awaken teshuvah
forms: תורה שמאירין להם אל מקום שהם שם

gloss_en: hitbodedut — the Breslov practice of secluded personal prayer: setting aside time alone (in a room or field) to pour out one's speech before God in one's own words, in supplication and conversation with the Creator
coming to bittul — attaining self-nullification (nullifying desires, bad traits, and corporeality to be included in one's root), possible only through hitbodedut
attaining mochin zakkim — pure, clarified mental faculties (holiness/purity of thought), the prerequisite for sweetening judgments, sought by traveling to tzaddikim for Rosh HaShanah

garments, clothings (Aramaic plural of levush) — the 'garments' in which spiritual light or the Divine face is clothed/veiled, associated with tzedek (righteousness) as in 'tzedek lavashti' (I clothed myself in righteousness)
nullifying the body entirely — speaking Torah and prayer until the body becomes naught and one flesh with the speech ('ve-hayu le-vasar echad')

canonical_he: מתבודד ומפרש שיחתו בינו לבין קונו
gloss_en: hitbodedut practice — secluding oneself and pouring out one's conversation between oneself and one's Creator, the means to bittul
forms: מתבודד ומפרש שיחתו בינו לבין קונו

gloss_en: the counsel (eitza) of speaking abundantly in words of Torah study and prayer — converting one's blood/vitality into holy speech so as to nullify contentiousness and attain peace (Likutey Moharan I:75)

canonical_he: לבטל מדת הנצחון והמחלקת, ולרדף אחר השלום
gloss_en: nullifying the trait of nitzachon (contentiousness/winning) and machloket (dispute) and pursuing peace — the obligatory eradication of the blood-rooted urge to conquer
forms: לבטל מדת הנצחון והמחלקת, ולרדף אחר השלום

gloss_en: the student/disciple (talmid) — the receiver of teaching from his master (rav), who like the moon receiving the sun's light embodies Lower Wisdom receiving from Upper Wisdom

the Wicked Kingdom (Malkhut ha-Resha'ah) — the demonic counter-Malkhut of the Sitra Achra (the Other Side), the evil parallel to the holy Kingship; identified with the moon of the Other Side, the evil inclination as the 'old foolish king' that rejects wisdom, and the spleen/black bile
levanah de-sitra achra — the 'moon of the Other Side': the demonic counterpart-moon of the wicked kingdom (malkhut ha-resha'ah), of which it says 'the moon will be ashamed' (Isaiah 24)
banim — children/offspring: the merit of begetting sons, attained only through complete da'at (a minor cannot beget, lacking full da'at), as Abraham merited via making converts

legalot ha-hastarot — the devotional act of revealing/uncovering the divine concealments (hastarot), disclosing God hidden even within concealment-within-concealment, achieved by drawing arikhut yamim/Da'at into Malkhut
gilui — revelation/disclosure as a state, the emergence of the mochin from concealment likened to birth (leidah), opposite of he'lem (hiddenness)

she-tzarikh litz'ok — the required act of crying out (the seventy cries/seven voices of David) in prayer and Torah study to bring the light of the Countenance from concealment to revelation, like the cry of a woman in labor

the perfection/completeness of speech (shlemut ha-dibbur) — the state in which the letters of holy speech are made whole (via faith and the aspect of the World to Come), exemplified by the 'pure language' of Zephaniah 3:9 when all humanity will call upon God's Name

canonical_he: להחיות את עצמו, ולבוא לידי שמחה
gloss_en: lehachayot et atzmo ve-lavo lidei simchah — the practice of enlivening oneself and coming to joy by finding good points in oneself, warding off atzvut (sadness)
forms: להחיות את עצמו, ולבוא לידי שמחה

gloss_en: lihyot ish mofet — becoming a 'man of wonders' (wonder-worker), a status attainable only by one who has broken free of the craving for eating (ta'avat akhilah)

bringing the surrounding lights (makifin) inward — causing the transcendent encompassing intellects/lights, which hover outside the inner human intellect and outside the Torah, to enter and be internalized within the inner intellect (in Likutey Moharan I:21, achieved through sanctifying the seven lamps of the face)
lehakhnia ha-koach ha-medameh — subduing the imaginative faculty (medameh), accomplished through the 'hand'/joy and hand-played musical instruments that enable prophecy ('be-yad ha-nevi'im adameh')

lehakhnia u-levatel kesilut ha-sekhel — the tikkun of subduing and nullifying the foolishness of the intellect, effected through the aspect of the altar (mizbe'ach)/holy eating, cutting off the kelipot's nurture
lehamshikh le-atzmo dibburim chamim ke-gachalei-esh — drawing down for oneself burning words like fiery coals from the Supernal Heart ('Tzur levavi') as prerequisite for drawing Torah explanations
lehamshikh nekudot el ha-otiyot — drawing vowel-points (nekudot) into the letters through desire and yearning (cheshek/kissufin), per 'nekudot ha-kasef' (Song 1:11)

canonical_he: ימלא גרונם, על־ידי רקודין, או על־ידי פדיון
gloss_en: yemale gronam — 'filling the throats' of Torah scholars (Yoma 71a), done via dancing (rikkudin) or a pidyon (redemption payment), the means of pouring wine-libation on the altar
forms: ימלא גרונם, על־ידי רקודין, או על־ידי פדיון

canonical_he: להמתיק הדינים, על־ידי שרשם, שהוא יין המשמח
gloss_en: lehamtik ha-dinim al-yedei shorsham — sweetening the harsh judgments at their root, which is Binah, the 'wine that gladdens' (yayin ha-mesameach)
forms: להמתיק הדינים, על־ידי שרשם, שהוא יין המשמח

gloss_en: lehinatzel mi-tachat memshaltam — being rescued from under the dominion of the shepherds of the Sitra Achra (false famous leaders who coerce people under their subjugation)
she-margishin ta'am metikut be-ha-Torah — the experience of tasting sweetness in Torah study, a sweetening that saves one from the punishment of widowerhood (alman)
lehistakel be-Elokut — gazing upon/contemplating Godliness, attainable only after rectifying the brit ('mi-besari echezeh Eloka'), the goal of tikkun ha-brit

Torah study at night (limmud ha-Torah ba-laylah) — the devotional practice of learning Torah during the nighttime hours, which draws down a thread of kindness (chut shel chesed) and enables elevating speech to its root
leha'alot et ha-dibbur le-shorshah — elevating and binding speech (the 'sea,' yam) back to its supernal root, via the gevurot ('yarah ba-yam') and tefillin
lekasher et tefilato le-tzaddik ha-dor — the practice of binding one's prayer to the tzaddik of the generation (aspect of Moshe-Mashiach), who directs it to its proper gate

canonical_he: להעלות כל תפלה ותפלה לשער השיך
gloss_en: leha'alot kol tefillah la-sha'ar ha-shayakh — the tzaddik's act of elevating each individual prayer to its designated gate among the supernal gates
forms: להעלות כל תפלה ותפלה לשער השיך

gloss_en: leha'alot nitzotzot le-Hashem Yitbarakh — elevating the holy sparks in things one sees to God, by immediately believing with complete faith that letters and sparks inhere in each thing
leha'alot nitzotzei ha-dibbur — elevating the sparks of speech, the tikkun of speech achieved specifically through fasting (ta'anit), which blocks kelipot nursing from behind holiness

raising up fallen faith — the act of restoring emunah (specifically faith in the Sages) after it has collapsed, accomplished in Likutey Moharan I:57 through the aspect of Yaakov, i.e., by making and immediately fulfilling a vow

canonical_he: שבח הצדיקים. כשמשבחין ומפארין את הצדיקים
gloss_en: shevach ha-tzaddikim — praising and glorifying the tzaddikim, the practice ('ka-nesher ya'ir kino') by which Da'at is raised and the mochin roused from slumber
forms: שבח הצדיקים. כשמשבחין ומפארין את הצדיקים

gloss_en: lehakim u-leromem et ha-da'at — establishing and elevating Da'at (the mind/awareness), accomplished through praise of the tzaddikim

canonical_he: להרועים אי אפשר להתקרב כי אם
gloss_en: la-ro'im i efshar lehitkarev ki im — the principle that approach to the holy shepherds (source of emunah) is possible only through azut (holy boldness, 'az ka-namer')
forms: להרועים אי אפשר להתקרב כי אם

canonical_he: להרחיב ולהאריך ימיו בתוספות קדשה בכל פעם
gloss_en: leharchiv u-leha'arikh yamav be-tosefot kedushah — the 'elder' (zaken) aspect: expanding/lengthening one's days with added holiness each day, attained via yirah ('yirat Hashem tosif yamim')
forms: להרחיב ולהאריך ימיו בתוספות קדשה בכל פעם

canonical_he: להשלים את דעתו, שיהא שלם בדעת
gloss_en: lehashlim et da'ato — perfecting/completing one's Da'at so as to be whole in knowledge, the tzaddikim's true motive in drawing others near ('u-mi-talmidai yoter mi-kulam')
forms: להשלים את דעתו, שיהא שלם בדעת

canonical_he: רודפים אחר בני אדם לקרבם לעבודתו יתברך.
