gloss_en: rodfim achar bnei adam lekarvam la-avodato — the tzaddikim's pursuit of people to bring them close to God's service, done for completing da'at not for honor
forms: רודפים אחר בני אדם לקרבם לעבודתו יתברך.

gloss_en: lehashlim da'atam — the tzaddikim's aim of completing the da'at of others (and thereby their own, via students), not increasing their honor

joy of the heart (simchat ha-lev) — inner gladness seated in the heart itself, the heart's rejoicing (as in 'wine gladdens the heart of man'), which requires uprightness of heart and empowers prayer and dance
luchot ha-even — the Tablets of Stone of Sinai, symbol of Chokhmah Ila'ah (supernal Wisdom), linked to the even shetiyah/Holy of Holies
the left (שְׂמֹאל) — the left side/hand as a kabbalistic aspect (the Gevurah side), associated with Levi, purity, and material bounty ('in her left hand riches and honor'), opposed to the right
Levi — the tribe/priestly-levite lineage as symbol of the left side (smol), aspect of purity ('ve-tihart et bnei Levi') from which impurity seeks its hold
lizkot la-kavod ha-zeh — meriting true honor (kavod with the kaf of Keter/Ehyeh), attainable only through teshuvah, chiefly by remaining silent when hearing one's disgrace
she-tishmeru la'asot be-atzmekhem ha-mishpatim — executing judgment upon oneself (self-judgment of one's deeds), which nullifies the judgment from Above

melody and joy (niggun ve-simchah) — the spiritual practice of music/song joined with gladness that sifts the good spirit from the evil spirit, thereby guarding memory of the World to Come (Likutey Moharan I:54)
lizkor atzmo be-olam ha-ba — the constant remembrance of oneself in the World to Come ('ezkerah neginati ba-lailah'), keeping the alma de-atei always in mind
the 'double bread' (lechem mishneh) — the twofold portion of manna/loaves associated with Shabbat (Exodus 16:22), used as a symbol of doubled blessing on Shabbat
yekasher et libo le-da'ato — binding one's heart to one's knowledge (da'at), so the general knowledge that God exists actually governs the heart and its middot
lit'om ta'am or ha-ahavah she-be-da'at — tasting the light of the love contained within Da'at, accessible to each person even now 'within the days' according to his level
mi she-yukhal la'asot niggunim — the one able to fashion the aforementioned melodies (niggunim), who thereby knows which children belong to each tzaddik and all future generations
aniyut u-dechakut — poverty and material hardship/pressure as a condition of distress, aspect of night, the setting for redemptive Torah study
tzar — distress/straits ('ba-tzar la-adam'), the state of affliction identified with night, in which Torah study rectifies speech

the small luminary (ha-ma'or ha-katan) — the lesser light of Genesis 1:16, i.e., the moon that rules the night, serving as the kabbalistic symbol of Malkhut/faith/prayer, the diminished recipient light illuminated by the great luminary (Moses/the tzaddik)
Gemara — the Talmud/Oral Torah as text of study, symbolizing night (vs. Written Torah = day, per the Midrash of Moshe on the mountain)
orev — the raven/crow (pushkantza in the Bava Batra tale), figure for studying Torah in order to be called 'Rabbi' (shelo lishmah)
leilekh be-darkhei ha-teshuvah — walking the paths of repentance, requiring twofold expertise: baki be-ratzo (ascent, 'im esak shamayim') and baki be-shov (descent, 'atzi'ah she'ol')
segulah lehinatzel mi-gadlut — a segulah (efficacious remedy) against arrogance: honoring the festivals and receiving Yom Tov with joy and expansive heart
kavod di-kedushah — holy honor/glory, the sanctified honor attained only through humility, elevated via converts and penitents (as opposed to profane honor)
malakh — 'angel' in the verse, read as symbol of the lamdan (Torah scholar) and the angel Metatron (Mem-Tet), guardian of the lower covenant of Oral Torah study

lamdan — a Torah scholar learned in halakhah, specifically one versed in the laws of forbidden and permitted (issur ve-heter), paired with 'tzaddik' as the second requisite of a rabbi and identified with the angel/Metatron aspect (Likutey Moharan I:31)
the heart's yearning to learn Torah — the burning desire itself, which counts as actual study for one unable to learn (an am ha'aretz, bookless, or in the wilderness)
limmud mitokh ha-sefer — study from within a physical book, the aspect virtually fulfilled by the heart's longing when actual study is impossible
limmudei Hashem — 'those taught of God' (Isaiah 54:13), epithet for children/sons whose souls are saved when justice rescues the oppressed
above time (le-ma'alah me-ha-zeman) — the spiritual state or level that transcends temporality, where time is nullified; attained e.g. through faithful business dealings, thought, or repentance
above nature (le-ma'alah me-ha-teva) — the supernatural realm transcending the natural order, where miracles occur and which prayer accesses by overriding nature's dictates

makifim — the 'encompassing/surrounding lights' (Kabbalistic or makif, plural): transcendent intellect or divine influx too great to enter the brain/inner vessels, which instead surrounds them from outside (e.g., sukkah, chuppah, Atika), as opposed to penimi (inner light)
above human intellect — the supra-rational realm beyond sekhel enoshi, like a segulah-remedy; identified with the makkifin (transcendent encompassing lights)

canonical_he: על־ידי האמירות והדבור של איש הישראלי
gloss_en: the sayings and speech of the Jewish person — Israelite utterance that illuminates the places ('vegetable town') where one must do teshuvah (from the amrei inshei saying)
forms: על־ידי האמירות והדבור של איש הישראלי

gloss_en: bandits/highway robbers (listim, from Greek lēstēs) — armed brigands who waylay travelers; in Likutey Moharan 4 paired with 'wild beast' (chayah ra'ah) as the danger of the road, representing the evil trait of pride arising from the 'speaking' (human) element
shalosh kavin — the three kabbalistic lines/pillars (right-left-center), mapped onto the Talmudic rule to divide one's money in thirds: merchandise, land, and cash in hand (Bava Metzia 42)
simchah ve-chedvah — joy and gladness as the source through which one attains holy boldness (azut di-kedushah), per 'the joy of the Lord is your strength'

"this wealth" (לָעֲשִׁירוּת הַזֹּאת) — the specific spiritual wealth of contemplation (hitbonenut) discussed in Likutey Moharan I:60, attained via the rectifications of Atik, length of days, and the aspect of the elder; not literal monetary riches
machar — 'tomorrow' in Pharaoh's locust warning, symbol of the World to Come, the future day of receiving reward (Eruvin 22a)
le-atid lavo — the eschatological Future to Come, era of receiving reward when the paradox of the Vacated Space (challal ha-panui) will be understood

canonical_he: להמשיך קדשת שבת, לקדש ימי החל
gloss_en: drawing Shabbat's sanctity into the six weekdays — sanctifying the profane days to repair the serpent's 39 curses/labors ('doing your affairs on My holy day')
forms: להמשיך קדשת שבת, לקדש ימי החל

gloss_en: tempering excessive spiritual ardor — the act of contracting (tzimtzum) the heart's burning for God so it not consume the body, via Torah as the lungs' wings fanning the heart
'kol basar yachdav' — the phrase 'all flesh together' (Isaiah 40:5), read as the ingathering of all souls by the wise soul-taker (tzaddik)
gathering of all the souls — the tzaddik's collecting of nefashot, per 'he who takes souls is wise' (Proverbs 11:30), signified by 'all flesh together'

canonical_he: לקרב את הגרים עם בעלי התשובה
gloss_en: drawing converts and ba'alei teshuvah near — the act of bringing gerim and penitents close, possible only through Torah ('let your springs spread outward')
forms: לקרב את הגרים עם בעלי התשובה

gloss_en: beholding the light of the tzaddik — the perception attained when the intellect is perfected via charity, blocked by murky deeds that cloud the mind
witnessing the downfall of the wicked — seeing mappalat resha'im, possible only through the aspect of the Land of Israel/the Right ('sit at My right hand')

canonical_he: שמתיגע בתורה, עד שזוכה לידע אותה ולהבינה
gloss_en: toiling in Torah until one knows and understands it — the laborious study that heals and elevates the soul to its root
forms: שמתיגע בתורה, עד שזוכה לידע אותה ולהבינה

canonical_he: לרפאות נפשו, דהינו להעלותה למקום שרשה
gloss_en: healing one's soul by raising it to its root-place — the soul-cure achieved through exertion in Torah study
forms: לרפאות נפשו, דהינו להעלותה למקום שרשה

gloss_en: ishah chakhamah — 'wise woman' (chokhmot nashim, Proverbs 14:1) as figure for the Holy Spirit/Holy Tongue that the serpent seeks to seduce
shnayim mikra — 'twice Scripture' (the weekly reading practice), midrashically read from 'bekerev shanim' as the Holy Tongue that arouses the power of Creation
lashon shel zehorit — the crimson thread of Yom Kippur (which whitened when sins were forgiven), linked by wordplay to 'zohar ha-rakia' (radiance of the firmament)

deep sleep (tardemah) — the divinely-cast slumber of Genesis 2:21, treated in Likutey Moharan 19 as the aspect of Targum-language and the state in which dreams occur, through which the Holy Tongue is perfected
leshon Targum — the Aramaic translation-language, aspect of tardemah (deep sleep) whose good is elevated to build the Holy Tongue and fell the seventy nations' tongues

the all-inclusive evil (ra ha-kolel) — the comprehensive, general evil that encompasses all particular evils, identified in Likutey Moharan 19 with the blemish of the covenant (pegam ha-brit) and with the seventy languages of the nations
guarding memory (zikaron) — protecting remembrance, seated between the eyes, from falling into the evil eye and death-of-the-heart which breed forgetfulness

canonical_he: לתן כח בהם שיוכלו לילך כראוי
gloss_en: empowering the three 'legs' to walk properly — giving strength via threefold blessing to the legs/supports (faith-truth-Shabbat) so they can stride correctly
forms: לתן כח בהם שיוכלו לילך כראוי

gloss_en: hesped — funeral eulogy, which rectifies the departure of glory caused by a tzaddik's passing; forbidden on Chanukah (Shabbat 21b)

canonical_he: זריזות גדול בעבודתו יתברך, ולרוץ מאד מאד
gloss_en: great zeal (zerizut) in divine service — running exceedingly swiftly on the path, requiring mighty exertion ('rejoices like a strong man to run a course')
forms: זריזות גדול בעבודתו יתברך, ולרוץ מאד מאד

gloss_en: the forty (Mem) days of the embryo's formation (Niddah 30) — gestation period symbolized by the closed final-mem formed from the womb's two dalet-doors
people of great spiritual stature — the 'great ones' (gedolim) as a rank of persons, contrasted with the small, in bringing all to judgment/prayer
the great luminary (ha-ma'or ha-gadol) — the sun of Genesis 1:16, used as the symbol of Moshe/the tzaddik of the generation who illuminates prayer (the small luminary, the moon)
yanuka — the child/infant (of Rav's dictum 'smite the child only with a shoe-strap'), symbol of the lesser luminary (moon) and the state of sleep
people of small spiritual stature — the 'small ones' (ketanim) as a rank of persons, contrasted with the great, in the scheme of judgment/prayer
'me-achar alot' behind holiness — unholy melody drawn from 'behind the nursing ewes' (Psalm 78:70), i.e., neginah originating outside/behind kedushah, unlike prophetic holy song

vocally articulating words of Torah — the practice of speaking Torah study aloud with the mouth (מְדַבֵּר, piel 'speaks', not מִדְבָּר 'desert'), which brings one to the Torah's deep insights and illuminates where teshuvah is needed (LM I:11)

canonical_he: מאירין ההתנוצצות האותיות שיש בכל דבר
gloss_en: illuminating the sparkling of the letters in everything — making the otiyot embedded in all things (esp. foods) shine via perfected Holy Tongue, enabling dream interpretation
forms: מאירין ההתנוצצות האותיות שיש בכל דבר

canonical_he: שכשהנשמות עושין פרות שעושין רצונו של מקום
gloss_en: souls bearing fruit by doing God's will — the state in which the neshamot 'make fruits,' illuminating the eyes of the Master of the Field (sedeh tzofim vs. sedeh bokhim)
forms: שכשהנשמות עושין פרות שעושין רצונו של מקום

gloss_en: "the end of the matter" (sof davar) — the concluding phrase of Ecclesiastes 12:13 ("The end of the matter, all having been heard: fear God"), used as the scriptural emblem of the final endpoint/culmination that gathers everything, identified with Malkhut and the ultimate purpose

the 'gatherer of all the camps' of holiness (me'assef le-khol ha-machanot di-kedushah) — the rear-guard function of Malkhut of holiness that collects and closes off all the holy camps (as the camp of Dan did in Numbers 10:25), identified with 'the end of the matter' (Ecclesiastes 12:13)
ma'arikh rucheih — 'lengthening one's spirit' (Aramaic for erekh apayim), patience/long-breath of the ruach-chayim drawn from Torah, absent in Egypt's kotzer ruach
nullifying strife (machaloket) — the abolition of dispute via hand-clapping, uniting left (Korach) with right (Aharon) into oneness

canonical_he: נעשה מכל הדמים, דבורים של תורה ותפלה
gloss_en: transforming all of one's blood (the drops of blood of the nefesh/life-force) into words of Torah and prayer — the practice (from Likutey Moharan I:75) of speaking so extensively in Torah and tefillah that every drop of unserved blood is converted into holy speech, thereby rectifying the fallen sparks and nullifying contentiousness and dispute
forms: נעשה מכל הדמים, דבורים של תורה ותפלה

canonical_he: למסר המלחמה על ה. שה ילחם המלחמה
gloss_en: handing the war over to God — the act of entrusting the battle to Hashem to fight, the tikkun for heretical thoughts falling on the upright amid strife
forms: למסר המלחמה על ה. שה ילחם המלחמה

gloss_en: nullifying the wicked's thoughts — the cancellation of heretical thoughts (machshavot resha'im) that befall upright people, achieved by giving the battle to God
tefiloteinu — 'our prayers,' the eighteen Amidah blessings (chai birkhaan) through which Israel overrides nature ('mother of all life') and subdues heretics
mevatlim ha-teva — the action of nullifying/overriding nature's determinism through Jewish prayer, countering the philosophers' claim that nature ('mother of all life') is fixed
chai birkhaan — the eighteen (chai=18) blessings of the Amidah prayer (excluding birkat ha-minim), whose recital nullifies nature ('mother of all life') and subdues heretics

seeing the tzaddik — the first of three modes of attachment to the tzaddik (per Isaiah 30:20 'your eyes shall see your Teacher'), whose gaze nullifies bad traits from the mineral/vegetative elements (sadness and evil desires)
gazing upon temunat Hashem — beholding the 'image of God,' i.e. the prophetic anthropomorphic likenesses (Compassionate, Gracious, etc.), attained through clapping palm against palm in prayer

playing an instrument by hand — the musician's hand-motion on the instrument that sifts the good spirit (ruach of prophecy/joy) from the evil melancholy spirit, subduing the imaginative faculty (as David's playing for Saul)

clarifying/refining the good from the evil (birur) — the spiritual act, accomplished through Torah study (delving into halakhic rulings) and prayer, of separating, distinguishing, and nullifying the evil that is admixed with the good, as taught in Likutey Moharan I:8

Extracting and elevating the good contained within the Targum (the intermediate Aramaic 'translation' language, aspect of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil), thereby perfecting the Holy Tongue — the spiritual avodah of clarifying the good from the Targum taught in Likutey Moharan I:19
magdilim otah — raising/growing the newborn soul (nefesh) through love (ahavah), the 'great hand' (yad ha-gedolah), following its birth through fear

wisdom-and-da'at (chokhmah va-da'at): the paired holy intellective faculty of wisdom together with knowing awareness of God, the mochin/consciousness by which one penetrates concealment and which is bound up with fear of Heaven
chut shel chesed — the 'thread of lovingkindness' drawn upon a person (Abrahamic chesed of 'he planted an eshel'), a protective kabbalistic emanation shielding from the serpent
protection from the serpent — the shielding effect of the thread of chesed (Abraham's aspect, the tree in the Maharsha's parable) that guards a person from the serpent of lust/evil
burning heart-heat for God — the fervor of the heart aflame toward Hashem, whose fire-nature expels the spirit of impurity (as fire expels air)
chamimut ha-lev — the heart's heat/fervor as a fire-element force that drives out the impure spirit, analogized to gunpowder's ignition expelling air
greater boldness (more azut di-kedushah) — an increased measure of holy audacity/brazenness that enables one to speak freely with the tzaddik and thereby become closer to him (LM I:271)
speaking more with the Rebbe — the increased personal converse with one's master that flows from holy boldness (azut di-kedushah), the measure of one's closeness to the tzaddik

"the city of blood" (ir ha-damim) — the biblical epithet for a bloodstained city (Ezekiel 22:2; Nahum 3:1), invoked as the aspect of impure blood/menstrual defilement caused to the Shekhinah by blemish of the covenant; from עִיר (city) + דָּמִים (bloods), not to be confused with עֵר (awake) or דָּמִים as money

the bonfire of seventy stars (medurah shel shiv'in kokhvin) — the Zoharic image of a blazing pyre of seventy celestial fires representing the seventy nations, their seventy languages, and the lust for adultery, which is spoken down, cut, and nullified through the Holy Tongue and circumcision (the 'mal' of Chashmal) in Likutey Moharan I:19
MaL (מל) — the word 'circumcised' from ChaShMaL (chash-mal), gematria 70, whose cutting nullifies the bonfire of the seventy stars; circumcision as tikkun ha-brit

mochin — the 'brains'/mentalities: the kabbalistic term (Aramaic plural of מֹחַ, brain) for the illuminations of consciousness/intellect that enter and elevate a spiritual configuration (as in the mochin raised through tikkun ha-brit, the mochin of the Land of Israel, and the tefillin as mochin)
birthing the mochin — the Shekhinah's 'giving birth' to the withdrawn mentalities: one's cry in prayer/Torah, like a laboring woman's cry, brings the mochin out of their gestational concealment
molid — begetting/procreating, dependent on the letter heh ('hei lakhem zera') and on da'at ('a minor cannot beget'); why Abraham and Sarah bore children only upon receiving the heh
the two hands — yad ha-gedolah (great hand = love, which raises the soul) and yad ha-chazakah (strong hand = fear, which births it), as in 'in Your hand is power and might... to make great'
birthing and raising the soul clothed in Kavod — the twofold action (via fear and love, the two divine hands) of begetting and then growing the nefesh that is garbed in the King of Glory/Malkhut
galgalei ha-rakia — the celestial spheres/star-wheels of the firmament that determine terrestrial conditions (roads, deserts, settlement) and mark time; cause of travelers' sufferings
mo'ed — 'appointed time/festival' in Lamentations 1:4 read as the celestial spheres by which time is reckoned ('roads of Zion mourn without comers to the mo'ed')
charity's efficacy against lustful thoughts — tzedakah as a segulah that protects from hirhurei ni'uf (adulterous fantasies), though one may not rely on it to mingle with women
faith in the tzaddik's words — the believers' emunah in what the tzaddik says, which is itself the agency that causes his latent wonders (moftim) to become revealed
moftim — wonders/miracles of the tzaddikim, revealed publicly (as in the Kaiser's lands) only where the populace has faith in the tzaddik's words

livelihood earned in sorrow/toil (parnasah she-hu be-itzavon) — sustenance pursued with anxious grief, echoing the curse 'be-itzavon tokhelenah' (Gen 3:17), the bitter unrectified mode of earning a living, likened to 'more bitter than death is the woman' (Eccl 7:26), opposed to livelihood of holiness

canonical_he: מוצא אני מר ממות את האשה
gloss_en: 'more bitter than death is the woman' — Ecclesiastes 7:26 applied to livelihood earned in sorrow (parnasah = 'woman'), the bitter mode of sustenance needing sweetening
forms: מוצא אני מר ממות את האשה

gloss_en: siftotayikh — 'your lips' (Song of Songs), symbolizing the bringing of the intellect from potential into actuality (mi-ko'ach el ha-po'al) through speech
extracting her from the kelipot — tzedakah's rescue of the soul/Nukva ('her feet go down to death') from among the husks that suck her light and constrict one's sustenance; 'charity saves from death'

canonical_he: מוריד גם־כן חמימות והתלהבות להשם יתברך
gloss_en: movement generating fervor for God — how thought-to-thought motion in contemplating God's greatness 'brings down' heat, setting the heart aflame, like motion melting wax on an arrow
forms: מוריד גם־כן חמימות והתלהבות להשם יתברך

gloss_en: power of prayer-in-awe — the force drawn from tefillah performed with yirah (fear of God, 'my house'), by which the tzaddik rules ('You shall be over my house')

bringing down shefa and magnifying His kingship — the tzaddik's ruling in fear of God draws divine abundance into the world and enlarges God's Malkhut ('by your mouth all my people shall be sustained')
moshel — 'ruler,' the meaning of dabar ('one leader for a generation'); Malkhut as leadership/dominion restored to God via verbal confession before a Torah scholar
atzirut — constipation/retention as the bodily figure of motarot (waste/superfluities); Doeg's Torah study 'detained before Hashem' derived from this excremental aspect, yielding crooked judgment
superfluities/excess (motarot) — the surplus waste-products of holiness (bodily excrement, surplus brain-matter/hairs) from which the kelipot, sadness, and harsh judgments derive
surplus of the mochin (motrei mochin) — the kabbalistic excess/waste overflow of the brains/mentalities that exits the skull as hairs, source of judgments and baseless haters

the completeness/perfection of the altar (shleimut ha-mizbeach) — the restored wholeness of the Temple altar, rectified from its flaw when its fallen holy sparks return through converts, associated in LM 17 with 'the altar in the portion of the ravener (toref)' and 'yochal taref'

mizbe'ach be-chelko shel toref — the altar standing in the territory of the 'predator' (Benjamin, per Yaakov's blessing); the completeness of the altar whose flaw empowers idolatry, rectified through converts
the menorah (seven-branched lampstand; Aramaic מְנַרְתָּא), which in the Zoharic image expounded in LM 21 symbolizes the head/brain whose seven facial apertures are the seven lamps
the brain (moach) — the physical/spiritual brain in the head as seat of intellect and consciousness, source of the mochin (mentalities), symbolized by the menorah's head and the tefillin
'Reprove a wise man and he will love you' (Proverbs 9:8) — verse assigned to the brain-aspect of the ears (udnin), i.e. hearing the words of the wise
'The beginning of wisdom is fear of the Lord' (Psalms 111:10) — verse assigned to the brain-aspect of the nose (chotem), the moach manifest in smell/awe
'And the eyes of both were opened' (Genesis 3:7) — verse assigned to the brain-aspect of the eyes (aynin), the moach manifest in sight
'The beginning of Your word is truth' (Psalms 119:160) — verse assigned to the brain-aspect of the mouth (peh), the moach manifest in speech
heart's desire revealed in the hands — the cheshek of the heart becoming manifest through the hands ('ki vi' = 42 = 3×yad), i.e. the basis of clapping the palms in prayer
tevel (world) — gematria 432 = 2×216 (right hand 72 subsuming 3×72=216 plus left hand 216), the cosmos-name signifying the union of right and left in hand-clapping
kupah shel sheratzim — the 'basket of vermin hanging behind him' (Yoma 22b): a discrediting blemish required of a communal leader so he not grow arrogant

canonical_he: מחזיק את עצמו בבחינת מה ואפס ואין
gloss_en: self-abnegation of the leader — holding oneself as 'mah,' naught and nothing (ayin), the humility stance that protects the generation's leaders from arrogance
forms: מחזיק את עצמו בבחינת מה ואפס ואין

gloss_en: head (rosh, רֹאשׁ) — the head as seat of the brain and consciousness (mochin), used symbolically for whatever stands at the top/beginning: the tzaddik as head of Israel and of the generations, 'rosh bayit' (head of the house), and the 'head' of the year; distinct from רָשׁ (poor man) with which it is contrasted in the wine dictum

his hand — the noun yad (hand, the bodily limb) with third-person masculine singular possessive suffix (yado / yadav 'his hands'), used homiletically as a symbolic aspect (e.g., hands raised in holiness signifying mochin/consciousness, or steady hands signifying faith and prayer); not any homographic sense such as 'his monument' or a measure

YHVH — the Tetragrammaton, the four-letter proper Name of God (written ה' in the text), denoting the Holy One in His attribute of mercy, as distinct from the Name Elohim (judgment); not any common noun sharing these letters
Shem Yah (יה) — the divine Name Yah, aspect of the mochin (mentalities), by which Scripture testifies to Israel's purity ('tribes of Yah,' the added heh/yud of ha-Chanokhi)

the seven locks of his head (sheva machlefot rosho) — the seven braids of Samson's hair (Judges 16:19), expounded in Likutey Moharan 29 as the seven layers of the eye and the seven middot that pass (cholfin) through thought, hair being surplus of the mochin
kavanah — the prayer-intention/mental focus aroused by the voice ('the voice arouses the kavanah'), identified with the mochin birthed through crying out
bilbul ha-da'at — confusion of the mind, a mental state identified as mochin d'katnut (constricted consciousness), source of dinim and troubles
shoresh ha-neginah she-bikdushah — the holy root of melody, located in the mochin/da'at of Malkhut of holiness, from which the cantor must draw song
mochin ve-da'at shel Malkhut di-kedushah — the mental faculties and knowledge of the holy Malkhut, the prophetic source-consciousness from which holy melody is drawn
mochin she-be-Malkhut di-kelipah — the mental faculties of the Malkhut of the husks, identified by the Arizal with the impure 'birds' of the kelipah
Sitra Achra — the 'Other Side,' the demonic realm of impurity, here defined as the very aspect of machloket (dispute), rooted in dispute-within-holiness
'ein adam met va-chatzi...' — the rabbinic dictum 'no one dies with half his desires fulfilled,' read as referring to dispute via Targum's 'ba'alei chitzim' = disputants

kushya — a difficulty or unresolved question in Torah study, an apparent contradiction between texts or ideas that awaits a resolution (terutz); Rabbi Nachman treats it as the aspect of dispute (machloket) whose resolution is peace

hunger/famine (the noun רָעָב, ra'av — scarcity of food or the state of starving; in Likutey Moharan a symbolic bechinah, e.g. hunger arising from conflict/reproach in lm1:39, or the famine of Gen 12:10 read as self-imposed fasting in lm1:62; not the adjective רָעֵב 'hungry person')
kol ha-chola'at — all illnesses/diseases, defined as bodily machloket: the four elements warring instead of resting in balanced peace within the body
notzot — feathers (of the geese in Rabbah bar bar Chanah's tale), symbolizing strife and insults via the wordplay 'ki yinatzu anashim' (Deut. 25)
machloket u-vizyonot — quarrel and humiliations as a paired concept, the strife-and-disgrace symbolized by feathers (notzot/yinatzu)

dispute for the sake of Heaven (machaloket le-shem shamayim) — the holy, constructive controversy conducted purely for divine truth (Avot 5:17's paradigm, e.g., Shammai and Hillel), here identified with Da'at and with Moshe, as opposed to divisive quarrel for self-interest
machloket Shammai [ve-]Hillel — the archetypal dispute-for-the-sake-of-Heaven between the schools of Shammai and Hillel, whose initials spell MoSHeH
machaneh Dan — the camp of the tribe of Dan, the rear-guard 'gatherer of all the camps,' emblem of Malkhut collecting the holy camps
teiku — the Talmudic term for an unresolved halakhic question, read per Zohar (Ra'aya Mehemna) as 'tikkun' missing its final nun, i.e., lacking rectification
mechusar tikkun — the state of 'lacking rectification,' what teiku signifies: tikkun deprived of its nun, an unrepaired deficiency

committing some transgression (עָבַר אֵיזֶה עֲבֵרָה) — the act of a person violating a prohibition/sin, which engraves an evil letter-combination on his bones (Likutey Moharan I:4); not עֵבֶר 'side/beyond' nor עָבָר 'past'

inwardness (penimiyut) — the inner, hidden dimension of a thing, always contrasted with chitzoniyut (externality/outerness); e.g., thought as the inner counterpart of speech, or Torah/prayer as inner service versus bodily needs as outer service
thought (machashavah) — the mental faculty and its contents, cognition arising in the mind, as distinct from speech and deed
machashavah techilah — the primal thought preceding action (potential/koach), symbolized by the initial Yud of the Tetragrammaton at the head of the Aleph

corruption/damage inflicted upon the eyes (spiritual vision) — the blinding of the eyes (as by a bribe, 'the bribe blinds the eyes of the wise') that results from the corruption of judgment (mishpat), manifesting as alien thoughts/clouds covering the eyes during prayer (Likutey Moharan I:2)
alien/extraneous thoughts (machshavot zarot) that intrude specifically during prayer, which cover the eyes of the mind like clouds and stem from corrupted judgment (mishpat)

the corruption/perversion of judgment (kilkul ha-mishpat) — the impairment of the faculty of mishpat (e.g., through bribery), which, since judgment is the aspect of the eyes, blinds the eyes and is the root cause of alien thoughts in prayer (Likutey Moharan I:2)

Metatron — the archangel (abbreviated מט"ט), the 'angel-prince' whose name is like his Master's, who nests in the world of Yetzirah, rules the six weekdays, corresponds to the six orders of the Mishnah, and through whom God clothes Himself to govern the world (the Lower Unification)
Shaddai shel chol — the weekday manifestation of the divine name Shaddai, the contractions between labor and labor, identified with Metatron who rules the six weekdays
'mateh uzkha yishlach mi-Tziyon' — the verse 'the staff of your strength He will send from Zion' (Ps. 110:2), linked to sha'arei/se'arot (gates/hairs) of Zion in the first tikkun of the beard

canonical_he: מי שהוא כשר, נמשכת הנגינה שלו
gloss_en: the principle that a kosher (worthy) person's melody is drawn from the two pure birds of holiness — fitness as prerequisite for untainted neginah
forms: מי שהוא כשר, נמשכת הנגינה שלו

gloss_en: mayin metikin — 'sweet waters,' the taste of sweetness in prayer, identified with pure waters (mayin dakhyan), holy seed, and guarding the brit

bitter waters (Aramaic mayin meririn) — the kabbalistic aspect of undrinkable, bitter waters like those of Marah (Exodus 15:23), symbolizing the spiritual state caused by blemishing the covenant (pegam ha-brit), linked to impure waters/contaminated seed
MaL — the 'mal' component of ChashMaL, denoting milah/circumcision: cutting away the disgrace-foreskin after the silence (chash)
sanctity of the Covenant (kedushat ha-brit) — the holiness of the sexual/procreative covenant of circumcision, i.e., sexual purity and guarding the brit, personified by Joseph the tzaddik
shalhevet Yah — the 'flame of God' (Song 8:6), a descending holy fire that scorches the three impure kelipot so they cannot grasp holiness on erev Shabbat
mayim chamin — the hot water of pre-Shabbat washing, embodiment of the shalhevet Yah flame that burns off the kelipot on erev Shabbat
mayim karim — cold water that revives the soul, received via thunder generated by honoring an elder who forgot his learning
meimei ha-chesed — the waters of lovingkindness, Avraham's bounty (the well of living water), his attribute of chesed
'meisharim eshpot' — 'I will judge with equity' (Ps. 75:3), taken as the aspect of anavah (humility) in judgment, per Chullin 89
ha-noah veha-anachah — the groan and the sigh, which constitute a quasi-death of both body ('a sigh breaks a person's body') and soul
mitah be-guf va-nefesh — death in body and soul, the twofold dying effected by the groan/sigh (Berakhot 58b; Ps. 104:29)

death of the heart (mitat ha-lev) — the spiritual deadening of the heart, identified in Likutey Moharan I:54 with forgetfulness, the evil eye, and the broken Tablets, as in 'I was forgotten like a dead man from the heart' (Ps. 31:13)
ra ayin — the evil eye, equated with death of the heart; the cause of forgetfulness that destroys memory ('between your eyes')
the principle that honor rises to its root in proportion to one's rectification of kavod — each honors God-fearers according to how far he has repaired the glory

canonical_he: מכיר ומשיג יותר את השם יתברך
gloss_en: the ever-deepening recognition and apprehension of God — each new level of knowing Hashem that obligates teshuvah upon one's previous teshuvah
forms: מכיר ומשיג יותר את השם יתברך

gloss_en: subduing the 'breath of beauty' (hevel ha-yofi) — the shofar/beard tikkunei Atik action of humbling vain charm, narrow-above-wide-below (min ha-meitzar)
machnia ha-medameh — the subduing of the imaginative faculty (dimyon), achieved by the 'hand' that sorts the good spirit from the evil spirit

canonical_he: מכניע העבודה זרה שנעשה מפגם חלקי המזבח
gloss_en: subduing idolatry that draws its power from the blemished altar-portions — accomplished through converts who complete the pegam ha-mizbe'ach
forms: מכניע העבודה זרה שנעשה מפגם חלקי המזבח

gloss_en: machnia tola dikelipah — the holy worm ('I am a worm, not a man,' the olat tamid/chesed of Avraham) subduing the worm of the kelipah

tallit — the four-cornered prayer shawl (garment of enwrapment); in LM I:8 the white tallit of holiness in which the Holy One wrapped Himself to arrange the Thirteen Attributes, its four corners embodying the spirit of life from the four winds, subduing the red tallit/spirit of the kelipah
machni'in oto — subduing him/it (the impure ruach of Esav) via the white tallit and the Thirteen Attributes, the holy ruach-chayim
machni'in ha-ruach se'arah — subduing the storm-wind, the spirit of opponents of true tzaddikim, through the four tzitzit drawing ruach from the four winds (Ezek. 37:9)

"From the wing (edge/corner) of the earth" (mi-kenaf ha-aretz) — the phrase from Isaiah 24:16, "from the wing of the earth we have heard songs," where kenaf denotes the earth's extremity/corner (associated with the four wings/corners and, in Likutey Moharan, with Metatron and the lower unification); not kanaf as a bird's literal wing or garment-corner in another verse
'tzaddik moshel' — 'the righteous one rules [over Me]' (II Sam. 23:3), the tzaddik's power over God, present in every Jew ('your people are all tzaddikim')
melo pum — 'full mouth' (Aramaic), the letters of the melupum vowel: the tzaddik's mouth filled with Godliness, aspect of tzaddik-moshel
hitlahavut — fiery enthusiasm/ardor of the heart, an angel-like burning ('angel of God in a flame of fire,' Ex. 3:2) that scorches the chitzonim
malakhim — angels, the fiery beings to which heart-enthusiasm corresponds ('vayera elav malakh Hashem be-labat esh'), whose fire burns the external forces

"Open your mouth wide and I will fill it" (Psalms 81:11) — the Divine invitation to expansive request/prayer, homiletically linked to the melafum vowel (מְלֹא פּוּם, 'a full mouth'), signifying that abundance flows according to the widening of the mouth and the completion of lack

melupum (melafum) — the Hebrew vowel sign whose name Rabbi Nachman expounds as 'melo pum' (a full mouth), composed of a point (yud) with a vav, signifying the mouth/vessel filled with divine abundance ('open your mouth wide and I will fill it')
've-Yosef hu ha-shallit' — the verse 'and Yosef, he was the ruler' (Gen. 42:6), Yosef/Yesod as the melupum-vocalized channel of abundance
aseret ha-dibrot im ha-luchot — the Ten Commandments together with the stone Tablets, symbolizing the yud-vav that spell the melupum vowel (Tablets six-by-six handbreadths = vav)
nitmale ha-chisaron — the filling of a deficiency/lack, the state signified by melupum read as 'melo pum,' a full mouth ('open your mouth wide and I will fill it')
the war Mashiach will wage and all the conquests he will conquer — the Messiah's future military campaign, fought entirely through prayer (his 'nose'/chotem weapon)

king (מֶלֶךְ) — the sovereign ruler as archetype: the appointed monarch of Israel and the tzaddik/Divine King through whom rulership, sustenance, and honor flow; the noun 'king', not the verb מָלַךְ 'to reign', the abstract מַלְכוּת 'kingship', or the idol מֹלֶךְ
Torah scholars (talmidei chakhamim) — sages learned in Torah, 'disciples of the wise,' the rabbinic scholars themselves as persons (not their teachings)
ta'avat ashirut — the lust/craving for wealth, a vice identified with fallen Malkhut (money-hoarding of the Sitra Achra)
cherev nokemet — 'the avenging sword' of Leviticus 26:25, a scriptural phrase identified with Malkhut/Lower Wisdom (the tzaddik's rebuking blade)

the lower intellect (sekhel ha-tachton) — the contracted, lower level of intellect identified with Malkhut/Chokhmah Tata'ah, the wisdom of governance that garbs and constricts the higher intellect of divine perception, serving as the introduction/gateway to it (Likutey Moharan I:30)
yirat Elokim — the fear/awe of God as a spiritual quality, identified with Malkhut per 'were it not for the fear of the government' (Avot 3)
Yisrael as the nation who accepts God's kingship — Israel in their role as the people constituting Malkhut, since 'there is no king without a people'

Judah (Yehudah) — the biblical patriarch, son of Jacob, and his tribe/territorial portion; associated in Likutey Moharan with the aspect of Malkhut (kingship) and fear/awe (yirah), and with verbal confession
yeshut — existence/being, the totality of manifest 'is-ness' identified with Malkhut, which draws its vitality from the Infinite Will (ratzon Ein Sof)
Moav — the nation/land of Moab, symbol of Malkhut because King David descended from it (Moses buried 'in the land of Moab')
retzonot — the divine wills/desires embodied in the forms of the letters, expressions of God's Malkhut drawing vitality from the Will of Ein Sof
temunot — the graphic forms/shapes of the Hebrew letters, each embodying a divine will and revealing God's Malkhut
the letter Nun — the alphabet letter symbolizing Malkhut/kingship, per 'yinnon shmo' (Ps. 72:17) which Rashi reads as a term of kingship
d'leit lah mi-garmah klum — 'it has nothing of its own,' the kabbalistic defining property of Malkhut/the moon, receiving all from Chokhmah (the sun/Chet)
the kingship/royalty of David (Malkhut David) — the Davidic monarchy as the embodiment of the sefirah of Malkhut, associated with prayer, anointing oil, and song
malkhut d'sitra achra — the kingdom/kingship of the Other Side, the demonic counter-Malkhut personified by Haman, hoarder of holy sparks as money

transgressors (poshe'im) — persons who willfully rebel/sin, the active-participle plural of פ.ש.ע (as in Hosea 14:10 'transgressors stumble in them' and Isaiah 53:12 'numbered with the transgressors'); NOT the abstract noun pesha'im 'transgressions/sins'
malkhut nittaken — the rectification/repair of the sefirah Malkhut, effected through Judah's confession recalled by Moses ('Hear, O Lord, the voice of Judah')
avonotav — a person's sins/iniquities, the transgressions that degrade Malkhut and arouse the King's wrath (atoned by the Torah scholar/Moses)
menagen bikhlei zemer — playing musical instruments as a spiritual act: gathering the good spirit out of the depressed/evil spirit to form holy melody
chamrei — 'his donkey' (Aramaic, from the Choni sleeper tale) bearing herds, symbol of wealth per 'Yissachar is a strong-boned donkey'
ha-ochez b'midat emet — one who holds fast to the trait of truthfulness, whose livelihood thereby flows amply ('kushta ka'ei' — truth stands, sustaining one's money)
se'udah — a festive meal/banquet (from 'ein hasibah ela se'udah' on 'vayasev Elokim'), symbol of parnassah/sustenance, grain and food, the 'well'

standing (amidah) — the verbal noun of עמד, the act/state of standing upright and being firmly established; in Likutey Moharan the symbolic 'standing' that denotes prayer (per 'ein amidah ela tefillah', the Amidah), Torah received while standing, and money/livelihood that stands a person on his feet
the obstacle is automatically broken — the state in which intensified desire (cheshek) shatters the barrier, since obstacles exist only to increase longing
mimekomo — 'from His place' (of the Kedushah 'blessed be God's glory from His place'), identified with Keter, the supernal Crown
drawing the spirit of life from the tzaddik of the generation — the act of receiving ruach chayim from the generation's righteous master, who is attached to Torah
drawing new intellect from the Light of the Countenance — the act of importing fresh sekhel 'from afar' (Prov. 31:14) via faithful commerce/plain Torah study

canonical_he: ממשיכין אריכות ימים, ואז זוכה לדעת
gloss_en: drawing down length of days, thereby meriting da'at — extending one's days/measures via vocal Torah study that calls the life-force into them
forms: ממשיכין אריכות ימים, ואז זוכה לדעת

canonical_he: ממשלת וכח הצדיק שנעשה על ידי עבודתו
gloss_en: the dominion and power of the tzaddik earned through his divine service — the 'staff' (mateh) by which all enemies above and below are subdued
forms: ממשלת וכח הצדיק שנעשה על ידי עבודתו

gloss_en: Torah study and speaking good words — the devotional speech-acts that sweeten the gevurot (severities) inherent in all utterance
sweetening the words, which are gevurot — the mitigation of the five severities embodied in speech, accomplished through Torah study and good words
hearing one's own praise recounted — the situation of listening to others tell one's virtues, which inevitably arouses self-aggrandizement

canonical_he: מן הנמנע, שלא יבוא לו איזה גדלות
gloss_en: the inevitability that some grandiosity will arise — the impossibility of avoiding a feeling of self-importance when praised (context of Moses' 'erase me' prayer)
forms: מן הנמנע, שלא יבוא לו איזה גדלות

gloss_en: menagen ba-yad — playing music by hand (as 'when the musician played, the hand of God came upon him'), joy-producing act that subdues the imaginative faculty
manhig — a leader/ruler (from 'dabar echad l'dor,' one spokesman per generation), the leadership sense of 'davar' identified with Malkhut
meniot — obstacles/hindrances on the spiritual path, symbolized by firmaments (raki'in) that screen and divide the desirer from the desired
mesirat nefesh al kiddush Hashem — self-sacrifice/martyrdom for the sanctification of God's Name, the trait of Yosef uniting chasadim and gevurot
lomed b'iyun — studying Torah in depth/analytically, the intensive mode of learning (vs. casting off the Torah's yoke)
me'ayen u-mevin chokhmot ha-Torah — one who delves into and comprehends the wisdoms of the Torah, an intellectual attainment
'chokhmat adam ta'ir panav' — the verse 'a man's wisdom lights up his face' (Eccl. 8:1), prooftext that Torah wisdom illuminates the countenance
sippurei ma'asiyot — telling stories/tales (of tzaddikim), the practice that awakens people from spiritual sleep and draws wealth
awakening from sleep — the arousal from spiritual slumber (the fallen state of the seventy faces), effected through told stories
performing the mitzvah with joy — doing commandments in simchah, which completes the holiness and lifts vitality out of the kelipot (eleven incense-spices)
ma'alin et ha-yirah — the act of elevating fear to its root by judging one's own affairs (mishpat), from 'a king by justice establishes the land'
sheshet yemei ha-ma'aseh — the six weekdays of creation, the aspect of practical mitzvah-deeds through which World-Year-Soul were created
ma'aseh ha-mitzvot — the practical performance of the commandments, identified with the six days of work in which World-Year-Soul were created

canonical_he: ירשת ארץ־ישראל, על־ידי המשכת קדשת ארץ־ישראל
gloss_en: inheritance of Eretz Yisrael achieved by drawing down the Land of Israel's holiness ('sit at My right hand') — the means that fells the wicked
forms: ירשת ארץ־ישראל, על־ידי המשכת קדשת ארץ־ישראל

gloss_en: mapaltan shel resha'im — the downfall/collapse of the wicked, effected through inheriting the holiness of the Land of Israel (Abba Shaul's 'deer' chase)

name (the noun shem, שֵׁם) — an appellation/designation, encompassing one's renown or reputation in the world and the Divine Name, homologized in Likutey Moharan with soul/nefesh, vitality, and Malkhut; not the adverb sham (שָׁם, 'there') or the verb sam (שָׂם, 'placed')
mefursam — the famous/renowned person, one's public name and reputation (equated with the nefesh), which can be 'lost' though everyone speaks of him
tapuchin — the 'apples' (of the holy Apple Field), symbol of the openings of the heart when the supernal heart's mercy is stirred and warm words flow
maftechei ha-lev she-niftachim — the keys/openings of the heart being opened, i.e., the supernal heart's compassion kindled to pour forth warm speech
Mei Merivah — the biblical 'Waters of Strife' (Numbers 20), read as the aspect of matzah/quarrel (matsuta) of the tzaddikim
the Zoharic letter-operation making matzah from the letters of chametz — breaking the chet of 'kaneh' into a heh so one's wisdom does not ferment
the protective power of tzedakah (charity) as a segulah that saves one from lustful thoughts of adultery — though one may not rely on it to mingle with women
metzulot — the 'depths' of the sea (Exodus 15:5), read as Mitzrayim/Egypt via 'va-yenatzlu et Mitzrayim' (despoiling Egypt)
Egypt (Mitzrayim) — the biblical land of Israel's bondage and exile, site of the descent of Jacob and his sons and of the Exodus; homiletically linked to constriction (meitzar)
azut di-kedushah she-yesh bo — the holy boldness a person possesses, opposite of brazen-facedness, prerequisite for a portion in Torah
receiving holy boldness (azut di-kedushah) from Hashem — the divine grant of sacred audacity needed to receive Torah
meriting good deeds and good character traits (middot tovot) through contraction and good thoughts — the achievement that reveals God's kingship

canonical_he: מקבל עליו על מלכות שמים שלמה
gloss_en: accepting upon oneself the complete yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven (kabbalat ol malkhut shamayim shelemah) — the state attained via good deeds and traits
forms: מקבל עליו על מלכות שמים שלמה

canonical_he: שמקשר לבו לדעתו, שלבו ברשותו וכו
gloss_en: binding one's heart to one's da'at ('his heart in his control') — the act of subordinating the heart to the mind above time
forms: שמקשר לבו לדעתו, שלבו ברשותו וכו

canonical_he: מקבלין המדות אור האהבה שבדעת וכו
gloss_en: the middot (character traits) receiving the light of the love-within-Da'at — supra-temporal Chesed flowing into the traits when heart is bound to mind
forms: מקבלין המדות אור האהבה שבדעת וכו

gloss_en: mikveh of Shavuot — the festival immersion-pool corresponding to the Fiftieth Gate, highest of the fifty gates of Binah (per the Shavuot kavvanot)
mekomot ha-nemukhim — the low places, i.e., the filthy places (mekomot ha-metunafim) of extreme spiritual descent where one can still recall God through speech

the filthy places (mekomot ha-metunafim) — places of filth/excrement, i.e., the lowest, spiritually defiled locations (symbolizing the depths of impurity into which a person may fall), where holiness is concealed
fulfilling the positive commandment of 'Ve-ahavta' (loving God), root of all positive mitzvot, achieved by conducting business in faithfulness

tekhelet — the sky-blue dye/thread of the tzitzit fringes, expounded (via Zohar) as that which 'consumes and destroys all' (linked to kallah/takhlit and judgments/gevurot), symbolizing Malkhut and encompassing lights
've-hatznea lekhet' — the verse-phrase 'walk humbly [with your God]' (Micah 6:8), identified as the encompassing lights (makifim) and the sukkah
Atika — the Zoharic 'Ancient One' (Atika Kadisha), the partzuf that is utterly hidden, symbolizing the makifin concealed until the future revelation

divine influx (shefa Eloki) — the divinely bestowed flow of intellect/holy inspiration that comes to a person without preliminary steps, identified in Likutey Moharan 21 with Ruach HaKodesh, the sukkah, the face of the menorah, and the surrounding lights (makifin)
mikneihu — 'his livestock' (as in Exodus 9:20-21), the domestic animals whose untimely death results from laxity in the mitzvah of sukkah
cooling one's bodily heat by means of leshon ha-kodesh — the Holy Tongue's power to chill lustful heat ('my heart was hot within me... I spoke')
one who sanctifies himself — the person whose free choice of self-sanctification binds him to the rope (chevel) of holiness
binding oneself to the rope of holiness (chevel di-kedushah) — the attachment effected by self-sanctification, opposite the rope of impurity
mar'ah meluteshet — a polished mirror, symbol of the student's shining countenance (anpin nehirin) enabling him to receive the light of his master's face

the father's heart becoming circumcised (נִמּוֹל, nif'al 'was circumcised') — the removal of the foreskin/blockage of the parent's heart so it truly feels the pain of his sins, which in LM I:141 awakens the hearts of his descendants (not any other sense of מ-ו-ל or לבב)
omer — the Omer barley offering, letter-rearranged as Mordekhai/'mar deror' (pure myrrh), signifying freedom (cherut) and revealed Torah
being sent compassion so that he will have mercy on another — God's device of giving a needy person someone to pity
merachamin alav — Heaven having mercy upon him, the reciprocal mercy earned by one who shows mercy to another (whoever pities creatures is pitied)
'Ki Tetze' — the verse-phrase 'When you go out' (Deut. 21:10), read as the aspect of commerce/business ('Rejoice, Zevulun, in your going out')
expertise in dinei mamonot — monetary law study ('who wishes to grow wise, engage in monetary laws'), equated with faithful commerce renewing the mind/soul
niguna de-Leiva'ei — the Zoharic 'melody of the Levites' that gladdens the heart, identified with faithful commerce done in contentment with one's lot
cheshek — intense desire/yearning, the longing that all obstacles exist to intensify and that forms the vowel-points bringing potential into actuality
the desire's breaking of the obstacle — cheshek shattering the meniah, since obstacles exist only to arouse greater longing
breaking through the encircling klipah and entering the second rung — piercing the husk surrounding each spiritual level by joy of the mitzvah

canonical_he: לזה עזות דקדשה – הינו קולות הנ"ל
gloss_en: the holy boldness required, namely the aforementioned voices/cries — azut di-kedushah of voice that breaks the body's brazenness (a sigh breaks the body)
forms: לזה עזות דקדשה – הינו קולות הנ"ל

gloss_en: shepherd (רוֹעֶה) — the spiritual shepherd/leader of the generation, the tzaddik in the aspect of Moses the Faithful Shepherd (רעיא מהימנא) who constructs the Tabernacle from which the children of the generation receive; not a literal herder of flocks, nor רֵעֶה (friend) or רָעָה (evil)
'to build them the Beit ha-Bechirah' — the commandment to build the Temple, read as the aspect of Moshe/Da'at ('one with da'at, it is as if the Temple were built in his days')

Torah scholar (talmid chakham) — the sage learned in Torah who, in Likutey Moharan 4, embodies the aspect of Moses: the true scholar before whom one makes verbal confession, who is bound to the light of Torah, and who guides each person on the path according to the root of his soul
telat me'ah — the 'three hundred' (barrels of oil in the Rabbah bar bar Chanah tale), symbol of Moshe/'mah': the tzaddik's threefold self-diminution in wisdom, might, and wealth
ba'al aveirah — the habitual sinner/transgressor as a personal type, deemed insane per Sotah 3a's 'spirit of folly'
meshuga — madman/insane state; the sinner's condition caused by the entering ruach shtut (spirit of folly)

blemish of the covenant (pegam ha-brit) — the spiritual damage caused by sexual sin, i.e. violation of the covenant of circumcision through wasted seed or sexual immorality, the counterpart of shemirat ha-brit
mashukh be'orlato — 'drawn/extended in his foreskin' (one who stretches skin to undo circumcision); emblem of pegam habrit (covenant blemish) caused by unelevated Aramaic/Targum
restoring the soul (meshivat nafesh) — the phrase from Psalms 19:8 'the Torah of God is perfect, restoring the soul,' denoting the Torah's power to revive and return the nefesh to its root
shoresh hamalkhut — the root of Kingship (sefirah of Malkhut), identified with Mashiach per 'and raise the horn of His anointed' (I Sam 2), where arrogance's evil eye must be subdued
diminishing and belittling oneself — the practice of self-effacing humility (making oneself small/few, like dust), which draws the Divine presence (per Chullin 89a on Deut. 7:7)

completing/filling the deficiency (mashlim ha-chisaron) — the remedying of a lack in any matter by drawing the spirit of life (ruach chayim) back to it, e.g., through sighing or Torah and prayer, since every deficiency is essentially a departure of that thing's vital spirit (Likutey Moharan I:8)
shishim giborim — the 'sixty mighty men' around Solomon's bed (Song 3:7), kabbalistic gevurot from which sustenance/rain descends; hinted in Rabbah bar bar Chanah's 'sixty cities'
the flow of parnassah (livelihood) issuing from the sixty giborim/gevurot, as in 'gevurot geshamim' — rains as mighty acts (Berakhot 33a)
the drop-by-drop descent (of rain/bounty) from the gevurot — thunder-linked trickle of sustenance descending in individual drops

the Mishnah — the corpus of Oral Torah (six orders of tannaitic teaching) that delineates legal opposites (pure/impure, forbidden/permitted, valid/invalid), identified in the Zohar/Tikkunim with the angel Metatron and the six weekdays; not מִשְׁנֶה 'double/copy/viceroy'
Mishneh Torah — 'the repetition of the Torah' (Deuteronomy), wordplay with lechem mishneh (double Shabbat bread): doubled Torah insights innovated on Shabbat

square (ribbua) — the quadrate/squared figure, paired with the circle (iggula) in LM 59 as the aspect of judgment (mishpat), associated with 'hand'; the geometric-kabbalistic square, not any other sense of the root רבע
'meimekha' ('your water,' Num 20:19, Edom episode) — water as symbol of mishpat/judgment, per 'let judgment roll down like water' (Amos 5:24)

the first-person pronoun "I" (ani, אֲנִי) — the scriptural word for selfhood/divine self-reference, expounded as the aspect of Malkhut/judgment (e.g. "va-ani natati lekha", "va-ani betokh ha-golah"); not אֳנִי (a fleet of ships) or עָנִי (a pauper)
the verse 'mishpatim bal yeda'um' (Ps 147:20, 'judgments they did not know') — gentile courts' alien judgments empowered when an unworthy rabbi is ordained
mishpat me'ukal — 'crooked/perverted judgment' (Hab 1:4): distorted justice of gentile courts/writings, opposite of clear mishpat
mishpetei hanhagot yesharot — upright judgments/norms of conduct on the middle path, attained via faith in the Sages
'mishpetei emet' — 'true judgments' (Ps 19:10): clear, true judgment emerging through emunat chakhamim and the central pillar
one immersed/sunk in ta'avat mamon (lust for money) — the state of anpin chashukhin (darkened countenance), diagnosable when the master cannot see himself in the student
met — a corpse/death itself, the avi avot hatum'ah (ultimate source of ritual impurity), equated with adulterous thoughts from which tzedakah saves ('charity saves from death')
the prevailing/triumph of the tzaddikim over the wicked via the ruach chaim (spirit of life) — Rashi's 'future standing and rising for the righteous' on 'tzvi latzaddik'
the act of binding and attaching oneself to God and His tzaddikim — the peacemaking/unification achieved through resolving disputes, raising mayin nukvin

canonical_he: מתחלה היצר הרע מתלבש עצמו במצוות
gloss_en: the yetzer hara's initial tactic of garbing itself in mitzvot — enticing a person as if to a mitzvah; the deceptive 'white fire' (tzutzita denura chivarta) that is nonetheless a destructive angel
forms: מתחלה היצר הרע מתלבש עצמו במצוות

canonical_he: מתמלל ומשתבר אש המדורה של שבעין כוכבין
gloss_en: the breaking-down and nullification through speech (mitmalel u-mishtaber) of the bonfire-fire of the seventy stars — i.e., the Holy Tongue's power to 'speak down' and shatter the fire of the seventy nations' languages/celestial powers (the 'mal' of Chashmal, in Likutey Moharan I:19)
forms: מתמלל ומשתבר אש המדורה של שבעין כוכבין

gloss_en: tefillah ketikkuno — prayer performed in its proper/rectified form, which sparks the light of zekhut avot ('chalah zekhut avot,' via 'vayechal Moshe')

canonical_he: התנוצצות האור שמקבל הלב מל"ב אלקים
gloss_en: the sparkling illumination the heart (lev) receives from the 32 (lamed-bet) occurrences of 'Elokim' in the Creation account — source of the heart's name and light
forms: התנוצצות האור שמקבל הלב מל"ב אלקים

gloss_en: the shining of the Patriarchs' lights (orot ha'avot: Avraham-Yitzchak as right/left hands, Yaakov as neder) upon a person when the hands are rectified by a vow
praying also with yirah (awe/fear of God) — the awe flowing from humility ('ekev anavah yirat Hashem'), yirah being Malkhut, joined to prayer
praying and begging forgiveness for one's sins — the penitent's supplication accompanying teshuvah and the shame that becomes the light of tefillin
kodem gezar din — the temporal stage 'before the decree is sealed,' when prayer may be uttered plainly in its standard order without disguise

canonical_he: מתפללין כסדר התפלה, ואין צריך להלביש התפלה
gloss_en: praying in the fixed liturgical order without 'clothing' the prayer — the undisguised mode of petition permitted before the decree, since no angelic accusers need be evaded
forms: מתפללין כסדר התפלה, ואין צריך להלביש התפלה

gloss_en: hearing the melody/music (listening to the נְגִינָה played by a worthy musician, which in Likutey Moharan I:3 rectifies the aspect of malkhut)
rectifying/building one's own personal malkhut (kingship-structure) by hearing holy melody — the sense of 'aseh lekha rav' in Avot 1
rectifying and elevating the aspect of Malkhut back to its root — restoring kingship to God, effected by verbal confession before a talmid chakham
the proportional increase of da'at (knowledge/awareness) — the measure by which peace and easy livelihood grow

canonical_he: מתרבה הרחמנות והשלום. ועל כן הפרנסה בנקל
gloss_en: the increase of compassion and peace — and consequent ease of parnassah — that results from expanded da'at ('the earth is full of knowledge,' Isa 11)
forms: מתרבה הרחמנות והשלום. ועל כן הפרנסה בנקל

gloss_en: nisu'in shel rasha — the 'marriage/union of the wicked one' (the serpent's seductive coupling), the adulterous liaison from which tzitzit protects
ni'uf — adultery/sexual licentiousness as the category of sin countered by the mitzvah of tzitzit (covering the arayot)
being attached to the tzaddik and believing in him — the mere faith-attachment that benefits one's divine service even without receiving teaching

canonical_he: נאכל להצדיק ונתהפך למהות הצדיק ממש
gloss_en: being 'eaten' by the tzaddik and transformed into the tzaddik's very essence — the food-becomes-eater metaphor ('a land that consumes its inhabitants,' Num 13) for the follower's absorption
forms: נאכל להצדיק ונתהפך למהות הצדיק ממש

canonical_he: נאספו החרפות, הינו השלש קלפות כנ"ל
gloss_en: the 'gathering in' (removal/nullification) of the disgraces (charafot) that beset a person — identified with the three impure kelipot associated with the foreskin — accomplished through circumcision/guarding the covenant (as in 'God has gathered in my disgrace' at Joseph's birth and 'today I have rolled away the disgrace of Israel')
forms: נאספו החרפות, הינו השלש קלפות כנ"ל

gloss_en: chazan — the cantor/prayer-leader, so named from chazon (prophetic vision) because his melody draws from the place from which prophets suckle
menagen — the musician/singer of melody, whose neginah issues from the two live pure birds nursing from the prophetic source
the multiplying/increasing of prayer — each added prayer, though seeming barren, is 'kneaded and baked,' further building the Shekhinah
the progressive building of the Shekhinah's stature through accumulated prayers, preparing Her for the zivug (union) — the true fruit of seemingly unanswered prayers

canonical_he: נבנה ירושלים, קריה נאמנה, הינו שזוכין לאמונה
gloss_en: the rebuilding of Jerusalem as 'kiryah ne'emanah' (faithful city, Isa 1) = attaining emunah (faith), achieved through holy boldness (azut dikedushah)
forms: נבנה ירושלים, קריה נאמנה, הינו שזוכין לאמונה

gloss_en: the creation of heaven and earth — the world-creating power latent in Torah novelties born of the imaginative faculty resting on those who repeat halakhot
the growth/magnification of shalom (peace) — peace enlarged in step with da'at, enabling opposites ('wolf with lamb,' Isa 11) to dwell together

Nogah (kelipat Nogah) — the fourth, translucent 'glowing' husk of the kabbalistic kelipot (from Ezekiel 1:4, 'a radiance surrounding it'); the intermediate shell mixing good and evil that, unlike the three wholly impure husks, can be clarified and absorbed into holiness — locus of free choice and trial, linked to Chashmal, Targum, and the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. Not the planet Venus, not generic 'brightness,' and not the verb נָגַהּ 'to shine.'

canonical_he: ברור הרוח טובה מן הרוח רעה
gloss_en: birur ha-ruach tovah min ha-ruach ra'ah — the act of sifting/separating the good spirit (joy, prophecy) from the evil spirit within the mixed breath, effected by the skilled musician on a whole instrument
forms: ברור הרוח טובה מן הרוח רעה

gloss_en: melody/tune (niggun) — musical melody as a spiritual act that gathers and clarifies the good spirit from the evil/animal spirit; not the verb 'to play' nor the player

"We will do" (na'aseh) — Israel's declaration at Sinai/Horeb (Exodus 24:7, "na'aseh ve-nishma"), signifying the revealed commandments one knows how to fulfill, as opposed to nishma (the hidden); not the passive verb "is made/done"

the revealed things (niglot) — the openly revealed dimension of Torah and its commandments, which each person knows and is able to fulfill according to his level; paired opposite of nistarot (hidden things), and identified in LM I:22 with 'we will do' (naaseh)

"his Torah" (torato) — the Torah that becomes the person's own possession (per Avodah Zarah 19a on Psalms 1:2: first 'the Torah of God,' then 'his Torah'); the internalized, revealed level of Torah corresponding to na'aseh ('we will do') and 'the revealed things belong to us,' in contrast to torat Hashem, the hidden nishma level
nigl(ot) — 'the revealed things' of Deut 29:28 ('ve-hanniglot lanu u-levaneinu'), the disclosed dimension of Torah that becomes 'his Torah' (na'aseh) after the hidden stage
the fall and nullification of malkhut ha-resha'ah — collapse of the wicked kingdom (Sitra Achra's dominion) when holy Malkhut (nun) is joined to Chokhmah (chet), 'when this rises, that falls'

canonical_he: התגלות ההתפארות שמתפארין ישראל עמו יתברך
gloss_en: hitgalut ha-hitpa'arut — the revelation of God's glorying/adornment in His people Israel (pe'er, tefillin), whose disclosure by the tzaddik brings down fear and love
forms: התגלות ההתפארות שמתפארין ישראל עמו יתברך

gloss_en: nofel yirah — the 'falling' (descending/alighting) of awe-fear upon beholders, effected by the revealed pe'er/tefillin-glory of Israel ('all peoples will see... and fear you')
the single (first) collapse of Sha'ar Aram — one fall of the Gate of Aram/Sitra Achra in R. Yosei ben Kisma's sign of Mashiach (it must fall three times before Ben David comes)
the downfall of all seventy languages/nations — collapse of the shiv'im lashon when the good of Targum is raised into leshon ha-kodesh and its evil cast down (tardemah = gematria targum)

the engraving of an evil letter-combination (tzeruf ra) upon a person's bones as the imprint of his transgression (per Ezekiel 32:27, 'their iniquities were engraved upon their bones'), whereby each sin inscribes its destructive letter-permutation into his very skeleton
nokem bo — the sin-engraved letter-combination 'takes vengeance' on the sinner; the punitive backlash of an evil tzeruf carved on his bones (Ezek 32:27)
nizdakekh ha-avir — the purification/clarification of the air of the world, effected by the love and friendship acquired through giving tzedakah to many people
nachal ha-nimshakh min ha-ma'yan — the stream flowing from the wellspring: Binah as river issuing from Chokhmah's point/yud-spring (the vav of the melupum)

the upper point's division into three drops — the supernal nekudah (throne/Moshe) splitting into the three dots of segol, corresponding to teshuvah's three conditions: seeing, hearing, understanding-and-returning (Isa 6)
nechkak bo emet — truth being engraved in a person through receiving and following the counsel of tzaddikim ('hen emet chafatzta,' Ps 51)

canonical_he: נחקק ונרשם מקום בלב המתבקש לקבל הבקשה
gloss_en: the engraving (tav-mark) of a receptive place in the heart of the one petitioned — chen (chet+nun) carving room so requests are accepted, as in 'vehitvita tav' (Ezek 9)
forms: נחקק ונרשם מקום בלב המתבקש לקבל הבקשה

gloss_en: tanina — the sea-serpent/dragon (Aramaic, from the Rabbah bar bar Chanah tale) that swallowed; symbol of the nachash enticing one to pray for self-benefit
dina dimsa'ava — 'impure judgment' (Aramaic Zoharic term): defiled din stemming from the serpent's contamination of Chavah, opposed to holy judgment/loving rebuke
nachash hitil zuhama be-Chavah — the Talmudic dictum (Shabbat 146a) that the primordial serpent injected filth into Eve, source-event of impure judgment
the heart's kindling and burning toward God — the state of inflamed devotional ardor arising in personal prayer/hitbodedut before one's Maker
nit'har ha-lev — the purification of the heart ('lev tahor bera li,' Ps 51) achieved through private speech between oneself and one's Creator (ruach ha-kodesh)

one's thought becomes purified — the cleansing of a person's mind/thought (נִטְהָר, nif'al of ט-ה-ר, 'is purified' + מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ 'his thought'), the spiritual outcome (in LM I:234, effected by telling stories of tzaddikim) whereby mental confusion and impure thinking are removed

canonical_he: שספורי מעשיות מצדיקים. הינו ממה שארע להם
gloss_en: sippurei ma'asiyot mi-tzaddikim — telling stories of what actually happened to tzaddikim, a practice that purifies the hearer's thought
forms: שספורי מעשיות מצדיקים. הינו ממה שארע להם

gloss_en: minut — heresy/sectarian unbelief, the state of denial into which the heart is enticed, linked to Asaf's 'my feet nearly slipped' (Ps 73)
natayu raglai — 'my feet slipped/turned aside' (Ps 73:2), Asaf's phrase for the feet-swerving that figures the lapse into minut (heresy)
kedushot nefulot — 'fallen holinesses': degraded holy potentials (fallen sparks) awaiting elevation to their place through commerce (massa u-mattan)
nitzotzot she-naflu — the fallen sparks of holiness (Lurianic term) scattered below, lifted and restored to their place via buying-and-selling

canonical_he: שישראל עושין רצונו של מקום, ונכללין בשרשם
gloss_en: Israel doing the will of the Omnipresent and being included in their Root — the purpose of creation: Israel's fulfilling His ratzon and re-cleaving into God, the Necessary Existent
forms: שישראל עושין רצונו של מקום, ונכללין בשרשם

canonical_he: נכלל כל העולם שנברא בשבילם, בחיוב המציאות
gloss_en: the inclusion of the whole world (created for Israel) in Necessary Existence — creation's elevation into chiyuv ha-metziut when Israel returns to its Root
forms: נכלל כל העולם שנברא בשבילם, בחיוב המציאות

gloss_en: nikhlal libo be-lev ha-tzaddik — one's heart becoming incorporated into the true tzaddik's heart through soul-love attachment (hitkashrut), expelling the spirit of folly
bittul be-emet — true self-nullification: the ego-annulment by which one's soul is absorbed into its Root in God, the Necessary Existent
yedi'ah — knowledge/da'at whose completeness removes all lack, suffering, and exile ('if you have acquired da'at, what do you lack?')
nikhlalim bo — being included/absorbed in Him (in complete Da'at/God), the state in which all deficiencies, troubles, and exile are resolved

canonical_he: נכללים שמאל בימין, וימין בשמאל ונעשים אחדות.
gloss_en: the mutual inclusion of left in right and right in left forming unity — reconciliation of semola/yemina (Korach vs. Aharon strife) achieved by hand-clapping
forms: נכללים שמאל בימין, וימין בשמאל ונעשים אחדות.

canonical_he: לשפך שיחו בתפלה לפני השם יתברך
gloss_en: lishpokh sicho bi-tefillah — pouring out one's speech in prayer before God, which stirs His mercies and opens the Supernal Heart to flow forth words
forms: לשפך שיחו בתפלה לפני השם יתברך

canonical_he: נכנסין כל הנדחין מקדשת ישראל לתוך הקדשה
gloss_en: the ingathering of all who were thrust out of Israel's holiness back into kedushah — nidchei Yisrael yechannes via self-sacrifice for kiddush Hashem, building holy speech
forms: נכנסין כל הנדחין מקדשת ישראל לתוך הקדשה

gloss_en: nikhna ha-kaved lifnei ha-moach — the liver (seat of appetite/blood) being subdued before the brain through fasting, restoring wisdom's shining face
the spiritual outcome whereby foolishness (kesilut, the kelipot's folly) is subdued and the intellect (sekhel) is elevated/magnified — the effect achieved through eating with kashrut (LM I:17)
niggun ba-yad — playing melody by hand upon an instrument (music-making with the hand), the act that subdues the imaginative faculty (medammeh)
the subduing of the medammeh and consequent attainment of zikaron — the imaginative faculty humbled by hand-played melody, opening memory (devekut-awareness of the World to Come)
nikhna ha-ruach di-klipah — the subjugation of the spirit of the husk (klipah's tallit/ruach) by the holy tallit-encompassment (makif, ruach chayim) and the 13 Attributes of Mercy

canonical_he: מזבח כתקונו, הינו שהאכילה בכשרות כראוי
gloss_en: mizbeach ke-tikkuno — the altar in its proper order, i.e., eating in fitting kashrut/propriety ('one's table atones like an altar'), which starves the klipot
forms: מזבח כתקונו, הינו שהאכילה בכשרות כראוי

gloss_en: nikhna'im ha-klipot, haynu ha-kesilut — the subjugation of the husks, i.e., the foolishness of the intellect, effected by the altar-aspect of proper eating

canonical_he: לעין בתורה, עד שמשיג חכמות התורה
gloss_en: iyyun ba-Torah until grasping its chokhmot — deep analytic Torah study attaining the Torah's wisdoms, producing anpin nehirin (shining countenance) that subdues gentile traits and lusts
forms: לעין בתורה, עד שמשיג חכמות התורה

gloss_en: the subduing of the character traits and desires of the idolatrous nations — the evil middot and lusts rooted in the darkened faces (anpin chashukhin), which are subjugated when one attains the Torah's wisdom (illuminated faces)
nimmol levavam — the circumcision of the heart: removal of its orlah (foreskin/blockage), creating a hollow in the heart that truly feels the pain of one's sins
nemalah — the ant of Proverbs 6:6 ('go to the ant, sluggard'), symbol of the sage who teaches wisdom and God's ways to the people

"a grease-stain found on his garments" (Talmudic phrase, cf. Shabbat 114a, רְבָב on a scholar's clothes) — used in LM 29 as the emblem of soiled garments signifying the blemish of the covenant (pgam ha-brit)

the drawing of wealth into length of days — the process (in Likutey Moharan I:60) whereby material riches (עשירות) are channeled into and contained within the aspect of longevity/length of days (אריכות ימים, the elder/Atik rectifications), so that wealth becomes bound to extended life rather than standing alone
nimtak ha-din — the sweetening/mitigation of a judgment, effected by moving from mochin de-katnut to mochin de-gadlut (Chokhmah)
making a beautiful garment for the tzaddik — the act of clothing the tzaddik finely, which serves to sweeten judgments
nimtak ha-dinim — the sweetening of the judgments (plural dinim), the effect produced by making a fine garment for the tzaddik
sweetening the din and charon af — mitigating judgment and divine wrath via the all-inclusive pidyon (redemption) at the eit ratzon of the 24 courts
sweetening of the idolatrous nations so they become converts (gerim) — transformation of gentiles through the sweetening of judgments
holy fervor/enthusiasm (hitlahavut she-bikdushah) — sacred ecstatic ardor termed 'the wine that gladdens' (yayin ha-mesameach)
nimtakim ha-gevurot/behorot — the sweetening of the harsh judgments (twice Elokim = ekev) at the heels through dancing, expelling the chitzonim
nimtakim kol ha-dinim — the sweetening of all judgments, achieved when Torah draws from supernal Chokhmah (even shetiyah, Holy of Holies)
nisayon — the trial/test of free choice, located together with the scale (matkela) and bechirah in kelipat nogah

miracles (nissim, plural of nes) — supernatural events above and contrary to the course of nature, wrought through prayer and faith and centered in the Land of Israel; not נָסִים 'fleeing' (participle of נו״ס) nor נֵס as mere 'banner/pole'
tehomot — the subterranean depths/abysses from which the Land of Israel drinks, an aspect of miracles (nissim, per 'vatehom kol ha-ir')
tehoma tata'ah — the 'lower depth' (Zoharic term), the abyss corresponding to lower miracles (nissim tata'in)
nissim tata'in — 'lower miracles,' miracles clothed in nature, corresponding to the lower depth (tehoma tata'ah) that waters the Land of Israel
tze ('Depart!') — the word addressed to idolatry in Isaiah 30:22, expounded as the aspect of journeying and displacement
nesiah ve-tiltul — journeying and wandering/displacement, the exile-travel state signified by 'tze' said to idols

"the Torah of the LORD" (torat HaShem) — in R. Nachman's reading of Avodah Zarah 19a on Psalms 1:2, the Torah as it belongs to God before one has labored in it: the hidden, not-yet-attained dimension of Torah (bechinat nistar, 'the hidden things belong to God'), corresponding to nishma ('we will hear'), as opposed to torato, 'his own Torah,' the revealed/naaseh portion

Sha"Kh (שַׁ"ךְ) — the kabbalistic number 320, the 320 judgments (Shach dinim): five times din (דין = 64, ×5 = 320), equal in gematria to na'ar (נער, 'lad'), associated with the bride/Malkhut as the aspect of concentrated judgments
NA'AR (נע"ר = 320) — gematria equivalent of ShaKh (320), the five-times-Elokim judgments of the bride/Malkhut before receiving the heart's alephs
ne'im zemirot Yisrael — 'sweet singer of Israel' (II Samuel 23), epithet of King David, the melodic aspect of Malkhut of David
hishtalshelut ha-gevurot as external fear — the downward chaining of the gevurot manifesting as outward/worldly fear (yirah chitzonit)
planting the reed in the sea of Chokhmah — Gabriel's na'atz kaneh ba-yam read as external gevurot-fear fixing the voice (kol from the kaneh) in wisdom
dances / dancing (rikkudin) — the joyful bodily act of dancing, especially at weddings and in worship, by which the feet are elevated and judgments sweetened
've-ha-niglot lanu u-levaneinu' (Deut 29:28) — 'the revealed things are for us and our children,' identified with na'aseh ('we will do')

the residual trace (reshimu) of the unity of Ein Sof that remains imprinted in a person after returning from ecstatic cleaving (devekut), preserving the knowledge of that unity in his restored conscious mind

entering the 'returning' (va-shov) phase — the ebb of 'running and returning' (ratzo va-shov) in which, after ecstatic self-nullification and cleaving to the Ein Sof, one returns to embodied existence and conscious mind (da'at) so that his being is sustained
explaining the matter in a language one understands — the tzaddik's act of translating Torah into the hearer's own tongue/level
na'aseh bi-vchinat chal — becoming 'profaned/wounded' (chal, from mecholal mi-peshaeinu), the tzaddik-Mashiach's state of bearing Israel's sufferings
shimush ha-chakham — serving/attending the Torah sage, the apprenticeship-service by which one becomes 'flesh' to the sage
becoming the aspect of flesh (basar) to the sage — the transformation of the attendant into the sage's own flesh through service

canonical_he: שמעורר בני אדם משנתם על־ידי ספורי מעשיות
gloss_en: awakening people from their sleep by telling stories — the tzaddik's rousing of spiritually asleep souls via sipurei ma'asiyot ('ve-alehu li-terufah')
forms: שמעורר בני אדם משנתם על־ידי ספורי מעשיות

gloss_en: shaping the letters for good — configuring the letter-combinations (tziruf otiyot) toward good so the prayer-request is fulfilled

the fulfillment of one's petition — 'his request is done/actualized' (naʿaseh baqashato): the granting of a prayer-request, brought from potential into actuality (through speech/Torah shaping the letters for good); not 'we will do' (naʿaseh of Sinai) nor a request merely uttered
making Da'at, i.e., Torah — producing knowledge/Torah ('mah') out of the double concealment (hastarah she-betokh hastarah, Esther/haster astir)

canonical_he: מש הגוף להנשמה בעשית מצוו‍ת מעשיות
gloss_en: the body serving the soul through performing practical mitzvot — physical mitzvah-action as the body's shimush of the neshamah
forms: מש הגוף להנשמה בעשית מצוו‍ת מעשיות

gloss_en: the body becoming 'flesh' (basar) to the soul — the state attained when the body serves the soul, completing Jerusalem (mevaser)
na'aseh ha-dibur — the formation/creation of speech, effected through charity which rests on trust (bitachon) rooted in intellect
ratzon as kisufin — the will identified with holy yearnings/longings, which forms the soul in potential
the soul made in potential (nefesh be-koach) — the soul's potential state created by yearning/will, awaiting actualization through speech
expressing one's desire aloud with the mouth — vocalizing the heart's longing, which actualizes the soul from potential
the soul made actual (nefesh be-fo'al) — the actualization of the potential soul through spoken utterance ('nafshi yatzah be-dabro')
the mouth/speech made through charity — formation of the peh (dibur), man's defining trait ('na'aseh adam'), via tzedakah
God becoming, as it were, in the aspect of a woman — the divine 'feminine' state of receiving delight when Israel fulfills His desire for their prayer
forming the speech of confession from them — transforming the sin-combinations engraved on one's bones into the words of vidui (verbal confession)
na'aseh moftim u-fla'ot — wonders and marvels being wrought (new heavens and earth) through praise spoken with strength eaten via Eretz Yisrael's shefa of truth
hishtokekut ba-lev — yearning/longing in the heart, which creates the soul and vowel-points in potential but requires verbal expression
nefesh u-nekudot be-koach — the soul and vowel points formed in potential by heart-yearning, prior to actualization through speech

canonical_he: העלאת מיין נוקבין של תורה ותפלה
gloss_en: the elevation of mayin nukvin (feminine waters) effected by the words of Torah study and prayer — the arousal from below through sacred speech that unites and makes peace above (Likutey Moharan I:75)
forms: העלאת מיין נוקבין של תורה ותפלה

gloss_en: the forging of a combination (tzeruf) from the fallen sparks (nitzotzot) whereby a world is made — cosmogonic act of birur/rectification underlying strife's transformation
