healing / medicinal remedy (refu'ah) — the cure of illness, whether bodily or spiritual, effected through means such as peace, faith, herbs, joy, or the shining sun
Shavuot, the Festival of Weeks — the holiday of the giving of the Torah (not שְׁבוּעוֹת 'oaths' nor generic 'weeks')
healing/remedy for the lungs (refu'ah le-ha-re'ah) — a cure for the lung organ (the five-lobed re'ah that moistens the body), effected e.g. by Shavuot/Torah or by oil; not any generic healing
medicinal remedies / cures (רְפוּאוֹת, plural of רְפוּאָה) — healing agents for bodily illness, such as herbal medicines; not 'healing' as an abstract act nor any other root
other people's wills that oppose one's own will — the inner definition of machaloket (conflict), annulled by fasting per 'nullify your will before His will' (Avot 2)
he'arat ha-raglayim — the illumination/light of the feet, revealed through dancing (rikkudin), paired with the illumination of the hands in clapping
'Adonai sefatai tiftach' (Psalms 51:17) — the verse opening the Amidah, 'O Lord, open my lips,' expounded as the aspect of wedding dancing
rikkudin shel chatunah — wedding dancing as a mystical act drawing the alephs/light of the heart down through the feet to the bride (Malkhut), sweetening her 320 judgments
reshimah — an engraved mark/inscription, like the letter tav inscribed on foreheads ('ve-hitvita tav,' Ezekiel 9:4); the trace-imprint sense of the root
rasha ve-ra lo — 'a wicked man who fares badly' (Berakhot 7a theodicy category): here the wicked person attached to the tzaddik whose halakhic opinion is NOT followed

canonical_he: רשע שמקרב להצדיק שאין הלכה כמותו
gloss_en: the wicked person who is drawn close to the tzaddik whose halakhic ruling is not accepted — the referent of 'rasha ve-ra lo' in the theodicy scheme
forms: רשע שמקרב להצדיק שאין הלכה כמותו

gloss_en: rasha ve-tov lo — 'a wicked man who prospers' (Berakhot 7a theodicy category): here the wicked person attached to the tzaddik whose halakhic opinion IS followed
the wicked person who is drawn close to the tzaddik whose halakhic ruling is accepted — the referent of 'rasha ve-tov lo' in the theodicy scheme
five times din — gematria device: din (64) × 5 = 320 (ShaKh), the harsh judgments of the bride/na'ar before the heh is drawn to her making five times 'Adonai'
tamar of the Sitra Achra — the demonic counterpart date-palm (temurah, 'exchange'), embodiment of the totality of harsh judgments opposing 'the tzaddik flourishes like a tamar'
se'or ke-kotevet — 'leaven the size of a date' (halakhic Yom Kippur measure, Berakhot/Yoma): leaven = concentrated judgments, the kotevet-date marking the Other Side's tamar
the phenomenon that one disciple is closer to the Rebbe than another — explained as due solely to his greater holy boldness (azut di-kedushah) to speak with him
the person who senses a slight impurity confusing him — one just outside/behind holiness (after the twelve tribes), disturbed by minor tumah, in the Rabbah bar bar Chanah tale
the aforementioned Jewish man's (the Israelite who had strayed) awakening/arousal to repentance (teshuvah), which restores even the wicked as a throne for holiness (Likutey Moharan I:4)

book (sefer) — a written sacred volume/text, as in a book of questions-and-answers formed from dispute, or the holy book equated by gematria with the Divine Name (not sfar 'border', sapar 'barber', or safar 'counted')
she'elot u-teshuvot — 'questions and answers' (responsa): the book generated from every dispute, punning teshuvah-answer with teshuvah-repentance
the attainment of the tachlit — meriting to reach the ultimate purpose/end, for whose sake the soul must ultimately leave the speech and 'glean in another field'

canonical_he: שבילי התורה, שיש בהם התבוננות גדול מאד.
gloss_en: shevilei ha-Torah — the hidden pathways of Torah containing very great contemplation, attainable only through great wealth ('if there is no flour, there is no Torah')
forms: שבילי התורה, שיש בהם התבוננות גדול מאד.

gloss_en: the breaking of the heart (shevirat ha-lev) — the heart shattered by shame/disgrace, as in 'cherpah shavrah libi' (Ps. 69:21), linked to forgetfulness and paralleled to the breaking of the Tablets ('the tablet of your heart')
shevirat ha-luchot — Moses' breaking of the Tablets, identified with the broken heart via 'write them on the tablet of your heart' (Proverbs 3)

the rectification of the coinage (tikkun ha-matbe'a) — Jacob's establishing/rectifying of coinage for the city (per the Talmudic reading of "vayichan penei ha-ir", Gen. 33:18), signifying in Likutey Moharan 23 the spiritual repair of money and the breaking of the craving for wealth through the shining light of the face
ruach nedivah — 'a generous/willing spirit' (Psalms 51:14): tzedakah as the cooling spirit that descends to quench the heart's burning craving for money
sheva gildei eina — the seven membranes/layers of the eye (Tikkunei Zohar), corresponding to Samson's seven locks and the seven middot of the mochin
sheva middot — the seven emotive attributes (lower sefirot) that pass fleetingly (cholfin) through the thought of the brain, matching the seven locks/eye-layers
shiv'ah gildei eina — the Tikkunei Zohar doctrine of the eye's seven layers (Intro 12, Tikkun 70), basis for the eyes being 'hairs'/seven machlefot of the head
shiv'im lashon — the seventy languages of the nations, identified with the storm wind/spirit of folly that rises via Targum-sleep to suckle from the Holy Tongue
shiv'im panim la-Torah — the seventy 'faces' (modes of interpretation) of the Torah, each distinct, clothed in stories to awaken the sleeper
shiv'im shanim — the seventy years (of a human lifespan), each different from the next, corresponding to the seventy faces of the Torah
shiv'ah ananim — the seven Clouds of Glory that form the sukkah, identified with the seven lamps (of the menorah) through which one attains divine influx
shiv'at yemei ha-mishteh — the seven days of wedding feasting after the chuppah, corresponding to the seven lamps/attainments of the surrounding light
shivrei luchot — the fragments of the broken first Tablets, the root of forgetfulness ('had the first Tablets not been broken, Torah would not be forgotten,' Eruvin 54)
b'nes — 'by miracle/sign': expounded as Shabbat, the eternal sign ('ot hi le-olam,' Exodus 31:17), the miraculous supra-natural order
the joy and delight of the World to Come — the future bliss identified with Shabbat ('a taste of the World to Come')
tefillah bi-dvekut — prayer said in devoted attachment to God, when the words flow willingly, elevating all previously scattered prayers
'shegurah tefillati be-fi' — R. Chanina ben Dosa's dictum (Berakhot 34b) 'my prayer is fluent in my mouth,' the sign of accepted prayer/devekut
the state in which God Himself prays — one's prayer becoming God's own prayer ('that He, blessed be He, will pray'), attained through Torah study
Lowliness/humility (shiflut) — the spiritual trait of holding oneself lowly, beneath one's own place and level, breaking one's pride before all others and even before one's own attained level

canonical_he: שומרת מההפך של עשירות, דהינו עניות,
gloss_en: the protective function of yirah guarding against poverty — fear of God as the treasure-house (otzar) that preserves wealth from its opposite, want
forms: שומרת מההפך של עשירות, דהינו עניות,

gloss_en: shokayim — the thighs/legs of the divine stature, symbolizing concealment ("the thigh is hidden"), identified with Esther as counterpart to Mordekhai's hands
shokin ve-raglin — thighs-and-legs as limbs of the supernal structure built through words of Torah and prayer, the "standing" aspect that elevates fallen sparks from food, drink, and clothing
the practice of reviewing one's learning 101 times — repetition of received teaching, contrasted with hearing the sage's fresh innovation directly
remembering what one receives from one's master — retaining the teacher's teaching, likened to ink whose clarity depends on hearing at the moment of innovation
the black of the eye (pupil, bat ayin) — the dark part of the eye that contracts and encompasses vast objects, symbol of holy tzimtzum/limitation
Shacharit — the morning prayer instituted by Avraham (Berakhot 26b), linked here to the "blackness" (shacharut) of dawn/Malkhut elevated through kindness

canonical_he: שצריך כל אחד לדבר בינו לבין קונו
gloss_en: the devotional practice of hitbodedut — each person speaking privately between himself and his Creator to make the point of wisdom shine and nullify the heart's foreskin
forms: שצריך כל אחד לדבר בינו לבין קונו

canonical_he: להמשיך את עצמו תמיד אל האמת לאמתו
gloss_en: the imperative to constantly draw oneself toward absolute truth (emet la-amito) — orienting one's descents and openings toward genuine truth so falls become ascents
forms: להמשיך את עצמו תמיד אל האמת לאמתו

gloss_en: guarding oneself from falsehood — avoidance of sheker as the condition for God's providence ("My eyes are on the faithful of the land") and closeness to divine Oneness
"shemor pitchei fikha" — the verse-phrase 'guard the openings of your mouth' (Micah 7:5), guarding speech in relation to trust and the procreative faculty

canonical_he: צריך האדם לצמצם אור התלהבות לבו
gloss_en: the requirement that a person contract (metzamtzem) the infinite blazing light of his heart's fervor — self-tzimtzum of enthusiasm so divine service becomes possible
forms: צריך האדם לצמצם אור התלהבות לבו

canonical_he: שיוכל לעבד את השם בהדרגה ובמדה
gloss_en: serving God with graduated measure (be-hadragah u-midah) — orderly, measured divine service enabled by contracting the heart's infinite fervor
forms: שיוכל לעבד את השם בהדרגה ובמדה

gloss_en: the attained capacity to hear melody (neginah) from any person — a rectified state achieved through nightly study of the Oral Torah/Gemara
conquering one's anger — subduing ka'as, the self-mastery linked to the reward of "a hand and a name" (yad va-shem) for keeping the Sabbaths
many mitzvot — a multitude of commandments performed, related to joy pervading the full stature of 248 limbs and 365 sinews
departing from nature (tiv'iyut) — transcending the natural order into divine providence (hashgachah), the totality of holiness attained via the Land of Israel
God's silence toward the sinner — the Holy One's forbearance (hecherashti, Ps. 50:21), which unlike human silence is not for Ehyeh but to reserve punishment for the World to Come
receiving one's punishment in the World to Come — the deferred retribution that is the purpose of God's silence toward sinners
subduing the material body (hakhna'at ha-chomer) — the soul "consuming the flesh" to unite the two inseparable companions (Chokhmah and Binah)
shir — song/melody as such, the future song (simple-double-triple-quadruple) linked by wordplay to Sarah's rulership (sarah/shir)
the simple-double-triple-quadruple song (shir pashut kaful meshulash meruba) — the future eschatological song of the fourfold expansion of God's Name, symbolized by the dalet of the letter Hei
she-yesh dai b'Elokuti — Rashi's exposition of the divine Name Shaddai: 'there is enough in My Godliness for every creature,' tied to guarding the covenant
hosting a Torah-scholar guest (hakhnasat orach talmid-chakham) — the act of receiving a sage as guest, remedying one's bad prayers
total nullification of the body as nothing (bittul ha-guf) — speaking Torah and prayer until the body becomes naught, 'one flesh' unified with speech
the verse-phrase 'cherpah shavrah libbi' — 'disgrace has broken my heart' (Ps. 69:21), disgrace identified as the aspect of forgetfulness
mas (מַס) — tribute / compulsory labor-service, as in Jacob's blessing 'va-yehi le-mas oved' (Gen 49:15), the tribute-bearing servant; homiletically linked by sound to מסמוס (dissolving/melting away)
the Supernal Land (eretz ha-elyonah) — the upper 'earth' identified with the Shekhinah, God's indwelling Presence

canonical_he: מי שזוכה ללמד להשכינה, שלמודו עולה להשכינה
gloss_en: learning Torah 'for the Shekhinah' — the elevated mode of study whereby one's learning ascends to the Shekhinah, the intermediary between humans and God
forms: מי שזוכה ללמד להשכינה, שלמודו עולה להשכינה

gloss_en: shulchan — the table, associated with intellect (sekhel via shikkul wordplay) and the deeds of charity that perfect the mind
the very great and lofty intellect (sekhel gadol ve-gavoah) — the supreme Da'at of Shavuot, which is supernal kindness and great compassion (God as merciful elder at Sinai)

canonical_he: שונא בצע, שישנא הממון בתכלית השנאה
gloss_en: sone betza — hating unjust gain: despising money with utmost hatred, from the side of Malkhut, prerequisite for attaining the lower intellect
forms: שונא בצע, שישנא הממון בתכלית השנאה

gloss_en: hakdamot — preliminary premises/introductions, the preparatory steps of reasoning constituting the lower intellect that precedes the higher
sa'ara ukama — 'black hair' (Zoharic term), symbol of the lower intellect from the side of Malkhut
the supernal intellect and Da'at (sekhel ve-da'at elyon) — the fiftieth gate of Binah, the mikveh of Shavuot
not distinguishing between kindness (chesed) and judgment (din) — the unification of chasadim and gevurot that constitutes true Da'at, blessing 'ha-tov ve-hameitiv' on all
fasting or Shabbat eating — either practice alone as sufficient means to nullify and subdue one's enemies (vs. charity for abundant peace)
nullifying and subduing the enemies (bittul ve-hakhna'at ha-oyvim) — the defeat of one's foes achieved through fasting or Shabbat eating
the heart's flame ascending continually of itself (shalhevet ha-lev olah me-eleha) — the spontaneous rising fervor of the heart born from the intellect's motion
tzedakah la-aniyim — charity given to the poor, as in 'sun on Shabbat is charity for the poor' (Ta'anit 8b), increasing peace
Yaakov (Jacob) the patriarch as the embodiment of he'arat panim — the illumination of the face (his beauty like Adam's), the source of peace
he'arat panim / hadrat panim — illumination and splendor of the divine countenance, the shining face that is the prerequisite for peace
kavod she-mekhabed yirei Hashem — the act of honoring God-fearers, by which the exiled glory (kavod) returns to its root in yirah (fear)

'ad she-tikhleh regel min ha-shuk' — the halakhic time limit for lighting Chanukah lamps ('until foot traffic ceases from the marketplace'), read as the cessation of commerce that betokens universal peace

domestic peace (shalom bayit) — the particular, localized peace within one's own house/body, attained through fear of God elevating glory to its root, which in turn enables prayer and leads to universal peace (Likutey Moharan I:14)
de-nashkei ar'a u-reki'a — the spot 'where earth and heaven kiss' in Rabbah bar bar Chanah's tale, symbolizing peace within one's own bones/self

the universal/all-encompassing peace (shalom ha-kelali) — the general peace drawn into the entire world and all creation, as opposed to localized domestic peace (shelom bayit), attained through prayer in Likutey Moharan I:14
shalom ha-klali as shleimut ha-olamot — the universal peace defined as the perfection/completion of all the worlds, attained through prayer-as-korban (drawing the worlds near to wholeness)
shilum sakhar — requital/payment of reward (here, punishment-recompense to the wicked in the World to Come), linked to the letter Heh via 'hegeh va-hi' (Eruvin 21)
shulchan shebi-kdushah — the holy table, a symbol of Malkhut/kingship whose blemish (via lust for eating) lets the brazen-faced seize honor

"a pure (clear) language" — the phrase שָׂפָה בְרוּרָה from Zephaniah 3:9 ("then I will transform the peoples to a pure language, that they may all call upon the Name of HaShem"), which Rabbi Nachman reads as the future perfection/completeness of speech (shlemut ha-dibbur) attained when all humanity calls upon God, achieved through faith
'yakiru ve-yed'u kol yoshvei tevel' — the Aleinu phrase 'all inhabitants of the world will recognize and know,' signifying the perfection of da'at (knowledge of God)
'yokhal teref' — 'he devours prey' (Benjamin the wolf, Gen 49:27), signifying the completed altar built 'in the portion of the tearer' (Toref) in Benjamin's territory
shleimut ha-simchah — the perfection/completion of joy, achieved through yirah (fear = 'nishma'/prayer), which grounds holy boldness (azut di-kdushah)
le-karev davka ha-meruchakim — the action of drawing near specifically the distant ones (even idolaters) to Israel's faith, per Zephaniah 3:9
shleimut ve-kishutei emunah — the completeness and adornments of faith (emunah), consisting precisely in bringing the far-off close to God
shleimut la-mochin — completeness/wholeness of the mochin (mental faculties), i.e., pure holy thought needed to sweeten judgments on Rosh HaShanah
shlosh-esreh middot — the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy God arranged wrapped in a tallit (RH 17b), identified as the holy ruach-chaim (spirit of life)
eilu ha-shloshah sikhliyim — the three intellectual faculties of Torah wisdom, each containing Chokhmah-Binah (Yud-Heh), together numerically 'Adam' (45)
shalosh pe'amim Y-H — three times the divine name Yud-Heh (15×3=45), the gematria of 'adam,' encoding Chokhmah-Binah within each of the three intellects
shalosh klipot ha-nal — the three impure husks (kelipot) constituting the orlah (foreskin), the root-source of disgrace removed by circumcision
'teshuvat ha-shanah' — the phrase 'the return/turn of the year' (II Sam 11:1), read as the season of the three festivals, days of judgment and repentance
shalosh regalim — the three pilgrimage festivals (Pesach, Shavuot, Sukkot) as days of judgment/teshuvah when the exiled Malkhut is brought out
gildana — the sea-fish in Rav Ashi's Talmudic tale, whose letters encode the divine name AGLA ('Atah Gibor Le'olam Adonai'), an aspect of gevurot
meshaber et libo — breaking one's heart/spirit within oneself in shame over one's fall, the inner act constituting a burnt-offering (olah)

the Divine Name Chata"kh (חֲתַ"ךְ) — the kabbalistic Name of sustenance formed from the final letters of "פּוֹתֵחַ אֶת יָדֶךָ" (Psalms 145:16), associated with cutting/sawing apart (nesirah), as in the Arizal's kavvanot
nesirah — the kabbalistic 'sawing apart' of the back-to-back configuration (as with Adam) enabling face-to-face union, effected via the name Chata"kh

baki — 'expert, proficient' (Hebrew בָּקִי): mastery/expertise, specifically the twofold expertise 'expert in running forward, expert in returning' (baki be-ratzo, baki be-shov), whose letters are homiletically identified with the Divine Name YB"K (gematria 112)
shem YB"K — the divine name Yud-Bet-Kuf (gematria 112), whose letters spell 'baki' (expert), underlying the twofold expertise 'baki be-ratzo, baki be-shov'
shefa gashmiyut — material/physical abundance, identified with the 'left' side of Torah ('in her left hand riches and honor')
Korach — the Levite rebel against Aaron, archetype of the left (smola) opposing the right, root-pattern of all machloket (strife)
smola — the kabbalistic 'left' side (vs. yemina/right), the polarity whose inclusion into the right via hand-clapping nullifies strife
smolah — 'her left' (of Torah, Prov 3:16), the left-side aspect into which the Tanna slipped by a hairsbreadth error while teaching

Names (שֵׁמוֹת) — holy/divine Names, i.e. sacred Names of God such as 'Eheyeh Asher Eheyeh' engraved on the clubs that subdue the yetzer hara, identified with the Torah (all of Torah being Names of God); distinct from the homograph שַׁמּוֹת 'desolations'
shmirat ha-brit via mezuzah — guarding the covenant through the mezuzah scroll, which nullifies coveting/lust for money ('lo tachmod' ↔ 'u-khtavtam al mezuzot')
she-nikhlalim yachad kol ha-nefashot — the merging/inclusion of all souls (each a 'candle') together into one light, generating joy ('or tzaddikim yismach')
min ha-mitzvot — the commandments as the primary source of joy ('pikudei Hashem... mesamchei lev'), the joy that lights up the face

canonical_he: נעשה ונשמע, שהוא בחינות תורה ותפלה וכו
gloss_en: na'aseh ve-nishma as Torah u-tefillah — the Sinai declaration 'we will do and we will hear' identified as the pair Torah ('do') and prayer ('hear')
forms: נעשה ונשמע, שהוא בחינות תורה ותפלה וכו

gloss_en: nirsham ha-kol ba-lev — the voice's imprint inscribed on the heart (tevel = tav-lev, 'mark on the heart,' Ezek 9:4), the thunder that straightens the heart
simchah gedolah ve-nitchadshu ha-mochin — the state of great joy that renews one's mochin (mental faculties), arising from knowing one's lack is in the Shekhinah

canonical_he: שיסיר עקמומיות שבלבו, שיהא לו ישרות לב
gloss_en: hasarat akmumiyut she-ba-lev — removing the crookedness of the heart to attain yishrut lev (uprightness of heart), the precondition for joy ('u-le-yishrei lev simchah')
forms: שיסיר עקמומיות שבלבו, שיהא לו ישרות לב

gloss_en: simchatan shel Yisrael — 'the joy of Israel,' an epithet of the heart/Shekhinah whose exile is the exile of Israel's joy
'yoshev ohalim' — Jacob's epithet 'dweller in tents' (Gen 25:27), read as the aspect of heaven ('He stretched them out like a tent to dwell in,' Isa 40:22)
shemi'ah — hearing, the faculty by which the heart is aroused: the forceful voice strikes the brain (galgalta de-mocha) producing thunder that awakens the heart

canonical_he: כשיוצא משרירות הלב, ומשבר לבו האבן
gloss_en: yotzei mi-shrirut ha-lev u-meshaber lev ha-even — exiting the heart's stubbornness and shattering the heart of stone, i.e., leaving imagination for intellect
forms: כשיוצא משרירות הלב, ומשבר לבו האבן

gloss_en: shamir — the legendary stone-cutting worm/agent (used for the Temple stones), symbolizing what subdues the stone heart so one follows intellect over imagination
Guarding oneself against sexual immorality (ni'uf/adultery) — the protective practice of shielding one's purity from lustful transgression, associated with withstanding the serpent's counsel
shmirat tzitzit — the guarding afforded by the tzitzit fringes over the eyes, protecting from the serpent's counsel and from adultery ('lo taturu... acharei eineikhem')
simlah as tzitzit — the garment Shem and Yefet laid over Noah (Gen 9:23), read in Tikkunei Zohar as tzitzit, the covering that shields from sexual sin

The paired Kabbalistic term 'Yichuda Ila'ah and Yichuda Tata'ah' — the Supernal Unification and the Lower Unification, the two divine unifications enacted respectively by 'Shema Yisrael' and 'Baruch Shem Kevod Malchuto' (Zohar Bereishit 18b), corresponding in Likutey Moharan I:11 to the two aspects of guarding the covenant (shemirat ha-brit)

canonical_he: לשבר הגדלות והכבוד של עצמו לגמרי
gloss_en: shattering one's own gadlut and self-honor completely — the act of breaking personal arrogance/pride so that God's honor becomes whole, achieved via shmirat habrit in both unifications (LM I:11)
forms: לשבר הגדלות והכבוד של עצמו לגמרי

gloss_en: niggun played by hand — instrumental melody as the aspect of joy (simchah), the hand-music that gathers the good spirit from the evil spirit (LM I:54)
guarding the memory (shmirat ha-zikaron) — the practice of constantly remembering the World to Come, protecting the faculty of holy remembrance from forgetfulness (LM I:54)
guarding oneself from ka'as — restraint from anger as the essential protection of one's soul/name and of the wealth-flow being bestowed from Above (LM I:68)
shmirat ha-shem / shmirat ha-nefesh — the paired guarding of one's name and soul, effected solely by refraining from anger, per Job 18:4 'he tears his soul in his anger' (LM I:68)
the lachluchit (bodily moisture/humors) that ascends to the brain — physiological fluid functioning as the 'oil' feeding the wick (brain) and flame (soul), sustaining the intellect via the lungs
beginning to compose a commentary — the moment a Torah expositor starts to offer an interpretation, requiring prior outpoured prayer to arouse the heart's warm words from the rock/heart (sela)
speaking much with him (the Rebbe) — the action of frequent bold conversation with one's master, enabled by holy azut, which is what makes a disciple 'closer'
becoming more aroused — the heightened spiritual awakening a disciple gains through holy boldness and increased speech with the tzaddik

canonical_he: כשמוציאם אל הדבור, ובונה מהם דבור דקדשה
gloss_en: bringing the sparks out into speech and building holy speech from them — the tikkun-act of constructing dibbur d'kedushah, 'vayiven et ha-tzela' rectifying the limping thigh (tzole'a)
forms: כשמוציאם אל הדבור, ובונה מהם דבור דקדשה

gloss_en: being redeemed through teshuvah from the malkhut of the kelipot — liberation of the holy Kingship (dalet, 'nothing of its own') from the four kingdoms of the Sitra Achra via repentance, the essence of Yom Tov

Rosh Hashanah — the Jewish New Year festival on 1 Tishrei, the annual day of judgment and shofar-blowing (the 'head of the year'), homiletically linked to sleep/awakening, the head/mochin, and gathering by the tzaddik; not the Talmudic tractate of that name nor a generic 'beginning of a year'
koach u-fo'al — the pair potential-and-actualization, mapped onto the two hands right and left as instruments through which spirit comes into existence
the two hands, right and left — bodily limbs as kelei ha-asiyah where the ruach is revealed ('into Your hand I entrust my spirit'), symbolizing potential and act

Jacob (the patriarch) together with his twelve sons who descended to Egypt — collectively embodying prayer, as the aspect of the twelve versions/gates of prayer (nuschaot/shaarei tefillah) brought down into exile
the twelve nuschaot (liturgical rites) of prayer — the twelve prayer-versions corresponding to Yaakov and his twelve sons, brought down into Egyptian exile
the twelve gates of prayer — the twelve heavenly sha'arei tefillah through which each tribe's prayer ascends, embodied in Yaakov and his sons
speech becoming rectified and built — the state of dibbur repaired/constructed through abundant mitzvot and joy nullifying the anxiety of sin, enabling confession
expelling the ruach shtut (spirit of folly) from within oneself — the urgent act of driving out the folly-spirit clinging to the heart, accomplished by soul-love binding to the true tzaddik
'Mi' (fifty gates of Binah) through which the mouth (peh) comes into being — Exodus 4:11 'Mi sam peh la-adam,' the mouth formed via the fifty of Understanding at the Exodus

canonical_he: שעל ידי שדנים את הכל לכף זכות
gloss_en: judging everyone favorably (dan le-khaf zekhut) — the practice of finding merit for all, which enables silence under insult and forms the chirik point
forms: שעל ידי שדנים את הכל לכף זכות

gloss_en: remaining silent when someone shames him — the response of shtikah to public disgrace (enabled by judging favorably), forming the chirik/footstool point beneath the Alef
atzat nachash / atzat resha'im — the serpent's counsel, counsel of the wicked (the 'scorpions' encircling Sinai) that blocks receiving the tzaddikim's counsel of true seed
the principle that the main strengthening of the Gevurot comes only through Chasadim — inclusion of the left in the right, kindness empowering the severities (while fear still precedes)

canonical_he: שעקר עשיה ותקון של לשון הקדש
gloss_en: the making/rectification of leshon ha-kodesh depending on yirah — 'vayiven, He made her like a storehouse': the Holy Tongue's tikkun hangs on 'the fear of God is His treasury' (Isa. 33:6)
forms: שעקר עשיה ותקון של לשון הקדש

gloss_en: the hairs (se'arot) of the wise man — the chakham's surplus mentalities (motrei mochin) figured as hairs, which become gates for transmitting his wisdom
sha'ar with the shin vowelled to the right (kamatz/yamin) — 'gate': the wise man's hair-surplus read as ShA'aR, gates opening wisdom for divine service (vs. se'ar of the fool)
the Gate of Aram (sha'ar Aram/Rome) — the specific gate in R. Yosei ben Kisma's prophecy that must fall three times before Ben David comes
the gate of the Sitra Achra — the Other Side's gate (identified with the Gate of Aram), whose repeated collapse precedes Messiah building the gates of holiness
speech in its completeness (dibbur bi-shleimut) — perfected speech, the 'clear lip' (safah berurah, Zeph. 3:9) when all nations call on God, completing the letters of speech
penei ha-menorah — the 'face of the lamp' (Num. 8:2) symbolizing the divine influx (shefa Eloki) toward which the seven lamps/orifices shine

canonical_he: שיקדש את פיו וחטמו ועיניו ואזניו
gloss_en: sanctifying one's mouth, nose, eyes, and ears — the prerequisite purification of the four facial organs (truth, fear of Heaven, guarded eyes, faith in sages) to receive the divine influx
forms: שיקדש את פיו וחטמו ועיניו ואזניו

gloss_en: the aforementioned shefa Eloki — the divine influx identified with ruach ha-kodesh and the sukkah, a makif-intellect too great to enter the brain, encircling the head
doubled abundance (shefa kefulah) — the 'lechem mishneh' double portion (Ex. 16) / 'mirkevet ha-mishneh' of Yosef, granted for subduing Amalek's kelipah and rectifying the brit
'mayim mayim' (water, water — Chagigah 14b warning) — symbol of falsehood: tears/salty water that increases rather than quenches thirst
being drawn after the medammeh — the state of following the imaginative faculty of the heart instead of ascending to intellect, equated with stubbornness of heart
shrirut lev — 'stubbornness of heart' (Deut. 29:18): the stone-heart condition of following the heart's imagination, broken by the shamir
the six days (of creation/week) — corresponding to the six handbreadths of the amah/brit, all 'rested' into the seventh day, Shabbat, which is the covenant (Ex. 31:16)
the six tefachim (handbreadths) of the cubit — measure of the amah/brit in the circumcision-kavvanah, paralleling the seraph's six wings and the six weekdays
the Six Orders of the Mishnah (Shas) — corresponding to Metatron whose dominion is the six weekdays, aspect of the lower unification (yichuda tata'ah)
tikkun of the kaneh (windpipe/voice-organ) — rectifying the vocal conduit ('kenei lekha chaver' read as kaneh), linked to hearing the niggun and building one's malkhut

canonical_he: שעקר עבודת השם, לזכות למדות ומעשים טובים,
gloss_en: the principle that the essence of avodat Hashem is attaining good middot and good deeds — service in measured gradation, possible only via tzimtzum of the heart's infinite flame
forms: שעקר עבודת השם, לזכות למדות ומעשים טובים,

gloss_en: joy and gladness (sason ve-simcha) — the paired biblical expression for exultant rejoicing, in LM I:179 the state of joy whose full stature is built up through fasting and attained when there is peace
chalal ha-semali she-balev — the left chamber/cavity of the heart, the anatomical-spiritual site where the evil inclination dwells
she-sham medor ha-yetzer hara — the left heart-chamber described as the dwelling place (medor) of the evil inclination (yetzer hara)

"two mouths" (שְׁתֵּי פִּיּוֹת) — the two edges of the double-edged sword (חרב פיפיות, Tehillim 149) as expounded in Likutey Moharan 2, identified with prayer's twofold mouth (פי שנים): praise of God and petition for one's needs; not the numeral phrase in any mundane sense
shtei pe'amim ha-shem YB"K — twice the divine Name YaBaK (gematria 112), whose double (224) equals derekh, the 'way in the sea' of the Elul kavanot
the keruvim (cherubim) — the winged angelic figures atop the Ark of the Covenant, from between which prophecy and the holy spirit are drawn
shtei tzipporim — the two birds (of the metzora's purification/of holiness), source of prophecy and building of holy Malkhut, corresponding to the keruvim
me-atar de-nevi'im yankin — the supernal place/site from which the prophets suckle, the source-locus of prophecy (Zoharic phrase)
cha"sh — the letter-pair chet-shin of ChaShMaL denoting silence (chash), the holy quiet of bearing insult without reply
shetok kakh alah be-machashavah — 'Be silent! Thus it arose in thought' (Menachot 29b), God's reply to Moshe on Rabbi Akiva's fate, silence before the supernal unknowable thought
tav — the letter Tav as a mark of engraving/inscription ('ve-hitvita tav,' Ezekiel 9), the imprint that grace (chen) carves in the listener's heart
the beloved object's reciprocal yearning back toward the one who longs for it — the male-desire pole that generates a male soul
te'avuteih di-dekhar — 'the desire of the male' (Zohar Lekh Lekha 85b), the reciprocal yearning that fashions a male soul (nefesh dekhar)
a person's own initial yearning/longing for a thing — the female-desire pole of the coupling that fashions a female soul
te'avuteih de-nukva — 'the desire of the female' (Zohar Lekh Lekha 85b), the yearning that fashions a female soul (nefesh nukva)
ta'avot u-middot ra'ot — lusts and evil character traits, the 'darkened faces' (anpin chashukhin) deriving from the seventy nations
love arriving of itself once fear is given precedence — ahavah (male) automatically pursuing yirah (female) as an owner seeks his lost object
teven — 'straw' (in Yochani and Mamre's taunt to Moshe, Menachot 85a), symbol standing for tevunah, the Torah's understanding
tevunah — understanding/discernment ('tevunah tintzrekha,' Proverbs 2), the Torah insights Moshe sought to instill in Israel
hearing the quarrels between tzaddikim — the act of overhearing disputes of the righteous, which is really a rebuke for one's own blemished brain-drops
nissin ila'in — supernal/upper miracles, the higher class of miracles corresponding to the upper depth (tehom ila'ah)
tehom ila'ah — the supernal/upper depth (abyss), the kabbalistic upper tehom from which supernal miracles flow and the Land of Israel drinks

canonical_he: תשבעו ולא תהיו משקעים בתאות אכילה.
gloss_en: being satisfied with whatever one eats and not sunk in the craving for food — the state of broken ta'avat akhilah
forms: תשבעו ולא תהיו משקעים בתאות אכילה.

canonical_he: תהיו בבחינת נשיאות פנים, ונזונין ממדת אמת.
gloss_en: the resulting state of nesi'ut panim — receiving the Divine 'lifting of the face' (favor) and being sustained from the attribute of truth
forms: תהיו בבחינת נשיאות פנים, ונזונין ממדת אמת.

gloss_en: hitgalut ha-chesed — the revelation of Chesed (kindness) via wisdom and the rebuker's opened mouth, which cuts the dalet free of the four exiles
breaking the body's brazenness and toughness (azut ha-guf) through holy-boldness voices and the sigh that shatters a person's body

canonical_he: תוכל הנשמה להתקרב עצמה אל הגוף
gloss_en: the soul's consequent ability to draw near the body — the neshamah safely approaching the body to share its perceptions once its brazenness is broken
forms: תוכל הנשמה להתקרב עצמה אל הגוף

gloss_en: olat tamid — the daily burnt-offering (Temple sacrifice), the holy 'tamid' that overpowers the worm of the kelipah and sweetens Leah's judgments
tola'at Yaakov — 'the worm of Jacob' (Isaiah 41:14), Israel as the holy worm-aspect embodied in the olat tamid, opposing the impure worm of the kelipah
ve-shavita shivyo — 'and you take his captives captive' (Deut 21:10), scriptural phrase read as capturing the Torah, per 'You ascended on high, you took captives' (Ps 68:19)
money (ma'ot) given as charity to a Torah scholar — the coins donated to support a talmid chakham, which Rabbi Nachman teaches are the aspect of Torah itself and thus cannot be extinguished by sin
naval — the wicked fool/Naval as acronym for the lamed-bet (32) netivot, hence the Torah called 'novlot' (fallen fruit) of supernal Wisdom
kanfei re'ah — the lobes/'wings' of the lungs that fan the heart lest it burn the body, symbol of the Torah cooling the heart's fire
kinnor shel chamesh nimin — the five-stringed harp, symbol of the Torah (whose graspers 'hold the harp,' Zohar Tzav 32a)
mamlekhet — 'kingdom' in 'a kingdom of priests' (Exodus 19:6), signifying the revealed Torah (nigleh) by which kings reign, the Malkhut everyone needs
aliyat ha-yirah li-vechinat da'at — the elevation of fear to its root in Da'at, symbolized by the frog (tzefardea = tzipor de'ah, 'bird of knowledge')

canonical_he: שמקשרין היראה על־ידי משפט לבחינת דעת
gloss_en: binding fear to Da'at by means of mishpat (judgment) — the act that earns revealed Torah, then prayer, then the secrets of Torah
forms: שמקשרין היראה על־ידי משפט לבחינת דעת

canonical_he: חשך, הינו מסירת־נפש, שמשחיר פניו כעורב
gloss_en: choshekh as mesirat nefesh — darkness meaning self-sacrifice that blackens one's face like a raven, the price of attaining the Torah's secrets ('He made darkness His secret place')
forms: חשך, הינו מסירת־נפש, שמשחיר פניו כעורב

gloss_en: raising the attribute of fear (yirah) to its root — the prerequisite practice for tasting the hidden light, the Torah's future secrets

prayer offered with mesirat nefesh (self-sacrifice) — tefillah in which one surrenders and annuls all one's physicality, thereby transcending limitation; in Likutey Moharan I:15 the means of attaining the hidden Torah (the limitless Torah of the future) already in this world
David — King David as personification of the Oral Torah (Torah she-be'al peh), whose 'Tehillah le-David' addresses its fall into mixed combinations
Rachel — the matriarch Rachel as symbol of the Oral Torah, 'like a ewe before her shearers' from whom all shear and decide halakhot that become garments
meriting the wisdoms of the Torah — attained by 'seeking His face always,' i.e., through charity given for the Land of Israel
takhlit shel kol ha-nivra'im — the ultimate purpose of all created beings, identified with the perfection of the letters culminating in the yud (World to Come)
kallah — bride (the betrothed woman as symbol of Malkhut/Shekhinah and of the Torah betrothed to Israel); the noun כַּלָּה, not the verb כָּלָה 'to cease/consume' nor kilyah 'destruction'
nefesh David — the soul of David ('va-tekhal nefesh David,' 2 Sam 13:39), identified with tekhelet, the blue that 'consumes all and destroys all' (judgments/gevurot)
avukah shel or — a torch of light: parable-image for the talmid chakham who lights the way past thorns (tzome'ach) and pits (domem), punning avuk/attached to Torah's light
she'erit — 'the remnant' of Micah 7:18, homiletically read as sherayim/leftovers: one who makes himself insignificant, for whom God passes over transgression
shuruk — the Hebrew vowel-point of three dots (kubbutz form), symbolizing the three drops/three mochin descending from brain toward the kidneys

the 'three dots' (telat tippin, Aramaic) — the three points forming the shuruq vowel per Zohar/Tikkun 56, homologous to the three mochin (brains) and to the drop (tippah) of seed descending from the brain
telat mochin — the three brains/mentalities (kabbalistic mochin triad), paralleled to the three drops of the shuruk vowel and the seminal drop descending from brain to kidneys
tam — 'wholesome/simple' as in 'Yaakov ish tam' (Gen 25:27), symbol of the inner intellect (sekhel) present in every thing
hitlahavut ve-chamimut la-Shem — the state of burning enthusiasm and warmth toward God, kindled through bodily movement in devotion
tenu'ah — physical movement/motion as the generator of spiritual heat (like friction melting wax), rooted in thought and arousing fervor for God

canonical_he: שמה שתעשו משפט, ותצילו גזול מיד גוזלו
gloss_en: the act of executing mishpat by rescuing the robbed from his robber — judicial rescue of stolen property (per Isaiah 1:17), which saves the victim's children's souls
forms: שמה שתעשו משפט, ותצילו גזול מיד גוזלו

gloss_en: 'you do good for the children' — the beneficial effect on the sons/daughters (bechinat banim) achieved by performing justice and rescuing the robbed

canonical_he: תפלה תלוי בלב, שישים כל לבו עליה
gloss_en: the principle that prayer depends on the heart — placing one's whole heart into tefillah, opposite of 'honoring with lips while the heart is far' (Isa 29:13)
forms: תפלה תלוי בלב, שישים כל לבו עליה

gloss_en: 'Tov Hashem la-kol' (Ps 145:9) — the verse-phrase 'God is good to all,' read as the aspect of prayer/faith that God alone supplies healing, livelihood, and everything

canonical_he: שלום־בית יהא שלום בעצמיו, בין גופו ונפשו
gloss_en: shelom bayit as inner peace within one's own bones — harmony between one's body and soul, the prerequisite peace through which one merits prayer
forms: שלום־בית יהא שלום בעצמיו, בין גופו ונפשו

gloss_en: prita sifvateih — 'his lips move/are opened' (Talmudic phrase), read as the aspect of prayer per 'Adonai, open my lips' (Ps 51:17)
Emor — the opening word 'Say [to the Kohanim]' (Lev 21:1), read as the aspect of prayer/declaration per 'et Hashem he'emarta' (Deut 26:17)
the devotional practice of binding oneself in prayer to the tzaddikim of the generation, each of whom is an aspect of Moshe-Mashiach
tefillah be-sekhel tzach — praying with a clear, lucid mind, attainable only after complete teshuvah removes the heart's foreskin
the principle that prayer subsists in the air/atmosphere of Eretz Yisrael — standing (amidah) prayer as 'before Hashem your God,' i.e., the Land of Israel
the teaching that a prayer fluent and pleasing in one's mouth is accepted — praying even without devekut, since fluency signals acceptance
the task of elevating and rectifying speech (dibbur) — raising the word to its source (Malkhut-peh, the sea), prerequisite for attaining tefillin
hitpa'arut shel Yisrael — Israel's glorying/adornment in God, identified with tefillin which are called pe'er (glory), source of fear falling on the nations
tefillin shel HaKadosh Barukh Hu — God's own tefillin (Berakhot 6a), the aspect of God's glorification in Israel ('Who is like Your people Israel')

tekumah le-ha-rinnah — the 'arising/restoration of the joyous song (rinnah)': the reestablishment and empowerment of holy melody/song, effected through nighttime study of the Oral Torah (Gemara), per LM I:3's reading of 'kumi roni ba-lailah' (arise, sing in the night)
the specific list of the Ten Psalms (16, 32, 41, 42, 59, 77, 90, 105, 137, 150) constituting Rebbe Nachman's Tikkun HaKlali

canonical_he: תקון גדול מאד מאד למקרה חס ושלום
gloss_en: the Tikkun HaKlali as 'a very very great remedy' for a nocturnal emission (mikreh lo tahor) — reciting the ten Psalms on the day it occurs
forms: תקון גדול מאד מאד למקרה חס ושלום

gloss_en: tikkun ha-milah — the rectification effected by circumcision, the aspect of tikkun ha-brit; man created incomplete so as to perfect himself
the action of bringing people back in teshuvah — 'extracting the precious from the vile' (Jer 15:19), itself a rectification for keri (seminal emission)
tikkun ha-ka'as — the rectification of anger, accomplished through fasting; symbolized by chametz ('chamutz begadim' coming from Edom/the liver)
the specific remedy of rectifying anger by means of fasting — subduing the liver/Edom heat through abstention from eating (chametz-aspect)
tikkun ha-malkhut — the rectification of fallen Malkhut/kingship, returning it through fire ('pass it through fire') via verbal confession before the scholar
tikkun ha-me'uvat — 'setting straight what is crooked,' the aspect of Yosef ('God has gathered [asaf] my disgrace,' Gen 30:23)
tikkun ha-re'ut bi-shleimut — the complete rectification of eyesight/vision achieved on Shabbat (light restored by Kiddush after being diminished by large strides)
tokpa de-dina — 'the intensity of judgment' (Aramaic), the harsh-judgment force of the kelipot linked to sadness ('vayit'atzev el libo,' Gen 6:6)
shigyonot — 'errors/inadvertences' (Hab 3:1), the aspect of Targum/Tree of Knowledge: a mixture of good and evil like the inadvertent sin
shogeg — the inadvertent sinner, whose deed is evil but intention good: a mixture of good and evil paralleling Targum and the Tree of Knowledge
the voice/sound of melody (kol ha-niggun) — the audible sound produced by musical song, which in LM 1:22 is the aspect of teruah/shofar and in LM 2:8 waters the garden and makes its fragrances grow

canonical_he: תשאר אך יראת־השם ולא יראה אחרת
gloss_en: the state in which only fear of Heaven remains and no other fear — achieved by judging one's own affairs (mishpat), removing all mundane dreads
forms: תשאר אך יראת־השם ולא יראה אחרת

gloss_en: yarka — 'vegetables/greens' (Aramaic), midrashically a symbol of teshuvah via 'vayarek et chanikhav'/orikan with Parashat Shoftim ('the fearful and fainthearted')
'kol ha-zove'ach et yitzro' — 'whoever slaughters his evil inclination' (with confession), the Talmudic phrase identified as the aspect of teshuvah
teshuvah on one's first teshuvah — repenting over the earlier repentance itself, since even 'I have sinned' was said with ulterior motive
teshuvah sheniyah — the second repentance (over the slaughter of the yetzer/first teshuvah), aspect of the honor of the World to Come outshining the first

teshuvat ha-mishkal — 'repentance of the counterweight': the penitential practice (from the Rokeach's system) of counterbalancing a sin, measure for measure, by accepting suffering or restorative acts equal in weight to the illicit pleasure taken, thereby rectifying the blemish (esp. of the covenant) and extracting the holy sparks
yarka shekul — 'weighed vegetables' (Aramaic idiom), symbol of teshuvat ha-mishkal: repentance calibrated in measure against the sin
the word/utterance that issues in truth — 'the tevah (word/ark) going out be-emet,' whose 'opening is at its side,' drawing God to dwell with man

canonical_he: תשים לך פתח בחשך שאתה נצוד בו
gloss_en: "You shall set an opening in the darkness in which you are trapped" — homiletic reading of the ark's side-door (petach ha-teivah) as making an exit of truth from one's darkness/obstacle
forms: תשים לך פתח בחשך שאתה נצוד בו

gloss_en: Tishrei — the month of the High Holidays, identified with holy boldness (azut di-kedushah), called 'yerach ha-eitanim' (month of the mighty)
"You will prevail over your enemies" — the state of overcoming foes achieved through love/chesed ('many waters cannot extinguish the love')
"The melody will be elevated and perfected" — future messianic perfection of neginah within the da'at of holy Malkhut when God is King over all the earth

the rectification (tikkun) of one of the three character traits on each of the Three Pilgrimage Festivals — i.e., each festival (regel), through the renewal of the mochin/Da'at, repairs one of the three flawed middot discussed in Likutey Moharan II:1
"He can make Rosh Hashanah" — the tzaddik's capacity to enact/create the Day of Judgment itself, an action-power derived from holiness
The Throne of Glory (Kisei ha-Kavod) as the root-source of souls — kabbalistic locus where the souls of Israel are rooted

canonical_he: הוא גם כן בחינת מקומו של עולם
gloss_en: "He is also the aspect of the Place of the world" (mekomo shel olam) — the theological principle that God contains the world rather than being contained by it
forms: הוא גם כן בחינת מקומו של עולם

gloss_en: "He drew His holiness there" — God's act of extending (himshikh) His kedushah into the Temple because of its beautiful things, without self-constriction

God's knowing the place (makom) of each and every individual — His unique cognizance of every person's particular situation and standing, which is why He alone, being the Place of the world, is fit to judge everyone

canonical_he: הוא לבדו יתברך ראוי לדון את העולם
gloss_en: "He alone, blessed be He, is fit to judge the world" — statement of God's exclusive prerogative as Judge on the Day of Judgment
forms: הוא לבדו יתברך ראוי לדון את העולם

canonical_he: מאחר שהוא יתברך בעצמו מבקש אז כפרה
gloss_en: "Since He Himself, blessed be He, requests atonement then" — God's own plea 'bring an atonement for Me' on Rosh Chodesh (Chagigah motif) that emboldens Israel
forms: מאחר שהוא יתברך בעצמו מבקש אז כפרה

canonical_he: אין לנו בושה ביום הדין לבקש כפרה
gloss_en: "We have no shame on the Day of Judgment to ask atonement" — the state of unashamed petitioning on Rosh Hashanah enabled by God's own request for kapparah
forms: אין לנו בושה ביום הדין לבקש כפרה

canonical_he: וקבע יום הדין ראש השנה בראש חדש
gloss_en: God's fixing of the Day of Judgment, Rosh Hashanah, on Rosh Chodesh — a divine act of chesed in calendar design
forms: וקבע יום הדין ראש השנה בראש חדש

canonical_he: מרימין פנינו לבקש כפרה מאתו יתברך
gloss_en: "Raising our faces to ask atonement from Him" — the act of daring to petition God for kapparah, made possible by His kindness
forms: מרימין פנינו לבקש כפרה מאתו יתברך

gloss_en: "They are all borrowers from him" — the supernal ministers and heavenly host as debtors ('all the stars borrow from one another') to one who grasps the root, the word of Hashem/prayer
"Their brazenness falls before him" — the collapse of the unholy azut of falsely famous leaders before the master of prayer

canonical_he: יכול להכיר המפרסמים שהם על ידי עזות
gloss_en: The ability to recognize the falsely famous leaders (mefursamim) whose renown comes through brazenness (azut) — a discernment granted by attaining prayer
forms: יכול להכיר המפרסמים שהם על ידי עזות

gloss_en: "When a person prays about some illness" — the act of petitionary prayer directed at a specific sickness (context of healing through dvar Hashem)

the redemption of prayer (נִגְאֶלֶת הַתְּפִלָּה) — prayer being redeemed/liberated from its exile, as in Chizkiyahu's juxtaposing redemption to prayer (Berakhot 10), whereupon all medicines lose their power and healing comes through the word of Hashem alone
Being healed through the word of Hashem (dvar Hashem) — healing drawn from the supernal root rather than from herbal remedies
Dvar Hashem — 'the word of the Lord' as the supernal root of all creation ('by the word of Hashem the heavens were made'), identified with prayer
Departing from the three servitudes (avodot) — exiting the three evil traits (idolatry/lust for money, sexual desire, gluttony) as the means of rectifying prayer

canonical_he: כשאוחזין בבחינת דבר ה, בחינת תפלה
gloss_en: grasping/holding fast to the aspect of 'the word of Hashem' (devar Hashem), which is the aspect of prayer (tefillah) — the practice of cleaving to divine speech through prayer (Likutey Moharan II:1), which enables healing through all things, even bread and water
forms: כשאוחזין בבחינת דבר ה, בחינת תפלה

gloss_en: The capacity to be healed through anything in the world — even bread and water — once prayer is perfected ('bakol mitrap'in', Pesachim 25)
The condition of being 'outside' the three servitudes — the exclusion clause 'except idolatry, sexual immorality, and bloodshed' read as freedom from the three traits
Exiting the three traits (money-lust, sexual desire, gluttony) — the state of departure from the three middot that permits universal healing
"Through anything one may be healed — even with bread and water" — Talmudic dictum (Pesachim 25) reread as healing via ordinary food blessed from the root

canonical_he: וכשאוחזין בהשרש, דהינו דבר ה בחינת תפלה
gloss_en: Grasping the root — dvar Hashem, the aspect of prayer — holding fast to the supernal source from which bread and water receive blessing and healing power
forms: וכשאוחזין בהשרש, דהינו דבר ה בחינת תפלה

gloss_en: the word of Hashem (דְּבַר ה') identified with prayer — the divine utterance that is the root of all existence and healing, through which all cures are received (Likutey Moharan II:1, based on Psalms 33:6 and 107:20), rendering herbal remedies unnecessary; not 'word' in a generic speech sense

the principle from Likutey Moharan II:1 that one who attains true prayer (the word of Hashem, the root of all) no longer needs the healing power of medicinal herbs, since all herbal remedies draw their force only derivatively from stars and constellations
Prayer as the aspect of dvar Hashem — tefillah identified with the creative word of God, attained through prophecy (navi as acronym of 'bidvar Hashem shamayim na'asu')
The redemption and ransoming of prayer (ge'ulat ha-tefillah) — prayer's liberation from exile/disrespect, which topples all medicine

canonical_he: נופל כל הדאקטיריי, כי אין צריכין לרפואות
gloss_en: The fall of all doctoring (doktorai) — the collapse of physicians and the needlessness of remedies once prayer is redeemed
forms: נופל כל הדאקטיריי, כי אין צריכין לרפואות

gloss_en: Prayer in its completeness (tefillah bi-shleimut) — the perfected state of prayer through which one heals via dvar Hashem in all things
Prayer redeemed from exile — the freeing of tefillah from its degraded, despised state ('kerum zulut') via the flow of prophecy
Hashpa'at ha-nevuah — the flow/effluence of prophecy present in the world (even without an actual prophet), which redeems prayer

canonical_he: בנין ירושלים, דהינו תקון שלמות היראה שבלב
gloss_en: the building of Jerusalem, meaning the rectification of the completeness of awe (yirah) in the heart — Rabbi Nachman's identification (LM II:1) of rebuilding Jerusalem with perfecting heartfelt fear of Heaven, which creates the angel that channels prophecy
forms: בנין ירושלים, דהינו תקון שלמות היראה שבלב

canonical_he: נברא מלאך, שמשפיע נבואה לכלי הנבואה
gloss_en: The angel created through building Jerusalem (perfected fear in the heart) that channels prophecy to the vessels of prophecy (the Cherubim, anpei zutrei)
forms: נברא מלאך, שמשפיע נבואה לכלי הנבואה

gloss_en: Sukkot — the festival of Tabernacles, one of the Three Festivals, at which the desire for eating/food is rectified
The rectification of the desire for eating (ta'avat akhilah) — repair of gluttony effected through the festival (Sukkot) among the Three Festivals
The rectification of sexual desire (ta'avat mishgal) — repair of carnal lust effected through the festival (Shavuot) among the Three Festivals

Pesach (Passover) — the festival of the Exodus from Egypt, including its offering; in Likutey Moharan homiletically read as 'peh sach' (the mouth speaks), but always denoting the festival פֶּסַח (not the homograph פִּסֵּחַ, 'lame one', or the verb פָּסַח, 'skipped over')
The mitzvah of the Three Pilgrimage Festivals (shalosh regalim: Pesach, Shavuot, Sukkot) — commandment through which the three evil traits are rectified
Meriting to rectify the three traits (money-lust, sexual desire, gluttony) — the attainment achieved through the Three Festivals
"On each festival of the Three Festivals" — each individual regel as an occasion of renewed da'at/mochin rectifying one trait
Rectifying these three traits — the tikkun of the three middot accomplished by drawing da'at into the heart ('know today and take it to your heart')
Milk of a kosher animal (chalav kesherah) — permitted milk symbol in the three-watches homily, contrasted with nursing from impurity (context of the woman nursing in the third watch)
nursing milk of a kosher woman — the act of an infant suckling from a fit/worthy Jewish wet-nurse, whose permitted milk shapes the child's purity
binyan Yerushalayim as the heart — the building of Jerusalem identified with the lev, since Yerushalayim = yirah shleimah, complete awe that depends on the heart

canonical_he: להכיר את המפרסמים, איזהו על ידי עזות
gloss_en: recognizing the mefursamim — the task of discerning which famous leaders gained renown through holy azut (brazenness) versus false ones
forms: להכיר את המפרסמים, איזהו על ידי עזות

gloss_en: binding oneself to the mefursamim — the practice of attaching oneself to the generation's famous leaders under whom the souls are divided

canonical_he: הוא מקשר עם כל פרטי נשמות ישראל
gloss_en: resulting state of being bound to every individual soul of Israel — achieved automatically by attachment to the leaders who encompass them
forms: הוא מקשר עם כל פרטי נשמות ישראל

canonical_he: לקשר עצמו לשרשי הנשמות של ישראל
gloss_en: hitkashrut to the soul-roots of Israel — binding oneself to the roots of Jewish souls hewn from beneath the Throne of Glory
forms: לקשר עצמו לשרשי הנשמות של ישראל

gloss_en: being saved from the angels' envy (kinat mal'akhim) — protection from accusing jealous angels, as when Moshe ascended on high
binding oneself with the souls of Israel — the counsel (eitzah) of attachment to nishmot Yisrael as protection
state of rescue from them (the envious angels) — deliverance effected through the soul-bonding just prescribed
'this psalm' — Psalm 100 (Mizmor LeTodah) itself as the object whose 168 letters and 43 words are counted
segulah for a woman in hard labor — the auspicious remedial power of reciting Psalm 100 for a mekashah leiled
chesed as halakhot — divine kindness (gematria 168 of the psalm by atbash) identified with the aspect of legal rulings that ease birth
easy childbirth (holadah be-nakel) — the state of delivering without difficulty, effected through chesed/halakhot
Mizmor LeTodah — Psalm 100, the thanksgiving psalm whose initials spell 'mal' and whose letter-count encodes chesed
being efficacious for the birthing woman — the property of the psalm's recitation as remedy for obstructed labor

canonical_he: נחמה לכל האבלים הנ"ל, הינו שמחה
gloss_en: comfort for all the mourners, i.e. joy — consolation that is itself simchah, flowing to all limbs/souls grieving with the heart
forms: נחמה לכל האבלים הנ"ל, הינו שמחה

gloss_en: all are comforted and joy is drawn to all — the collective state when the heart/tzaddik is relieved and gladness spreads to every member
blood of the tzaddikim — the righteous ones' blood/suffering, over which the heart is distressed (as the body's bloods flood the heart)

The Shekhinah (Divine Presence) laments/mourns — per Sanhedrin 46a, the Shekhinah cries out in pain ('My head is heavy, My arm is heavy') over spilled blood, of the wicked and all the more so of the righteous; in LM II:2 this is the Divine analogue of the heart in distress when the blood surges over it
blood(s) of the wicked — the reshaim's blood whose shedding (their downfall) appeases, contrasted with the tzaddikim's blood
the tzaddik in pain and distress — the state of the generation's heart-figure suffering, which puts the 'lungs' (sustainers) in distress too
moistening (melachleiach) — the lung's action of imparting lachluchit/moisture that counters the body's drying movements
the heart in distress — the lev's state of tzarah when bloods rise and flood it, paralleling the tzaddik's affliction
the heart pounding with great beats — the violent palpitations (defikot) of the distressed heart flooded by blood

canonical_he: מקימת הלחה לבנה וממשכת הלחלוחית להגוף
gloss_en: sustaining the white humor and drawing moisture to the body — the lung's physiological function of maintaining leichah levanah and hydrating the body
forms: מקימת הלחה לבנה וממשכת הלחלוחית להגוף

gloss_en: kiyum ha-guf — the sustenance/preservation of the body, the role assigned to the lungs (reiah) via moisture
the chasadim as halakhot — kindnesses (of 'Your Tumim and Urim') identified with legal rulings, the oil of the Chanukah lamp

canonical_he: נתגלה אור האמת, בחינת: תמיך ואוריך
gloss_en: revelation of the light of truth, 'Tumekha ve-Urekha' (Deut 33:8) — emet's light disclosed through the chasadim/halakhot, symbolized by Chanukah oil
forms: נתגלה אור האמת, בחינת: תמיך ואוריך

gloss_en: unity revealed in Israel below — oneness manifested among Jews on earth (no machloket), mirroring the divine unity
revelation of His simple oneness above — God's achdut pashut disclosed on high, corresponding to the unity below
when simple unity is revealed below — the condition of manifest oneness among Israel that triggers the supernal revelation

canonical_he: גם למעלה נתגלה אחדות הפשוט יתברך
gloss_en: the simple unity of the Blessed One revealed also above — the heavenly disclosure of achdut pashut consequent on unity below
forms: גם למעלה נתגלה אחדות הפשוט יתברך

gloss_en: 'individual vs. many — the halakhah follows the many' — the Talmudic decision-rule (yachid ve-rabbim halakhah ke-rabbim) preserving unity in ruling
avoiding the multiplication of machloket in Israel — the purpose of ruling like the majority: not to increase dispute among Jews

canonical_he: שממשיכין קדשה של שבת לששת ימי החל
gloss_en: drawing Shabbat's holiness into the six weekdays — the practice of extending kedushat Shabbat into yemei ha-chol
forms: שממשיכין קדשה של שבת לששת ימי החל

gloss_en: revelation of the simple divine unity (achdut pashut) — disclosure that all diverse weekday actions stem from the One, effected by Shabbat-into-weekday
the Holy Tongue's connection to Shabbat — leshon ha-kodesh bound to Shabbat ('your Shabbat speech unlike weekday speech'), channeling its joy
leshon ha-kodesh, bound to Shabbat — the Holy Tongue itself as the uniquely complete language linked to the Shabbat day

canonical_he: ממשיכין השמחה של שבת לששת ימי החל
gloss_en: drawing the joy of Shabbat into the six weekdays — extending simchah shel Shabbat into the sadness-tinged yemei ha-chol via perfected speech
forms: ממשיכין השמחה של שבת לששת ימי החל

gloss_en: the four-fold square of speech, completed — ribua ha-dibbur brought to shleimut when truth illuminates it via the three Names El–Elohim–YHVH
when they become bound together — the coupling/attachment (as in shiddukhim and unions from Hashem) through which speech is perfected

nitchabrim v'nishlamim chelkei ha-dibbur — the joining and completion of the scattered portions of speech (the ten kavin of sichah) through shidduchim/zivvugim, the Name Hashem (YHVH), which perfects the dibbur
koach u-gevurah — divine power/might as the etymology of the Name El, denoting the Mighty One and Master of ability, linked to prayer

canonical_he: מבטלין גזרותיו יתברך, ואזי ישראל נקראין אל
gloss_en: mevatlin gezerotav yitbarakh — the act of annulling God's decrees through prayer, whereby Israel earns the name El
forms: מבטלין גזרותיו יתברך, ואזי ישראל נקראין אל

canonical_he: כביכול, אנו לוקחין לעצמנו הכח ממנו יתברך
gloss_en: the audacious appropriation ('kaviyakhol') of taking power from God Himself via prayer — seizing His koach to nullify decrees
forms: כביכול, אנו לוקחין לעצמנו הכח ממנו יתברך

gloss_en: Israel being called by the Name El (as God called Jacob 'El,' Megillah 18a) — the honorific state attained through prayer
emet me'ir b'ribua ha-dibbur — truth illuminating the four-fold 'square' of speech via the three Names El-Elohim-YHVH

canonical_he: כשיוצאין מהצרה, שזה בחינת תודה הלכה
gloss_en: emerging from distress (tzarah) as the moment of the thanksgiving-offering, identified as the aspect of 'todah = halakhah'
forms: כשיוצאין מהצרה, שזה בחינת תודה הלכה

gloss_en: the shining/illumination of emet (truth) that occurs upon exit from distress, per 'titen emet l'Yaakov'
meriting the level of 'todah-halakhah' — thanksgiving conceived as halakhah (orderly flow), the state that reveals truth's light
the revelation of the light of truth (or ha-emet) illuminating speech, reversing the blemish caused by blood flooding the heart
tikkun v'kiyyum ha-raglin — the rectification and sustaining of the legs effected by halakhot (cf. Asa's leg illness for impressing Torah scholars, Sotah 10a)
hashpa'at ha-chesed — the flow/bestowal of divine kindness (chesed) drawn down, from which halakhot are born
the refilling of the lack (chisaron) — the return-and-replenishment after depletion, pattern of blood returning to its place
the money/wealth by which laypeople support the Torah scholar — material patronage of talmidei chakhamim
the birthing of halakhot which are themselves chesed — new halakhic rulings born as an act of kindness
the fetus/newborn (valad) pushed outward at birth by the crowding of the risen blood
the blood's return to its proper place after childbirth — the orderly restorative flow (tahalukhot ha-damim = todah/halakhah)
the upward surge of the blood (damim olin l'ma'alah) during labor that crowds the space and expels the child
the cooling of the birthing woman's thighs (yarkhoteha mitztannenot, Sotah 11b) — physiological trigger of easy childbirth
the accomplishment of childbirth (holadah) itself, effected by the blood's rise and push
the exit from distress as the occasion for bringing the korban todah (thanksgiving-offering)
tzarah — distress/trouble befalling a person, whose main seat is the heart ('the heart knows its own bitterness')

distress, trouble (tzarah) — a state of affliction or crisis that befalls a person or a place, felt most acutely in the heart, and from which one emerges to bring a thanksgiving offering; not the homograph tzarah 'rival co-wife'

canonical_he: מתכנסים כל הדמים ועולים אל הלב
gloss_en: the ingathering of all the bloods rising to the heart in time of distress — physiological image of anguish concentrating in the lev
forms: מתכנסים כל הדמים ועולים אל הלב

canonical_he: כל מה שיודעין ומכירין אותו יתברך ביותר
gloss_en: increasing knowledge and recognition of God (yediah v'hakarah) as the measure of closeness to Him
forms: כל מה שיודעין ומכירין אותו יתברך ביותר

gloss_en: the state of being nearer/closer to God in proportion to one's recognition of Him
semukhim u-krovim — closeness and proximity to God attained through thanks and praise, essence of World-to-Come delight
'after the pidyon' — the post-redemption stage, once the monetary pidyon nefesh has sweetened the judgment
the physician's permission/license to heal (reshut la-rofe), which exists only once judgment is sweetened
the performance of a pidyon (redemption payment) that sweetens the din — the act of hamtakat ha-din
the nullification of the decree (gezerah) of illness once the pidyon sweetens the judgment

sweetening [of harsh judgment] together with the pidyon (redemption-money ritual) — the paired act of mitigating the heavenly decree via a redemption offering, which must precede and permit medical healing (Likutey Moharan II:3)
the physician's actual ability to heal — capacity to match the right remedy, possible only after hamtakah
the dictum 'permission is granted to the physician to heal' (reshut la-rofe l'rapot), operative specifically after pidyon

canonical_he: טוב לרפאות החולה על ידי רפואות
gloss_en: the goodness/appropriateness of healing the sick through medicines specifically after the sweetening and pidyon
forms: טוב לרפאות החולה על ידי רפואות

gloss_en: the world's sustenance through God's chesed (olam chesed yibaneh) — via tzedakah no labor is needed, kindness maintains existence
the revelation of yirah (awe/fear of Heaven) that becomes manifest through the chain begun by tzedakah

extracting/removing the parasitic nurture (yenikah) of the 'Forehead of the Serpent' (metzach ha-nachash) — the kabbalistic force of brazen impurity — cutting off its drawing of sustenance from the elders of the generation, accomplished through charity (Likutey Moharan II:4)

the revelation of the Divine Will (hitgalut ha-ratzon) — the disclosure that everything in creation is governed solely by God's free will rather than by any compulsion of nature, a revelation effected especially through the festivals and the holy elder, and which engenders fear of Heaven (Likutey Moharan II:4)
'melekhet avodah lo ta'asu' — the festival prohibition of servile labor (Num. 28:26), read as exemption from work via tzedakah/chesed

canonical_he: שמכניע את מצח הנחש, חכמת הטבע
gloss_en: the subduing of the 'Forehead of the Serpent' (metzach ha-nachash) — natural-science heresy (chokhmat ha-teva) overcome by tzedakah
forms: שמכניע את מצח הנחש, חכמת הטבע

gloss_en: the nullification of the sustenance (yenikah) drawn by the 'forehead of the serpent' (metzach ha-nachash) — the kabbalistic force of impudence/evil that nurses from holiness — whose parasitic drawing is cut off (in LM II:4, through beginning charity anew, which rectifies the elder/forehead-of-will aspect)

canonical_he: מנחה חדשה שהוא בחינת התחלת הצדקה
gloss_en: minchah chadashah — the 'new meal-offering' (Num. 28:26) as the aspect of beginning charity anew (hatchalat ha-tzedakah)
forms: מנחה חדשה שהוא בחינת התחלת הצדקה

gloss_en: the complete closing of the wound and its perfect healing (nisgar ha-makkah, nitrapei bi-shlemut) — final stage of the wound-healing scheme
the closing of the wound's mouth (pi ha-makkah) — the sealing stage of healing, counterpart to tzedakah's 'opening' (patoach tiftach)
hadachat ve-khibus ha-damim — rinsing and cleansing the blood, the third stage of wound-healing (purifying the circulating blood of contamination), the medical analogue of a spiritual remedy
petichat pi ha-makkah — the act of opening the mouth/orifice of the wound, first stage of healing, identified with tzedakah via 'patoach tiftach' (Deut. 15)
refuot ha-makkah — the multi-stage healing of a wound (opening it, drawing out pus, rinsing the blood), the medical schema mapped onto spiritual remedies
mekablin ha-chesed — the state of receiving the divine kindness (Chesed) once a vessel/channel of fear has been made for it

the revelation of the Divine Will (hitgalut ha-ratzon) — the event/state in Likutey Moharan II:4 in which the 'Forehead of Will' (metzach ha-ratzon) is disclosed after the Forehead of the Serpent (natural wisdom) is subdued, and which in turn generates fear/awe (yirah); i.e., 'when the Will is revealed'
the act of killing and subduing the Forehead of the Serpent (metzach ha-nachash) — vanquishing the root of heretical nature-wisdom

canonical_he: נשמע קול הקריאה של יום טוב
gloss_en: the hearing of the festival's voice of proclamation (kol ha-keriah shel Yom Tov) — the Yom Tov's audible call that reveals the divine Will, heard once the wild beasts' roar falls
forms: נשמע קול הקריאה של יום טוב

gloss_en: subjugation of the roaring voice of the evil beasts — silencing the clamor of the nature-philosophers so the festival's call can be heard

canonical_he: שהכניע מצח הנחש, שרש חכמת הטבע
gloss_en: the one who subdued the Forehead of the Serpent, root of natural wisdom — the holy sage's decisive victory over nature-philosophy
forms: שהכניע מצח הנחש, שרש חכמת הטבע

gloss_en: metzach ha-nachash in its defeated state — the Forehead of the Serpent (root of atheistic nature-wisdom) after it has been subdued and slain

canonical_he: ועומדת תמיד כנגד מצח הנחש כנ"ל
gloss_en: the Forehead of Will standing perpetually opposed to the Forehead of the Serpent — the permanent confrontation of revealed divine Will against nature-wisdom
forms: ועומדת תמיד כנגד מצח הנחש כנ"ל

canonical_he: התגלות הרצון על ידי ימים טובים
gloss_en: hitgalut ha-ratzon al yedei Yamim Tovim — the revelation of the divine Will effected specifically through the festivals
forms: התגלות הרצון על ידי ימים טובים

gloss_en: The Jewish festivals (Yamim Tovim) — the appointed holy days of the calendar, called 'mikra kodesh,' which proclaim and reveal the Divine Will by commemorating God's supernatural signs; not the generic phrase 'good days' or a wish for good times
the state when Chesed flows — divine kindness being actively bestowed from above, requiring no arousal from below
the capacity to receive the Chesed — being able to absorb the divine kindness through the graduated vessel formed by fear

canonical_he: כשנכנע מצח הנחש ונתגלה בחינת מצח הרצון
gloss_en: the moment when the Serpent's Forehead is subdued and the Forehead of Will (metzach ha-ratzon) is revealed — the turning point that silences the evil beasts
forms: כשנכנע מצח הנחש ונתגלה בחינת מצח הרצון

canonical_he: מאחר שמתגבר ומהפך אכזריות שבטבעו לרחמנות
gloss_en: the inner act of overpowering and inverting one's innate cruelty into compassion — the essence of tzedakah-service ('the ravens') that transmutes anger into Will
forms: מאחר שמתגבר ומהפך אכזריות שבטבעו לרחמנות

gloss_en: the transformation of rogez (anger/wrath) into ratzon (favor/Will) — divine displeasure turned into acceptance through inverted cruelty
the strengthening of the aspect of Ratzon (divine Will/favor) — the Will gaining force through the transformation wrought by charity
the elders as they should be — zaken she-bikdushah, 'the elder who has acquired wisdom,' whose proper long days empower the revelation of Will (vs. fallen elders who feed the Serpent)

canonical_he: לקשר כל הרצונות שיש בעולם לשרש הרצון
gloss_en: binding all the wills in the world to the Root of Will (shoresh ha-ratzon) — the great holy sage's task, linked to the moment of Moshe's passing
forms: לקשר כל הרצונות שיש בעולם לשרש הרצון

canonical_he: והכנעתם של אלו החיות רעות, חכמי הטבע
gloss_en: the subjugation of the evil beasts who are the nature-scholars — overthrowing the natural philosophers (chayot ra'ot = chakhmei ha-teva)
forms: והכנעתם של אלו החיות רעות, חכמי הטבע

gloss_en: the revelation of the divine Will (ratzon) disclosed on the festival (Yom Tov) — the festival's proclamation that everything occurs solely by God's will and not by natural necessity
yismach tzaddik — 'the righteous one rejoices' — the tzaddik's joy at revealed Will/vengeance, cited as festival-joy of the righteous

canonical_he: הימים טובים שעל ידם נתגלה הרצון
gloss_en: the festivals as agents of revelation of Will — Yamim Tovim through which the Ratzon is disclosed
forms: הימים טובים שעל ידם נתגלה הרצון

gloss_en: the revealed knowledge that everything is by His blessed Will alone — the disclosure that all is governed by divine volition, not natural necessity
Yom Tov as the embodiment of hitgalut ha-ratzon — the festival itself defined as the revelation of divine Will
each and every festival individually — every single Yom Tov on which God wrought supra-natural signs proclaiming the Will

canonical_he: מכריז וקורא את הרצון בבחינת מקרא קדש
gloss_en: the festival's proclaiming and calling out of the Divine Will — each Yom Tov announces and reveals that everything is governed solely by God's will, in the aspect of 'mikra kodesh' (holy convocation, Lev. 23), read as 'the holy one calls out/proclaims' the Will (LM II:4)
forms: מכריז וקורא את הרצון בבחינת מקרא קדש

gloss_en: each one of the festivals as proclaimer — every Yom Tov that announces, calls out (mikra kodesh) and reveals the Will

canonical_he: יש שכר וענש, ושיך להתירא מפניו יתברך
gloss_en: the truth that there is reward and punishment and that it is fitting to fear Him — the doctrinal basis of yirah flowing from revealed Will (vs. natural determinism)
forms: יש שכר וענש, ושיך להתירא מפניו יתברך

gloss_en: yirah as the aspect of regel (foot/leg) — fear of God identified with the foot, via 'u-mechokek mi-bein raglav,' the site of the engraved channel

canonical_he: חקיקה וצנור לקבל בתוכו את החסד
gloss_en: the engraving and conduit (chakikah ve-tzinor) hollowed out by fear to contain and receive the Chesed gradually
forms: חקיקה וצנור לקבל בתוכו את החסד

gloss_en: the condition of His kindness flowing forth (shofea chasdo) — when God bestows Chesed spontaneously from above
the state of needing to do nothing at all — no arousal-from-below required while Chesed flows freely of itself

canonical_he: כשעושה המלאכה והעסק כראוי, כמו שצריך לעשות
gloss_en: performing one's labor and business properly, as it should be done — right execution of a craft so that it arouses its supernal form in Creation
forms: כשעושה המלאכה והעסק כראוי, כמו שצריך לעשות

gloss_en: the human being as performer of the craft and occupation — the worker whose action below stirs the corresponding form above
the occupations and labors people perform — mundane work/business as arousal-from-below animating the Work of Creation
the trades and crafts done by human beings — the totality of human labors, all subsumed under the 39 avot melakhot mirroring Creation
tzedakah's power of opening and widening all openings — charity as the universal opener/enlarger of every entrance into divine service

canonical_he: שכשעושין איזהו פתח באיזה עבודה ונותנין צדקה
gloss_en: the practice of giving tzedakah upon making an opening in some service — charity given at a beginning so as to widen that newly-made entrance
forms: שכשעושין איזהו פתח באיזה עבודה ונותנין צדקה

gloss_en: koach ha-tzedakah — the operative power of charity itself, the force that opens beginnings and is 'found among the long of days'
the ongoing widening and further opening of the entrance — tzedakah's continuous enlargement of an already-opened path in divine service

canonical_he: שבהתחלה צריכין לשבר ולפתח פתח מחדש
gloss_en: the difficulty of beginnings — that at the start one must break through and open an entrance anew, why 'all beginnings are hard'
forms: שבהתחלה צריכין לשבר ולפתח פתח מחדש

gloss_en: kasheh me'od — the state of being 'very difficult/heavy,' describing the beginning (hatchalah) of charity and every divine service, per 'all beginnings are hard'

canonical_he: צריכין לפתח שם פתח לכנס באותו הדרך
gloss_en: the required act of opening an opening (petach) at the start of a path — the necessity to breach an entryway before entering any way of divine service
forms: צריכין לפתח שם פתח לכנס באותו הדרך

gloss_en: entering that path and that service — the act of stepping into a specific derekh/avodah of serving God through its newly opened doorway

canonical_he: כמה קלין וכמה חבלים וצירים יש להיולדת
gloss_en: the many cries, birth-pangs and contractions (chevalim ve-tzirim) of a woman in labor — image for the groans preceding any deed of divine service
forms: כמה קלין וכמה חבלים וצירים יש להיולדת

gloss_en: the moment 'before she gives birth' — the pre-birth stage of the birthing woman, analogue of the difficult pre-beginning of an avodah

canonical_he: וצריכין כמה יגיעות וכמה תנועות כנ"ל
gloss_en: the requirement of many exertions (yegi'ot) and many bodily movements/swayings (tenu'ot) — the cries, groans, bowings, and strainings of divine service — needed before one merits to accomplish any deed in serving God (LM II:4)
forms: וצריכין כמה יגיעות וכמה תנועות כנ"ל

canonical_he: וצריכין כמה קלין וכמה גניחות וכו
gloss_en: the needed many cries (kalin) and groans (genichot) — the preparatory sighs/oy-vey sounds and strange movements God-fearers make before a deed
forms: וצריכין כמה קלין וכמה גניחות וכו

gloss_en: the stage 'before one begins any beginning' — the hardest pre-initiation moment prior to starting a new divine service
nadvan — the donor/philanthropist, one who gives charity; specifically one whose giving must be avodah, not mere natural kindness

canonical_he: צריכין לשבר את האכזריות שלו להפכו לרחמנות
gloss_en: the act of breaking one's cruelty (achzariyut) and inverting it into compassion (rachmanut) — the essential inner work of tzedakah
forms: צריכין לשבר את האכזריות שלו להפכו לרחמנות

gloss_en: the initial stage of beginning to donate to charity — the first act of volunteering tzedakah, when cruelty must first be broken
the renewal and rectification of the brain/mind (moach) — restored mochin achieved through the yeshivah gathering of faith

the 'man of understanding' (ish tevunot, Proverbs 20:5) — the person of tevunah who, like one drawing deep waters, draws up and reveals the hidden counsels (eitzot); in Likutey Moharan II:5 he is one possessing a refined soul ('the breath of Shaddai gives them understanding'), who by drawing divine spirituality into constrictions purifies the soul and thereby rectifies faith

the rectification of faith (nitakken ha-emunah) — the state in which emunah, fallen or damaged faith, becomes repaired and restored to true holy faith (e.g., through the 'man of understanding' or through the clarification of the imaginative faculty by prophecy)
me'irat einayim — 'illuminating the eyes,' the lung's (re'ah) property of brightening the judge's sight; acronym for 'tokho ratzuf ahavah mi-bnot Yerushalayim'
the blowing wind/breath of the lung (re'ah) that fans and cools the heart's heat — respiratory action effecting tikkun ha-mishpat

the rectification of judgment (tikkun ha-mishpat) — restoring the faculty of holy judgment/justice, whose seat is the heart, by cooling the heart's overheating (via the lung's breath), thereby repairing the Divine Chariot and holy love; opposite of kilkul ha-mishpat, the corruption of judgment (Likutey Moharan II:5)

cold-and-moist (kar va-lach) — the paired humoral quality of coldness and moisture, characteristic of the lung and of rain, which Rabbi Nachman identifies as the physiological cause of sleep and dream-imagination
