the magnification of the tzaddik's name — his fame growing in the world, within which God's own Name is clothed
the magnification of God's Name (shemo yitbarakh) — the divine Name growing great as a consequence of the tzaddik's name growing great
the revelation of this tzaddik — his becoming known and famous in the world, the 'shem' through which God's Name is magnified

canonical_he: יכול לראות ולהסתכל בגדלת השם ולהסתכל בעולם
gloss_en: the capacity to see and gaze upon God's greatness and upon the world — opened eyes/power of sight granted through the tzaddik's revealed splendor
forms: יכול לראות ולהסתכל בגדלת השם ולהסתכל בעולם

gloss_en: the verse 'from there it divides and becomes four heads' (Gen 2:10) — the Eden-river splitting into four, source-text for the four elements/middot
the four elements (fire, air, water, earth) — the arba yesodot from which all the character traits (middot) are drawn
nahar yotze me-Eden — 'a river goes out of Eden' (Gen 2:10), the supernal flow/shefa issuing from Eden, symbol of the tzaddik as channel of the world's beauty
the act of drawing close to the true tzaddik — attaching oneself to the genuine righteous leader who is the world's beauty and grace
bekhiyah — weeping/crying, the mournful response linked to the destruction and the dominance of the luminaries of fire
weeping/crying (bekhi) — the act of shedding tears, which in LM II:67 causes the light of the eyes to depart, per Shabbat 151b
the departure/dimming of the light of the eyes (loss of eyesight caused by weeping, per Shabbat 151b), likened to the sun's light setting in the west
berakhah — the spoken blessing customarily given (with drink) to the messenger who carries wine/mead to guests or a wedding
niset ve-noset — Zoharic category (Pekudei 242a) of a thing that is 'carried yet carries,' borne by another while itself bearing/supporting

canonical_he: תקונם של אלו המחין של חוץ לארץ
gloss_en: the tikkun (rectification) of the 'mentalities of outside the Land' — repair of the chutz-la'aretz mochin damaged by the blemish of honor, effected when Supernal Pleasantness flows
forms: תקונם של אלו המחין של חוץ לארץ

gloss_en: the flowing of No'am ha-Elyon — the streaming of Supernal Pleasantness/Delight whose influx reveals divine honor and enables tikkun

shalhovin di-rechimuta — the Zoharic Aramaic term for 'flames of love,' the fiery arousal of passionate love awakened from the Supernal Pleasantness (No'am ha-Elyon), through which procreation (holadah) comes about

the Supernal Pleasantness (No'am HaElyon) — the divine delight/sweetness of the higher realm, from which flames of love (shalhovin dirchimuta) are aroused and through which procreation comes about (Likutey Moharan II:71)
mochin shel chutz-la'aretz — the diaspora mentalities/consciousness, aspect of 'chovlim' (destroyers, Zech 11:7), Torah scholars outside the Land who wound each other in halakhah

Chovlim ("Destroyers/Wounders") — the staff named in Zechariah 11:7 ("one I called Pleasantness and one I called Chovlim"), interpreted per Sanhedrin 24a as the Torah scholars outside the Land of Israel who wound each other in halakhic debate; in Likutey Moharan II:71 it designates the mochin (mentalities) of outside the Land, opposite the mochin of the Land of Israel which are No'am (Pleasantness). Distinct from חֲבָלִים (ropes/pangs) and from חוֹבְלִים as sailors (רַב הַחוֹבֵל).

No'am — 'Pleasantness' (נֹעַם), the divine sweetness/delightfulness of Zechariah 11:7 ('One I called No'am'), identified in Likutey Moharan II:71 with the mentalities (mochin) of the Land of Israel and with the Supernal Pleasantness (No'am HaElyon) whose flow arouses the flames of love; not the proper name Naomi (נָעֳמִי) nor any verbal form of נ־ע־ם
Yaakov and Yosef as a paired figure — the patriarch Jacob together with Joseph, joined aspects in the flow of Supernal Pleasantness and generosity

becoming/forming a vessel (keli) to receive the flow of the Supernal Pleasantness (No'am HaElyon) — the opening of the heart's pathways, chiefly through tzedakah, that enables one to receive the flames of divine love from the ever-flowing supernal delight (Likutey Moharan II:71)

the heart being opened and moved to give generously (שֶׁנִּפְתָּח וְנִתְנַדֵּב הַלֵּב) — the inner act of generosity of heart in giving charity, which opens the pathways of the heart to become a vessel for the flames of divine love (LM II:71)

generosity of heart (nedivut lev) — the willing, freely-moved impulse of the heart to give, identified with charity/terumah (per Exodus 25:2, "whose heart moves him"), whereby the heart is opened and becomes a vessel for the Supernal Pleasantness
shefir ve-shilya — the amniotic sac and placenta, embryological terms for the membranes accompanying birth, imagery of the birthing of the mochin
chevlei leidah — birth pangs, the pains of labor (wordplay on chovlim), the travail accompanying the birth/rectification of the diaspora mentalities

inheritance/heritage (נַחֲלַת, construct of נַחֲלָה) — the hereditary portion or estate, as in 'nachalat Yaakov' (the boundless heritage of Jacob, Isaiah 58:14) and 'nachalat' of Psalms 16:6, linked in LM II:71 to tzedakah and the flow of the Supernal Pleasantness

beautiful of form (yefeh to'ar) — the biblical epithet of physical comeliness/handsome appearance (as said of Joseph, Gen. 39:6), used in LM II:71 as an aspect of beauty (linked to Shifrah, 'making beautiful') connected to the revelation of honor and the Supernal Pleasantness

"who are pleasant [to one another] in halakhic discussion" (she-man'imim ba-halakhah) — the Talmudic description (cf. Sanhedrin 24a) of Torah scholars of the Land of Israel who treat each other graciously in halakhic debate, linked here to no'am (Supernal Pleasantness) as the aspect of the rectified 'mentalities of the Land of Israel,' in contrast to the 'destroyers' (chovlim) of outside the Land

pleasantness (noʿam) — the Supernal Pleasantness (nōʿam ha-ʿelyon), the sweet delightful divine flow associated with the mentalities of the Land of Israel; not the proper name Naʿam or naʿim as adjective

terumah — the dedicated offering/heave-offering (as in the Tabernacle donation, 'you shall take My terumah'), which Rabbi Nachman identifies with charity given from generosity of heart, forming a vessel to receive the Supernal Pleasantness (its letters being the final letters of 'lachazot be-no'am H' u-levaker be-heikhalo')

greatness (gedulah) — the noun for exalted stature, eminence, and majesty that a person receives (identified with the sefirah Malkhut and, at its core, with humility); not the feminine adjective gedolah ('large/great')
nedivei ha-am — 'the nobles/generous ones of the people' (Num 21:18), the generous-hearted donors of Israel who 'excavate' the well of Torah
chafaruha — 'they dug it' (Num 21:18), the act of digging the well, i.e., drawing forth Torah elucidations by the officers of Israel
matanah — 'a gift' (Num 21:18, 'from the wilderness a gift'), Torah insight received as a free gift via self-abasement (midbar/wilderness)
hitnotzetzut ha-moach — the sparking/flashing of a person's mind, its illumination kindled when the comprehensive sage gazes at him

canonical_he: מקבל כל אחד גדלה כפי מדרגת מחו
gloss_en: each individual's receiving of greatness according to the level of his mind — apportionment of gedulah measured by one's sparked mochin via the sage's gaze
forms: מקבל כל אחד גדלה כפי מדרגת מחו

gloss_en: the sparking/illumination of one's mind (mitnotzetz mocho) — the flash of mental enlightenment kindled in a person's individual intellect when the comprehensive sage (chakham ha-dor) gazes upon him, which is the channel through which he receives greatness (LM II:72)
mekabel gedulah — the receiving of greatness/eminence, obtaining one's rank through being seen by the comprehensive sage (tzaddik)
chakham ha-kolel — the comprehensive sage, the generation's all-inclusive mind (moach kelali) from whom all individual mochin receive

chiddushin de-Oraita — original novel Torah insights/novellae (Aramaic: 'novelties of the Torah'), the new interpretations and elucidations of Torah that the tzaddik-leader of the aspect of Moshe attains through the sparkling of his mind

canonical_he: חוזר ונחיה השפלות של כל אחד
gloss_en: the reviving of each person's dormant humility — reawakening the shiflut of Moshe embedded in every limb, which lies as if dead until aroused
forms: חוזר ונחיה השפלות של כל אחד

gloss_en: bushah u-teshuvah — shame paired with repentance, the salutary embarrassment that arouses return to God
the qualification to be a leader of Israel — that only one purified of sexual desire, with clarified 'visions,' can serve as manhig Yisrael

canonical_he: מחיב שירגיש כל אחד שפלותו באמת
gloss_en: the obligating of each person to genuinely feel his own lowliness — the tzaddik's Torah compels true felt shiflut in every hearer
forms: מחיב שירגיש כל אחד שפלותו באמת

gloss_en: the Torah that the true tzaddik draws down — his channeled Torah teaching, which draws shame/humility on hearers as at Sinai

canonical_he: שבא אצל צדיק אמתי ושומע מפיו תורה
gloss_en: the act of coming before the true tzaddik and hearing Torah from his mouth — direct oral reception from the genuine righteous one
forms: שבא אצל צדיק אמתי ושומע מפיו תורה

gloss_en: bushah ve-shiflut gadol me'od — very great shame and lowliness, the state fittingly drawn upon one who hears the true tzaddik's Torah (sign of authenticity)

fear and shame (yir'ah u-vushah) — the paired experience of awe of God and shame at one's distance from Him, which together constitute the essence of repentance and are identified with Shabbat (via the Tikkunei Zohar anagram of Bereishit: 'fears shame / fears Shabbat')

the eternal life (chayim nitzchiyim) of the World to Come (Olam HaBa) — everlasting afterlife-existence, which repentance and Shabbat embody as a foretaste ('Repent and live'; 'those who taste it merit life')
the state when the dormant humility is revived — the moment Moshe's implanted shiflut comes alive within a person
each person's seeing and feeling his own lowliness — the experiential perception of one's shiflut in every limb
the revival of every individual's humility — the collective quickening of the Moshe-humility rooted in each Jew from Sinai
meriting to originate chiddushim in Torah — attaining novel Torah insights (chiddushin de-Orayta) through the revived spirit

the comprehensive/all-inclusive spirit (ruach ha-kollel) — the collective ruach possessed by the true leader of Israel (the aspect of Moshe), which encompasses and knows how to engage the individual spirit of each and every person (Numbers 27:18, 'a man in whom there is spirit'), identified with the spirit of God and the mochin (Likutey Moharan II:72)

the true leader (manhig ha'amiti) of all Israel — the singular authentic tzaddik-leader of the whole Jewish people, identified with the aspect of Moshe and the comprehensive spirit (ruach ha-kollel) who knows how to engage the spirit of each individual (Likutey Moharan II:72)

The comprehensive Da'at (da'at ha-kollel) — the all-encompassing, collective knowledge/mind embodied by the true leader of Israel (the aspect of Moshe), identified with the comprehensive spirit (ruach ha-kollel) and the mochin, from which every individual's mind/spirit receives
seeing oneself together with the tzaddik — the act of being seen with/by the true tzaddik, which itself confers greatness even without hearing Torah
chayim nitzchiyim — eternal life, the unbounded life of the World to Come beyond all limit (gevul)
one who tastes the delight of Shabbat — the person experiencing oneg Shabbat, a semblance of the World to Come, earning a boundless inheritance

lowliness and humility (shiflut va-anivut) — the self-abnegating trait of meekness that renders a person like absolute nothingness (ayin) and thus without limit, the paired virtue-term for humble self-effacement in LM II:72
bilti gevul — limitlessness, the state of being without boundary that characterizes the spiritual pleasure of the World to Come

the fiftieth day (yom ha-chamishim) — the day following the forty-nine days of the Omer count, the day of the giving of the Torah at Sinai (Shavuot), corresponding to the fiftieth gate of repentance and God's own teshuvah
the teshuvah of God Himself — the fiftieth gate: repentance/return attributed to Hashem as it were ('Return to Me and I will return to you,' Mal 3:7)
the 49 days of Sefirat ha-Omer — the counting of forty-nine days from Egypt to Sinai corresponding to the 49 gates of teshuvah
meitzar ha-garon — the 'strait of the throat,' kabbalistic locus of constriction (wordplay on Mitzrayim), site of teshuvah ila'ah per the Arizal

Teshuvah Ila'ah — the kabbalistic 'higher/supernal repentance' (Aramaic ila'ah, 'upper'), the elevated level of return associated with Binah in Lurianic Kabbalah, here identified with the constriction of the throat (meitzar ha-garon) symbolized by Egypt; distinct from ordinary/lower repentance (teshuvah tata'ah)

the Fiftieth Gate (Sha'ar HaChamishim) — the fiftieth gate of understanding/repentance beyond the forty-nine gates of teshuvah, identified with God's own 'return' (ve-ashuvah aleichem) at the giving of the Torah on the fiftieth day
amirat Tehillim — the recitation of Psalms as a practice with segulah-power to arouse and attain teshuvah
being regularly accustomed to reciting Psalms — the habitual practice of Tehillim recitation recommended for one seeking teshuvah
Purim — the festival named for the pur (lot, Esther 9:26), stage preceding Parashat Parah and preparation toward Pesach (pur → parah)

the freedom (cherut) of Passover — the spiritual liberation from bondage/exile that Pesach embodies, toward which Purim (via Mordechai) is a path and preparation; not charut ('engraved,' as on the Tablets)
histaklut ba-tzaddik — gazing upon the face of the tzaddik, itself a great practice since the Torah scholar is greater than the Torah scroll
kedushah — holiness as a state/quality; here the sanctity in which eating and the tzaddik's presence are invested, distinct from mere separateness

eating in holiness (akhilah bi-kedushah) — the spiritual practice of consuming food in sanctity and fear of Heaven, which sweetens daily suffering and harsh judgments and elevates the mouth from an animal state to the stature of Adam

canonical_he: נעשה המתקה, שלא יתגבר הצער ביותר
gloss_en: the sweetening effected through eating in holiness so that daily suffering (tza'ar) does not overwhelm — an act of hamtakah (mitigation of pain/judgment)
forms: נעשה המתקה, שלא יתגבר הצער ביותר

gloss_en: fear/awe of the side of holiness (yirah di-kedushah) — the holy fear of God, counterpart of fallen fear (retzu'ah bisha), identified in LM II:77 with the holy tefillin strap passing through the ma'abarta
retzu'ah dikedushah — the 'strap of holiness': holy fear (yirah) figured as the tefillin strap, counterpart to the evil strap
retzu'ah bisha (Zohar, Intro 11b) — the 'evil strap': the demonic lash of fallen fear that inflicts suffering and judgment
yirah nefulah — fallen fear: awe of Heaven degraded into worldly fears/anxieties, identified with the evil strap

canonical_he: רצועה שעוברת בתוך המעברתא של תפלין
gloss_en: the tefillin strap (retzuah) that passes through the ma'abarta, the hollow passage-loop at the back of the tefillin box — in Likutey Moharan II:77 the physical strap threaded through this channel, homiletically identified with holy fear (yirah) passing through and binding to the mochin (the tefillin as mind/intellect)
forms: רצועה שעוברת בתוך המעברתא של תפלין

canonical_he: ממתיק הצער והדין הבא מרצועה בישא
gloss_en: the act of sweetening/mitigating the suffering and judgment (din) that descends from the evil strap (retzu'ah bisha), accomplished via holy eating
forms: ממתיק הצער והדין הבא מרצועה בישא

gloss_en: the transformation whereby eating in holiness makes the mouth into the 'stature of Adam' (komat adam) — human, not animal, per 'Who placed a mouth for man' (Ex. 4:11)
the resulting state: the mouth rendered into komat adam (full human stature) by bringing Malkhut/fear into it during holy eating

canonical_he: שאוכל עם יראת־שמים, בקדשה ובטהרה כראוי
gloss_en: the practice of eating with fear of Heaven, in holiness and purity as is fitting — the devotional mode of eating that draws Malkhut into the mouth
forms: שאוכל עם יראת־שמים, בקדשה ובטהרה כראוי

gloss_en: making from the mouth the stature of Adam (fashioning the full spiritual 'komat adam' out of the mouth/speech through eating in holiness and fear of Heaven, Likutey Moharan II:77)

the leather strap of the tefillin (רְצוּעָה שֶׁל תְּפִלִּין) — the binding strap attached to the phylactery boxes, which in LM II:77 embodies fear/Malkhut (Yehudah) entering the mochin/da'at of the tefillin (Binyamin); not a whip-strap of punishment nor any other strap

the sustaining/existence of the world before the giving of the Torah — the pre-Sinai era in which the world endured solely through the Ten Utterances of creation (with the Torah still concealed in them), i.e., through God's free, unearned gift (matnat chinam)
matnat chinam — an unearned free gift; what Moshe requested via 'va-etchanan' (Deut. 3:23) in pleading to enter the Land of Israel
mitzvot zemaniyot — time-bound commandments, given so as to bind and elevate time itself into the aspect of above-time

canonical_he: שיתאחד הזמן ויעלה הזמן לבחינת למעלה מהזמן
gloss_en: the goal that time be unified and ascend into the aspect of above-time (lema'alah mehazman) — the essence of the avodah of nullifying time
forms: שיתאחד הזמן ויעלה הזמן לבחינת למעלה מהזמן

gloss_en: the nullification of time (bittul ha-zemanim) — the transcendence and abolition of temporal divisions, i.e., rising above time itself; identified in Likutey Moharan II:79 as one aspect with teshuvah (repentance) and with the splitting of the Sea of Reeds, through which one merits to hear the voice of holiness
the hearing of the holy voice (kol dikedushah, the voice of Yaakov), attained through teshuvah/nullification of time

The Splitting of the Sea of Reeds (Kriat Yam Suf) — the miraculous parting of the sea at the Exodus, which Yitro heard about; treated in Likutey Moharan II:79 as the aspect of the nullification of time (bitul ha-zemanim), linked with the war of Amalek and teshuvah.
milchemet Amalek — the war against Amalek (Ex. 17), interpreted as teshuvah, fought while Moshe, Aharon and Chur fasted
Yitzchak son of Avraham — the patriarch Isaac as symbol of time (letters of 'keitz chai') born from Avraham who is above time
the unification of time achieved through teshuvah — time rising to be bound and included in the above-time realm
lema'alah min hazman — the supra-temporal realm/aspect above time, associated with Avraham's love, into which time is elevated
hit'achdut hazman — the unification of time itself: time becoming one, connected and included in the above-time
kolo yitbarakh — the voice of God Himself, the holy voice (voice of Yaakov) heard through teshuvah

canonical_he: זוכין לשמע קולו יתברך, הינו הקול דקדשה
gloss_en: the merited state of hearing His blessed voice, i.e., the kol dikedushah/voice of Yaakov, gained via teshuvah as nullification of time
forms: זוכין לשמע קולו יתברך, הינו הקול דקדשה

gloss_en: time (zman) — temporality itself, the created order of time that is bound up with sleep and the 'end of days,' and which teshuvah nullifies; not the verb זִמֵּן 'to summon/prepare' or זִמּוּן 'invitation'
keitz (קֵץ) — 'end,' the appointed end-point of time; the eschatological 'end of days' (as in 'mikeitz' and the anagram keitz chai within Yitzchak), signifying temporality itself
the shortening of time — the sun setting early for Yaakov ('ki va hashemesh'), an instance of time's nullification
bitul hazman — the nullification of time, equated with teshuvah; time annulled by absorption into the above-time

dibburim — spoken utterances/words of speech (plural of dibbur), the articulated speech formed from combinations of the twenty-two letters of the Torah; linked here to teshuvah via 'Take words with you and return' (Hosea 14:3) and to the stones/letters of 'avnei ha-makom'
kedushat hamachshavah — holiness/purity of thought ('merashotav'), the faculty that clarifies and repairs all blemishes, root of teshuvah's rectification
payis — the Temple lottery for assigning the ash-removal service (Yoma ch. 2), read as the enactment against pursuing leadership
yefaysu — the people's act of appeasing/entreating a person to accept leadership; only such conciliation legitimates exaltedness
hatzbi'u — 'extend fingers' read as a hint to intellect/attainment: displaying one's grasp (sikhlam) of Torah in the leadership contest
hatzbi'u — the Temple finger-count command ('extend one or two'), reinterpreted as the yetzer's incitement to display oneself for leadership

canonical_he: שיראה איזה צביעות בפני המון עם
gloss_en: tzevi'ut — showing off/hypocritical religious display before the masses in order to win leadership, the yetzer's counsel
forms: שיראה איזה צביעות בפני המון עם

gloss_en: the memuneh — the Temple official who runs the lottery, allegorized as the yetzer hara (evil inclination) inciting rivals

the kevesh — the inclined ramp ascending the Temple altar (כֶּבֶשׁ, Yoma ch. 2), which the priests ran up to win the terumat ha-deshen, homiletically linked to kivshono shel olam, the hidden secrets/depths of the world (Chagigah 13); NOT כֶּבֶשׂ 'lamb/sheep' and not the verb כָּבַשׁ 'to conquer/subdue'
kivshono shel olam — the 'hidden furnace/ramp of the world' (cf. Chagigah 13), the concealed divine mysteries; punned on the Temple ramp (kevesh) climbed by leadership-seekers

canonical_he: כל המדרגות התחתונות המכנים בשם רגלים, נתעלים
gloss_en: the elevation of all lower spiritual levels termed 'feet' (raglayim) through the joy of Torah and mitzvot
forms: כל המדרגות התחתונות המכנים בשם רגלים, נתעלים

gloss_en: the lower rungs/levels (madregot tachtonot) themselves — everything designated 'feet' in the cosmic stature awaiting elevation
dibbur hara — evil/slanderous speech, called 'regel' from 'lo ragal al leshono' (Ps. 15:3), also elevated by joy
the collective elevation of everything named 'foot' (regel) — speech, wealth, wife, lower levels — via mitzvah-joy that reaches the feet
kar'a — 'leg' (Aramaic): the wife as her husband's leg ('itto kar'a debala'), the regel elevated by rejoicing her in a mitzvah
the letter Heh — the letter symbolizing the wife/Malkhut ('raglei chasidav'), which joy raises and binds upward
Torah and mitzvah as a pair — the joy of whose performance ('tzedek yikra'ehu leraglo') elevates the feet/lower levels
supporters of the Torah (tomkhei de-oraita) — those who uphold/financially sustain Torah study, the Zoharic term for patrons of Torah scholars, identified with samkhei keshot ('supporters of truth')
samkhei keshot — 'supports of truth' (Zoharic term for Netzach and Hod, the leg-pillars), elevated to the heart through dance-joy
the elevation of all supporters of Torah (tomkhei de'oraita — those who uphold/fund Torah, the Netzach-Hod 'legs') through mitzvah-joy
prophets (נְבִיאִים) — the prophets as bearers of prophecy, identified kabbalistically with the sefirot Netzach and Hod, the 'legs' of the divine structure and the source of prophetic inspiration
the divine name YHVH spelled out with alefs (milui alfin) totaling 45 = MaH — the gematria linked to Adam (45), aspect of order (kesseder)

order / proper sequence (seder) — the state of things proceeding in their correct arrangement, as in the aleph-bet in its forward order (kesseder, 'kedem') versus reversed tashra"k (shelo kesseder, 'achor'); the divine flow received in order via the yud, whose disruption brings heart-sickness
achor — 'behind' of Psalms 139:5, symbol of the reversed order (tashrak alphabet), the not-in-sequence aspect linked to Chavah/Malkhut; not the body's back per se
tashrak — the alphabet recited in reverse order (tav-shin-resh-kuf), emblem of 'not in order' / achor
the alphabet in its proper forward order (aleph-bet-gimel...), the sequential arrangement of the Hebrew letters from aleph onward, as opposed to the reversed tashrak order

shleimut — completeness/wholeness (שְׁלֵמוּת): the perfected, undeficient state of a thing, attained only when it is unified and bound to God; identified with fullness (milui) and vitality (chiyut), whose absence in a limb is called a deficiency (chisaron)
milui — fullness/completion of a thing, identified with its vitality (chiyut); the state of being whole through connection to God, not a letter-filling spelling
dalet-vav-yud — the letters of the spelled-out yud (yu"d), Chokhmah's vitality drawn into Malkhut-dalet; a letter-filling, not 'illness' (dvai)
kaf — the letter kaf as numerical value 20, from the al-tikrei reading of 'kapekha' (Ps 139:5), equal to yud's gematria doubled into Malkhut
the letter dalet — letter-symbol of Malkhut who 'has nothing of her own' (dal, poor) until receiving the yud of Chokhmah
a thing drawn down from a high place — an occurrence whose root is in an exalted supernal source, which therefore may arrive below 'not in order'
shevi — the captivity/captive of Deut 21:10 ('and you take its captives'), the opposing will taken captive and subdued in the inner war
binding His divinity into your thought — the contemplative act of attaching awareness of God to one's mind during opposition

canonical_he: יתבטלו כל המלחמות וכל הרצונות נגד רצונך
gloss_en: the nullification of all wars and all wills opposing your will — the promised state of 'Hashem delivers him into your hand'
forms: יתבטלו כל המלחמות וכל הרצונות נגד רצונך

gloss_en: milchamah — war defined as opposition of wills, the existential aspect of 'not in order'; the war of Deut 21:10 read inwardly

opposition of will (hitnagdut ha-ratzon) — the clash between a person's desire and contrary reality or opposing wills, when things go 'not in order' against what one wants; identified in LM II:82 as the essence of war
his blood is spilled — suffering shame/humiliation as literal bloodshed (the blood draining from the face), functioning as slaughter of the self
zera merei'im — 'seed of evildoers' (Isaiah 1:4), the corrupt brood/external passions assailing the heart, akin to the flood-waters
the waters of the Flood (mabul) — archetype of the overwhelming 'many waters' of alien loves and fears
mayim rabbim — the 'many waters' of Song 8:7 that cannot quench love: external loves and fears threatening the heart's holy ardor
external loves and fears — fallen, outward ahavot and yir'ot (the 'many waters') opposed to holy love and awe of God
shin — the letter shin of 'Shabbat' (shin + bat), whose three strokes signify the three elements fire, wind, water
fire, wind, water — the three primal elements (telat gevanin) symbolized by the three heads of the letter shin

Shabbat garments (bigdei Shabbat) — the special clothes donned in honor of Shabbat, expounded in LM II:83 as the holy body from the Garden of Eden that one puts on after stripping off the leprous body of the serpent's skin
the holy body from the Garden of Eden — the pure 'Shabbat-garment' body donned after stripping the leprous serpent-skin body
the fallen souls — souls that have no ascent except through the spilled blood (shaming/martyrdom) of Israel
kisui ha-dam — the ritual covering of blood, read as the Shekhinah covering Israel's blood spilled through shame borne in love
shefikhut damim — spilling of blood: shame/humiliation as bloodshed serving as the 'shechitah' that permits the tzaddik's mitzvot to be 'tasted'

shechitah — ritual slaughter of an animal that renders it permitted for consumption; in LM II:83 the paradigm for shame as a purifying 'spilling of blood' that permits God to 'taste' the tzaddik's mitzvot (as slaughter permits ever min ha-chai)
the holiness of Shabbat — identified with 'the ultimate of knowing is that we do not know,' the takhlit of heaven and earth

the ultimate purpose/culmination of knowledge (tachlit ha-yedi'ah) — the epistemic apex expressed in the dictum 'the ultimate of knowing is that we do not know,' i.e., attaining the realization that Divine wisdom is beyond one's grasp

arrows (חִצִּים, plural of חֵץ) — projectiles shot from a bow; in Likutey Moharan II:83 the arrows shot from the bow of the rectified covenant (brit), symbolizing prayer / the eighteen blessings formed of three vavs

the 'chai birkan di-tzelota' — the eighteen (chai = 18) blessings of the prayer service (Aramaic/Zoharic term for the Shemoneh Esreh/Amidah), identified here with prayer as the 'arrows' shot from the bow of the rectified covenant
the three vavs — 3×6=18, the chai (eighteen) blessings of the Amidah as 'arrows' shot from the bow of the rectified brit
connection and cleaving (devekut) to God — the essential attachment to the Blessed One attained through the gate of prayer

praying with strength (tefillah be-koach) — investing one's physical force/energy into the words of prayer, which empowers prayer (the aspect of Malkhut) to overcome the kingdom of wickedness and emerge from exile
the renewal of the oath to the Patriarchs — the sworn covenant to the Avot reawakened/re-established through prayer's power
the rectification (tikkun) of the Shekhinah — restoring Malkhut from her darkened exile state
the upholding/establishing of the covenant (brit) — making the brit stand firm, linked to 'u-vriti ne'emenet lo'
eshet chayil — the 'Woman of Valor' (Proverbs 31) as a name of Malkhut to be rectified through the strength God gives
'you shall rectify the eshet chayil' — the act of repairing Malkhut through the koach (strength) of Deut 8:18, read as la'asot chayil

Elokim — the Divine Name E-lohim (written euphemistically with a kuf, אֱלֹקִים), the name of God associated with judgment/immanence and, kabbalistically, with Malkhut / Lower Wisdom (chokhmah tata'ah); not the generic plural 'gods' or human judges

kodkod (קָדְקֹד) — the crown/top of the head, the anatomical skull-point; in LM II:85 identified by gimatria with the doubled "nachamu" (Yeshayahu 40:1) and linked to the oref (back of the neck, aspect of Leah) as the passage-point through Luz into Beit El
his shoulders — the shoulders as anatomical locus in the partzuf-scheme, the region behind/below the neck associated with Leah at the oref
the aspect of Leah — the first nukva (feminine partzuf) positioned at the oref (back of the head/neck), alluded to by luzim-nuts
the aspect of Rachel — the second, lower feminine partzuf, counterpart to Leah of the oref
beitzah — an egg, the enclosed shell-covered form likened to the nut/luz in this imagery of hidden inner content

the doubled word "nachamu" ("Be consoled, be consoled") of Isaiah 40:1, whose combined numerical value (2 × 104 = 208) equals that of "kodkod" (crown of the head), linking the consolation to the aspect of the oref/kodkod through which one enters Beit El (Likutey Moharan II:85)
Beit El — the place Jacob named 'House of God' (identified with the Temple), entered by way of the city Luz
entering the Beit HaMikdash — the act of coming into the Holy Temple (Beit El) by first passing through Luz/Leah
nuts called luzim — the egozim/luz-nuts (hazelnuts) whose name alludes to the city Luz and to Leah at the oref
the oref — the back of the neck / nape (anatomical rear of the head, kabbalistically the locus of Leah, the first feminine aspect, associated with the kodkod and the gateway to Beit El)
the luz tree (hazel/almond tree, ilan luz) whose nuts (egozim/luzim) symbolize Leah at the back of the neck and the town Luz as gateway to Beit El — in Likutey Moharan II:85

Luz — the nut called 'luz' (hazelnut/almond) homiletically identified with the biblical city Luz, the gateway through which one enters Beit El; symbolizing Leah, the first feminine aspect located at the back of the neck (oref/kodkod)

the luz bone — the indestructible almond-shaped bone at the nape of the neck (oref/kodkod) from which the body is rebuilt at the resurrection of the dead; linked to Leah at the back of the neck and to the city Luz as gateway to Beit El
the essence of our consolation — the core nechamah, rooted in 'nachamu nachamu' whose double gematria equals kodkod (crown of the head)
Shabbat Nachamu — the Sabbath after Tisha B'Av when Isaiah 40:1 'Nachamu nachamu' is read, Shabbat of consolation
ma'arikh rucho — patiently extending one's spirit: forbearing endurance in divine service, the counterpart to needing harsh fasts
ketanei amanah — 'those of little faith': the spiritual state/category of people deficient in emunah, whose weak faith necessitates fasting and harsh devotions
ketzar ruach — 'shortness of spirit/breath': the state of impatience and constricted spirit (cf. Exodus 6:9) stemming from little faith, opposite of patient, expansive breath of emunah
"af ein yesh ruach bahem" — verse fragment (Habakkuk 2:19/Jeremiah 10:14, of idols) 'there is no breath/spirit in them,' cited as prooftext for absence of ruach/spirit linked to faithlessness
kavvanat Elul — the Arizal's kabbalistic meditative intentions for the month of Elul, keyed to 'He who makes a path in the sea' (Isaiah 43:16), functioning as tikkun for the blemished covenant

canonical_he: מוצא זווגו, והיא אינה כנגדו, רק כרצונו
gloss_en: finding one's zivug (destined marriage partner) such that she is not 'against him' (a menagedet, opponent) but rather in accord with his will — the restored-match state achieved via tikkun ha-brit
forms: מוצא זווגו, והיא אינה כנגדו, רק כרצונו

gloss_en: the Elul kavvanot as the specific tikkun (rectification) for pegam ha-brit — the secret Avraham transmitted to Eliezer when sending him to find Yitzchak's match
the reversal whereby desire toward him is re-created in her — the restored ratzon of the destined bride toward her partner effected by tikkun ha-brit/Elul kavvanot
the remedial action of coming to the bar-da'at (the man of Da'at, the tzaddik) to hear Torah directly from his mouth — the means of finding one's shidduch
the resulting capacity to find one's shidduch (marriage match) — outcome of hearing Torah from the bar-da'at, since Da'at mediates the two opposites of every match
the customary breaking of an earthenware (clay) vessel at the time of an engagement match (tena'im/shidduch), whose reason Rabbi Nachman expounds
Sha'ar ha-Charsit — the 'Pottery/Potsherd Gate' (Jeremiah 19:2, gate facing Gei Ben-Hinnom), place-name invoked in the symbolism of breaking a clay vessel at an engagement
Gei Ben-Hinnom — the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem, the toponym underlying 'Gehinnom' (purgatory), linked to the bad-wife teaching of Eruvin 41b and the broken clay vessel

the opening (entrance) of Gehinnom — the gateway through which one enters purgatory, invoked in Likutey Moharan II:90 as the aspect symbolized by breaking a clay vessel at an engagement (since accepting a bad wife with love spares one from seeing the face of Gehinnom)
hitkashrut — the act of truly binding/attaching oneself to true tzaddikim, which yields complete teshuvah, atonement, sweetening of judgments, and the unification of the Holy One and His Shekhinah
mi'ut ha-levanah — the kabbalistic 'diminishment of the moon': Malkhut/Lower Wisdom shrunken when worldly wisdoms separate from Torah, synonymous with the exile of the Shekhinah
the totality of the holy Torah identified as Chokhmah Ila'ah (Upper Wisdom) — Torah as the supernal wisdom from which all lower worldly wisdoms derive

the exile of the Shekhinah — the kabbalistic state in which the Divine Presence (Shekhinah, identified with Lower Wisdom / Malkhut) is estranged and cut off from its divine source, as when worldly wisdoms are severed from Torah and God (paralleling the diminishing of the moon)
the filling of the moon's blemish (pegimat ha-levanah) — restoration of diminished Malkhut/Lower Wisdom, read from Targum on 'the wisdom of Shlomo increased' (I Kings 5)

canonical_he: נמתקין כל הדינים ונתכפרין כל העוונות
gloss_en: the sweetening/nullification of all judgments (dinim) and atonement of all sins — the effect when the two 'kings'/wisdoms unite and the moon's blemish is filled (Zohar Vayigash)
forms: נמתקין כל הדינים ונתכפרין כל העוונות

canonical_he: שהצדיק מלביש אור התורה בספורי דברים
gloss_en: the tzaddik's act of clothing (halbashah) the light of Torah in mundane stories/conversation — garbing Upper Wisdom in narrative so lower minds can receive it
forms: שהצדיק מלביש אור התורה בספורי דברים

canonical_he: מקשר חכמה תתאה עם חכמה עלאה
gloss_en: the tzaddik's function of binding Chokhmah Tata'ah (Lower Wisdom/Malkhut) with Chokhmah Ila'ah (Upper Wisdom) — the coupling that unites the two worlds
forms: מקשר חכמה תתאה עם חכמה עלאה

gloss_en: leimor (לֵאמֹר, 'saying') — the biblical infinitive 'to say' as homiletically read in LM II:91 as a term of clothing/garment (from emrah = garment, per 'bitza emrato'), signifying the tzaddik's clothing of Torah light in stories and words
halbashah — 'enclothement': the kabbalistic mechanism of garbing a higher light (Torah/Upper Wisdom) within lower garments (stories, worldly speech)
'et' (אֵת) — the accusative particle in 'Vayedaber Elokim et,' read as a symbol of Chokhmah Ila'ah (Upper Wisdom), as in 'et hashamayim'
'Vayedaber' ('And He spoke,' Exodus 20:1) — the word read as a term of zivug (coupling/connection), per 'they saw her medaberet' (Ketubot 13a)

"li" (לִי, 'for Me') — the word from Psalms 94:16 'Who will rise up for Me (li) against evildoers,' cited in Sotah 13b at Moshe's death, homiletically decomposed into its letters lamed and yud, signifying the bond of Lower Wisdom and Upper Wisdom that the tzaddik effects
the paired kabbalistic terms Chokhmah Ila'ah and Chokhmah Tata'ah — Upper Wisdom (Torah/supernal world) and Lower Wisdom (Malkhut/worldly wisdoms), the two worlds whose union the tzaddik effects

the letter-pair Lamed–Yud that spells the word לִי ("for Me") in "מִי יָקוּם לִי עִם מְרֵעִים", expounded as the joining of the letter Lamed (alluding to Upper Wisdom, chokhmah ila'ah) with the letter Yod (alluding to Lower Wisdom, chokhmah tata'ah) — the union effected by the true tzaddik; not the verb לָמַד ("he learned")

the Hebrew letter Lamed (ל) — the alphabet letter whose name evokes learning (limud/talmid), expounded in Likutey Moharan II:91 as the aspect of the student who learns and receives Lower Wisdom from the teacher's Upper Wisdom
the student learning from the master — the rav–talmid relation as the model for how Chokhmah Tata'ah suckles and receives from Chokhmah Ila'ah

the 'tower floating in the air' (migdal ha-poreach ba-avir) — the Talmudic/Zoharic image of a suspended aerial tower, used in Likutey Moharan II:91 as a symbol of esoteric wisdom associated with Lower Wisdom (Chokhmah Tata'ah); not a physical tower
the Ten Psalms (Tikkun HaKlali) — the set of ten chapters of the Book of Psalms prescribed by Rabbi Nachman as recitation for rectifying a nocturnal emission, corresponding to the ten kinds of melody
the Ten Kinds of Melody (asarah minei neginah — Berakhah, Ashrei, Maskil, etc.) with which the Book of Psalms was composed, the power basis of the Tikkun HaKlali
tikkun le-mikreh lailah — the rectification for a nocturnal seminal emission: reciting the ten psalms (Tikkun HaKlali) corresponding to the ten kinds of melody

the 'head of the children of Israel' (rosh bnei Yisrael) — the true tzaddik as the collective head/leader of the Jewish people, to whom each Jew binds his mind (esp. on Rosh Hashanah, forming one of the 'three heads')
mocho ve-da'ato — the tzaddik's brain/mind and consciousness, one of the 'heads' (rosh) that gather on Rosh Hashanah when one is with the tzaddik
go'el — 'redeemer': the kinsman-redeemer role (Boaz with Ruth), keyed to the secret of joining ge'ulah (redemption blessing) to tefillah (prayer)
the practice of innovating a novel Torah insight (chiddush) in the Rebbe's teachings — the act Rabbi Nachman urged his followers to attempt when studying his Torah
a great tikkun for hirhurim — the rectification of illicit/stray thoughts effected by innovating chiddushim in Torah
dabbar — leader/ruler/spokesman of a generation ('dabbar echad le-dor', Sanhedrin 8a)
wilderness/desert — as in 'u-mi-midbar matanah' (Numbers 21:18), symbolizing lowliness/self-effacement (making oneself ownerless like a wilderness)
'he will see / will be seen' (verb from ראה, seeing — associated with direct light, or ha-yashar)
son (Aramaic), as in the dictum 'b'ra kar'a d'avuha' — the son is the leg of his father
field (poetic form of שָׂדֶה), as in 'ziz sadai' — the creature/bird of the field (Ps. 50:11), here darshened as the Supernal Unification
profit/gain (revach), monetary earnings figuratively termed 'birth'
gnats/mosquitoes (Aramaic baqei, plural of בָּקָא), which the ox swats away with its long tail in the Talmudic passage (Shabbat 77b) 'they dwell in marshes and need to swat gnats'
